title: The Parcel Industry in the Emerging Logistics Landscape
problemStatement: As part of IBM’s role on our engagement with the USPS Office of Inspector General, we are reaching out to thought leaders in the global IBM community as we explore the disruption, transformation, and future in this critical industry. ,The current parcel and logistics landscape is the prototypical case study of examining the effects of disruption, transformation, innovation, incumbency, desire for monopoly protection, and agility, all set against the backdrop of a sharing economy that affects nearly every citizen of the world. Myriad forces require us to ask whether we have reached a tipping point, are we nearing an equilibrium, or is the ride just starting to get bumpy? ,The U.S. Postal Service and global postal operators understand that they risk being marginalized in an age of declining letter volumes and growing e-commerce unless they can compete in a marketplace defined by quality, flexibility, and agility, and outstanding customer experience. They are looking for help in identifying the most critical forces that will shape the global logistics landscape over the coming years and the opportunities and threats these forces will create and have asked IBM for help. ,Primarily, this will provide a great opportunity to contribute to a key client for IBM, and an industry undergoing significant global transformation. Many of the challenges global posts are facing through disruptive transformation are relevant to other companies and agencies in myriad sectors, so please feel free to share any and all ideas generated here to your clients as well.
outcome: The main outcome is an exhaustive list of thoughts and responses on the ideation blog that answer the 5 key questions we are researching for the USPS OIG. The answers will focus on the trends, forces, and disruptors are affecting the parcel and logistics sector and how these might affect postal operators, delivery companies, global commerce, the environment, and emerging delivery firms such as Amazon.
legacyParticipantType: People with varying backgrounds can participate!n1. title: IBM DT + Agile + DevOps POV
description: Iterative Outcome Delivery POV
problemStatement: IBM Practitioners are unclear about why, when and how to use IBM Design Thinking, Agile and DevOps on client engagements. Therefore, we need to clarify how these techniques interweave to deliver the best possible business outcomes for our clients.,To date, many practitioners have held the belief that simply following Agile practices is enough for iterative outcome delivery, but in fact this is not true. Agile empowers teams to be far more responsive to the users’ needs, however, it does not help teams to focus on the user experience, which is what IBM Design Thinking does so well. Further, simply using Agile to quickly get outcomes is not necessarily going to lead to value gained by the end user, and for this reason, Dev Ops techniques must also be employed. So, to put it simply, all three of these techniques cannot be used effectively in isolation.
outcome: A truly successful project delivery requires all three of them used together. IBM Design Thinking, Agile and DevOps, are the three techniques or practices which are essential for any user-centered client engagement and iterative outcome delivery.,The key objectives of this POV are to:,- Clarify for our practitioners, the importance of using all three techniques together, and exactly how all three techniques are interwoven,- Explain how and when all three techniques are used on different types of engagements in order to achieve the best possible business outcomes,- Communicate a consistent message across all of GBS and IBM as a whole, on what is the best approach to deliver user-centered outcomes; fast, and to,- Empower our go-to-market teams with the right messages to communicate with our clients regarding IBM’s value proposition for delivering user-centered iterative outcomes at speed and scale
finalOutcome: This POV is a great assets for our team that are engaging the client on either of these fronts and bring together the synergy between these practice and can materialize much bigger value for IBM compared to going after agile, IBM Design Thinking or Dev Ops on its own.
closeValue: Clarify a point of confusion to a lot of IBMers both practitioners and executives. Help us differentiate ourselves in the market given our strength in these practices, and allows our sales team to work together not against each other.

title: Identifying Integration Opportunities and Imperatives
description: Cross-Organizational Integration Opportunities and Imperatives
problemStatement: With its many acquisitions and key strategic themes, such as CAMSS, Cognitive Business, and IoT, adequate integration across IBM’s organizations offers unique opportunities to increase the value proposition of service offerings and solutions alike. Today, some IBM initiatives are managed by various organizations having limited interaction and collaboration across the board. Acquisitions are often integrated by a single organization (e.g. Analytics), sometimes neglecting the impact for other organizations, for instance services or solution teams. ,The IBM AoT is in a unique position to oversee and identify integration opportunities and to suggest integration imperatives to be adopted across various IBM organizations. The AoT should have an advisory role to identify integration opportunities and gaps, and the potential impact of products, tools, and assets for other organizations.
outcome: Depending on the topic, the AoT should assemble a team from various organizations to evaluate the current value proposition and potential for improving this value proposition by increasing the state of integration. This should yield a set of integration recommendations and imperatives. Integration could be related to product and tools integration, increasing the industry-relevance of existing solutions by leveraging new products and tools, or taking into consideration products and tools for higher-level service provisioning. The will result in an improved business value proposition of better integrated individual components and assets. ,This process to identify integration imperatives can be done iteratively with different themes. The driver could be manifold: an acquisition could represent a unique opportunity, a new initiative driven by IBM across the board could trigger an initiative, and a new set of products and tools should be evaluated as a potential value for other organizations. The turnaround time from launch to making available a set of recommendations should be 6-8 weeks. ,The AoT will become more relevant can develop suggestions (identifying gaps, leveraging value across organizations) proactively, without necessarily waiting for someone to request this ‘service’.
finalOutcome: Related to this initiative, we have now created 2 SPRINT activities, which have been validated with Dirk Wittkopp as the executive sponsor.,1st SPRINT activity: https://aot.raleigh.ibm.com/aot/aotact.nsf/activitiesLUp/A7792A4E4EA597E985258083004B8E14?open&login&From=myactivities,2nd SPRINT activity: https://aot.raleigh.ibm.com/aot/aotact.nsf/activitiesLU/DAFCC7830E9E0D0485258083004D0939?open&login&From=myactivities,.

title: Internet of Things in Banking
problemStatement: The banking industry is being deeply impacted and transformed by technology and the digitization process that are changing the customer behavior, of hyper connected social users that rely mainly on peers to make very informed financial decisions, and tearing down entry barriers allowing the participation of new players, who are creating new strong competition that commoditize a formerly profitable businesses. ,Currently, technology is fostering a completely new age in the Internet. This platform, born to connect people to enterprise systems, evolved during the last decade to support much more complex interactions not just with people but with communities of people as social platforms. More recently it evolved to support the integration and interaction of systems and enterprises through the API Economy platforms. ,Now it is the time of Things becoming part of the Internet ecosystem, with the explosion of the Internet of Things (IoT) where those things can interact among them, with systems and also with people.  IoT is transforming all the industries (automotive, healthcare, etc.) and for sure will impact and transform the financial services industry. In the IoT economy participants (Smart Cars, Smart Homes, Smart Appliances, Smart Machines, Smart Shops, Smart Healthcare, Smart Cities, etc) will get connected each other on platforms that will provide the support for interactions and transactions that could include interchange of value with financial impact. These IoT platforms will require not only payments capabilities but also more sophisticated financial products and services like lending or leasing that could be adapted based on the things economy. Additionally, banking customers using new sophisticated devices like bracelets, smart phones, smart watches, glasses or smart clothes could have a much better experience if those devices (wearables) are integrated into the banking systems providing a much more friendly and convenient access to the banking services and also capturing contextual customer information to improve the customer experience. ,Currently many banks are starting to explore what should be their role in the IoT economy but there is no any deep analysis (neither in IBM nor externally) defining what new financial business models can rise in the IoT economy or uses cases showing the new banking roles. Our banking customers are requiring our vision on what should be their role in this new IoT economy.
outcome: An IBM AoT/IA/BBVA PoV identifying the key IoT technologies, business models and uses cases for IoT in banking showing the kind of financial products and services banks could inject in the IoT economy. The three main areas where to explore IoT in banking scenarios and use cases are: ,Physical asset management. Managing the physical assets of the bank: buildings, spaces, devices, presence, etc. Very focus on energy and operations efficiency.,IoT for improving customer experience. How things like wearables or the instrumented branch offices or financial devices (ATMs, Kiosks, etc) can improve the customer interaction,Financial services in IoT ecosystems. Scenarios of financial services in cross-industry IoT ecosystems identifying the services to be injected (payments, loans, leasing, etc). The role of banks in the new ecosystems ,Also it would analyze the IoT impact on the banks’ business and IT architecture.
legacyParticipantType: Passionates of Internet of Things, open minded out of the box thinkers ready to submit their spare time to work on a study
legacyValue: Confirm IBM Though Leader position in Banking industry and IoT space

title: Solution Architectures for the Cloud
problemStatement: ‘Cloud’ is profoundly affecting ‘how we do business’ at multiple levels. Much attention has been attracted by the shifts in the server market and pervasive availability of all kinds of XaaS(*) offerings, specifically PaaS, SaaS and Solutions as a Service. It should not come therefor as a surprise that ‘Cloud’ is also having an effect on how we architect and build our solutions. However, until date, this effect has minimally been captured, analyzed and fed back into the best practices\methods\techniques we use to define solution architectures (TeamSD, AD 2.0,…) whereby we particularly focus on the techniques used by IT Architects. ,The current solution architecture methods focus firstly on identifying the functional building blocks out of which the solution will be assembled (mainly via the Component Modeling technique), then use the Operational Modeling technique to ensure that these building blocks are combined in such a way that the system will deliver both on the functional and non-functional requirements. ,‘Cloud’ re-visits the options we have at various points of the system engineering cycle, and our current set of techniques does not completely take this into account. Although the responsibility of the architect still covers both driving the definition of the solution and its management, the use of ‘cloud’ will decidedly affect his\her ‘solution thinking’.,Without recognizing the impact of ‘cloud’ on our set of techniques and not having access to cloud related best practices, it remains up to the practitioners on a project to decide on how best to deal with XaaS in their proposed solution architectures. ,This can translate to an inconsistent use of Cloud related technology across IBM solutions. This also translates to the effect of not being able to harden solutions to the level required. It is therefore imperative for us to understand how we should approach the architecture of such cloud-based systems and be able to rely on best practices for doing so.,This study aims to determine the impact of the XaaS environment on our current set of Solution Architecture related techniques and best practices. Hereto we propose the following activities:,•	Evaluate the impact on our currently established techniques of making them also suitable for designing cloud based solution architectures,•	Determine best practices and patterns to enable cloud based solution architectures,•	Gather examples of ,o	how we are currently architecting solutions based on XaaS (both IBM and non IBM),o	how this topic is addressed in our methods and curriculum, if at all
outcome: The study will formulate recommendations on how we can improve on our current approaches to incorporate XaaS into our solution architectures by ,•	Providing direction on how our techniques can explicitly address the impact of ‘Cloud’,•	Identifying required updates to the curriculum ,•	establishing a first set of best practices and patterns for designing solution architectures taking advantage of XaaS,The Academy of Technology is best placed to tackle these kinds of questions, given the cross line of business scope and the wide range of expertise we need to draw upon to drive this study to a successful outcome.
legacyParticipantType: - Field IT Architects proficient with current UMF modeling techniques (Component Modeling and Operational Modeling) who have a working interest in Cloud solution designn- Cloud Architect with a deep knowledge of CCRA or who have participated in the CCRA development
legacyValue: The study will generate guidance on how architectural techniques should evolve in Cloud projects and on the identification of assets that can be used during project delivery.,In addition the community that will be created, is expected to be both a source and a diffusion mechanism for best practices, references and repeatable patterns, supporting the quality and profitability of IBM Cloud projects.

title: Practical Operational Modelling - OM for Cloud Services
executiveChampionReason: Kathy is looking after the future of global solution design (with Jenny Ang)
description: Practical Operational Modelling - OM for Cloud Services
problemStatement: How is Operational Modelling performed effectively?  Even in the Cloud world, the need to model a system in order to ensure that the Non-Functional requirements will be met is still just as important as ever. However there is often a gap between what modelling is actually performed on projects, and what the method says should be done. Further, the premise is that Operational Modelling for cloud could be optimised.,The word 'Practical' in the title is deliberate.  This is not intended as a theoretical study, but is intended to look at the practicalities of working within a real project, with the pressures which come from delivery, time-scales and cost.,The study is split into three ‘streams’,1.	OM for Cloud Systems – how to adapt Operational Modelling to better handle systems which are being built to be hosted in Cloud,2.	OM for Cloud Services – how to adapt Operational Modelling for the build of Cloud Services (IaaS, PaaS, SaaS),3.	OM Revisions – how should the techniques and notation be revised for the new world,This stream is OM for Cloud Services
outcome: There is significant scope for improving the way that we design and build cloud services.  This study looks into how we can optimise this to focus on what is important for cloud, reducing cost and risk.

title: The expanding role of the Information Architect
problemStatement: In the past the Information Architect specialization was centered around delivering systems that were essentially inwards looking, that delivered strong 'system of record' and analytic solutions to help a business understand its operations, partners and customers.,The last 5 years have seen a profound change in the skills needed to be up to date in this profession, not only in the breadth of data now accessible by business (system of engagement opening up many new avenues) but also the critical data of much of the information generated to add competitive insights and disruptors to industries that have been established for years.,Information Architects now need to be aware much more than was the case ranging from the standard solutions (EDW, MDM, Information Integration, etc) to a whole new wave of solutions - streams, graph, visualization, NoSQL dbs (such as graph, documents stores, key value pairs, and column), open data, are just a few of the topics we are expected to discuss now. The 4 'V's' have added new challenges to the role and this initiative will describe the changes an Information Architect now needs to understand and how this changes his / her role to an Enterprise one as a key individual sitting alongside Programme Managers and Enterprise Architects. ,It will introduce some new ways of thinking around method and training to help Information A4rchitects with these problems (some already in existence but not well publicized) and will outline the broader and richer role an Information architect needs to undertake to truly have impact at an Enterprise level
outcome: A ppt that describes what is required of an Enterprise Information Architecture now and for the next few years, AND a set of reference docs that will aid this specialization to achieve such goals
publicationDescription: This paper outlines the changing role of the Information Architect and how IBM need to respond to meet those challenges
legacyParticipantType: Other Information Architects, some consultancy skills required
legacyValue: Enable our Information Architects to take on the new roles required of business today. That is one which will allow them to encompass all forms of data, the channels they arrive and leave in and the new ways of manipulating data into insights that are beginning to surface.,Without this both boutique consultancies and our major competitors will begin to place an "air gap" between their capabilities and our own.,With these augmented skills our information architect community will be in a strong place to drive new business across all sectors.

Fraud scheme increases in complexity and frequency causing economic and societal costs and intensified customer expectations goes out of style current post-processing or sampling fraud detection and investigation capabilities. Fraud has a lot of consequences such as operational effectiveness, customer confidence, brand reputation and support regulatory compliance obligations are also increasing the need to reinforce current solutions. title: Cloud Application Operations & Integrated Service Management
executiveChampionReason: Shankar Kalyana is the CTO of GBS Cloud Service line within the Cloud Application Innovation growth platform. Shankar, several others including myself (Balakrishnan, Distinguished Engineer) have build several solutions with clients and have significant learnings in this space of cloud application operations and we have collaborated significantly with IBM Cloud, GTS teams in this process. It is important that Shankar champions this cause so that we get the right PoV across to various IBM teams to ensure we are doing the right things for our clients w.r.to Cloud operations and integrated service management.
description: This initiative is to establish a PoV on Cloud application operations and integrated service management and accumulation of best practices from various client situations.
problemStatement: How we develop software and manage it is changing rapidly - and how they are integrated and deployed on a continuous basis. Traditionally all the software and hardware are within the reach of the teams (directly or remotely) so that deployments, configurations, troubleshooting, collaboration across teams were much more simpler. With cloud, the architectures have transformed into a multi-service provider architecture with limited visibility into characteristics and operational data of each of the services. Yet there is a need to ensure integrated visibility into the solution operations. Multiple service providers at different SLA / SLO levels and lack of common integration models drives significant challenges. Over this, clients are expecting solution providers to take end to end ownership. There is a need to ensure right level of performance and availability that line up with Service Level Agreements (SLAs) and Service Level Objectives (SLOs) of different service providers. Cloud technologies (including multi-cloud scenarios) are changing rapidly posing additional set of problems w.r.to upgrades / patching etc. There is also a need to build Site reliability engineering skills which is in front and center of building, deploying and run-managing complex cloud solutions. Overall, there is a need to build a point of view on what it takes to build and operate cloud solutions optimally. This initiative is meant to build the point of view through various client experiences.
outcome: A cohesive point of view on what are the best practices to build, deploy and manage cloud applications.

title: Natural Disaster Management using Cloud, IOT and Blockchain
executiveChampionReason: Idea indicates Government as a primary stakeholder which is the Champion's primary work area
description: Cloud-IOT-Blockchain solution connecting multiple service providers during a natural disaster
problemStatement: In the past few months, the world has been witnessing the devastation caused by hurricanes. It has displaced many residents. Many moved to make-shift shelters. Many churches, auditoriums were converted to shelters during the crisis. But for residents to know the location of the nearest shelter and if there is still space to accommodate them was a challenge.  Additionally, some residents needed to know which of the shelters is equipped to deal with certain medical conditions. ,I spoke to two families who were caught in hurricane Harvey in Houston and they expressed the dire need of a mobile application that could have helped them get more latest information. Here are some of the inputs they shared:,- They were registered with National Weather station which gave them alerts on the hurricane,- They had to go to a local government website to know about shelters. But many shelters were closed and the website did not show the latest information. There was no website which gave information on the shelters that newly opened up for people during the event.,- During the crisis, many volunteers delivered food. All communications were via social media (Facebook) or word of mouth.,- People went to multiple sites to get an update on a particular location. Most latest updates were posted by residents themselves.
outcome: Outcome:,Solution architecture of an application which connects the following types of users on a Blockchain network:,Shelter owners, medical services/institutes, food suppliers, government agencies, transportation agencies, residents, telecom companies, Benefits:,- This solution requires data to be shared by multiple organizations. It may be led by the government or an authority that is managing disasters. Service providers can become a member of the network and conduct all transactions on a trusted single platform. They do not need to know each other. They trust the application running on Blockchain will authenticate the users and record their transactions accurately.,- Funds are distributed by the fund providers (like Government, etc.) and residents or service providers consume the funds as needed.- Govt spending calculation and claims and aid estimation and utilization of the aid  ,Which industry?,- Government Disaster Management Department,- Telecom industry has been participating in many smart city initiatives. This could be a new innovative space for them to look at. This solution can be provided to all their subscribers for a nominal fee. ,From my interview with the Houston affected residents, I learnt that they would be more than happy to pay and register for such a service.,Business Value:,- Foundation for a much larger commercial eco system (Suppliers, Government Services, etc.),- Solution uses IBM Cloud Platform (Bluemix), IBM Blockchain, Watson IOT Platform, Weather Company Data, etc. ,- IBM to be the first to provide a holistic solution to address such a problem ,- IBM's social responsibility to provide a solution that makes the world smarter

description: Clinical Informatics Partnership w/ Geisinger Health System: WEX and ML Driven Insight into Sepsis Indicators leveraged at the Point of Care
problemStatement: Sepsis is a complex clinical syndrome resulting from the body’s response to infection.  Sepsis accounted for 1.7 million hospitalizations (2009) and 6.2% ($23.4 billion) of aggregate costs of all hospitalizations. While significant improvements in patient outcomes may have resulted from more rapid diagnosis/treatment, hospital mortality remains high and survivors remain at substantial risk of persistent physical/cognitive disability.  Although remarkable scientific advances have generated tremendous volumes of data and provided new insights into sepsis, translating them into clinical practice has been difficult.  Current reductionist approaches distill this complex disease state into a prescriptive set of actions and produce a standard set of results.  These methods fail to address larger systemic issues that may impact overall outcomes or provide the ability to generate new insights.  To generate low cost, high impact, rapid-cycle insights, a larger integrated data-driven, systems approach to understanding both existing knowledge and the complex adaptive health care environment is required
outcome: The proposed Academy Sprint Initiative will workshop, validate, architect, and demonstrate a framework for delivering NLP and ML driven insight into Sepsis indicators and predictors at the Point of Care.  This will be done through the analysis of publication (e.g. PubMed) and patient medical data using standard technologies (e.g. medical ontologies: MeSH, UMLS, etc). This will be a partnership between IBM and Geisinger Health System and will include a Research Data Worksheet allowing IBM to get clinical De-identified Geisinger data for analysis alongside the analysis of medical research papers. At the end of the initiative, IBM will provide a technical and executive summary including proposed IBM solutions and services that could then funnel into Geisinger's grant proposal.  The team would also create technical documentation of how the demonstrated ML and WEX models/jobs were created for future internal and external enablement.  The collateral produced by this Initiative can be used directly with numerous IBM clients considering ML and Watson driven insight in the healthcare market.  An example is Argus Health, where this team partnered with the Chief Medical Officer to close a $4.1M Q2 deal including ML capabilities.
finalOutcome: Amazing collaboration between Geisinger medical researchers and IBM leveraging IBM Analytics products WEX and DSX to find new insights for treating Sepsis patients! The work generated 3 Medium Blogs, 2 YouTube videos and a conference paper submission (CSCE'18).
closeValue: Huge reference value demonstrating impact of IBM Analytics to find new insights for Sepsis, a disease with high mortality

title: Today’s Infrastructure must be like brains for AI

description: Today’s Infrastructure must be like brains for AI
problemStatement: Servers, storage and workload management need to be designed from the ground up for cognitive workloads. There are several critical requirements such as: rapid access to data (low latency and fast storage), faster time to insights (compute infrastructure designed for big data), accelerated performance for complex analytics/machine learning algorithms (hardware acceleration) and preventing data ingestion bottlenecks (unified access to block, file and object data).
outcome: The goal is to write a TechNote on a comparison between the infrastructure and the brain. AI is often a loop composed of 3 elements: Learning, Transmitting and Improving. When we talk about “Transmitting”, we talk about Systems able to process information. A well-known “System” to process huge amounts of data and provide cognitive insights in real time is the brain
finalOutcome: Businesses today require cognitive systems that can gain insight from the structured and unstructured data stressing their IT infrastructure.
closeValue: If the brain does not work as it should in the different areas described, the system is not more able to process the data correctly causing neurological disorders. It’s similar for any IT infrastructure. It is desired for an infrastructure to process the data efficiently and faster than the brain.
publicationCategory: TechNote (one page and NOT IBM Confidential)
publicationDescription: Artificial Intelligence (AI) is no longer considered science fiction. The main raison of this shift from various AI research disciplines into an array of applied cognitive businesses is mainly due to data explosion and technology improvements. AI is often a loop composed of 3 elements: Learning, transmitting and improving. When we talk about “Transmitting”, we talk about systems able to process information. A well-known advanced “system” is the brain. Scientists around the world are working on architectures inspired by the brain. There are still huge differences between computers and the brain but also similarities. What happens if the IT infrastructure doesn't reach the expected speed and efficiency? The System will lose memory and thus data, will have I/O bottlenecks, will not store the data in the right location, will not provide answers when they need to be provided, will not be able to process all needed data. This means that the infrastructure is not designed for cognitive workloads. Servers, storage and workload management need to be designed from the ground up for cognitive workloads.

title: Securing/controlling non-textual  PHI/PII data (spoken words, images ..) transmitted by IoT devices
executiveChampionReason: Bret Greenstein owns cognitive consumer IOT solutions. The output of this study directly benefits his "Cognitive Spaces" offering targeted at patient rooms, senior citizen homes, hotel rooms, etc.
description: Study and discover best practices to protect PHI/PII data  expressed and transmitted via voice, images, and video.
problemStatement: With the advent of IoT devices in nursing homes and hospitals we will have a new set of privacy issues. So far HIPAA-compliant solutions only worried about patient data that is in computer readable textual forms (whether structured or unstructured). However with speakers in patient rooms and elder citizens' homes we have to worry about Personal Health information (PHI) and PII (personally identifiable information) going into public clouds.   Given this problem with commercial devices (e.g., Amazon Echo, Google Home, etc.), how do we ensure that PHI/PII data spoken by people (sometimes inadvertently)  is protected/masked/obfuscated/.. before going to a public cloud? What are the best practices?  What other complexities arise if we go beyond speech to images and video (e.g., via cameras in patients' rooms)?  This study is intended to capture the problem scope, current state of the art, best practices and recommendations for a range of solutions  with cost/benefit tradeoffs.,Bret Greenstein (VP, Cognitive Consumer Business) and George Eisenberger (CTO, Watson Health) are the exec sponsors for this study.
outcome: Expected benefits of this study are 1) Thought leadership in an emerging area 2) Potential solutions with IBM offerings 3) Best practices 4) Clear recommendations for customers in the near term 5) Identifying relevant Product/Offering enhancements.
finalOutcome: Thought leadership in a fast emerging area of IOT devices and privacy implications. Visibility to the current state of the products and offerings within IBM and outside. Clearly identified short term actions: Speed up HIPAA compliant Watson cognitive services, partner with others to fill gaps, educate/build awareness of GDPR and HIPAA,  and achieve competitive pricing on suitable solution components.
closeValue: Creating awareness to a fast developing market opportunity and identifying gaps in our portfolio to address the opportunity.
publicationDescription: Reduced cost of sensors, increased connectivity, cloud-based resources and advances in analytics have made IOT solutions pervasive. End-user speech-based devices (e.g., Amazon's Echo) are rapidly entering enterprise solutions (in cars, offices, factories, hospitals and hotels). The increased end-user orientation also brings increased privacy concerns (e.g., HIPAA and GDPR regulations). The problem of compliance is exacerbated by new data types like audio, video, images and unstructured text that IOT devices are easily able to gather and ship around. A recognition of this problem prompted the study to investigate potential solutions and generate recommendations for IBM.

title: Prompt Detection of Warning Signs and Symptoms of Stroke
executiveChampionReason: Fabrizio is the Italy Technical Executive and Innovation Director
description: FasthHealth application aspires to improve lives and gives hope by raising awareness and education to address as many people as possible to early detecting signs and symptoms of a stroke.
problemStatement: Stroke is the 2th leading cause of death in the world after coronary artery disease and the 3th in Italy. About 6.5 million deaths resulted from stroke. About half of people who have had a stroke live less than one year and it is the leading cause of adults disability. In particular, 40% of PEOPLE who have a TIA ( transient ischemic attack)  will have an actual stroke and the  80% of stroke can be prevented both though an adequate lifestyle and through effective monitoring of the population.,To date, the monitoring only takes place with the hospitalization, therefore, the number of monitored patients is contained and at high cost.
outcome: FasthHealth application aspires to improve lives and gives hope by raising awareness and education to address as many people as possible to early detecting signs and symptoms of a stroke. Create a prototype for the patience self prediction of developing stroke conditions based on the internationally recognised medical procedure using the Mingazzini's tests,The aims are to:,1. Improving clinical outcomes and monitor a range of larger patients at the same time .,2.Cost control linked to reduced hospitalization and the use of value-based services.,3.Using cognitive and analytics tools to find clinically and economically unrelated correlations.
finalOutcome:
The initiative gave a great contribution to develop new cognitive business in the Healthcare industry. The initiative developed a prototype of a healthcare solution (FastHealth) that aims home monitoring of patients in a post TIA (Transient Ischemic Attack) phase to prevent ischemic stroke. The prototype  encodes  the neurological examination ( through four test ), how the patients were in the hospital and  allows the doctor to monitor multiple patients simultaneously with higher frequency, increasing the patient’s awareness of the disease. 
In the first phase of the study the emphasis was on recognizing the signs and symptoms of stroke and the real possibility of predicting its occurrence, in this phase there is the identification of population could be use the prototype.  In the second phase, we defined the cognitive solution from the identification of the patients suitable for home monitoring, to the analysis of the data and the use of analytics and cognitive tools aimed at identifying correlations between data that today are hidden.
The study describes the clinical and economic benefits that the use of the solution will bring to the hospital: the reduction in the number of hospitalizations, the reduction of healthcare costs, the improvement of the patient's quality of life, the improvement of clinical protocols and the timely detection of events at risk.
closeValue: The iniziative created a user friendly application designed to improve people's lifestyle through their awareness and education about disease, It could revolution the way to care patients affected by a Transient Ischemic Attack. It helps IBM to propose innovative solution in the healthcare market. The asset was very appreciated by some important hospital and currently we have negotiation to evaluate real implementation. The initiative generated a great interest with healthcare specialists and with the technical community. It contributed to demonstrated the capability of the IBM Cloud platform and the innovative cognitive Watson services. It is an important asset to build innovative solutions and develop cognitive business with clients.

problemStatement: The current process causes long loops of mails requesting changes, approvals and generates a large number of DoU versions that can result in distrust for the client and confusion for the Team.
outcome: Create a Smart Contract App:,Follows the DOU process as a FILE (asset).,Keep organizations connected all over the process.
finalOutcome:

closeValue: We will deliver an improved engagement system with a fast and trusted process for IBM internal contracts, saving time and effort.
publicationDescription:
Project Title: Blockchain for DOU - BlueContracts App

Nowadays, IBM manage internally lots of agreements and each business unit has their own system, this “Smart Contract App” will standardize the process providing transparency, security and agile management between all the internal contracts at IBM - Worldwide.
With this tool, we focused in Document of Understanding (DOU) but it is easily scalable to other kind of agreements such as: ICAs, SoW, internal authorizations or approvals, etc.

BlueContracts features: 
- Follows the DOU process as a FILE (asset) - Smart Contract.
- Keep organizations connected all over the process.
- Blockchain Business Logic records the transactions: document uploaded, create new version, actions for approvers, modifications.
- In real time (Bluemix App), users can consult the document. 
- The end of process will be the approval and sign between the Managers.
- The record of DOU versions will be stored at the Shared Ledger.

title: Using a Relational DBMS as a Persistent Store in Hyperledger Fabric
executiveChampionReason: Mohan is the IBM expert in this area and the initiator of this challenge
description: Explore the Relational DBMS as a Persistent Store in Hyperledger Fabric V1
problemStatement: The Hyperledger Fabric Version 1 (HLF V1) supports the concept of smart contracts. A smart contract or chaincode is business logic that has been written in one of many supported languages and executed within the fabric’s peers. In order to support the management of assets using chaincode execution, the HLF V1 provides persistent memory in the form of the world state DB. The current implementation of the world state DB supports NoSQL back ends, with limited query functionality, thus, making it difficult to do the most basic of lookups. Our project aims to enhance the HLF V1 by introducing a new SQL layer, which will have support for rich query capabilities, making it easier for smart contract writers to implement business logic using the various SQL primitives they are used to. There are two immediate extensions from this work: 1) explore the concept of in-place analytics in the world state DB itself and 2) get deeper insights that would help us explore how a relational database management system by itself could be made to support blockchain functionality without the surrounding fabric layer.
outcome: One of the biggest complaints we are facing today by clients as well as critics is the lack of basic querying support under the blockchain fabric. This project aims to add that level of support natively to the Hyperledger Fabric V1 (HLF V1). By doing so, IBM will be the first to introduce native SQL support to the HLF V1, while at the same time, help keep IBM’s Blockchain Platform (which is based on HLFV1) at the cutting edge of blockchain technology as more companies enter the market (e.g., Oracle). By introducing rich queries into the world sate DB, we hope to provide a more appealing backend to chaincode writers, so that we can have richer solutions for our customers. Moreover, as we continue this work, and explore in-place analytics within the world state DB itself, we hope to help make HLF V1 the blockchain of choice for any blockchain specific analytics workloads.

title: Buildings Gone Cognitive - Optimizing our Energy Consuming Systems

description: At its core, this project proposes to replace the hard-coded logic that defines how our buildings operate today, with flexible machine learning algorithms, that continuously optimize buildings’ efficiency. problemStatement: Today, nearly all buildings largest energy consuming systems are operated by small computers with extremely limited processor power and are connected via networks with very limited bandwidth. These systems, usually decades old, tend to attract human attention only when problems arise, yet they often waste energy, and are responsible for nearly half of energy consumed in the world.  Imagine if we could bring the power of cognitive computing to these legacy control systems, to continuously optimize them in real time, allowing them to learn over time and share what they’ve learned with each other.
outcome: The project aims to build a cognitive cloud platform upon which building controls manufacturers will integrate their existing and new products, unlocking Watson machine learning technology for use with their existing customers. We conservatively estimate that this technology will save 10-15% of buildings' annual energy use and maintenance costs. In addition, we anticipate this becoming a business-to-business offering that creates recurring revenue for IBM by leveraging existing partnerships in this space. This will be the industry’s first real-time, cloud-based, cognitive platform for control of buildings.
finalOutcome: This project demonstrated that cognitive system have tremendous potential in the Building Energy Management space and can significantly improve upon existing technologies. Additionally, the project sparked significant interest in the larger IBM IoT community about the potential for IBM to build a true business case for this technology.

title: Managing the health of the cloud
problemStatement: The whole area of health surveillance of our cloud offerings is something we have to improve, so the goal of the initiative should be to identify best practices to ensure continuity of service and facilitate problem determination and resolution. Many teams have made attempts at creating solutions that address their specific monitoring priorities and It seems a given that at least parts of what was created could be reused generically.,We don't  know how we compare to the rest of the industry: Amazon, Microsoft, Google, Facebook, etc. all have highly available services - what are they doing that we're not? Etsy are recognised as being in the forefront of service monitoring, particularly in the area of anomaly detection: can we do something like that?,Applying structure to a holistic view of the health of the service, referring to personae à la  UCD, we can consider:,* The business persona focuses on availability and business readiness,* The app persona focuses on middleware and infrastructure health insofar as it affects availability and performance,* The offering persona focuses on the supply of services which address her business objectives,* The infrastructure persona focuses on SLA, user satisfaction and continuous improvement.,This whole question can be made very broad, such that initially the scope needs to be well-defined. The questions below may be more than the initiative can realistically address, at least initially:,* How do you determine the cause of failures in a hybrid cloud service?,* What strategies are required to ensure the service remains operational and to mask the visibility of failures?,* How can health monitoring identify trends and improve the overall hybrid cloud service?,* How does DevOps approaches help or hinder?,* How should the ITIL processes be adapted for hybrid clouds and devops?,* How can Service Integration and an end-to-end view of the service improve the speed of root cause analysis and monitoring of SLA's in a Hybrid Cloud Environment? ,* How can Pattern-based topology deployment help to keep environments like test, system integration etc. consistent to keep cloud application environments healthy? ,* What about the organisational aspect of the retained organisation? How do we make sure that the right roles and responsibilities are defined and implemented? ,* How does an approach look like to do root cause analysis in a multi-sourced cloud environment? Think about an environment which consists of e.g. SL and AWS to serve a single app, although this could also be a hybrid app.,* How can a predictive approach for "Dynamic Automation" in a multi-sourced cloud environment look like? Is there a need for "service aggregation" with event correlation service based across different cloud environments ,We need to be careful that we do not apply apply "old IBM" thinking to what is a "new IBM" problem.  Once can approach the question from the point of view if the application is written properly for the cloud then it doesn't need to worry, it can fix itself - if the answer isn't Tivoli,what should it be?  In other words, the question needs to be framed correctly.
outcome: Documented best practices and new/improved tooling, with a preferably consistent approach across our stack of IaaS, PaaS and SaaS, as well as guidelines for cloud solutions, both internal and customer-focused.
finalOutcome: The study highlights a number of different aspects of managing the Cloud from the aspects of availability and reliability, as well as how to identify how well it is performing. As a side effect, it emphasized how other efforts that address related areas were not visible across the community of those who are focused on Cloud, something that needs to be addressed.
closeValue: It pulls together in a single place, what people are doing and what they are missing in order to address the requirements of a reliable, healthy cloud service.
publicationDescription: This describes the difficulties and appropriate responses and actions vis-a-vis cloud solutions, emphasizing that while there are many extant mechanisms and recommendations, this is still very unclear and lacking focus. The recommendations will hopefully address these
legacyParticipantType: The participants are those who are involved in the operational and monitoring aspects of our cloud offerings. These are folk from our IaaS, PaaS and SaaS teams, including the NOC and app specialist communities, as well as those in development teams charged with creating monitoring solutions, particularly Tivoli.nSpecifically, I would expect Jonathan Young and Klaus König because of their "Health as a Service" effort, and there are doubtless others in similar positions who would be interested in this initiative.
legacyValue: Improving our ability to see what's happening within our Cloud offerings gives clear benefits: ,* Improved quality of service, with associated improvement in levels of customer satisfaction ,* Reduced service outages, resulting in reduced payments to affected customers ,* Tivoli have products that address parts of this problem domain. SmartCloud Notes did investigate these and found them lacking and are now using external paid services like New Relic, LogEntries and PagerDuty instead. One potential result of this initiative could be to help Tivoli's products get to the level where we in IBM are happy to use them, particularly potentially ground-breaking products like Predictive Insights, which would help their consumption by customers too. ,* Potential savings in operational costs from improved service stability

title: Watson Conversation Continuous Learning Dashboard
executiveChampionReason: IMT Italy Technical and Innovation Executive
description: A handful tool to perform Watson Conversation learnings would take the form of a dashboard, that combine visual data-driven analysis of conversation performances and punctual errors analysis.
problemStatement: Fine tuning a dialog built with Watson Conversation service to finally mimic a real human dialogue, requires acting on three different aspects: enriching existing intents and entities, creating new ones if the need arises and verifying the clearness, fluidity, and overall dialogue structure. ,All those parameters, set during the first design phase, are usually revised and validated through multiple user tests. When testers number and testing time is high, it becomes harder to track all errors encountered as well as new needs expressed by final users to be turned into future functionalities to be implemented.
outcome: WHY,The goal of the dashboard is to provide a tracking and analytic tool for conversations made by users to find insights and enrich dialogs in Watson Conversation,WHAT,A reusable asset developed and experimented in a real use case scenario for continuous monitoring and learning of dialogues built with Watson Conversation.,HOW,The benefits stemming from the integration between visual graph representation and Watson services integration, allow developers to easily spot points of improvement, both acting on existing intents and entities enrichment and future nodes and functionalities implementation,A dashboard integrates complementary sections, which combined offer a useful support to developers and managers that need to use Conversation service on a daily basis. ,a) Insightful graph visually represents the dialogue tree structure, displaying additional information for each node in the network. ,b) Nodes, intents and entities use over time are filtered to obtain data-driven analytics charts. ,c) Retrain section allows users to track and classify logged errors and/or chatbot users feedbacks,d) Integration with Watson NLU service, which provide additional suggestions on which possible intents and entities could be added to enrich the Conversation
finalOutcome:
The outcome of this initiative was a handful tool that enrich, verify the clearness, fluidity and overall dialogue structure of the Watson Conversation service. It takes the form of a dashboard, that combine visual data-driven analysis of conversation performances and punctual errors analysis. 
The dashboard developed in collaboration between IBM and Politecnico of Milano, is intended at simplifying and making more effective SMEs work in retraining a Conversation-based chatbot.
The tool runs on IBM Cloud using Watson services. 
From the technical point of view, the overall goals we achieved were: 1) integration between visual graph representation and Watson services integration; 2) allowing developers to easily spot points of improvement; 3) easily enrichment on existing intents, entities, future nodes and functionalities implementation; 4) easy, complete and ready-to-use tool
closeValue: The asset created with this initiative and based on a cognitive dashboard was deployed into a customer project between IBM Italy and Technogym, a world-wide leader wellness company. The asset gave us the opportunity to evaluate the great capability and flexibility of the cognitive platform
ratingComments: excellent and used also at client side in technogym

title: Operational and Business analytics for Watson Conversation
executiveChampionReason:
As Rome Lab leader Marcello is often involved to support deals in EU that require expertise in developing solutions based on Watson Cognitive services. He is very interested in sponsoring activities that enable the lab community to: 
- Learn new cognitive technologies
- Expand the family of people able to develop apps on IBM Cloud
- Build a reusable asset 
- Encourage IBM to eat its own cookie
Marcello sponsored a brainstorming with the Watson Cognitive service team to identify the most common useful areas for building reusable assets.
description: The prototyped solution provides operational and business analytics for Watson Conversation and provide actionable reports to improve the conversation graph relying on IBM Cloud services like NLU and Tone Analyzer
problemStatement:
Building chatbots with Watson Conversation services is easy, maintaining them is not. The chatbot utilization needs to be continuously verified and improved based on customer experience and feedback. This is very complicated to understand: 
If the conversation graph is correct?
If intents are correctly defined?
If the user is satisfied with the answer(s)?
Which are the most exploited branches?
Which are the most popular intents and entities?
Is the mood of recurrent users getting better over time?
outcome:
A working prototype that is providing analytics on the history and current status of the customer to chatbots conversation. The analytics enable administrators to get insights on the effectiveness of the chatbot and guidance how to improve it (e.g. topics that are not covered and need additional intents, dead conversation branches, etc.)
The system is easily extensible to be applied to very diverse contexts and tools where the Watson chatbot is plugged into. e.g. ticketing systems (Servicenow, Parature, etc.), help desk we application, and in general any system based on the Q/A interaction between customer and chatbot.
finalOutcome: The prototype we built as outcome of this initiative is a reusable asset that can provide a significant help in showing not only that using the Watson Conversation service is easy, but also that the whole life cycle of the conversation graph can be supervised and managed leveraging the provided operational and business analytics reports. The reports take into consideration the accuracy of the conversation graph as well as the mood of the customer and the confidence level associated to the answer. The extensible design, based on a plugin model, allows reusing the same asset for legacy environment where Watson Conversation is not present and more in general for ticketing system solutions opening the door also to a possible adoption of this prototype as the embryo for an innovative revolution in how IBM internally manages customer support.
closeValue: The prototype is a key asset in managing the life cycle of an application based on Watson Conversation service
ratingComments:
There is a lot of basic samples on how to build chat bots, but it is very hard, relying just on them, to explain customer how to manage the whole life cycle of chat bot itself: how to verify the conversation graph is accurate, where and how to fix it, how to enhance it adding more branches or deleting obsolete or unused ones, how to improve the dialog itself relying on user interaction and mood.
The prototype built by the team fits this purpose. It is an interesting and useful asset to augment sales in the Watson and Cloud space. The fact that it runs on our public cloud platform, that includes some of the most popular Watson services (Conversation, Natural Language Understanding, Tone Analyzer) and that relies on of of the most popular  cloud runtimes (node.js) and that can be automatically deployed in minutes in fully automated and continuous delivery mode make it a key tool for proof of concepts and demos. I loved the idea of proposing it also for our internal IBM consumption: it has been presented to three IBM Cloud vice presidents and to the second line managers of the Security pillar with the aim to start injecting cognitive technology into our customer support daily job and metrics. The audience has been enthusiastic and I plan to keep pushing on this front as well. A great job in adopting agile methodologies and in showing how relying on well known libraries like angular and without having to be a super machine learning expert you can build a powerful and meaningful tool.

title: Watson for Genomics: Enhance toolset to track, visualize and manage reports accura
executiveChampionReason: Steve is the VP for Genomics.
description: Expand our toolset to improve how we track, manage and visualize accuracy. We currently have a set of tools and processes to test the accuracy of our system. However, there is still a lot of manual la
problemStatement: Watson for Genomics analysis thousands of DNA alterations and categorize them in relation to drive the patient cancer based on the medical literature. Then it associates therapies to the actionable alterations. As a cognitive system that learns, the results changes overtime. For instance, new clinical trials are opened or other trials are completed. An unknown alteration becomes known as a new functional study is published. A new trial is completed and results are published changing the drug level of evidence. A drug is approved or a study is published showing the drug resistance to a certain biomarker. As a result of these changes, there are several challenges during validation and accuracy tests (expected results vs. actual results comparison, coverage of testcases, etc).
outcome:
This AoT was split in 2 workstreams:
  WS1: Tool prototype for validation. This workstream slowed down as WfG had a significant reduction on resources per various reasons.
  WS2: Brainstorm ideas on how to measure accuracy on a cognitive system where expected results changes overtime.
finalOutcome: Validation that measuring accuracy in a cognitive system is a big challenge and traditional methodologies do not work. Using a combination of techniques, including what was already being done by the team, is required to track accuracy.
closeValue: Validation on approaches being implemented and that an obvious "technique/approach" does not exist to address this challenge
publicationDescription:
For the second workstream in the initiative, we documented the challenges and ideas discussed to measure accuracy on a cognitive system:
Challenges faced by the team, including to identify the right approach, triggered to initiate AoT study to brainstorm for new ideas and/or validate the development team findings. We explained the challenge and that we were looking for help. We purposely did not describe the current approach used by WfG , because we were looking for innovative, unbiased ideas. Our thoughts were that if similar ideas would be presented – that would be seen as a positive validation of our testing for right way to measure accuracy. As if new ideas were presented, we could improve the test process. We wanted to have this study as a collaborative exercise, where we can ask really good questions, explore new ideas, discover some things that we may never thought about, better understand how we can better achieve accuracy measurement, while keeping track of multiple dynamically changing references.
ratingComments: It was a great experience and we learned a lot about launching, sponsoring and completing a study. We had a lot of delays, from our side due to resources constrains and I would imagine it was the same challenges from the AoT side on approving the publication. Nevertheless I wanted to complete this internal, confidential publication as there was a lot of good work performed by the various participants. The study met the objectives.  Thanks to all for the great effort doing the study and leading to completion.

title: Study for distributed cognitive system (AI Ecosystem)
executiveChampionReason: He is CTO, IBM Japan and drives technical aspect of cognitive strategy.
description: Study emerging trends for building cognitive system on distributed knowledge network such as information bank, open AI, and AI network.
problemStatement: The volume and variety of data defines the performance of a cognitive system. Though 80% of data are said to exist within enterprises, these data are separated into millions of silos by the barrier of companies and their departments. Most of the current cognitive systems seem to be built on the silo of data. In society, new trends are emerging to exchange data and/or abstracted knowledge across these barriers such as information bank, openAI, and AI networks. In August, 2017, for example, Microsoft and Amazon announced a plan to realize communication between Cortana and Alexa. These trends implicate the future where a cognitive system is built on distributed knowledge network.　These emerging trends will impact to IBM’s cognitive strategy.
outcome: In this initiative, we will create a report summarizing the study of emerging trends and providing recommendations for IBM. This will provide us with the necessary insight to drive cognitive strategy.
finalOutcome: Create PoV for next stage of AI
closeValue: Create momentum for IBM to generate next stage of AI
publicationDescription:
The report provides recommendation for IBM about the forthcoming era of AI ecosystem where AI systems in the world communicate
1. Trend and Vision:
-Emergence of standard and reuse of AI (Acumos, ONNX, Transfer Learning, etc.)
-Emergence of initiatives to exchange data among companies（Information bank, CDLA, etc.）
-The emergence implies the era of AI ecosystem where AI systems in the world exchange knowledge each other

2. Era of AI Ecosystem
-At the forthcoming era of AI ecosystem,
    -Competitive advantage of a company is established by leveraging the knowledge of external AI systems
    -Needs increase for managing stray AI systems developed internally in the past
-The needs generate demand of AI Ecosystem Manage Layer 
-Primitive AI functions are commoditized
-The AI ecosystem starts to be formed from beneficial domains such as financial regulation. IT vendors battle to conquer the beneficial territory

3. Recommendation
IBM precedes competitors with business-purpose AI and has deep relationship with clients.  Recommend IBM to 
    -Build a laboratory where clients, IBM R&D, and IBM Services can refine client requirements of AI ecosystem for several focus industry domains
    -Specialize client offerings to go in advance at the battle to conquer the beneficial territory
ratingComments: Atsushi Yamada has been strongly leading the initiative with the team. I believe that this study is very important for the future success of IBM.

title: Measuring the Hybrid Cloud Benefit Using the Balanced Scorecard Approach
executiveChampionReason: Innovation initiative sponsor
description: Measuring the Hybrid Cloud benefit using the Balanced Scorecard approach
problemStatement: Measuring the benefit of a HC project using only financial metrics (e.g. TCO/ROI) is incomplete. There are a lot of other aspects that are impacted by the HC project that are not financial, even if they will have at least an indirect financial giveback (e.g. speed, flexibility, innovation). The consequence is that it will be very challenging to prove the value of the HC project without using non financial evidences. The drawback is that usually taking into account the non financial metrics is not straightforward also because the non financial metrics are accused to be subjective and not measurable. The main reason of this initiative is to address these points with a more objective and measurable approach.
outcome: The expected outcome is a readily available living artifact: it will be a set of measurable metrics grouped by the four dimensions of the original BSC and a manual for the utilization. ,It can be tailored during the different stages of the sales cycle and improved by the community during the engagements.,The Business value for IBM is the artifacts itself that can be used as a consulting service. The initiative is "inclusive" and can include HW, SW, services and cloud. ,The business value spans the whole sales cycle: ,i) during the pre-sales stage, it can be used to highlight to the customer which are all the benefits of the HC approach;,ii) during the delivery stage, can be sold to the customer as a consulting service delivered together with the HC contract and ,iii) it can also be useful for our counterpart (e.g. CIO) to show to its stakeholder (e.g. LOB, CEO) the project effectiveness.,The Impact is a better understanding of the benefit of the HC project for the customer, answering at a very difficult question including financial and non-financial metrics.  ,The initiative will produce a deliverable that not foresee other IBM investments.
finalOutcome:
The business value covers the whole project lifecycle: 
i)	During the pre-sales stage, it can be used to highlight all business benefits of a HC project to the customer
ii)	During the delivery stage, the approach can be sold to the customer as a consulting service delivered together with the HC contract 
iii)	It can also be useful for our counterpart (e.g. CIO) to show to its stakeholder (e.g. LOB, CEO) the project effectiveness

The business value for IBM is the artifacts itself that can be used as a consulting service. Additional value can be derived over time to capture and collect measurements and analyze by industry.

As required by the AoT, the initiative is "inclusive" and can include HW, SW, Services and Cloud.
closeValue: An approach to measure the business benefit of a Hybrid Cloud (HC) project in a not-subjective way.
publicationDescription: The main objective of this study is to develop an approach to measure the business benefit of a Hybrid Cloud (HC) project in a not-subjective way. It includes the report and other four deliverables.
ratingComments: produced high value tech presales material, directly usable in client situations, as well as a prototype of a balanced score card, to be deployed in the IBM Services Platform with Watson

title: Performance engineering on Agile Engagements
affiliateName: WW CoP for Performance and Capacity
description: Agile projects do not focus sufficiently on operational performance requirements. This paper shows how to integrate Agile and performance engineering.
problemStatement: Building complex IT solutions quickly remains difficult despite progress in tools and methods.  Agile is an iterative process which became available in 2001 and is increasingly used.  Agile encourages greater collaboration between stakeholders and delivers functionality in short increments.,The Agile method focuses on the organisation and processes to deliver working software frequently to customers.  Often Agile projects do not focus sufficiently on the support for performance requirements and operation within performance constraints.  This can increase delivery costs or result in problems in Production.  This paper aims to set out recommendations for introducing robust performance engineering on Agile projects.  It aims to show how  existing practices such as Performance Engineering and Management Method can be extended to support Agile.
outcome: Whitepaper, education in the context of the AoT PEMMX virtual education initiative
finalOutcome: The paper provides guidance for architects and specialists on agile programs how to embed non-functional aspects integrally in the agile devops cycle
closeValue: Whitepaper, follow-on initiatives such as education materials, presentation on external conference
publicationDescription: The Agile manifesto was published in 2001 and advocates an iterative style of development, which progressively converges on a solution.  Agile is now widespread and used by over a third of IT projects worldwide.  However, Agile does not pay specific attention to how the resulting system will perform, scale to large volumes or use hardware resources efficiently.  Any large-scale engagement has many performance requirements that are critical to its success, and so it is important to understand how an Agile approach can address those performance requirements effectively.  ,This paper recommends how performance engineering can be incorporated in a large-scale Agile programme, although note that most of the material also applies to smaller programmes.  It is written for two audiences: those familiar with Agile and interested in how to manage performance challenges and those familiar with performance engineering methods and keen to apply them in the context of an Agile programme.
legacyParticipantType: Practitioners (architects and specialists) with experience in Agile development methods and with affinity with non-functional aspects such as performance., availability
legacyValue: Agile methodologies are becoming more and more popular but fail to include non-functional aspects sufficiently early and in a structured way. This paper and education helps IBMers to avoid performance and availability problems when using Agile development methods.

title: A testing framework for Visual Recognition
executiveChampionReason: He is the Technical Executive and Innovation Director for Italy
description: The application will fully rely on services of the IBM Bluemix platform: web services, IBM Cloud Object Storage services, Watson Visual Recognition services, etc.
problemStatement: Training image classifiers is very difficult: at the moment there is no unique method to verify the reliability of custom visual recognition classifiers. After the training of a classifier, a proper statistical technique must be found in order to identify the best threshold on which the confidence score of the classifier should be calibrate. At the moment, there's no tool that addresses this task.
outcome: The outcome will be a framework based on a single web application and on Watson Visual Recognition API.,Using the framework the user can train custom classifiers, test his own images and iteratively retrain them till results are satisfying.,Test results are shown in a user friendly dashboard where the user can evaluate the performances of the classifiers and choose the proper Watson confidence score that maximizes the accuracy of the classification.,No coding skills nor statistical knowledge are required to utilize the application.,Tests are performed accordingly to the ROC methodology and other machine learning metrics.
finalOutcome: The initiative gives a great contribution to develop new cognitive business in areas where the image recognition is mandatory. It opens new scenarios in a lot of industries from healthcare to engineering and constructions where a lot of processes are linked with images evaluation.,We developed an asset which helps to understand how is easy to design and deploy applications based on the IBM Cloud Platform using Watson services.,The initiative contributes to improve the general awareness of IBM Visual Recognition service capabilities in the technical community. It puts into practice the main differentiating features of IBM Visual Recognition Service and explores the capability of the full customization which allows to build your own classifier based on your specific needs and the capability to use the classifier within your own applications.
closeValue: The initiative provides an asset which helps business lines to develop new cognitive business in innovative areas where the images recognition plays a key role for the processes and business of the enterprises and organizations. The initiative has generated a great interest on IBM technical and non-technical personnel involved in image recognition activities with clients.

problemStatement: Subsidies have been a major item in government expenditures in Egypt for more than 5 decades. Till today, there are key challenges with the systems and processes that are currently in place to achieve the goal of this subsidization.
outcome: 1- To demo a prototype of innovative IT solutions based on Blockchain to provide government regulators strong control and oversight of the distribution of subsidized food supplies while streamlining the process throughout the different participating entities.,2- To enrich the local job market with IT professionals who are open-badged for both IBM Blockchain and Bluemix essentials.,3- To build a pipeline of candidates to be considered for hiring by IBM as demand on Blockchain or other areas grows.

The list is categorized as A, B, and C to grade each candidate.
closeValue: The spread of knowledge on IBM technologies (Bluemix and Blockchain) among fresh grads, as well as the identification of hand-picked candidates for hiring by IBM.

title: Towards a Social IoT Ontology
problemStatement: The so called “smart objects” that conform the Internet of Things (IoT) are not smart because they have so much computing power and stored information to perform better; they are smart because they are able to sense aspects from their context and connect to services that use this data, together with data from other sources, to produce useful information for the object to behave in a form that seems more intelligent of what might be expected from the object by itself. This can be considered a pseudo-social behavior: objects collaborate with other objects and services to achieve their goal, but their relationships are defined by an external entity, their user.,In some situations it’s desirable for the user to be the one deciding what other objects and services made transactions with their own personal objects, as when private data or personal space may be compromised. For some other use cases, we would like to entitle objects with more freedom to establish relationships with others based on contextual information and learned behaviors, as when we as an end user don’t want to worry much about the low level details of how an object is geolocated, or in industrial scenarios when we want a large number of heterogeneous objects to auto-organize to find an optimal configuration to execute a task.,If we want objects from different origins, with diverse capabilities and varied goals to automatically form collaborative relations at Internet scale, it is essential to enable them to communicate their capabilities and intentions, to agree on joint actions, and even to form groups with rights and responsibilities.,The foundational requirement is to define a common language capable of semantic representation of the institutional reality of the Social Internet of Things.
outcome: Develop an OWL ontology capable of representing social smart objects and their relationships. This ontology will serve as a common language to enable the establishment of collaboration relations between objects based on common objectives, and govern rights and obligations derived from such associations; facilitating the emergence of a Social Internet of Things.
legacyParticipantType: This endeavor requires a truly interdisciplinary team in order to identify potential types of smart objects relations and detail its characteristics.nTechnical members with experience in IoT and/or semantic technologies will be needed to make sure the outcome is sound.nTechnical members with AI knowledge would help to ensure the proposed structures are useful for negotiation and collaboration algorithms.nEditors/writers to guarantee the quality of documentation
legacyValue: Today IoT market is mainly focused on basic connectivity and end user devices, whereas the largest value could be found in analyzing the massive quantity of data produced by smart objects.,By setting the foundations of open standards for enabling the Social IoT IBM will be well positioned to influence the ecosystem to focus on IoT use cases where cognitive solutions are required, creating demand for a market where IBM excels.
