title: GDPS-like solution architecture for Power and high end storage
problemStatement: IBM need to exploit the cross brand capabilities of technologies to provider greater competitive advantage and customer advantage,The IBM technical sales community needs arguments and examples of why the Power platform provides value to our enterprise clients especially for critical Systems of Record which are the core strength of this platform. Specifically looking at SAP we are also experiencing significant competitive pressure from SAP HANA and have a significant risk of losing some of these major accounts especially with the divestiture of the x86 business.,For the mainframe we have had significant success with the GDPS solution which has defined a standard architecture and brand for continuous availability and disaster recovery. The GDPS solution is a combination of server, storage and software capabilities that together deliver greater value than the sum of the parts. On the Power platform we have the component parts with AIX HyperSwap, SVC and/or DS8000 storage combined with database capabilities such as DB2 purescale or Oracle RAC to deliver a similar solution but we have not taken these component parts to create a compelling end-to-end solution.
outcome: 1) Taking the model of the GDPS offering on System z define/document an architecture and solution stack for Systems of Record environment on the  Power/AIX,  and High End storage platforms that  provides continuous availability and disaster recovery and leverages the strengths of both the hardware and software capabilities. This will include both IBM and ISV middleware and applications.,2) Identify existing or planned client configurations as proof-points using some or all of the components of this model,3) Identify any competitive gaps that would encourage a client to go with individual best of breed components or alternative architectures such as HANA.,4) Create sales enablement materials and education to the technical sales community and discuss the potential for sales plays.,5) Identify existing or new items on product roadmaps that could improve this architecture blueprint and provide this input to the relevant product development teams and teams responsible for cross brand planning and interlock,6) Identify any current or future proof of concept activities that could demonstrate and validate these solution
legacyParticipantType: The people participating in this activity should have an active interest and skills in one of the aspects of the proposed solution either from a development perspective or through engagement with one of their clients in the field. The team should involve people from storage (SVC and DS8000), Power/AIX, SWG (DB2, Tivoli etc) and our client technical advisor community.
legacyValue: To compete with the alternatives of commodity hardware and piece-part solutions from individual vendors we need to demonstrate the strength of IBM as a provider of end-to-end solutions. Creating an architecture blueprint and sales enablement materials will provide ammunition to the technical sales community to demonstrate that IBM is able to provide these integrated solutions for the Power platform. If there are gaps in our existing capabilities then it will also highlight these and enable the development teams to correctly prioritise these enhancements taking into the wider IBM picture not just the perspective for their individual platform.

title: Evolution of IT Services Creation, Consumption, and Delivery in a world with proliferation of cloud and XaaS
executiveChampionReason: Arun Hampapur is a Director of Development of the platform (IBM Services Platform with Watson). The initiative we propose is directly going to influence the platform architecture in terms of how IT services will be created for and provided to the end consumers.
description: For large IT Services providers such as IBM, it will become very daunting to maintain a large portfolio of IT Services that remains competitive for long as the market conditions are becoming more dynamic by the day with multiple options for consuming IT Services becoming available. Further, the clients' continual focus to reduce their cloud spend will make them demand sophisticated services that help achieve their target. Because of the dynamics as well as existence of other independent players, it will not be feasible to maintain the competitiveness of each service in a large portfolio. This will entail such large IT services providers to reorient the way in which IT services are created-for, consumed-by and delivered-to end-clients. In this report we explore the drivers and trends, and how the problem will be addressed by the large IT Services providers.
problemStatement:
How will the creation, consumption, and delivery of IT services evolve when trends indicate that: (a) 92% of the workloads move to cloud data centers by 2020 (Gartner), and it is estimated that there is an opportunity to save 35% from the cloud spend made by the enterprises requiring sophisticated AI/Data-driven IT services to identify and remediate inefficiencies, (b) Most enterprises will be sourcing from multiple IT-as-a-service providers and clouds, potentially retaining an in-house IT department (Gartner), (c) A given IT service may excel only in a subset of client usecases but customers will desire to address all the usecases in the field, and can only be possible by rapidly "collaborating" with other IT service providers.

We envisage a more agile platform (not seen before) to emerge allowing multiple 3rd parties to provide to the clients under the leadership of IBM. Integrations (that may be short-lived) at the level of data and process between these providers and IBM are expected to exist. We will study the ideal nature of such a platform and what components are needed to ensure that other IT service providers can collaborate with IBM to provide an overall service to clients. See https://w3-connections.ibm.com/blogs/alt/entry/Evolution_of_IT_Services_Creation_Consumption_and_Delivery_in_a_world_with_proliferation_of_cloud_and_XaaS?lang=en_us
outcome:
Publish an AoT Report that will provide answers for the above problem statement.This will include a high-level architecture which will help IBM GTS and potentially other units to understand and prepare (in advance) for changes/overhaul to be made to adapt and provide a winning difference to the IT service delivery. The architecture will expectedly discuss how to bring about an integration between the processes, data, and tooling from different IT service providers and that of IBM to deliver a cohesive and desired experience to the end-clients. We will consider various IT services such as event management, ticketing, patching, health-check, discovery, configuration and inventory management, etc and show how they will be delivered under the new model.

The initiative is looking for volunteers having knowledge of:
(a) IT Services (knowledge in one or more of monitoring/event management, patch management, compliance, discovery, ticketing/ITSM, etc) 
(b) business modeling so that we can see how IBM can still make money under the new model
(c) IT architecture of SaaS, etc

Last but not least have about 2-4 hours per week for this initiative

title: Cognitive Bias in Machine Learning
executiveChampionReason: Ruchir is a respected IBM Fellow and Chief Architect of IBM Watson, which is the platform most likely to be interested in the effects of cognitive bias.
description: Examining the potential for systematic bias in machine learning systems and developing techniques to mitigate such bias
problemStatement: One of the most important cognitive activities conducted by humans is that of decision-making. Decision-making involves thinking that may be rational or irrational, i.e., not always based on evidence. Bias in decision-making is usually unintentional – the person making the decision is unaware of the bias in judgment. Bias can result from previous experience, from the environment, from the input presented, or from other factors influencing the learning process. With machines contributing significantly to, or even taking over, the role of decision-making in everyday life, it is prudent to examine whether their decisions could be affected by similar bias. For example, the nature and distribution of samples presented during training have an effect on predictions made by a model. But could there be a systematic bias in such predictions? If there is bias, is it possible to characterize features of the training input that cause such bias? What factors other than input lead to bias? Could, for example, the choice of network used to solve a deep learning solution lead to bias?
outcome: This initiative will attempt to gather information about cognitive bias in machine learning, provide a taxonomy for various types of bias that could manifest in machine learning systems, and discover potential reasons for possible bias. As cognitive systems developed by IBM, or developed on IBM frameworks, become more prevalent, there is likely to be a greater expectation for the integrity of decisions made by such systems. Thus, possible follow-up activities resulting from this initiative could be the development of techniques and processes to evaluate systems for potential cognitive bias, as well as techniques to alleviate or eliminate the cause of such bias during the synthesis and training of machine learning models.
finalOutcome:
Bringing awareness of bias issues to all programmers, especially those engaged in AI and machine learning applications is a first step towards making IBM's products more sensitive to bias-related decision-making. As seen from recent lapses in the industry around privacy, proactively addressing issues such as bias, gives a company a better image from a societal point of view, and therefore contributes to better business results. 

Beyond this, IBM has the potential to be viewed as a leader, by engaging other companies as well as members of communities, to define guidelines in the area of bias in ML/AI products. The importance of such issues is beginning to be felt with the deployment of the GDPR regulations. IBM, through its experience and research, could provide services to other companies and users, leading to a potentially new source of revenue.
closeValue: This initiative has studied various aspects of bias in machine learning, has identified IBM's exposure to bias problems in its products, and has proposed important recommendations that will help IBM become a leader in the industry.
publicationDescription: Decision-making is one of the most important cognitive activities conducted by humans. With machines contributing significantly to, or sometimes even taking over, decision-making in everyday life, it is prudent to examine whether their decisions could be affected by similar bias. This initiative attempts to gather information about cognitive bias in machine learning, provide a taxonomy for the various types of bias that could manifest in machine learning systems, and discover potential reasons for bias. As cognitive systems developed by IBM, or developed on IBM frameworks, become more prevalent, there is likely to be a greater expectation for the integrity of decisions made by such systems. Follow-up activities proposed by this initiative include the research and development of techniques and processes to evaluate systems for potential bias, and to alleviate or eliminate the cause of such bias during the synthesis and training of machine learning models. The report recommends broadening the awareness of ML/AI bias-related issues to all IBMers, not just AI developers. It further encourages IBM to take a leadership position in this area, both through its products, through engagement with the broader community, and through its services.
ratingComments: The team did a great job putting together a very comprehensive analysis of the subject. Bias as we all know has become one of the most hotly debated topics with AI and is becoming increasingly important in conversation with our clients. I would like to commend the leads in taking the lead here and guiding IBM and in particular IBM Watson with this thoughtful work. title: Cognitive Community Dashboards
executiveChampionReason: Tory Johnson was selected as the Executive Champion since he supports our Olmsted County volunteer project.
description: Creating a Cognitive Community Dashboard with drill-down capability & automated updates
problemStatement: Businesses are becoming well versed with analytics. It’s not that way yet for the general population. A significant amount of data exists via the Census, State level mandates, and data collected locally. Much of the data isn’t fully analyzed and for what is, the information isn’t effectively communicated in the community.,A number of communities around the country have created static, annual reports, but few have real time dashboards with drill-down capability & automated updates. A huge amount of manual effort goes into creating the annual reports, and once completed, the effort starts all over again for the next year.,As a contribution to our community, this project focuses on Olmsted County Community Services and Public Health to automate the report generation process and create the transformation into a dashboard visualization. It will be created in partnership with county staff and use their Subject Matter Experts (SMEs) to identify the key community indicators and messages.
outcome:
1. Determine how to import data into an analytics platform, what the key community indicators are for the county, and communicate key messages by transforming information into a dashboard visualization.
2. Hold a Design Thinking Workshop to determine the metrics, net messages, and how to organize the metrics on the dashboard taking into account the personas (a. public community members, b. providers of the services, c. Olmsted County staff). 
3. Write up report based on the completed phases.
finalOutcome:
1. Project focused on Olmsted County Community Services and Public Health  to create a dashboard visualization in partnership with Olmsted County staff; started in January of 2017
2. Team completed the expected outcomes of Phase 1 Preparation:
2a. Learned how to import data into an analytics platform and make the process more efficient and automated
2b. Learned what the key community indicators are for the county and how to create and communicate key messages to the community
2c. Learned how to transform information into a dashboard visualization
3. Team completed the expected outcomes of Phase 2 Part 1 Pilot (Safety) with focus on Design Thinking Workshop and organizing the data:
3a. Determined the metrics to be used, the net messages and how to organize the metrics on the dashboard
3b. Held a Design Thinking Workshop to take into account three personas
4. In January of 2018 the Human Services group became part of Health, Housing and Human Services in an Olmsted County re-organization, and Olmsted County staff leadership asked to step away from this project 
5. Cognitive Community Dashboards Report published 7/31/2018 
5a. Executive Summary Report https://tinyurl.com/y74ops4n 
5b.  Full Report https://tinyurl.com/y7e487ya
closeValue: The greatest impact realized was using Design Thinking skills in a project involving Olmsted County joint collaboration for Rochester community give back.
ratingComments: Great effort by the team to bring technology to our external community.

title: Blockchain enabled AI driven Marketplace for Insurance
executiveChampionReason: Ramesh is the VP Blockchain solutions
description: Blockchain enabled AI driven Marketplace for Insurance
problemStatement: Blockchain technology has gained massive attention in recent years with significant expectations that it could transform every industry for its promise of providing a single source of truths for participants in a business network. Nevertheless, according to Garner’s 2016 hype cycle for emerging technologies, blockchain is entering its peak of inflated expectations and in fact, its years to mainstream to adoption is still 5 to 10 years ahead before the technology reaches a plateau of productivity. Since most of blockchain efforts nowadays are still in a nascent state, we believe the time is right for do an academy study on the AI driven marketplace for insurance industry. The usage of Blockchain and build an AI based marketplace to develop next generation solutions for fraudulent claims identification, persisting IoT data (telematics data) for micro-insurance, predicting drivers behavior and risk analysis, etc. The objective of this study to explore this untapped area and do the market study in Insurance sector, New trends/opportunities, key drivers/players, competitive analysis, what could be the AI based marketplace means, use cases leveraging AI, high-level architecture, etc.
outcome: We shall deliver a report. The report would be a compilation of our findings (listed in problem statement above) in this area and provide our recommendation. We plan to present this report to Marie Wieck (GM, Blockchain) and all other executives in her line. We also plan to work with Sandip Patel (Global Managing DIrector, Insurance) and his line to get their guidance/feedback time to time as we make the progress. We believe this report/study will provide new business insights which can lead to create opportunity for IBM.
finalOutcome: We have studies the trends and transformations in Insurance industry and what AI and Blockchain technologies can disrupt the insurance industry. The outcome of this study is to highlight what is happening in the insurance market and the complete AI insights the clients are looking for, and how IBM should address these challenges. We interviewed insurance clients execs and with their help to know the clients requirements and expectations, we proposed an architecture for decentralized platform for insurance analytics and marketplace.
mainCollaborationURL: Video calls, Slack, Emails and box
closeValue: New trends and clients expectations while the insurance industry is being disrupted, and how AI can be leveraged for shared data analytics.
publicationDescription: In this study we recommend building an AI-driven decentralized platform for federated insurance analytics and marketplaces that would enable various parties in the ecosystem to collectively develop shared analytics services for mutual benefit. Blockchain technology will play a key role in this platform towards improving trust in data, AI models, the learning process as well as the derived outcomes.  To develop this platform, there are many interesting technical challenges and this report briefly describes various problems and their solution approaches. Finally, we also describe the applicability of this platform to a pay-as-you-go automotive insurance marketplace. In such scenario, multiple auto-insurers compete via this marketplace to insure a trip request from a driver while also leveraging the platform for developing federated AI insights on various insurance models.
ratingComments: The team did a good job of studying the insurance space and how IBM could come up with offerings leveraging blockchain in this space.

executiveChampionReason: Kathy is looking after the future of global solution design (with Jenny Ang)
description: Practical Operational Modelling - OM for Systems on Cloud
problemStatement: How is Operational Modelling performed effectively?  Even in the Cloud world, the need to model a system in order to ensure that the Non-Functional requirements will be met is still just as important as ever. However there is often a gap between what modelling is actually performed on projects, and what the method says should be done. Further, the premise is that Operational Modelling for cloud could be optimised.,The word 'Practical' in the title is deliberate.  This is not intended as a theoretical study, but is intended to look at the practicalities of working within a real project, with the pressures which come from delivery, time-scales and cost.,The study is split into three ‘streams’,1.	OM for Systems on Cloud – how to adapt Operational Modelling to better handle systems which are being built to be hosted in Cloud,2.	OM for Cloud Services – how to adapt Operational Modelling for the build of Cloud Services (IaaS, SaaS, PaaS),3.	OM Revisions – how should the techniques and notation be revised for the new world,This stream is OM for Cloud Systems
outcome: Almost all new business is now delivering systems to be provisioned on Cloud.  Improving the speed and effectiveness of the way we create the Architecture for these systems will reduce the delivery cost and reduce the risk associated with delivery.
finalOutcome:
The Initiative has delivered two major items
(1) the definition and description of a MVP for Operational Modelling within Cognitive Architect.  This has provided the guidance to allow CA to cover this space.
(2) a Decision Tree and background information to guide an Architect in the deployment of Kubernetes on IBM Cloud Private.  This information has now been taken by the IBM Cloud Solutioning Center for incorporation into their solution guidance
closeValue: Driving the incorporation of Operational Modelling into Cognitive Architect

problemStatement: Additive Manufacturing (also known as 3D Printing) is a rapidly developing field with significant market-level investments being made; with significant new technology advancements coming to market daily. title: Ecosystem for Archive Business
problemStatement: As many surveys indicate the size of archiving data keeps growing, especially multimedia data. To hold an archive TCO in an affordable range, storage technologies have been developed pursuing lower $/GB. However, as the size of archived data is growing very rapidly, only reduction of $/GB will hardly catch up the growth rate. In fact, many archive owners are seriously considering giving-up archived assets because of difficulty in archive cost management.,The archive assets are very important resources which may contain a piece of data segment (e.g. a specific scene) that may be quite valuable in future but nobody knows which will be. Preserving all will be the best way but the TCO pressure makes it hard to do. So that, a new business cycle is highly required to mitigate the TCO pressure or recover the archiving cost by monetization with those assets themselves. It should be solved ASAP, otherwise the TCO pressure may discard some or all even though those are supposed a kind of natural resources.,The fundamental driver of the new business cycle  is a method to offer the right data to a potential consumer, where the new technology that can extract the piece of specific data (e.g. a very specific scene out of a video stream) that will drag a big customer attention and create a big demand.  It has not been available yet.
outcome: A new ecosystem as an IBM solution  is expected, where it will be composed of the following technologies.,- Smarter Analytics system analyzes consumer trend sensing consumers activities and external events. It helps us predict which multimedia contents will have a big demand.,- Archive storage system preserves a large amount of multimedia contents for long time in affordable cost keeping accessibility. According to analytics result, it retrieves multimedia contents from the archive storage and sends them to a cache storage of a content distribution system preemptively. It is expected just a right segment out of video stream is retrieved pin-point.,- Multimedia contextual analytics system scan and analyzes multimedia and give a specific segment a contextual metadata on timeline for later pin-point partial retrieval.,- Content distribution system has a cache storage to keep multimedia contents and distributes them to multiple devices in proper media format. According to each consumer's previous activity sensed by the smarter analytics system, personalized contests will delivered to each customer's device including mobile device and a consumer's activity is monitored by the smarter analytics system and a new ecosystem cycle is initiated.
legacyParticipantType: Global Media and Entertainment persons who develop multi-device content distribution businessesnResearch persons  who are working for or interested in multimedia (e.g. video, audio or text) analytics technology and contextual metadata nGBS persons who develop Smarter Analytics tool businessesnSTG persons who are doing business with tape products, LTFS related products, Flash Systems, iDataPlex or Video Grid.
legacyValue: IBM has a technology that take a role in the ecosystem. Smarter Analytics tools for the analytics, tape system products and Essence and Archive Manager for the archive storage system, IBM Multimedia Analytics and Retrieval System for the multimedia contextual analytics and Video Grid for the content distribution system. But those have not yet integrated in a single ecosystem. It means IBM is one of the companies who are the closest to the ecosystem.,There are huge amount of archived multimedia contents that have less or no chance to be accessed since no one knows which is where.,Once IBM has the ecosystem, where those multimedia contents are migrated to the archive storage system and an agent of multimedia contextual analytics is crawling in the storage system to give them contextual metadata on timeline, the smarter analytics can extract the segment out of a video stream then provide it to the consumer who may want it. As long as a specific web service deliver the favorite contents, a consumer repeats to visit it and a business cycle between a web service provider and the archived content owner is activated. The cycle will help the archived content owner recover the archive cost. ,It becomes a good business model that finds out a valuable material out of a big data as natural resources.

title: Practical Operational Modelling - Systems on Cloud Sprint 3
executiveChampionReason: Lead for Global Solution Design (with Jenny Ang)
description: Practical Operational Modelling - Constraint based modelling
problemStatement: Designing a system is a matter of creating an Architecture which meets the requirements whilst staying within the constraints which are imposed by the selected products or services. When creating an architecture for a system you start with a list of Non Functional Requirements. As you make decisions to satisfy these this in turn imposes constraints onto the system and the candidate architecture becomes increasingly formed.,In the past requirements generally were able to take precedence over constraints and many well understood trade-offs were available to enable them to be flexibly balanced, whereas now, clouds, shared services and ecosystems often impose binary decisions, constraints have a bigger role to play and new trade-offs are necessary. This study looks to understand this more, and to look to see if a different approach which imposes constraints could be used to drive out the architecture of a new system more quickly and with less effort.
outcome: Provide a decision tree which gives candidate solutions along with the requirement characteristics which might drive that choice – this should then drive a set of constraints. This should also consider the order in which decisions are made in order to ensure that big decisions are made early where this is possible.
finalOutcome: This initiative has discovered new ways to help an Architect to address NFRs when designing systems, particularly in the new Cloud/Agile world.  The approach of generating decision trees and architectural fragments is a powerful way to guide an Architect through the process, and as part of the next Sprint this will feed into the Cognitive Architect tool which is currently in development.
closeValue: Realisation of a new way to address NFRs when designing systems.

title: GDPR Considerations for Blockchain Architects
executiveChampionReason: Ramesh is the VP for Industry Platform Blockchain Solutions and supports blockchain related initiatives.
description: GDPR Considerations for Blockchain Architects
problemStatement:
The privacy rules established by the GDPR affect many business processes and technology solutions. Because of the GDPR’s broad definition of “processing,” compliance challenges arise in various contexts, including the collection, retention, modification, access and deletion of personal data. Projects with GDPR implications should have a clear idea of the types and amounts of data involved; the location of data storage; articulated policies for the retention, modification, access and deletion of that data; and the means to selectively delete data in an efficient,
effective and demonstrable manner. As a result, the GDPR may pose a challenge for architects of blockchain solutions that process EU personal data.
outcome:
* External Paper to be used by blockchain architects when building blockchain solutions which need to comply with GDPR.
* Blog post on AoT
finalOutcome:
An IBM point of view has been published on GDPR considerations for blockchain solution architects. The point of view has been affirmed by the EU report on blockchain and GDPR. AoT blog has also been published.

closeValue: Clarified GDPR options and their tradeoffs for blockchain solution architects

title: Data sharing for decision making in Industrial Products industry
executiveChampionReason: This initiative supports her business objectives.
description: Data sharing for decision making in Industrial Products industry
problemStatement: In global industrial product business the fleet consists of equipment around the world. The customers collect and store maintenance data to their own systems (e.g. CMMS) that is only seldom shared with the machinery manufacturing companies. The maintenance service and technology companies would profit from field data in their product design and service business. Technical solutions for data sharing have been on market for a while, but barriers related to costs and trust are still preventing data sharing. Cloud services offer a practical and secure solution for data sharing between companies.
outcome: A cloud service concept, which tries to overcome challenges related to trust and the fact that component users do not get any direct benefits from data sharing. The concept consists of several stakeholders; a component/system supplier, plants using components in their production line and a cloud service provider. In addition to traditional data collection, analysing and sharing from a cloud the concept presents the idea of using the collected and analysed data in contract verifications. Calculations of key performance indicators used in terms of contracts e.g. availability or overall equipment efficiency can result different values if source data varies. Thus if KPIs are calculated from the data stored in a cloud the results should be consistent for all stakeholders. The cloud service concept can be led by a plant, when component providers collect data from several clouds. The leader can also be a component supplier, when plants need to join several clouds. Besides concept level definition, this concept will also be built on real demo environment to bring the concept at practical level.

title: Cognitive Assistant for Student Engagement (CASE)
executiveChampionReason: Tory is supportive of our ideas and projects around Watson and many other areas.
description: CASE is a project that is focused on demonstrating feasibility of integrating 3rd party Student Information Systems with a personal Voice Cognitive Assistant.
problemStatement:
The K-12 school experience can be overwhelming at times for students and parents.  Understanding what schoolwork is due, when is the next test, or where you can get help can be very challenging.  Student Information Systems (SIS) such as Skyward and Infinite Campus provide a way to get some of this information but the web and mobile access to this information can be confusing and hard to recognize what is most important.  A cognitive assistant could make this job significantly easier.
     This cognitive assistant project, named CASE for Cognitive Assistant for Student Engagement, would help students stay engaged with their schoolwork by providing a voice assistant that interacts with their school’s SIS.   This personal assistant would enable students by providing them information on upcoming assignments and how to get help.  Parents would also be able to use this assistant to get school briefings on how their children are doing and where they may need to focus.
outcome:
This is a proof of concept project is focused on demonstrating feasibility of integrating 3rd party Student Information Systems (SIS) with a personal Voice Cognitive Assistant:
  - To enable better student engagement by providing them information on upcoming assignments and how to get help
  - To provide parents with school briefings on how their children are doing and where they need to focus 
Expected outcomes:
  - Experience working in an agile squad utilizing design thinking and lean startup practices.
  - Learn how to develop a chatbot and voice assistant using Watson Conversation Services.
  - Demonstrate feasibility of integrating 3rd party SIS like Infinite Campus and Skyward.  This will likely require development of a mock student information service.
  - Demonstrate improved student and parent engagement by using a voice assistant to more easily understand what schoolwork has been assigned.
  - Look at other potential integration such as Google Classroom, or visualization methods such as Wall of Work.
Business value:
  - Development and use of agile, design thinking. and lean startup skills that can be applied to other projects
  - Expanding the use of Watson Conversation Services 
  - Give back to community and world by improving the school experience and outcomes

title: Blockchain Solution Architecture - Key Architectural Decisions
executiveChampionReason: This work complements ongoing work in the area of blockchain solution assurance that Nitin is championing. He was also involved as a champion in the earlier initiative.
description: The purpose of this initiative is to develop a series of  key architectural decisions (ADs) when deploying blockchain solutions. To this end, there are two objectives: 1. To update ADs from earlier initiative to reflect v1.1 2. To create new ADs in areas including performance, security, disaster recovery, chaincode invocation, analytics, interoperability. problemStatement: The purpose of this initiative is to catalog a set of key architectural decisions that most blockchain solution architects are faced with when designing solutions using the IBM Blockchain Platform. There is a lack of available material to bring consistency and quality across developed blockchain solutions today. The intent of this work is to use both lessons learned and insights developed from field architects in implementing real-world solutions and capture those as a set of guiding ADs for knowledge dissemination to the field. The ADs produced will be housed in a web site and can be dynamically updated as the IBM Blockchain Platform evolves. We intend to both enhance earlier work done in an earlier initiative, but also add new ADs in areas including performance, security, privacy, interoperability, chaincode invocation, analytics and disaster recovery.
outcome: The developed collateral will serve as a living guide for field architects and for customers when developing blockchain solutions based on the IBM Blockchain Platform. We plan to continue the same format used in the earlier work and document the decision criteria, architectural considerations, pros and cons using a common AD template. By installing these ADs on a web site, we expect that they will be maintainable and can be widely disseminated within and outside IBM for best practice guidance.
finalOutcome: The key output of this initiative sprint is a living github repository of architectural decisions when designing blockchain solutions, that is both re-used and updated by blockchain practitioners.

title: IBM Academy Regional Summit - Yorktown Heights, November 2017

associatedBusinessUnitOther: All business units represented by attending Affiliate and Academy members
description: Annual Regional Summit for the AoT - Northeast Region
problemStatement: The Academy Regional Summit in Yorktown Heights, NY will provide a face-to-face opportunity to unite and ignite a sector of our Academy and Academy Affiliate membership through exploration of AoT priorities and our Academy's role in IBM's transformation.  This will be a client event and will, additionally, provide many opportunities for networking and collaboration among the participants.  The planning and coordination of the event will be handled by both the Mid-Hudson Valley TVA and the Manhattan TVC.
outcome: New Academy members will be welcomed and formally absorbed into our Academy's community.  Participants will leave with renewed insight into our Academy's role and priorities and with a broadened understanding of client perspectives.  Lightening talks and a poster session will highlight the technical and technical vitality achievements of our regional Academy Affiliates and their members. The poster session and the publicity around the event will increase awareness of the IBM Academy and its role among the many new hires in the region, helping them to understand the benefits of engagement.  Through networking, new connections will be made and old connections will be refreshed, enabling stronger collaboration within and across business units.
finalOutcome:
The Regional Summit provided the opportunity to immediately absorb new members into the larger Academy community.  Beginning with the networking dinner and continuing throughout the next day, they were welcomed and celebrated and incorporated into the work of the meeting.  In fact, some new members held key roles on the Summit planning committee and were, therefore, an integral part of the event before it even began.  

During a variety of sessions, Susan Smartt, our Academy President, provided an update on the AoT's transformation journey, discussed recent accomplishments, and indicated how we, as AoT and Affiliate members can best assist in maximizing our Academy's impact on the business.    

The two quantum mechanics presentations during the evening networking event, Dario Gil's discussion of the future of computing, and the array of technical topics covered during the 5 Minute Madness and poster sessions exposed the meeting participants to a wide variety of topics in a compact period of time while actively engaging many of the meeting attendees in developing the content of the event.

Claus Jensen's discussion of Aetna's view of living in a hybrid world was both thought-provoking and enlightening, and provided keen insight into an important client's perspective on today's IT landscape.  The MTA (Metropolitan Transit Authority) challenge was delivered to the attending ALT members and discussed in an offline session.  An initiative has been opened (https://w3-connections.ibm.com/blogs/alt/entry/AoT_initiative_on_public_transportation_in_New_York_City?lang=en_us) to cover the work requested in the challenge; results will be shared with the MTA upon completion.

The Initiative Creation session sparked with energy and generated close to a dozen concrete proposals for Academy initiatives.  This is a work in-progress.  Once the ideas have been vetted, leaders will be found to open the selected initiatives and the real work will begin.

One goal of the meeting was to strengthen the ties to the participating regional Affiliates.  In addition to the technical topics covered during the poster and 5 Minute Madness sessions, there were presentations from the nine Affiliates attending the event (MHV, Manhattan, Albany, Canada, Washington Metro, North Carolina, Austin, TSLC, TEC-SSC).  The Affiliate contributions were visible throughout the day and the importance of their role in the Academy was frequently stressed.   

While we were successful in involving some early tenure members of the IBM community in the event, we would like to be more aggressive in this area next time around.

Overall, this initiative is considered a great success, with enthusiastic complements coming both the meeting Attendees and the Academy stakeholders.

title: TLC-BR - Quantum Computing Study
executiveChampionReason: Since Quantum Computing is a cutting-edge topic, I believe that Rodolfo Taboada, as the IBM LA CTO, is the best person in LA to assess the value of this study.
description: The IBM Brazil AoT Affiliate TLC-BR - Technology Leadership Council, honoring its tradition since inception of being always abreast of the latest trends in IT, will be launching a study on the subject, spanning introduction to advanced topics, with an emphasis on coding to leverage IBM's experimental cloud-enabled quantum computing platform, known as Quantum Experience.
problemStatement:
There is a dirty little secret in IT. A number of problems that might seem simple to tackle with a conventional computer at first glance, can easily reach a scale that is insurmountable for the existing data processing paradigm. Regardless of the amount of resources that are thrown into it. These challenges span a number of areas, like encryption, big data search, combinatorial optimization and molecular dynamics, with implications of enormous commercial and scientific significance, such as drug and materials discovery, supply chain & logistics optimization, financial risk, AI and cyber security. The good news is that there is a branch of computing being developed by many organizations, with IBM at the forefront, that holds great potential to address these very problems by leveraging quantum mechanics, the physics that describes the very fabric of the universe - matter and energy, at its most basic level, called quantum computing.

Thus, the IBM Brazil AoT Affiliate TLC-BR - Technology Leadership Council, honoring its tradition since inception of being always abreast of the latest trends in IT, will be launching a study on the subject, spanning introduction to advanced topics, with an emphasis on coding to leverage IBM's Cloud-based quantum computing platform.
outcome: A presentation in English, going beyond the type of introductory material usually available on the Intranet and Internet, providing a comprehensive view on the subject, covering introduction, to advanced topics and future trends, including practical examples.
finalOutcome: Increased significantly awareness of Quantum Computing within the IBM Brazil technical community.
closeValue: Increased significantly awareness of Quantum Computing within the IBM Brazil technical community, which, in turn, can help foster IBM's technical leadership at a moment when we are being challenged by the competition.
sponsorMessage: The TLC-BR team involved has been preparing itself for this study for a while.

This is the AoT Regional summit, hosted by Susan Schreitmueller, President of AoT, following the AoT Inspiring Talks and the AoT New Member Class, held in IBM Japan.
Almost 50 AoT members and guests gathered at the summit to discuss how AoT can　help customers to solve their technical problems and also IBM to develop new business by taking advantage of emerging technologies. The attendees include eight AoT members from outside Japan, namely, Australia, China, Korea, Singapore, and US.
As a guest executive, Dr. Kuruma, Fellow at Nissan Motor Corporation, shared his perspective on where IBM is expected to provide technologies to contribute to the industry and the society. A detail report can be found at the following link :  
https://w3-connections.ibm.com/wikis/home?lang=ja#!/wiki/Wb4f529010fc5_4fed_8806_9580b015f595/page/AoT%20Regional%20Summit%202017%20in%20Japan%20Report

ratingComments:
Thank you very much for holding AoT Regional Summit and 2017 AoT New Members Class in Japan. These were very successful, and all the participants were encouraged very much. Technical communities in Japan such as TEC-J and COSMOS are very active, but they are still not enough to connect to IBM global technical teams. I and my CTO team are now actively to expand the connection between technical teams of Japan and Global. Holding these events in Japan is very timely and very important under this situation. 
I believe this outstanding accomplishment was definitely driven by Susan's strong leadership. She aggressively had additional activities such as round tables around the Summit and Class, and she is following up several key action items perfectly.
Kumura-san, Nissan Fellow, is one of my best friends. He was also very glad to joint the AoT Summit as keynote speaker. 
I will keep working tightly with Susan and AoT to maximize technical values of IBM.

title: Data Science to Enable Dazzling Digital Experiences
executiveChampionReason: Sandesh and Stefanos Manganaris, Chief Data Scientist for Digital, conferred and agreed that data science & technology platforms go hand in hand - and that a partnership would be helpful to make sure we collect the right data for advanced machine learning in support of client interactions.
description: DBG unleashes IBM to empower the world, with engaging digital interactions being fundamental.  Data science on digital platforms will create opportunities for new types of interactions and value exchanges.
problemStatement:
Are there common client needs that provide opportunities for specialized digital assistants to deliver personalized value in exchange for information that helps IBM understand the needs of the specific client?
Can we capture NEW data via a digital engagement for analytics – better understanding of users’ needs, inform offerings, sales & marketing plans, and future interactions, etc.? 
Are specific data better suited to machine learning?
Could our digital platforms evolve beyond delivering content and generic services to become "sensors" for personalized client interactions?
outcome:
This study will evaluate potential digital interactions and make recommendations for evolving DBG's platforms and cognitive capabilities to support those deemed valuable, achievable, and differentiating.
The initiative has three 6-week sprints: Sprint1A - Idea Generation.  The outcome will be a presentation to executive sponsors for new ways for DBG to design digital experiences.  Sprint 1B - Idea Evaluation & Selection - the outcome is a presentation using a framework to optimize business outcomes. Sprint 2 will be developing a technical prototype based on idea from Sprint1B.
finalOutcome:
IBM spends over a billion dollars in marketing programs to make people aware of our brand, products and services. The problem is that only 27% of the people visiting IBM websites actually engage with our content, and only 1% of people coming from paid media channels respond to our call to actions, creating the opportunity to implement a program to increase the level of engagement and conversion.
This initiative addressed the problem of low engagement and conversion with a cognitive personalization solution that: 
- traces users across all the stages of the engagement and marketing funnel
- solves financial attribution to the marketing programs that help in the conversion of an individual
- presenting targeted content based on user needs and interests
- deriving what content is most effective in converting users
- grow relationship to tie in additional offerings and trials

Key to this value is a multi-tenant technology solution that allows IBM to develop a universal progressive profile to capture all behaviors and journey interactions of all visitors to IBM. The plan is to deploy this in production in 2019.
closeValue: Because IBM endeavors to conduct the bulk of its marketing, sales, and customer interacion through digital channels, we regard this as a multi-billion dollar opporunity, hence the funding of $1.2 million for 2019.
sponsorMessage: Thank you for adding the additional information!

title: The journey to a Hybrid Software Defined Storage Infrastructure
description: Hybrid Software Defined Storage Infrastructure
problemStatement: Storage has seen a huge change in the last 15 years (DASD, SAN, Storage Virtualization, Cloud Storage); the introduction of Disaster Recovery solutions based on Storage Subsystem functionalities; Storage Copy Function moving to the SAN first;  and some important functionalities like Real Time Compression, Flash Storage and Data Deduplication. Storage Virtualization set the base where to build the Software Defined Storage Infrastructure and the next Cloud Storage and ISCI connectivity.,This study aims to show how it is possible to leverage a Software Defined Storage technologies in the design of general storage solutions with an emphasis about Hybrid Storage Infrastructure on premise, off-premise, and for DR solutions. ,The consumers of this study would be Sales, Pre-sales and Architects, all having a picture of nowadays IT dilemma in satisfying business needs and to be proactive in their approaches to our Clients.
outcome: The global cloud storage market was expected to grow from USD 18.87 Billion in 2015 to USD 65.41 Billion by 2020, at a Compound Annual Growth Rate (CAGR) of 28.2% during the forecast period.
finalOutcome: The main value of this study is the increase of awareness about Software Defined Storage and Infrastructure solutions, and helps in engaging in the firsts discussions with customers to expand business opportunities.,The study demonstrates that IBM is a valid partner not only for the traditional infrastructure, but also expanding to Hybrid and Software Defined thanks to our rich portfolio
closeValue: Revamp IBM business opportunities with Software Defined Storage

description: IBM Egypt University Relations team is creating an initiative in collaboration with Bibliotheca Alexandria to deliver a 5-day summer bootcamp to kids aged 14-16 leveraging IBM latest initiative IBM Digital - Nation Africa. outcome:

title: Explore the applicability of a convergent method in the IBM Method and Tools portfolio
executiveChampionReason: Sponsor of revised Complex System Integration method, leads CSI practice
description: To test the hypothesis that seeking a convergent approach by combining agile and waterfall techniques is more optimal than following a pure agile or waterfall delivery process
problemStatement: There are strengths and weaknesses of using Agile and Waterfall methods in Custom Application Development. The hypothesis of this study is that seeking a convergent approach by combining agile and waterfall is more optimal than following a pure agile or waterfall delivery process. This hypothesis will be tested through defining some key views of a convergent method and comparing it to pure agile and pure waterfall approaches.
outcome: A high level definition of an IBM Convergent Method with clear recommendation from the team if convergent method has a valid place within the IBM Method and Tool portfolio.
finalOutcome:
Convergent Thinking has value across a wide number of the emerging and legacy IBM GBS Methods, therefore incorporation into the current portfolio is preferred over a stand-alone method as follows:
- Incorporate into IBM Services Mosaic Method to drive large programs to operate in a “core out” mode
- Add an additional delivery process into Application Impact Custom Development that sits between the existing agile and waterfall delivery processes
- Develop a Convergent Thinking Approach for other methods to include where appropriate, IBM Cloud Garage Method would be a recommended adopter for this approach
closeValue: The Convergent method offers many unique selling points, offering a good balance between waterfall and agile approaches and providing the best from both delivery processes.
publicationDescription:
The hypothesis of this initiative is that defining a convergent approach that seeks a balance between agile and waterfall is more optimal than following a pure agile or waterfall delivery process. The term “convergent" is the idea that a delivery converges on an optimal solution within an agreed timeframe and for an agreed budget. It has an outline scope and direction early on, but details are fleshed out and refined over the delivery lifecycle.
This hypothesis will be tested through defining some key views of a convergent custom development method and comparing it to agile and waterfall custom development approaches.  The content produced is therefore aimed at large scale custom development projects that would be typically delivered through AD2.0 or AICD today (i.e. not enterprise scale methods such as IBM Services Mosaic Method or SAFe).
The initiative will recommend if IBM should add a convergent method into its M&T portfolio.
ratingComments: Colin Walkinshaw did an excellent job working across a diverse group of technical leaders to bring the Convergent method work to a great outcome.

title: Improving IBM's External Reputation among Millenials through Music
IBM Academy of Technology Point / Counter Point: Constructive Critique of Initiatives and Activities
problemStatement: IBM Academy of Technology: Point / Counter Point,Introduction,As IBM transforms itself, multiple initiatives are being launched and multiple technologies and solutions are being taken to market, often at great speed.  While this speed is dictated by the need to be Agile, and stay ahead of the rate of technology change and the competition, it imposes risks.  These include risk of misunderstanding market dynamics in the time available, risk of not crisply defining a solution in the way that it needs, risk of prematurely exposing some new technology, or risk of missing some potential synergy with other initiatives in IBM.  ,Our clients experience the same pressures, and the same risks.  They are in a similar position.  ,At the same time, the IBM Academy of Technology continues to look for ways to add value to IBM and our clients, as part of its own transformational journey.  We also look for ways to exemplify Agile.  An opportunity therefore arises at the point where these transformational journeys and risks intersect – for The AOT to provide a rapid, if necessary confidential, but respectful and above all constructive critique of initiatives and activities, as a service to sponsoring executives and implementation teams within IBM, and to those within our clients.  This short paper sets out how it might work.,Point / Counter Point,Devil's Advocate is an ancient term from the Catholic Church where someone was officially appointed to argue against a canonization in order to explore weaknesses in the argument and in so doing, improve it.  In the context of IBM, the idea would be independently to review product or technology development/roll-out initiatives, change programs and transformations to:,•	Validate overall direction.,•	Identify strengths and benefits – and how these could be enhanced.,•	Identify oversights and weaknesses – and how these might be addressed.,•	Identify potential linkages with other initiatives in the company that might otherwise be overlooked – and how to exploit these.,•	Identify potential conflicts or inconsistencies with other initiatives – and how to avoid these.,In a sentence, the reviews would provide a level of assurance that “we’ve thought of everything” – and if not what could be done about that.,The reviews would have the following features:,•	The “client” would be the sponsoring executive of the activity in question, who would then have the choice of whether or not to make the findings of the review public.  ,•	Reviews would be focused on the substantive content of the area being reviewed, and business impact – they are not intended to be mere project management audits.,•	The focus would be on “accentuating the positive, eliminating the negative”.  Reviews would assess what is working well, or looks likely to work well, and how to build on what has been done; what changes or additions (if any) would improve the chances of the desired outcome; and what specific actions are required to move forward?,•	They would follow a pre-defined process (to be created) and ideally produce output (a short report/presentation, with additional exhibits as needed) to pre-defined templates.  ,•	Reviews would, in a spirit if being Agile, be completed within 8-12 weeks.,•	They would be carried out by small independent teams of AOT members selected from a panel of reviewers, who would be both acknowledged SMEs and, crucially, people from other - un-related - disciplines to help ensure different perspectives and help avoid “group-think”.   ,o	Teams would not contain anyone directly related to the initiative being reviewed.,o	Teams may however seek to gather data and feedback from the wider IBM via symposia or workshops, as part of the process to be defined.  ,•	Individual reviews would constitute Academy initiatives in their own right.,•	If required, by a separate arrangement, the AOT team could assist with implementing recommendations, coaching implementation teams, and so on.,•	Success of the Point / Counter Point idea would be measured by the number of requests received and a satisfaction rating from the sponsoring executive (ideally backed by concrete examples of value added).,Reviews could also be offered by the AOT along the same lines to external clients.,Next Steps,This is an initial outline of the idea.  Comments, additions, deletions and disagreements are welcomed.
outcome: Point / Counter Point - Defined AOT Offering - process, deliverable templates, pool of practitioners, ,Pilot implementation

finalOutcome:
This initiative had a high impact on the application of robotics in educational sector and on IBM cognitive strategy. The activities engaged a team of more than 10 IBMers from different countries and with different skills (researchers, hw/sw developers, cognitive specialists, architects and developers). title: Ecosystems - How to Architect them
executiveChampionReason:
Marketing have a general interest in understanding effective ways to reach out beyond IBM. This is the very essence of the ecosystems culture.
Phil is also keen to sponsor as Ecosystems are key to the Industry Solutions team, partnering with many organisations to deliver our value propositions going forward.
description: How to understand and engineer in the ecosystems era
problemStatement:
The solutions that we are seeing are ever more reliant on a multi-party ecosystem of organisations (partners, suppliers, & clients) Whilst the term 'Ecosystem' has gained prominence, it is unclear how to create, build or manage such Ecosystems. Indeed there is little established thinking in this area. This is particularly relevant to aid in identifying key industry participants who are the key influencers, stakeholders and emergent business models.

We set out to produce initial thinking and guidance to provide a common and consistent viewpoint for these initial 'reference architectures'. The aim is to produce a common base model that can be re-used across all industry sectors and segments, with tailored top-coatings per individual domain requirements – ultimately producing a library of segment ecosystems using a common, consistent approach, structure and language.

We intend to provide IBM with the key tools to be able to improve its ecosystems influence, help our clients build them and help identify 'white space' opportunities for key technologies.

The full framework will need to cover business architecture, key information needs and potential solution building blocks – covering and including all IBM brands/lines of business and clearly allowing extension out across third party organisations/solutions.
outcome:
Increased understanding of ecosystems in relation to IBM's key business objectives and a collection of base mechanisms to help communicate and design effectively at the ecosystems level.

OUTPUTS: Guidance (presented as document) covering elements:
·	Paper or presentation capturing the need for and use of ecosystems, and our point of view on how to address.
·	Recommended Common Framework (generic)
·	Identified work products (generic)
Key ecosystem-driven opportunties for IBM
finalOutcome: Production of Ecosystems 8 keys
closeValue: Ecosystems 8 Keys checklist

title: IBM Blockchain Solution Architecture
executiveChampionReason: Gari Singh, Blockchain CTO directly reporting to Jerry Cuomo, fully supports this initiative and has requested to also keep Nitin Gaur, Director Blockchain Labs, in the loop.
description: Blockchain CTO, Industry Platforms
problemStatement: The knowledge is mainly within the Blockchain and Garage teams whilst IBM Blockchain opportunities and engagements are increasing at a high pace. This comes with the inevitable constraints:,• IBMers around the globe keep involving the blockchain garage and engagement teams which are limited in size and capacity. We need to scale out their knowledge throughout IBM.,• Other units such as IBM Global Services need to become self-sufficient progressively.,• The knowledge within the blockchain engagement teams need to be leveraged to scale out the work force and the knowledge within IBM.,• Clients are confronting more and more IBMers with questions on blockchain technology, use cases, architectures, topologies, etc. Knowledge and information needs to be disseminated towards our customers.
outcome: Expected Outcome,In this initiative, we will focus on producing the Minimum Viable Products for further development of the reference architecture:,1. Define a Blockchain Solution Architecture Overview Diagram and describe its high-level components.,2. Identify architectural patterns and critical architectural decisions ,3. Define a use case example that exercises #1 and #2. ,Expected impact,The developed work products will help both our clients and IBM make practical implementation decisions using the provided guidance which will be developed based on the harvesting of architectural, development, deployment and operations collateral from blockchain implementations worldwide. ,By leveraging best-practices experience and avoiding “reinventing the wheel”, we expect to reduce the implementation risk for our clients by building on a proven approach, methodology and technology. Ultimately, this will also help our clients and IBM reduce cost of implementation through the sharing of common functions across blockchain implementations. ,A key impact of this effort will be in helping bridge the knowledge gap between key individuals from the blockchain lab teams and the rest of IBM and our clients.
finalOutcome: Outcome,In this initiative, we focused on producing the work products to serve as starting point for further development within the IBM Blockchain Architecture Board:,1.	Logical and Deployment Architecture Overview Diagrams with a high-level description of its components.,2.	Identification of the key architectural patterns and decisions. ,3.	Solution Guide Template based on an IoT use case leveraging the deliverables mentioned in bullet 1 and 2.,Impact,The developed work products will be incorporated into the IBM Blockchain Architecture Board and help both our clients and IBM make practical implementation decisions. ,Seen the complexity of the recent blockchain projects within IBM, we expect that these work products will help reduce the implementation risk for our clients and thus also help our clients and IBM reducing the cost of implementation.,A key impact of this effort is that it was reviewed together with Bobbie Cochrane, Nitin Gaur and Krishna Ratakonda and will serve as starting point within the IBM Blockchain Architecture Board. ,Final deliverables can be found on Box: https://ibm.box.com/s/6ogkouohnxnb5rtzaaobjazppt798y15
closeValue: The deliverables of this AoT Initiative will be leveraged as starting point for the IBM Blockchain Architecture Board led by Bobbie Cochrane and Nitin Gaur and thus be made available to the wider IBM Blockchain community.

title: Preventive measures in IBM project delivery and development
executiveChampionReason: Mr. Olaru is the Director of IBM Client Innovation Centers in Europe focusing in project delivery and development.
description: Define a set of preventive measures to be applied in project delivery across IBM project delivery and development.
problemStatement: In practice, project delivery success is not guaranteed. executiveChampionReason: Mr. Koike is the leader of Technical Leadership in Japan and the sponsor of TEC-J which is an affiliate of Academy of Technology. This initiative is for TEC-J to hold an open event having Mr. Grady Booch as the main speaker.
description: TEC-J will present open seminar "Grady Booch talks about History of Software Engineering"  at Hakozaki, IBM Japan. This is an open event for outside IBM. Distribution via video is also planned to be available.
problemStatement: No matter what future we may envision, it relies on software that has not yet been written. Even now, software-intensive systems have woven themselves into the interstitial spaces of civilization, and we as individuals and as a species have slowly surrendered ourselves to computing. Looking back, we can identify several major and distinct styles whereby we have built such systems. In many ways, the entire history of software engineering can be seen as one of raising levels of abstraction. And yet, in each phase of this journey, there have been particular technical, social, and economic forces that have shaped each style, and even now act upon our field to shape its future. In this presentation, we will walk the landscape of how we have developed software-intensive systems, from the time when computers were human, to now, where we are crafting computers that act like humans. Along the way, we will present the technical details, but more importantly, highlight the stories of the people who made this work manifest.
outcome: Provide Japanese software engineers the opportunity to hear speech by Mr. Grady Booch
finalOutcome: We Provided Japanese software engineers the opportunity to hear speech by Mr. Grady Booch and they fully encouraged. Japanese engineers improved their knowledge of the history of Software Engineering.
closeValue: Deep knowledge of the history of software engineering.
ratingComments: Booch made great presentation with his passion.   He followed SW engineering history and included his experience with historical contributor of SW engineering.

title: Senior Inventor program in Global Services
problemStatement: IBM units like Research, Software or Systems have a long history of invention disclosures.  They have developed over years a strong culture of patents, typical to organizations that can monetize their inventions directly into products.  ,Patents are equally essential to our Services business in the areas of systems and methods. They are critical to formalize, protect and re-sell our services assets. There is no doubt that GTS and GBS have the required projects, customers, and technical talents to participate actively to the patent vitality of the wide IBM. But in that field, they do not have the same historical experience as the other units. They don’t have yet the maturity required to systematically and consistently identify and develop the ideas that are worth a patent. ,Global Services (GS) is currently in the process of educating and encouraging potential inventors, increasing their inventing community, and ramping up the (too low) number of their invention. The Global Services inventors’ connection community is helping GS, through initiatives similar to those already existing within IBM (cf. Patent Cafés, EMEA Patent days or Patent Clubs …). ,We want to propose an additional but very different initiative:  the setup of a world-wide GS Senior Inventor Program supported by the AoT and the GS patent program managers, and recognizing the inventiveness in Global Services. That recognition would be a “Senior Inventor” title, awarded according to specific criteria.,The Master Inventor title is the only official patent recognition that is supported by a world-wide announcement.  The formal and serious requirements to obtain this title, and the high support and visibility of its announcement are very impressive and inspiring. But for too many people in Services, becoming a Master Inventor looks like an impossible dream, as they believe that filing one patent is already a huge challenge that does not worth the effort. These people are indeed used to passing their time on billable hours for customer projects and are not rewarded for the additional time they could pass to identify and formalize inventions. The possible patents they could obtain from this activity look like a bet. The time passed on a disclosure that is not filed is in fact perceived as lost time, as it does not bring any recognition. ,We think therefore that there is a need ,• To create a GS Inventor Recognition Program with nomination criteria taking these GS specificities in account.,• To define and organize activities of GS (potential) inventors that will help them gathering points in the Senior Inventor Program,• To run the GS Senior Inventor Program first (in 2016) for a limited number of countries (still to be selected). Then the program can be extended, after application of the lessons learned from the pilot.,Being recognized as a Senior Inventor is an achievement in itself that must be supported and announced by the AoT and by high executives of GS. It can also be an intermediary step towards the Master Inventor nomination. In that sense, the SI program is also an effective way to create and follow a pipe of future GS Master Inventors.,Concretely, this AoT initiative will: ,• Identify and analyze the GS activities that pertain to inventiveness, the reasons why these are not formalized into assets like patents, and the ways that could encourage GS to produce more formal inventive assets. ,• Create a system of individual Inventiveness points to measure the activity of each GS (potential) inventor.  Candidates must have a certain amount of Inventiveness points to qualify for the Senior Inventor Program.,The system must assign points not only to ideas filing or publishing, but also to the multiple other invention or innovation activities that GS can perform. We think for instance of: simple disclosure (without filing), formal identification of an idea (even if the idea is not coming from the candidate, and even if it does not result in a filing), participation to ideas brainstorming (even without any contribution to the selected idea), contribution to patent reviews, contribution to patents helps (material to help inventors and reviewers), contribution to success stories from GS projects, etc.,• Create a system supporting the inventors in their quest for Inventiveness points, for instance:,o By establishing a world-wide network of GS invention reviewers. Provide these reviewers with education, mentoring, a guide to perform reviews and opportunities to review concrete cases.  Performing reviews can help candidates not only by providing them SI points; it is also a way to become acquainted with disclosure writing and patent criteria. Moreover, a good reviewer can contribute to the reviewed invention and become a co-inventor.,o By using a Connection Community providing helps to future SI : showing by examples how to conceptualize and generalize developments and ideas into inventions, relating GS success stories (examples of GS projects that led to patents), providing hints, tips, recommendations, presentations , contribution opportunities  and/or links to other communities already having such content.
outcome: • Increase of the patent awareness, inventors’ motivation and technical vitality within Global Services. ,• Growth in the number of GS patents. ,• Identification and nomination of “recognized Senior Inventors” , role models for the GS community of inventors.,• Creation and follow-up of a GS pipe of Master Inventors. ,In 2016, we could setup the recognition program and its relating support activities and run a first SI Board. title: Patterns for Legacy Modernization
description: IBM Patterns for Legacy Modernization
problemStatement: Legacy applications are rarely monolithic and often distributed with client/server architecture types and transaction and messaging middleware. Even so, legacy modernization involves externalization of business, interaction and interfacing logic, processes, rules into separate component layers that can be managed independently resulting in modernized applications with significantly higher degrees of distribution and agility. We believe that legacy modernization can be expressed as a set of common architectural patterns deployed by Agile epics that refactor business logic from the legacy application into the modernized application during a phase characterized by co-existence of the legacy application and the modernized application during which the technical debt of the legacy application is paid down. The initiative sets out to identify and describe the architectural patterns, their architecture principles, and the Agile epics and sprints, as well as the Agile method, with which legacy modernization can occur.
outcome: Legacy applications are rarely monolithic and often distributed with client/server architecture types and transaction and messaging middleware. Even so, legacy modernization involves externalization of business, interaction and interfacing logic, processes, rules into separate component layers that can be managed independently resulting in modernized applications with significantly higher degrees of distribution and agility. We believe that legacy modernization can be expressed as a set of common architectural patterns deployed by Agile epics that refactor business logic from the legacy application into the modernized application during a phase characterized by co-existence of the legacy application and the modernized application during which the technical debt of the legacy application is paid down. The initiative sets out to identify and describe the architectural patterns, their architecture principles, and the Agile epics and sprints, as well as the Agile method, with which legacy modernization can occur.
finalOutcome: Patterns for Systems Modernization represents a renewed pattern-based approach to technical vitalization and modernization of legacy systems, taking into account technology on z Systems, and proposes how systems modernization should occur relative to the use of Agile methods, DevOps, Hybrid Cloud, and modular procurement practices. It is highly useful for technical sellers and technical architects that engage in systems modernization initiatives from early stages of the Client Value Method and well into implementation.
closeValue: A substantial refresh of IBM practices and approaches to systems modernization, reflecting the confluence of Agile, DevOps, Cloud
publicationDescription: Patterns for Systems Modernization describes the common behavior, economy and strategy patterns that direct and guide decisions on legacy modernization. From there the Report describes the typical anti-patterns that represent technical debt in legacy systems and it proposes a finite set of concrete architecture and deployment patterns that realize the individual strategies. Finally, the report consider the Agile practices and DevOps patterns that can be applied to legacy modernization initiatives.
