title: Reputation of a Technical Leader
problemStatement: The invisible shadow that is an individual’s reputation influences the opportunities that can be pursued and the outcomes that can be achieved.  Yet most people remain oblivious to the reputational impact of their daily action.  Promotions and project roles hinge on having a good reputation.  It is often the case that the one person not participating in the discussions that lead to these decisions is the very person that the decision affects.  Only that person’s reputation is taken into account.,Everyone wanting to progress their careers needs to be able to assess and develop their reputations.  But the wider impact that results from the internal motivation that results from a good reputation accelerates the achievement of major business outcomes or inspires the creation of disruptive technologies.  Reputation of technical leaders is therefore not only of interest to our technical leaders, but also to our business leaders and IBM as a whole.,Our clients are looking for leaders who have the right reputation and of course the expertise to understand the opportunities arising from digital transformations so as to guide their strategic decision. This includes understanding of specific industries.  IBM has established technical roles that include being a trusted advisor for clients.  However our clients are expecting leadership at all levels of their technical engagement with IBM.,The objective of the Academy initiative is to refresh the various descriptions of reputation of a technical leader by defining an up to date view of reputation that reflects the future of our industry so that technical communities are better enabled and technical leaders engaged to achieve business outcomes more quickly.,Reputation is not something that should be left to chance, but rather needs to be actively managed.  Reputation should be nurtured at the outset by anyone who aspires to a technical career which includes any element of leadership to build sustainable value.
outcome: This initiative aims to standardise the description of reputation used across IBM’s technical community.  It will identify how corporate processes that define, develop and assess reputation can be harmonised, and intervene in those processes to drive alignment on the use of reputation.  This will drive:,•	Easy access to the best expertise for business leaders to help them develop market opportunities for IBM.,•	Clarity for technical professionals on how to build their reputations to realise their career aspirations.,•	A more engaged and inclusive workforce in IBM.
legacyParticipantType: The leadership team for this initiative welcomes any IBM technical professional who is passionate about leadership, reputation or eminence.  The initiative will explore the distinctions and intersections between these, and it will benefit from those individuals who have expertise and experience leading activity that is helping IBM realise its strategy of cognitive solutions and cloud platforms for our clients.nAnyone who leads a technical activity or engagement, however large of small, and however junior, will be able to make a significant contribution to how IBM defines, develops and assesses reputation in this initiative.  We are especially keen to include leaders who are early in their careers.nThe initiative will be run in conjunction with HR.  Participation by HR professionals who undertake learning and development activities for technical leaders and run the programmes that drive them, and those who assess technical leaders for projects, promotions and new roles will make a valuable contribution to this work.
legacyValue: The value of the reputation of a technical leader is highlighted in the following points for different stakeholders, and there is a natural value to clients in each.,•	A technical leader needs to have clarity how to put together and execute their development plan to maximise career success.  Understanding their current reputation (including what elements are attributes of a reputation) and how to build it is vital so that they have a clear trajectory on how to achieve their career objectives.,•	IBM is facing challenges as digital transformations change our industry.  Developing the reputation of technical leaders is essential for IBM to create and sustain a workforce that is engaged and inclusive.,•	Our business leaders face new market opportunities and technology disruption.  Reputations of technical leaders are necessary to access the best expertise and competence to exploit this change.  It requires business leaders to be equipped to help individual managers understand what they need to do to help create technical leaders by identifying and addressing gaps in their skills and reputation.

title: TechConnect
executiveChampionReason: In years past, Tom has been very supportive of the TechConnect initiative.  In addition, as VP, System Development for IBM Z, he has oversight of many of the teams that will participate in the event.
description: Competitive poster session showcasing technical achievements of the communities served by the MHV TVA
problemStatement: The work in the Mid-Hudson Valley produces a wide range of hardware and software deliverables that have a major impact on IBM's success in the marketplace.  Teams have limited visibility to one another if their work products aren't directly related.  We need a way to share the glorious variety of MHV work with the technical population in the area to spark the kind of creative thinking that only occurs through exposure to different ideas and approaches to problem solving.  ,In addition, we need a vehicle for giving early tenure employees the opportunity to showcase and discuss their work with the senior technical and non-technical leaders on-site.
outcome: TechConnect offers technical employees from across a diverse spectrum of specializations an opportunity to share their work with the entire local IBM community.  Poster presenters grow their personal eminence by exposing their work well beyond the boundaries of their local teams.  All participants - both presenters and visitors - have the opportunity to expand their networks and whet their intellectual appetites through exposure to a smorgasbord of delicacies sampled from the whole portfolio of work produced in the region.   ,In particular, early tenure employees are able to discuss their projects with DE's, Fellows, and upper level management while honing their presentation skills in a non-threatening, celebratory environment.  (We also open the event to interns from Marist College and can generally count on at least one poster entry from that group.)
finalOutcome: TechConnect provided an opportunity for employees to present their work in a format (poster) that outlines their accomplishments in technical innovation/invention, process improvements, quality enhancements, and other strategic priorities. A unique element of  this initiative was the fact that it was open to everyone on site, thus allowing the presenters to showcase their work to and get feedback from other IBM'ers regardless of their organizational affiliation. This year we had a record number of submissions --40 in all -- representing the collective work of more than 150 IBMers and spanning a wide variety of topics. Attendees learned about a number of technical achievements of their peer IBM'ers such as 1) Hardware random number generator, 2) IBM Systems Client Experience Portal,  and 3) IBM Voice Gateway and IBM Voice Agent with Watson.  The event was well attended by hundreds of IBM'ers including senior technical leaders and executives.,The initiative provided a venue for employees of various tenure ranges and experience levels to showcase their work. Posters submitted for the event were divided into four tracks (Hardware, Software, Manufacturing/ISC, and Solutions). Each of the four tracks had two sub-tracks, namely, "Early-Tenure" and "Open". Projects presented by those who have been in IBM for less than five years entered the Early-Tenure category. Others submitted to the Open track. The posters were judged by an esteemed team of technical leaders. Winners were announced for each track. We also had a special award called "People's Choice award", which provided all attendees an opportunity to vote for their favorite poster. One poster from Early-Tenure and one poster from Open categories were chosen for that award. Again, a record 160+ people voted for the People's Choice awards.,The 1st place winners from the event have been invited to present their posters at the Academy of Technology Regional Summit in Yorktown Heights on 11/15/17.  This will give the winning presenters an additional opportunity to further expand their networks and build their eminence within the IBM technical community. ,The initiative created a lot of buzz before, during, and after the day of the event. More details of the event and about the winning posters can be found at https://w3-connections.ibm.com/wikis/home?lang=en#!.  ,Tom McPherson's (our Executive Champion) endorsement of the event is obvious from his comment posted on our blog announcing the TechConnect Winners: https://w3-connections.ibm.com/wikis/home?lang=en#!/wiki/Wf70894c37f7b_48bb_86a3_3f59969c597c/page/TechConnect%202017%20Winners.
closeValue: This initiative provided a unique platform for the entire IBM community in the Mid Hudson Valley to come together and learn about the work of their peers, crossing all organizational boundaries.

title: Academy of Technology Input into the 2019 Global Technology Outlook Ideation Process
executiveChampionReason: Kathryn Guarini, Vice President, Research Strategy, IBM Research has responsibility for the Global Technology Outlook process.    Prasenjit Dey and Karin Murthy are the GTO-2019 leads.
description: This initiative is being launched as a means for AoT members and AoT Affiliate members to provide input into the IBM Research GTO-2019 ideation process.
problemStatement:
The GTO ideation process involves collecting input from IBM Research Labs located around the world.  This always generates many great ideas from our top research scientists.  However, the GTO-2019 team recognizes the importance of crowdsourcing ideas from outside IBM, otherwise we are developing ideas in a vacuum.  If we only develop ideas from internal sources, then we run the risk of developing a Global Technology Outlook that does not represent problems and issues that our clients actually need to be solved.  So in addition to other plans in place to crowdsource ideas through Design Thinking workshops, the GTO-2019 is interested in crowdsourcing ideas from AoT Members and Affliliate Members who are client facing.  

The GTO team wants to collect ideas in the form of textual answers.  They  do NOT want those providing ideas/input to see the ideas/input others have already provided (as this might bias them one way or the other).  This rules out many forms of social, collaborative and idea generation tools.
outcome: We will conduct a SPRINT from March 29 - April 13 that requests input from Academy members and Affiliate members by asking them to answer one question via email. We will analyze all the input and provide high level analysis of all input received along with all the detailed textual responses to the GTO-2019 team in time for a planned April 25 Design Thinking workshop to be held in Yorktown.  The output will have a significant impact on the ideation process for the GTO-2019 topics and is a great solution for the problem statement described above.
finalOutcome:
We asked IBM Academy of Technology (AoT) members, Academy Affiliate Members and IBM Market Development and Insights professionals to provide input on the gaps in IBM capabilities they were hearing about either from their work with clients (AoT members) or their work on analyzing markets (MD&I analysts).   We received 320 specific ideas/input from 147 IBM employees and we have sorted those ideas into major categories.  

This initiative identified specific examples of technical capabilities clients want, including:
    AI systems that are easier to implement, faster to train and are verifiable/trustworthy
    Improvements in conversational chatbot offerings
    More robust IBM cloud offerings including improved speed of migration, improved data compliance capabilities and improved integration with other IBM offerings.
    Solutions that can speed an organization’s transformation from old legacy systems
    Improved security capabilities in all offerings and solutions
    Improved analytics: 1) At the edge of IoT networks and 2) As an aid to helping users quickly generate insights in real time
    Technologies that can reduce IT complexity and are easily integrated into other existing IBM systems
    Solutions that align to open source technologies

For more outcomes, see AoT Initiative on Client Wants & Needs: Summary of Key Findings  https://w3-connections.ibm.com/blogs/alt/entry/Client_Wants_Needs_Initiative_Key_Findings?lang=en
closeValue: We received 320 specific ideas/input from 147 IBM employees  ideas related to specific client wants and needs that are impacting (negatively in many cases) overall client experience

problemStatement: The IBM Professions are, rightly, undergoing significant change at present, with no (as yet) widely publicised mechanism for technical professionals to re-certify or certify at the next level. outcome:

finalOutcome:
The last twelve months have seen a remarkable re-invention of the Technical Career Model, moving through concept, pilot, launch and now full deployment for certifications in the Architect and Specialist Professions. This UKI TCG initiative set out with the objective of raising awareness of these changes with UKI teams - both in the technical and leadership communities - and helping smooth the path to enable individuals to earn Badges and successfully complete the certification process as quickly and efficiently as possible.

A huge thank you to all of our active contributors to this initiative, and special thanks to the BetaWorks media teams, who have supported us with the video-making exercises.

Full details are available here:

title: Content Optimization: Technology Evaluation of Acrolinx, Watson, and Competitors
executiveChampionReason: his Executive Champion requested the activity, currently owns the IBM enterprise Acrolinx contract, works with many of the key stakeholders, manages key resources, supports internal IBM Information Development (ID teams) that have worked with and rely on Acrolinx since 2008, and has secured the interest in this AoT activity from Vice-Presidents in three business units who wish to evaluate content optimization options for a company-wide recommendation.
description: IBM desires to evaluate Acrolinx versus current and potential future Watson capabilities and other industry competitors in order to facilitate a choice among content optimization technologies and to establish a longer term direction that meets IBM content related business goals and the varied needs of stakeholders. This BU-requested activity will assemble a team of key content contributors and technology experts to evaluate key technology options on major evaluation criteria.
problemStatement: Content optimization is a critical area of technology for IBM, affecting IBM’s digital transformation and interactions and relationships with clients across marketing, support, and product functions of the business. With tens of millions of web pages, thousands of publications, and hundreds of web properties, IBM’s marketing and technical content reach anbd skills exceedingly broad. Optimizing content takes many forms, including identifying and tagging keywords for search optimization, analyzing content to improve tone and readability, measuring effectiveness, and deploying machine learning techniques to reason about content and link behavior to latent content attributes. In recent years, IBM has embedded Acrolinx as a vendor into several of its content creation solutions. With the rise in of AI and cloud in the enterprise IT marketplace, Acrolinx has changed its underlying offerings, even as new, differentiating IBM capabilities have emerged. This leads to significant questions of which technology options best facilitate IBM’s business objectives short and longer-term. A deeper look into these options by the Academy of Technology, involving technology representatives from IBM stakeholders as well as subject matter experts identified by the AoT is desired.
outcome: In the short term, this activity will provide in depth technology insight for IBM’s content optimization company-wide. Specifically, the activity will deliver:  a) key questions on all major options, b) evaluation criteria and generate a work-in-progress analysis available on a daily basis, c) findings with an emphasis on consensus recommendations if possible, or options and rationales if not, and d) briefings on an as-needed basis. Longer term, the prospective business value of this activity lies in choosing optimal technology options, providing possible future product directions, and fostering understanding and teamwork across marketing and technical content creation teams in order to help improve client relationships and drive improved business results.
finalOutcome: Insights on AI for Content space and evaluation of Acrolinx as enterprise solution. The business value is to expose AI for Content as a larger technology trend to which IBM must respond.  Technology recommendations and design considerations for interactive assistance for IBM creatives, leading to better content and business results via engagement with clients.
closeValue: The initiative shows that AI for Content, that is, the infusing of AI into content creation, is an emerging tech trend that affects every step of the content creation process for IBM, its clients and partners, and its competitors.
ratingComments: This was a very complex project from both technical, business, and political considerations.  The team did a fantastic job of providing a position on whether there were any competitors to Acrolinx, and more broadly, went beyond to provide many ideas on opportunities for utilizing AI to improve content.

title: Illustrative AI is an application of mechanistic models for self-explainable AI-based industry solutions. Towards explainable AI, Illustrative AI puts mechanistic models under the AI's control for self expression.
outcome: The technical outcomes of this initiative will be threefold: 1) a technical description of the scope of Illustrative AI, defining what it is and how it works; 2) an analysis and catalogue of industry problems that are best addressed with mechanistic models under the control of AI for self-expression; and 3) a review of AI architectures and scientific results demonstrating workable embodiments of Illustrative AI. By identifying strong mechanistic models of processes fundamental to clients in industries such as Healthcare, Financial Services, Industry, Commerce, Agriculture, and Environment, we will catalogue potential AI-controlled models for self explanation and expression. By identifying best-in-class prediction and categorization AIs in these same industries, we will identify which solutions have the strongest need for self-explainability through illustration. Finally, by identifying which AI architectures and methods are best able to participate in the illustration's parameterization, we will find the most readily implementable Illustrative AIs. This alignment between all three lists will provide the main outcome of the initiative: a direction for investment for client-specific demonstrations of Illustrative AI.

title: Analytic Software Complexity for Agile Software
executiveChampionReason: Tim Kane leads the system group test effort and is thus a natural receiver of this effort.
description: Measure software complexity through dynamic indicators
problemStatement: Software complexity helps us decide when to rewrite portions of software, what area of the software requires more testing or inspection and how much resource should be allocated for the implementation of the next set of user stories.  With the introduction and adoption of agile techniques, software actually ages more quickly due to these rapid development cycles.  In addition, modern software is complex, it is non-homogeneous ranging across many languages and environments.  Measuring software complexity is a well-known challenge.  Traditional software complexity is measured using static analysis techniques. These techniques don't scale well to non-homogeneous modern environments of software solutions.,This Initiative is sponsored by Tim Kane (VP), Tom Ramey (Director), Maria Boonie (VP).
outcome: Building on the results of the Pareto Principle study, a work item, entitled 'Related Parts', evaluated how software programs or modules are 'modified or changed' during the same development action. For example, the examination of library management system records on a particular part's change history can provide us with insight as to whether a part is changed in conjunction with other parts during the same feature, defect or maintenance. We can then look at the history of those changes and alert developers, testers, etc. to take note that a change to other parts may be necessary as well. It is our premise that the continued evolution of the 'Related Parts' technology can provide a much stronger indicator of software complexity than traditional static analysis techniques.,In the context of open source and cloud software, the related part technology will enable the efficient, high quality and safe consumption of open source code through appropriated impact analysis. ,The expected outcome of this proposed study will provide us with a more accurate set of measurable indicators of software complexity. With this set of indicators, software production teams can accurately identify the most critical areas in need of software simplification and improved quality.
finalOutcome: The main observation of this study was that design drift  from isolation is an area of focus  and concern in legacy systems.  This study built on the  Academy study on Pareto Principle (2015-2016).   The study developed new ML based related parts/change impact analysis  techniques.  They were deployed  in z/OS, Cloud, Power SW.   Related parts was embedded into the MAGMA tool, change impact analysis is planned to be integrated with Nirvana.  In DB2 for Z context-based change impact analysis  is  part of the APAR review tool.  Analytics-based skills and retirement assessment as well code review assistance is used by Z/OS development.  ZFD - i390 build regression effectiveness & zLPAR relationships are analyzed using the technology.
closeValue: Sound ML technolgy to analyze code dependencies.
ratingComments: Project identified innovative approaches to identify potential defects and to improve product quality.  Very good teamwork from all involved.
adminComments: 7/23: Richard Prewitt, Jr. is no longer at IBM - Eitan Farchi agreed to be the Leader.  TC

problemStatement: As part of the long-term R&D within TWC we are identifying new sources of data that could have value if appropriately ingested into our weather forecast models. Another dimension is how such data can improve the representation of current weather conditions as well as very short-term projections (e.g., minutes to an hour). title: Improving social media engagement by technical professionals
executiveChampionReason: Subject area is directly relevant to Caroline's remit in Global Markets, Caroline has also sponsored similar initiatives.
description: This initiative aims to increase engagement with IBM on social media in technical subjects.  It is simple for technical professionals to generate social media output, but only a very small percentage results in any meaningful engagement. This initiative will understand the reasons for IBM's lack of engagement on technical subjects and identify measures to increase levels of engagement.
problemStatement:
IBM has a substantial social media footprint as do its nearly 400,000 employees, but only rarely does this translate into engagement. The marketing messages and brand are efficiently distributed through social media platform like Twitter and are amplified (in the case of Twitter re-tweeted) by a large number of employees. However, this is mainly a one-way broadcast of tightly controlled marketing messages and does not lead to wider market engagement. IBM's technical employees rarely engage in conversations or crucially express an opinion 'online'. Technical professionals do not seem to feel able to share their technical opinions as they would in a face-to-face setting, such as at a conference. There are cultural and institutional reasons as well as corporate rules (the Social Computing Guidelines) that  inhibit the expression of opinions and the engagement 

Groups such as developers do not like to be 'sold to' and competitors such as Microsoft and Amazon seemingly do a better job at engaging at the technical peer level. This is often not in the traditional social media platforms like Linked-in or Twitter but on GitHub, Stackoverflow, Reddit etc.

In short IBM and its employees do not express a technical opinion which is required to engage.
outcome:
Customer and Industry engagement with IBM on technical subjects in social media
Increased instances of IBM and IBMers engaging in social media conversations on technical subjects
Increased engagement by mid level technology influencers on content posted by IBMers and in conversations where IBMers are participating
finalOutcome: In this initiative we have surveyed and understood how IBMers use Social Media and have put in place concrete steps and proposals to improve and enhance. We carried out a valuable survey across IBM and used this to drive execution. We have created a video to drive uptake and increase Twitter Eminence amongst the IBM technical community. We have established the prototype Content Creator Cafe that will continue to be the focal point for Academy Members and other technical professionals to go for content help, advice and mentoring. We created proposals for the introduction of social media badges and a social media buddy scheme.
closeValue: This initiative understood through survey and analysis that engagement is about content; the initiative created the prototype Content Creator Cafe to improve content (and hence engagement) amongst the technical community.

title: Systems Supply Chain Transformation Acceleration – Talent Enablement
executiveChampionReason: Robert Edge Jr (Director, Worldwide Server and Solutions Fulfillment) owns critical missions (quality, processing, testing) in Mainframe and Power Manufacturing across multiple geographies and is the Executive sponsor for the Supply Chain (SC) Skills Council - a group that is dedicated and relentlessly working on skill and talent development in SC.
description: Systems Supply Chain Transformation Acceleration through adoption of emerging technologies (such as IOT, Blockchain, Cognitive), showcasing of Supply Chain capabilities and talent development.
problemStatement: Systems Supply Chain is an area which has rich data that is extremely valuable to IBM, our suppliers and to our clients. We have data from IBM manufacturing process and test, as well as from our suppliers through agreed data sharing protocols. title: Transforming the Mainframe Experience: The Zowe Initiative
executiveChampionReason: Melissa is the Executive Champion of our umbrella initiative to 'Break the Cycle' of mainframe sales.
description: Many clients experience our most cutting edge IBM Z systems through an interface that was established over 30 years ago. While it may be efficient, it presents a barrier to professional seeking to exploit and manage mainframe systems today. Project Zowe is intended to address this issue, and requires the awareness and engagement of out Academy members.
problemStatement:
The user experience (UX) of IBM Z mainframes, whether via applications, data bases or systems management, has long since evolved from the traditional green screen interface. However, this UX remains the most-widely adopted way that many organisations choose to use the mainframe, which is deterring the new generation of users. This new audience - essential to the health of an IBM Z platform which underpins the top Fortune 500 companies - expect intuitive, CLI and browser-based interfaces that look and feel just like any contemporary platform. 

Addressing this challenge, IBM has partnered with CA and Rocket Software to conceive and release a transformational new technology that completely re-imagines the UX for IBM Z. Released in the summer of 2018, the outcome of this collaboration, "Zowe", was released as an Open Source solution, as part of the Open Mainframe Project to encourage and invite all developers, developer advocates and vendors to come together and build out the next generation of tooling to service one of the most venerable platforms in the world.
outcome: It is essential for the success of this initiative, that our colleagues, partners and clients alike, are aware of the tremendous potential of this technology - and to be able to understand and articulate the philosophy of the approach. Tapping the expertise, reach and influence of our AoT colleagues, we intend to educate the team to enable them to be able to articulate this message, supporting the broad ecosystem that has grown up around the IBM Z mainframe.
finalOutcome: This initiative set out to raise awareness of the Zowe initiative with IBM's technical leadership team in the AoT, in order for them to make informed decisions and recommendations with clients on this new Open Source capability. As a technology that contemporises the operational and management experience of z/OS, Zowe is a superb example of IBM's collaboration with partners Broadcom and Rocket Software, to address the skills concerns that many of our clients express. This initiative culminated in a recorded WW webcast and blog, with speakers from IBM, Broadcom and Rocket Software, sharing a perspective on the initiative and capabilities of Zowe.
closeValue: Transformation of the mainframe user experience, in order for our largest enterprise clients, to more effectively consume and operate one of their most strategic technical investments.
ratingComments: This was a great effort toward creating awareness of Zowe.
sponsorMessage: Great job Richard and team! I look forward to host your webcast about Zowe, which will become very important! Thank you for your dedication and passion about z Systems!

title: Supply Chain IoT Competency Acceleration Model for Advanced Manufacturing

problemStatement: The Industry 4.0 “Revolution” identifies the Advanced Manufacturing in being one fundamental aspect of the Cognitive Supply Chain Transformation, but there is a much less information about the necessary competences required to support this. Intelligent Automation and (human) Augmented Intelligence are the converging elements where innovation is actually crashing with the available workforce’s platform of skills and knowledge. The constant growth of new methodologies and solutions are requiring new levels of interdisciplinary competences. Implementing IoT solutions in manufacturing plays a critical part for achieving advanced manufacturing objectives. Regardless of the reduced role in the manufacturing of hardware, the Systems Supply Chain Engineering (SCE) is on the front line of this transformation, and still bears great level of responsibilities in being knowledgeable about manufacturing operations. A model for workforce reskilling is in execution, and to be exported in different GEOs. It aims supporting World Wide Clients’ engagements in collaboration with Watson-IoT.
outcome: The SCE executive sponsors, Robert Edge Jr (Director, Worldwide Server and Solutions Fulfillment) and Luis Raul Rodriguez (Director, System Storage & SWG Appliances), own critical missions (quality, processing, testing) in four IBM manufacturing sites across GEOs. The IoT competency acceleration model will engage dedicated engineering resources across the four sites in a steep learning curve on IoT implementation skills (sensor, network, solutions. etc). The reskilled engineering resources will be prioritized in implementing IoT solutions in all four sites for transformation in quality, cost and efficiency, which is critical for Cognitive Supply Chain enablement. ,The internal IoT “success stories” will be the flag ship “showcase” for client demonstration and engagement in collaboration with Watson-IoT. ,This TEC-SSC affiliate is in a unique position for geographical distribution, to activate the availability of skilled personnel with “Hands on” experience, to win trust over competences and helping the client in the construction of IoT solutions with IBM as a preferred partner. TEC-SSC sees this initiative a preferred channel to increase the opportunities of Watson-IoT revenue growth, thus supporting and accelerating Act-II Winning. The initiative will provide an evaluation and validation of the re-skilling acts in Singapore and Hungary, adjusting the planning and execution in other locations.
finalOutcome: The SCE IoT Competency Acceleration Model provides a holistic view of the skills required for implementing IoT solutions across different industry domains. Through the use of Design Thinking and Agile principles, training combined with  hands-on practices were employed throughout the whole execution phases at the sites in Singapore and Hungary, now starting execution in Poughkeepsie in US and being planned at Guadalajara, MEX. The effectiveness and efficiency of the skill acquisition has been verified through the results of hands-on practical projects and challenges which have been already successfully deployed into manufacturing operations at the aforementioned IBM factories.,More specifically, 21 talents have been well trained with an in-depth knowledge and proficient hands-on experience. They have been deployed for Advanced Manufacturing implementation in two manufacturing locations, with significant financial returns expected to be realized in next few years through process improvement and innovation.From the early adoption of a few of these hands-on projects  cost saving  is already projected at USD 80,000 hard saving per quarter and USD 160,000 cost avoidance per quarter in two locations with a rapid growth to more important financial figures, which would be even morte amplified once the other manufacturing plants are aligned to this strategy. The productivity enhancement is only one part of the results where additional contribution is being enabled by the availability of enhanced skills supporting IBM clients in different industries.
closeValue: The imitative created and delivered a skill development model, whose effectiveness and efficiency has been thoroughly verified through the results of implemennting projects onto mfg floors, creating a set of recommendations and guidelines replicated across IBM production sites,  that can also be adopted by other IBM organizations for their own IoT Skills development and growth as a mean to help clients reducing operational cost and to increase revenue.

title: Open Data Service Layer: Improving Data Sources for the Government Sector
executiveChampionReason: Because Anders left IBM
description: An Open Data Service Layer
problemStatement: Today, Open Data is provided by organizations to the public on a search basis.  Its like going to the Library and looking up a book.  You need to know the library exists, how to find a book, whether the book is relevant to you, how to read the book, and what to do with it.  This is why 99% of the public knows nothing about Open Data.  It would be much better if the government would serve up Open Data to us when we interact with them, on a proactive basis.  This study will explore a privacy-preserving technical architecture for providing an Open Data Service Layer - a cognitive intermediary that provides the right information to the public when they interact with government departments.  We will be working with The Danish Business Authority (Danish Government) on this Study collaboratively.
outcome: Service Layer Technical Architecture,Macro Solution Outline,Pilot Potential
finalOutcome: We developed an outstanding concept with use case examples and shared the idea with the governments of Denmark, Argentina, Chile, and Peru and got excellent feedback.  We also shared it with the Global Federal Account team and with NTIS, a division of the US Commerce Department, and got great feedback.  There is a demonstrated customer need.
closeValue: This is a solution IBM can sell and deliver.
publicationCategory: TechNote (one page and NOT IBM Confidential)
publicationDescription: The Data Service Layer relies on government departments publishing Open Data to a catalog, which gets indexed and provisioned to government users based on daily internet session profiles.  The session profiles, like Amazon shopping profiles, get generated by cookies which indicate interests and preferences.  The Data Service Layer keeps these session profiles for one day and then deletes them automatically to preserve the data privacy of government employees.  But while the profiles are active, the preferences are used to retrieve relevant datasets from the entire catalog of government Open Data and provision the data to users as sidebar advertisements, emails, and application links.

title: Practical Operational Modelling
executiveChampionReason: x
description: Practical Operational Modelling
problemStatement: How is Operational Modelling performed effectively?  Even in the Cloud world, the need to model a system in order to ensure that the Non-Functional requirements will be met is still just as important as ever. However there is often a gap between what modelling is actually performed on projects, and what the method says should be done. Further, the premise is that Operational Modelling for cloud systems could be optimised.,The word 'Practical' in the title is deliberate.  This is not intended as a theoretical study, but is intended to look at the practicalities of working within a real project, with the pressures which come from delivery, time-scales and cost.,The study is split into three ‘streams’,1.	Architecture for Cloud Systems – how to adapt Operational Modelling to better handle systems which are being built to be hosted in Cloud,2.	Architecture for Cloud Infrastructure – how to adapt Operational Modelling for the build of Cloud Infrastructure,3.	Operational Modelling Value – Operational Modelling is rarely, if ever, done as specified in the method – is this because it is not ‘value for money’ or are we losing out,We are looking to bring ‘Agile’ into the AoT study.  Each stream will be split into multiple sprints.  The team will be around 6-8 for a sprint.  There will be a call for participation for the sprint, and candidates selected based on the objectives of the sprint.  An AoT study report will be generated as output from each sprint.  Towards the end of each sprint the core team and sponsors will consider the objectives for the next sprint.,The study is being run as joint initiative between the Technology Architect Community of Practice and the AoT Cloud Technology Team.  The Technology Architect’s Community of Practice is a community for Technology (or Infrastructure) Architects – open to all LoB and Geographies.,The following are the specific problem statements which are due to be explored;,* Operational Modelling is rarely if ever done as specified in the method – is this because it is not ‘value for money’ or are we losing out?,* Operational Modelling for Cloud is different – the Cloud has inherent constraints which you should work to – how should we adapt the modelling to handle this?,* Operational Modelling for Cloud is different – ‘Born in the Cloud’ architectures exploit the dynamic nature of Cloud, which standard operational modelling does not cater for – how should we adapt the modelling for this?,* Operational Modelling for Bluemix is even more different – with Bluemix you no longer have any control over the infrastructure, so you can only meet non-functional requirements by devising a ‘functional’ solution,* Integration of different modelling approaches (as outlined above) will become vital
outcome: Validate whether Operational Modelling is too complex (especially in the cloud era), and it should be optimised.  The rigorous method/model is never fully adhered to – by reviewing the ‘value’ attached to each part of the model we should be able to understand better what is important and what is not and refine and refocus the model.,Determine if we would get value (particularly for Softlayer) from documenting the constraints and available components for a cloud in an Operational Modelling format.  These could be used as building blocks to help in the creation of a system Architecture/Model.  ,Validate if Operational Modelling should be extended to cover dynamic cloud models.,Validate if Bluemix requires a new approach, where non-functional aspects are understood, but then solved using a functional design rather than an infrastructure design.  This will need a radical change to the way we design systems,Given that different modelling approaches are likely to be required, and given that future systems are expected to be a mix of new and old – we will need to understand how to join new and old models together to form a cohesive whole and meet the overall client requirements
finalOutcome: This Initiative was the old wrapper for the various Sprints that we have been running - the sprints have been (a) Defining how Operational Modelling is done in Cognitive Architect (b) Exploring how Operational Modelling can be done more efficiently in a cloud context (c) Revising the Operational Modelling notation for new approaches to modelling (d) exploring how to model the creation of Cloud Infrastructure.
closeValue: The primary delivery was the specifications for the Operational Modelling within the Cognitive Architect tool
legacyParticipantType: Architects involved in Operational Modelling across all geographies and business lines.
legacyValue: Even in the Cloud world Operational Modelling is essential.  For small or non-complex systems it is not so important - but the systems which IBM delivers are not in this category and ensuring that a system is reliable, robust, performant etc is essential.  However the cost of  doing this can also be considerable, and at the moment different practitioners go about it in different ways, which makes sharing and reuse hard.  ,With the use of Cloud a number of decisions have already effectively been made, which should make the problem easier, but only if we find an effective way of harnessing this.  ,This study looks to look how Cloud is potentially a game changer for modelling.  It looks at what is actually being done, and to come to a conclusion of the business value of the modelling.  It looks to come up with a recommended approach to improve the quality and speed of delivery, whilst minimising unnecessary cost.

description: The rapid expansion of the Internet of Things (IoT) offers payments companies an opportunity to expand beyond mobile phones, cards, and point-of-sale devices, to a broad and diverse ecosystem of internet-connected devices.One of the objectives of customer service today is to create 'frictionless experiences'. Consumer demands for personalized experiences, regulatory and industry initiatives forcing innovation, openness and collaboration in the payment industry, development of new models and digital ecosystems with cross–border payments transformed by using block chain technology are disruptive and accelerating change in payment processing. Companies like Amazon and Starbucks have distinct frictionless payment approaches that both leverage available technologies to improve the end-to-end retail experience in stores and online. The rapid expansion of the Internet of Things(IoT) offers payments companies an opportunity to expand beyond mobile phones, cards, and point-of-sale devices, to a broad and diverse ecosystem of internet-connected devices. 
As new technologies are emerging, we want to explore new models for payments in new ecosystems, that will allow more and fare competition

title: IBM Research KnowledgeBridge Challenge:  Transferring IBM Research Technology Innovations to IBM Business Impact
executiveChampionReason: Dinesh proposed this KnowledgeBridge challenge to the Academy.  He announced the launch of the initiative during our July 24, 2018 event "KnowledgeBridge: Secret Decoder Ring: Research – Connect and Stay Connected".
description: We will develop recommendations designed to 1) Improve our ability to transfer tech innovations from IBM Research to IBM Business Units, and 2) Improve our ability maximize business impact when we do so.
problemStatement: IBM Research develops many innovative technologies but faces significant challenges in bringing them to IBM Business Impact.  The traditional approach of transferring through hardware, software and cloud-based XaaS offerings is proving challenging due to the realities of business environment with shrinking development expenses, and the channels through services has a spotty record. We need to explore whether there are other approaches of converting research technical innovation to IBM business impact, which would be more effective in the current business environment.
outcome: This IBM Research KnowledgeBridge Challenge will explore best practices for transferring innovations to IBM Business Unit processes (such as Offering Management) that are in place to realize business value and impact. Our expected outcome is a set of proposals for alternative approaches for transferring research technical innovations to IBM business impact.  This will include new ideas that can be followed in the future, as well as modifications from existing approaches that improve the rate of research technology conversion to IBM revenue.
finalOutcome:
We confirmed there are real challenges involved in the transfer of technology out of IBM Research.  We found three types of challenges: 1) Impedance Mismatch, 2) People Related, and 3) Environmental.  These challenges are barriers to IBM competing effectively in the marketplace, causing us to be late to market with important innovations.   Our study documented the implications to IBM if we did nothing to overcome these challenges.

The three main recommendations we propose are those that can help us accelerate changes in our culture, processes, and teamwork.   
1.	Innovate in a Standalone Hybrid Team.  For those IBM Research Assets that have the potential to be highly transformational, we recommend that IBM Research experiment with a “Hybrid-Organization” approach for potentially highly transformational research assets. 
2.	Strengthen the GBS / Research Innovation Management Partnership.  For disruptive innovations, we recommend IBM Research explore using the GBS-Research partnership to mature research assets and utilize market demands to drive resources and productization.
3.	Innovate with the OM Team.  For incremental innovations, we recommend IBM Research engage with the OM team to identify opportunities to increased collaboration, while eliminating barriers and improving innovation agility.
closeValue: The final deliverable for this initiative provides three main recommendations that IBM Research can take to accelerate changes the way we transfer innovations and assets from IBM Research in order to maximize the business value  impact to IBM
publicationDescription:
Dinesh Verma challenged the Academy of Technology to explore this important issue of how we can get better at Transferring IBM Research Technology Innovations to IBM Business Impact.  Over 80 IBM professionals volunteered and participated in this initiative.  These people helped us during brainstorming and crowdsourcing events as well as reviewing detailed boxnotes and providing their feedback.  Twelve IBMers stepped up and volunteered to lead the four Sprints we conducted.  

Jia Chen, Pei-Yun Sabrina Hsueh, Michael Rowe and Bill Chamberlin led Sprint 4.  This team analyzed all the Sprint 1, 2 and 3 outcomes, performed additional research and interviews, developed our final recommendations, prepared the final report deliverables and presented the findings on numerous executive calls.

This paper reports on the activities and findings of the Academy of Technology initiative team.   It describes the problem statement, the initiative approach, and the findings of all the work performed.   Included is a list of implications and recommendations for executive consideration.
ratingComments: Very happy with the breadth of the study done, and the concrete, actionable recommendations that came out of it.

title: IoT for Expert Beginners
executiveChampionReason: Stefano Rebattoni is the leader for Industry 4.0 initiatives in Italy.  He's willing to demonstrate to our customers the power of  IoT and Hybrid Cloud to solve real world problems through prototyping.
description: IoT for Expert Beginners
problemStatement: While there is a lot of content that is possible to find within IBM intranet and internet, it is not easy to find comprehensive technical material about the Internet of Things. Also,  the available content is usually redundant or  high-level. The objective of the study of TEC (Technical Experts Council) Italy is to create a technical asset that can be used by technical experts (IT Architect, IT Specialist and IT Consultant) in order to acquire a medium level technical overview of the IoT (Internet of Things) domain. The title of the study includes the word “beginners” because the output document is mainly oriented to technical experts who might not necessarily be "experts" in the IoT domain.
outcome: The first part of the study will be more academic: it will describe the main concepts, clarifying some misused words. It will also introduce and compare the most used reference architecture developed both within IBM or in the market. The second part of the study will be more pragmatic, illustrating some customer cases where the IoT has already been applied. The third part of the study will  be developed in collaboration with the IBM Rome FabLab, that is an incubator inside the software laboratory of Rome. It will illustrate some prototypes on the IoT and Industry 4.0 domain, leveraging the reference architecture introduced in the first part.
finalOutcome:
The study touches several business domains and use cases around IoT: from IoT used for smart cities to use cases for the Industry 4.0.
It touches also frontier discussion like the impact of blockchain on IoT domain as well as the impact of the 5G or Edge computing.
The main impact is on the IBM technical community: while there are a lot of information on the IBM intranet as well as on the Internet, it is not easy to find comprehensive technical material: the content is usually redundant and very high-level (or at marketing level) and it is not possible for a technical professional to understand the underline concepts.
The study outcome is a technical asset that can be used from technical experts (e.g. IT Architect, Specialist and Consultant) in order to have a medium level technical overview of the IoT domain. The title of the study includes the word “beginners” because this document is mainly oriented to technical experts that are not experts on the IoT domain. 
Finally, it also shows the capabilities of the IBM Rome FabLab to develop prototypes; here it is also possible to physically see all the prototypes.
closeValue: Make buzzwords around IoT solid concepts for the technical community in order to use them to extract business value.
ratingComments: Factual and cohomprensive - great piece of work!

title: Data Driven Performance Platform
executiveChampionReason: Amy is the Spectrum Scale Program Director.  Scale is the initial use case to work on the Data Driven Performance  platform.
description: To exploit data for improving the quality of IBM products by using descriptive, predictive and cognitive analytics during testing processes
problemStatement: A significant amount of data from GPFS performance evaluation is being produced. This creates significant challenges on how we handle and use the such data to generate insights about the quality of GPFS and the performance evaluation process itself. Current reports are time consuming, difficult to find, and complex to process in order to produce further analyses. It is necessary to build a platform to collect and concentrate this data and make it available to processing and analytic engines. It can support a data driven decision making and better performance data utilization across all the different involved teams.
outcome:
Estimated 30% time reduction in Spectrum Scale Real Fast performance tests by automating data processing & storage.
Easier for all scrums to review and compare performance results. 
Reduced human errors in data handling.
Ability analyze performance historic results.
Ability to blend a correlate data from different sources for a deeper analysis.
finalOutcome: Understand the performance of IBM products, such as GPFS, is fundamental to provide the expected service level to our customers and get competitive advantage over similar products. The objective of this project is to develop a Data Driven platform to collect, store, analyze and visualize performance data produced during testing phases. In this first approach, the project covers the functionally required to centralize, analyze and visualize the GPFS Core Regression Evaluation which is critical to ensure the quality of such product. Current implemented modules, allow to transform the data coming from different benchmarks, structure the data in a centralized repository, and display the results over interactive interfaces. Beyond the current reports and interfaces for GPFS Core Regression, this project enables a mechanism that could be used to exploit performance data in different ways including cause-effect analysis, development of predictive models and cognitive applications. This project addresses the lack of mechanisms to exploit performance data from IBM products in an efficient way. The particular focus is on analyzing and exploiting performance data coming from Spectrum Scale - Core GPFS evaluation phases.  https://ibm.box.com/s/zkqwklb0x31j0zj1jhhlm3znotzofwwc
closeValue: It enables a platform to consolidate GPFS performance data and exploit it in an efficient way.
ratingComments: The team working on this did a super job -- in their spare time, not impacting roadmap deliverables -- on this Data Driven Performance work.  This will help improve how we do performance engineering and analysis for Spectrum Scale.  This was a great collaboration across geos as well, which sets a wonderful example within the Storage Team.

title: Resilient AI via Adaptive Swarm Intelligence (ASI)
executiveChampionReason: We have been interacting with Dario Gil and the Research Frontiers Institute in the context of this initiative; and Hieke is the Executive Director of RFI
description: This research initiative is exploring a next generation AI paradigm that is capable of continuous in-field learning and is resilient to in-field data that deviates significantly from training dataset in the factory. We explore ASI from algorithms down to system architectural support.
problemStatement: Machine Learning/Deep Learning (ML/DL) systems that form the core foundation of today's AI systems are quite fragile when it comes to sudden changes in in-field data patterns that deviate significantly from datasets used during in-factory training. How to create reliable inference engines (classifiers) that do not break in the field, but can keep learning continuously from in-field date - is a key problem in AI today. We have started a Research Initiative to pursue solutions to this problem. Adaptive Swarm Intelligence, a bio-inspired paradigm promises to be a viable solution approach - but it requires innovations spanning algorithms down through system architecture, microarchitecture and circuits. This is the target problem domain.
outcome: The expected outcome is a comprehensive team report, with initial data obtained from a simulator (swarm-sim) that will be presented to our Executive Champion, and this will (hopefully) form the core of a new offering under RFI (Research Frontiers Institute). Through the auspices of RFI, we will attract external (commercial) investment to co-develop elements of the ASI technology that are well-aligned with IBM's strategic business initiatives in domains like cyber-security, autonomous vehicular technology, cloud-backed cognitive IOT (spanning many application sub-domains), etc.
finalOutcome: Dr. Heike Riel was very pleased with the report. She has given the team detailed instructions about follow-on steps, and how to make the business value proposition more concrete; how to follow this up with a deeper dive study and incorporate the value through the simulation-based study that we are pursuing. She also encouraged us to increase the span and reach of our IP portfolio in this area; and to work with the appropriate business development partner to explore the commercialization opportunities. In particular, she asked us to explore the possibility of presenting this line of work to BMW and other automobile companies. She offered help to arrange such meetings/discussions with BMW in particular.
closeValue: The initiative has identified Adaptive Swarm Intelligence (ASI) as a promising new AI paradigm that could potentially serve as a differentiating element of IBM's strategic business interests in building next generation resilient AI systems.
ratingComments: I am very pleased to confirm that you and August and team did an excellent job and the report is High Satisfaction.

title: Supra-governmental use case for Blockchain
executiveChampionReason: IBM Fellow and a VP for Blockchain Technology
description: The aim of the study is to document the best use cases for supra governmental use of blockchain
problemStatement: In today's world the collaboration among different governments has become a necessity, let's just think in the area of crime prevention, fraud detection, pollution reduction, tax verification, etc. There is a lot of exchange needed in many of these potential use cases, and when translated into a traditional IT this means there is either the need of a master dataset that consolidates the truth or governments can exchange data blindly. Fact is that governments are resistant in trusting another government or third party to manage that master dataset, and a change in the governments participating into the use case requires changes in the setup. Blockchain enables collaboration among multiple peers; where each peer in the network has a full view on the dataset, and transactions can be attached to additions to the dataset. As each peer in the network has the full data, there is no dependency towards someone else. Also additional peers cloud join the network, contribute to the network and work with the dataset.
outcome:
The aim of the study is to document the best use cases for supra governmental use of blockchain.
For each use case this includes:
(1) a high level description of the use case,
(2) the targeted governmental departments (tax, homeland security, ....),
(3) sample scenario,
(4) the benefits that can be achieved.
finalOutcome: This study focuses on the use of blockchain in business networks where government plays an important role. As a result, the study explains (1) the typical business network, (2) the relevant aspects of blockchain, (3) value of blockchain for government and the business network, (4) clusters of cases by characteristics, and (5) 21 cases of blockchain with a government involvement. The comprehensive description is a great point of departure for engagements with government clients.
closeValue: Comprehensive study on the use of blockchain in a government environment.
publicationDescription: The objective of this AoT study is to provide better insight into how blockchain can address business challenges with government scenarios. This study seeks to provide a deeper level of detail than other existing material, to enable IBMers to start their customer conversations with a greater level of understanding.
ratingComments: “Your report was twice as useful as our competitor's professionally produced one” -- Jerry Cuomo, IBM Fellow, VP Blockchain Technology.

title: Holistic management of IRROPS (disruptions)
problemStatement:
According to IATA, IRROPS cost airlines an average 4% of their gross revenue.
Most solutions in the market place are rather tactical & focused on human assistance (e.g. call center, customer service, airport staff) forcing passengers (pax) to queue.
My Solution Framework covers pax, crew, assets (aircraft, gates, maintenance) & bag mgt. Solutions address:
* Execution: innovative on the spot resolution by enabling pax to help themselves in SELF SERVICE mode after being personally informed. We are bidding this to a European airline, using CTS asset, gradually adding self-service functionality like flight re-accommodation/changes, web check-in, ancillary, bag drop...
* Anticipation: leveraging predictive analytics, e.g. precision forecasts from The Weather Company, delay propagation prediction and analysis of history (e.g. early symptoms of upcoming disruption, most effective actions taken). 
* IRROPS Control Center (ICC) to manage IRROPS in real-time and -better- leverage predictive analytics to anticipate & better prepare (e.g. dynamic rebooking like done by American Airlines).
* ICC could also benefit from Watson Explorer based knowledge recovery from experts & unstructured data sources like logs/documents/etc.
* ICC could also cover crew (e.g. crew pairing/crew scheduling), asset & bag management (e.g. accelerate bag transfer).
outcome:
Main ones: 
* Through self-service, address passenger expectations of self-service, helping improving customer satisfaction & loyalty
* Reducing workload on staff (call center, social media teams, customer service or airport staff) and reducing costs. I developed a business case illustrating this.
* Extends to additional use cases and IRROPS situations like delays, diversions & return to gate, building on the CTS platform.
* predicability helps with OTP (on time performance)

This leverages several IBM assets, solutions & services, to be built on CTS as the platform for self-service. 

While initially focused at airlines, such solutions are equally applicable to rail, airports & tour operators with some adaptations.

Note - A blog is under preparation and an initial version of the Point of View available.

title: Standard vs Custom in Automation
executiveChampionReason: works closely with team, expertise in subject
description: An examination of the best balance between the cost of customization against the savings of standardized response in error remediation. This is tied as a "sub-initiaitve" to the storage component of the AoT Systems Cote Team initiaitive.
problemStatement: Where is the balance?  When deciding to create automation to solve problems, what is the best way to account for individualism vs. standardization?  We particularly observe this problem in the domain of resiliency.  There are many “it depends” considerations for remediating backup failure –criticality of the data, last known recovery point, time of day, resource availability, service level agreement (SLA), industry and account specific policies –to name just a few! Our many customers each want a different response to their data protection position.
outcome: We will produce a white paper discussing the cost/benefit relationship of automation strategies offered by IBM so that business owners and account teams can make informed decisions for their automation journey.  This white paper will explain the various contributing factors to a decision on remediating error conditions and will consider how to find the best balance between the cost of customization against the savings of standardized response.  It will describe some of the current IBM offerings in the automation space with a view toward flexible and cost-effective customization options. Outcome will present a suite of products and sample use cases to show how the problem of managing varying client requirements can be integrated into a robust automation program.
finalOutcome: This white paper explains the various contributing factors to a decision on remediating error conditions and considers how to find the best balance between the cost and perceived benefits of customization against the savings of a standardized approach.  It  describes some of the current IBM offerings in the automation space with a view toward flexible and cost-effective customizable options.
closeValue: Allows business managers to understand and make better choices
publicationDescription: White paper that describes the considerations and impact of choosing automation for standard and custom environments

title: Cognitive Learning Platform
executiveChampionReason: VP ISL who sees Education as a big Growth market in ISA
description: Create a cognitive learning platform that is available to schools, universities and colleges to support their learning activities.
problemStatement:
Education is on the brink of dramatic transformations due to innovations in social, mobile, cloud and analytic technologies that cannot be ignored. Educators across are increasingly challenged to prioritize classroom time and push every single student to reach mastery. 
Tutoring and after school initiatives, once considered supplementary education, have now almost become a parallel school system as most schools are not able to customize instruction in order to ensure that very few students are left behind (source: https://yourstory.com/2016/01/future-school-education/)
1. Results in poor learning outcomes
2. Results in economic wastage due to the high investment costs (school + after school tutoring)
3. Time spent towards mastering a curriculum is higher than anticipated (school time = anticipated time)
4. Eats into a student’s extra-curricular and special interests time: Monotony leads to slower turn around on subject/ curriculum mastery
outcome:
A classroom learning platform (based on open source) that enables schools to deliver a focused curriculum customized for each student based on their individual subject/ curriculum mastery.
The impact is zero dependency on after-school tutoring. Goal: Ensure the student learns completely through classroom methods only.
finalOutcome: An initial prototype for demonstrating the impact of non-academic factors on the academic performance of K-12 students.
closeValue: Fixing non-academic factors can have a significant impact on improving academic performance of K-12 students.
ratingComments: The team needs to include outside in experiences i.e. how the users interact with the solution and ways to capture personalisation improvements.

description: The forecast of the air pollution in the Megalopolis of Mexico, is calculated currently by using a static model that allows to forecast 1 day ahead the levels of the air pollution. problemStatement:
The authorities of the Megalopolis of Mexico, are currently using a static model that allows to forecast 1 day ahead the levels of the air pollution. This forecast does not provide enough time to the decision makers to plan and execute the measures to decrease in an effective way the high levels or air pollution affecting to more than 20 million of inhabitants. 

The China Research Lab has developed a tool for air pollution episodes based on Cognitive and Analytics making use of all the Watson infrastructure. 
The challenge to implement this Cognitive solution is to tailor Green Horizon to the chemistry of the Magalopolis and also to tune the different meteorological and air pollution models that Green Horizon uses as a part of the machine learning process and then make a comparison with the current forecast system that belongs to the environmental authorities of Mexico City. It is expected that Green Horizon will improve in a 30% the precision of the current forecast system. 
Other challenge is the implementation of this solution in a SaaS environment and demonstrate that the ROI for the Government Industry is one of the key factors of this kind of solutions.
outcome:
It is expected that after a pilot of 8 months, Green Horizon will be implemented as a forecast of air pollution at national level. It is also expected that with the implementation of Green Horizon in the Megalopolis and in the rest of the country, will be a key factor to approach the all market in LatinAmerica. 

The business revenue of the Pilot is 450, 000 US Dollars.

title: Identify & Assess Healthcare Logistics Solution Portfolio for Resource-Constrained Geographies like Sub-Saharan Africa
executiveChampionReason: Baba has been sponsor of this project from its inception in South Africa and was instrumental in concluding a partnership agreement with the World Bank which led to a solution pilot in Zambia as the enhanced Zambia Inventory Control System (eZICS: https://www.facebook.com/MedicalStoresLimited/posts/982974698455289). He continues to support the project from his new base in Morocco by sharing any opportunities unearthed with customers in the North West Africa region.
description: The goal is to identify and assess suitability of IBM and third-party solutions to address the unique challenges of managing healthcare logistics systems in resource-constrained environments
problemStatement: Millions of lives can be saved and untold suffering prevented in Africa, simply by increasing access to basic essential medicines. A barrier to achieving access is that most parts of Africa are resource-constrained environments, and this poses unique healthcare logistics challenges which existing solutions have failed to adequately address. There is a need to understand what IBM solutions are available and whether they are a better fit for the purpose of resolving these constraints.
outcome: This initiative will identify a portfolio of solutions for these well researched and documented challenges, for inclusion in the next release of an IBM business partner solution which is currentlybeing piloted in the region and is slated for country-wide deployment. The expected outcome is a 'fit-for-purpose' solution that decisively addresses seemingly intractable challenges, and thereby increase access to life-saving essential drugs.
finalOutcome: The main findings are that the levels of supply chain status visibility can have a significant impact on drug accessibility, and that the design of logistics management information systems can drive logistics performance improvements by enabling end-to-end visibility, notwithstanding the often-intractable challenges associated with resource constrained environments. The output is a structured description of the core challenges, and an outline of specific technology and process improvements and innovations that can be deployed to counter each challenge.
closeValue: It contributes to a deeper understanding of healthcare supply chain challenges in Sub-Saharan Africa and the pivotal role that basic technology can play in resolving those challenges.
publicationDescription: A reliable healthcare supply chain which enables and integrates various functional components to assure accessibility of essential drugs. This article explores the multiplicity of challenges that prevent access in the resource constrained environments (RCEs) that pervade most of Sub-Saharan Africa (SSA), with the intent to analyse the essential nature of these challenges, and to explore interventions can play a role in providing resolutions.
ratingComments: Very strategic project and impacting human lives in Africa positively

title: Platform for inter-departmental coordination in public sector
executiveChampionReason: Executive Champion drives technical sales enablement in U.S.
description: Capabilities for inter-departmental coordination of care delivery
problemStatement: In public sector, information on clients and citizens are often held captive in departmental or program silos. Mainly this is because agencies don't know how to share information within the restraints of the agency's own security and privacy policy, let along share it with other agencies. Policies are typically derived from public standards that are open to interpretation, in North America for instance HIPAA, NIST and CFR 42. There is a growing recognition that many problems in social and health services only can be solved through cross-departmental approaches and that public agencies must collaborate and coordinate their efforts and share data on their clients while respecting existing security and privacy policies.
outcome: IBM is in the process of building a platform for data sharing, cross-departmental coordination and rules based alerts at one of the largest counties and health and human service agencies in the United States. The expected outcome of the AoT activity is to harvest a reusable set of assets and a reference architecture for an IBM Connect 360 platform that can be implemented with an Agile, incremental method in public agencies that wants to overcome their data sharing challenges and establish better coordinated care outcomes for their clients. We believe the approach - harvesting assets and a general platform for care coordination that can be scaled up or down depending on the Features required by an individual public organization - will allow us to propose a general and reusable sales and solution accelerator that will equip GBS and S&D teams and technical sellers with an informed, detailed and differentiated response to a prevalent and growing challenge within public sector.
finalOutcome: The report and proposed solution address a core challenges in public sector, particular in North America: how to regulate which data can be exchanged and shared by case and social workers in public departments, subject to various applicable regulations and security controls. It describes a pattern-based framework for delivering collaboration platforms that respect and adhere public regulations and allow governments to deliver true citizen-centric services.
closeValue: Awards IBM the ability to deliver true cross-disciplinary and citizen-centric services while adhering to applicable regulatory controls
publicationDescription: The reports describes the rationale for and architecture behind IBM Connect360, an IBM solution and framework that enables public sector departments and agencies to share data and engage in cross-disciplinary collaboration. The report lays out the challenges that characterize public sector organizations and seven essential, architectural patterns for inter-departmental collaboration.

executiveChampionReason: Fully  concerned  with  this initiative  outcomes because  the  Technical  Leadership  team she  manages  asked   for  a cloud  security  guide lines  for   for  executives  and  sellers.
description: We  are  geerating  a PoV  document for  sellers  and  managers  to use  the  cloud security  challenge  on  an  opportunity
problemStatement:
The on-demand cloud computing model is putting new demand on security because  nature of how businesses use information technology is being transformed by cloud computing model.  Customers need that information security leaders are engaged at this early stage to help assure that the rapid adoption of cloud computing builds in information security best practices without impeding the business.   This  is  a huge  challenge in  our  customers  but  is  also a  differentiator of  IBM  cloud offerings.
                                        Security  problem  is  on  every  cloud component:  development  (DevOps),  containers,  perimeter  cybersecurity,  edge  computing issues,  and  IBM  is  able  to  face  all  those  issues...but  we  need  a consistent  and integrated  view  of  those  capabilities.
outcome: A PoV document  to  be used by  sellers  in  order  to  differentiate  IBM  cloud  offering  with  a seamless security  architecture  for  cloud/edge computing security.

IBM Cloud should offer security capabilities that customer can leverage to adopt Cloud with confidence, and provide integrated offerings, solutions and managed services from IBM Cloud, along with IBM security and partners. problemStatement:
The problem statement is to increase awareness and active participation in the "Call For Code" global hackathon in Romania.
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                Call for Code® is a five-year global program, started in 2018. The inaugural focus was on natural disaster preparedness and recovery. The goal in 2019 is to once again to unite the world's developers and data scientists to unleash the power of cloud, AI, blockchain and IoT technologies, creating sustainable and scalable open source technologies to help save lives. The emphasis in 2019 is on the health and well-being of individuals and communities threatened by natural disasters.
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                Created by philanthropic producer David Clark Cause, IBM is the Founding Partner of Call for Code. The Linux Foundation is a partner and the charitable partners include United Nations Human Rights and the American Red Cross.  As Founding Partner, IBM is investing $30 million USD over five years to help build a better future, save human lives and utilize the full potential of developers to help people, their communities and society.
outcome:
Delivery a series of "Call for code" day events including with client enterprise developers to raise awareness, ensure team formation and ideation.

closeValue: Increased awareness on "Call for Code" global initiative in Romania including in mass media and among established non IBM software developer communities.
ratingComments: I would like to congratulate the entire team for the impact of the Romanian "Call for Code" federated event, setting the tone for more hackatons/ workshops/ meetups with local communities of developers incl Red Hat developers. Well done team and thank you!
