title: IBM Mexico synergy with IBM Peru : First Peruvian patent
executiveChampionReason:
Eugenio has always been supporting initiatives related to patents generation in Guadalajara. Thanks to him, we have been able to do several events in which a lot of IBMers in Guadalajara have been able to submit their first patent eventually file it.

description: IBM Mexico in Guadalajara will be helping and collaborating with IBM Peru in order to help them prepare and submit a set of disclosures with the objective of getting at least one of them accepted for a search and eventually to become the first patent of IBM Peru.
problemStatement: IBM Perú has zero patents granted and while several IBMers have shown interest in improving this situation, the lack of a mentor with experience in the patents process has stopped them from achieving this objective.
outcome:
This initiative is comprised of several stages and each stage has specific goals.
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                - During the first stage, a massive informative session will be held to generate interest among IBMers in Peru.
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                - During the second stage, invention circles will be formed and mentoring sessions will be scheduled with people from Guadalajara to help them develop their ideas.
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                - During the third stage, disclosures will be written and mentoring will be provided in order to be prepared for the phone call to defend the idea.
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                - During the fourth and last stage, all the disclosures that were prepared during the last stages will be submitted to anaqua.

finalOutcome:

description: Organising IBM Ireland employees to mentor students from Trinity College Dublin for their software engineering group projects
problemStatement: There are 3 problems involved. Firstly, for the educational institutions and students, there is a disconnection between industry and third-level education. At the same time, for the IT industry, there is a shortage of skilled labours. IBM has to competes with other IT companies to attract new talents into its workforce, especially in Ireland, where there is a high percentage of both IT companies and IT professionals. Lastly, there is a fierce competition among different cloud providers, and software engineers are becoming increasingly influential in deciding what service their companies will adopt. IBM need to be able to better tap into the software engineers community to let them familiarise themselves with our products and build a relation with us.
outcome: By providing IBM mentorships to software engineering students working on group projects from a leading third-level educational institutes, we are able to bridge the gap between industry and third-level education, helping the students to better equip themselves for entering the workforce. It will also give them a feel of how it is to work in IBM, what it means to be an IBMer, and be more aware of the different opportunities we have in IBM Ireland. All the projects chosen for the mentoring come from IBM Ireland's many submissions for the Call For Code initiative, and rely on IBM services heavily, thus giving these future engineers a chance to explore IBM's many cloud services under our guidance early on.
finalOutcome: During this initiative, 20 students split into 3 groups from the computer science department of Trinity College Dublin were mentored by 4 technical staff member from IBM Ireland, working on 3 projects proposed from the Ireland chapter of IBM’s Call of Code initiative. The initiative better prepared these future aspiring engineers to enter the IT industry in the future and give them a positive outlook of IBM. The feedback we received from the students were very positive. It also exposed them to the IBM Cloud platform and made them aware of the various services available there.
closeValue: Strengthening IBM's relation with future aspiring engineers and the academic world.
ratingComments: This was a great initiative in terms of engaging students in TCD with IBM technologies especially in the AI area. It raised IBM's profile in the University and helped build engagement with the four students directly involved.

title: State of California Medicaid Management Information Systems Security
executiveChampionReason: MD of Integrated Account
description: Analyze and understand the requirements of the state's vision of enterprise security solution - An enterprise security model needs to reconcile these added challenges introduced by modular CA-MMIS and integration between modules and legacy CA-MMIS - Based on the requirements, design a high level solution for an adaptive, scalable, robust, easy to maintain, reliable enterprise security architecture, considering various aspects of security - modularity of the system, authentication, authorization, monitoring, auditing, prevention, response, cybersecurity best practices.
problemStatement: As the CA-MMIS program is facing a modernization and modularity process, that will dissolve the State's Medicaid Management Information Systems into multiple modules, based on COTS, SaaS or fee-for-service process outsource, a new end to end security model is needed. Enterprise security models have changed from being based on firm perimeter defenses to being based on an immune system that is able to identify, encapsulate and mitigate/erase security breaches. As Medicaid enterprises move to a state of heightened modularity, the number of threat surfaces increase and the modules may have more cracks in between them. In addition, different module providers may have different interpretations of what HIPAA means.
outcome:
Analyze and understand the requirements of the state's vision of enterprise security solution
- An enterprise security model needs to reconcile these added challenges introduced by modular CA-MMIS and integration between modules and legacy CA-MMIS
- Based on the requirements, design a high level solution for an adaptive, scalable, robust, easy to maintain, reliable enterprise security architecture, considering various aspects of security - modularity of the system, authentication, authorization, monitoring, auditing, prevention, response, cybersecurity best practices, etc.

At the end of this exercise, produce the following:
- "What" and "How" of the authentication and security components of the enterprise security solution
- Rationale for why this solution will address a more modernized and modular MMIS, from an end to end perspective
finalOutcome: Security recommendations will be used with client.  Pending sales.
closeValue: State of the art security recommendations and futures will be used for this client and can be tailored for others.

title: Resilient timekeeping for services and operations
executiveChampionReason: Background in security and services, particularly in the Federal Sector where critical infrastructure resilience is a focus.
description: The importance of resilient timekeeping to IBM and IBM's customers.
problemStatement: What is IBM's exposure to a GPS (essentially, precision timekeeping) outage?  If there's a server farm in an area where regional actors are jamming/spoofing GPS, what impact would it have on IBM's customers and IBM itself?  If the local grid goes offline because of a solar event IBM has generators to keep key systems operating.  However, if the visible GPS array is offline what about precision time?  Sync'ing with unaffected IBM sites might be a solution as long as connectivity remains intact, but if the outage is severe there may be little or no connectivity outside the affected area. Is precision timekeeping important to IBM and its customers? If IBM has a contingency plan in place, does it address the the broad availability of jamming and spoofing tools as well as larger events? If no plan exists, this initiative will identify the key issues and provide recommendations for implementing an effective worldwide policy.
outcome: A better understanding of the importance of resilient timekeeping to IBM and its customers, with recommendations for new or updated policies to support that importance.  A first draft will be delivered in November for presentation to the Sponsor (John Kelly) in darly December, with the expectation of the work continuing into 1Q2018.

title: Zero-Cost Accessibility Enablement Through AI
executiveChampionReason: Our project primary revolves around brining accessibility to every webpage and application with the minimal man-hours of work from development. Jeoff Wilks has worked to create accessible websites in his roles. His insights in actual implementation of accessibility will be an asset for us when we are setting achievable goals for this project.
description: We are proposing a new way to build accessible products. Today making accessible websites and applications takes explicit planning and budgeting man-hours. This inherently causes many products and websites to not be accessible. Our objective is to have developers building accessible products without even knowing it.
problemStatement:
If we are not designing and developing solutions for everyone, we are leaving behind over 1 billion people. The problem is simple, how do we create an inclusive and stimulating environment on webpages and applications that everyone can enjoy. While solving problems such as color contrast, captioning, text summarization, page region segmentation, compliance certification, and many others. At the same time adding accessibility and removing it from the product cost. 

At a development level we hope to find ways to lower or completely remove the extra effort it takes to make applications and webpages accessible. For example solving accessibility on the front end UI by modifying DOM elements. Or instead solving things at a library level developers are able to pick pre-made accessible widgets. We hope to hear what solutions you come up with!
outcome:
The core outcome we are striving for is to make implementing accessible compliant websites so straightforward that products can be made with zero extra developer effort to make a project accessible. 

As part of this initiative we are going to be looking closely at how IBM can maintain its role as an industry trailblazer in Accessibility. We will investigate the value of open sourcing this project. Partnering with other businesses in this space to become a larger force for good. Using social avenues to get external contributors to this project. Patenting and submitting papers on novel approaches to Accessibility. Discussing making accessibility into a service that IBM can provide to others. These are just a few of the business cases that will be investigated. During the initial phases of the project we expect to use insights from participants to narrow down outcomes and business value for IBM.

Deliverables:
1) Document(s) containing:
1.1) Lessons learned about other BUs accessibility challenges
1.2) Business cases for open vs closed source accessibility
2) A architecture diagram for a system moves toward zero-cost accessibility 
3) A prototype system building a subset of the architecture diagram
4) Patents and papers around novel ideas
finalOutcome:
Most sites and applications today are missing the features that allow PwD to interface with them. With 15% of the world population having some sort of disability, we are leaving over 1 billion people behind. That number increases significantly when you include those with age-related functional limitations.

Ironically many mainstream technologies, including some AI, were developed as assistive technology for people with disabilities, but improve overall usability, especially in limiting situations. For example, providing sufficient contrast for those with vision issues benefits people using the web on a mobile device in bright sunlight or in a dark room. Creating enabled tools creates tools for everyone.

Business impact for this type of work is wide and varied, because making any one of IBM's products accessible can add many additional users as well as insulate IBM from liability. When we look at statistics for bug fixes we see the cost of fixing a bug at dev time to be negligible at around $45 but the same bug in production can cost almost $27,000. By automating accessibility earlier in the product life cycle we are able to have greater impacts on IBM's offerings and help the most numbers of users.
closeValue: Understanding accessibility challenges faced by developers, designers, and end users and applying those insights to inform future innovation in accessibility.

title: AoT Study to Define Use Case Adoption for Clients on SAP Cloud Platform (private) on IBM Cloud
executiveChampionReason:
Selected Distinguished Engineers from GBS EA who have also been collaborating with DE/CTOs of IBM Cloud for SAP (Brian Snitzer, Ann Corrao) to enhance client adoption. Mike from NA and Mark Dudgeon who is the Global EA CTO for SAP, are uniquely positioned to take the outcome of this initiatives to the clients and to IBM business partners. The teams are working together to bring the best of SAP and IBM cloud platforms to our clients. 
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                These Distinguished Engineers across GBS & IBM Cloud are working multiple workstreams around collaboration.  This is one of the workstreams.
description: Study to create an overview, roadmap, use cases, and procedures for setting up 3 use cases in IBM Cloud for SAP Using SAP Cloud Platform (Private).
problemStatement: SAP Cloud Platform SCP (Public) has limited adoption among the SAP customer base.  The primary reasons include use of the platform capabilities for hybrid cloud has challenges around security, latency, and functionality.  Many SAP clients have a limited hybrid cloud footprint and are just starting to explore the capabilities to include IoT, AI, machine learning, blockchain, etc to bring business innovation.  Also, the SAP offering has gaps from a cloud platform perspective.  Therefore, SAP decided to provide a "private" option with IBM and other vendors.  As SAP clients adopt SCP as innovation platform, IBM should leverage the opportunities to host our clients in our cloud and bring the best of IBM cloud and SAP cloud to our clients. This study will help to create that synergy between IBM Cloud offerings and our SAP expertise from GBS so that we can have an impactful offering for our clients. The outcome of this initiative will result in a redbook, a video log and a potentially a presentation in some major events like SAP TechEd and also IBM webinars.
outcome: The SAP Cloud Platform (Private) roadmap has limited functionality as of the availability date in November 2018 in the IBM cloud.  The technical community (GBS & Cloud & across locations) are best placed to assist our GBS & CLoud Business leaders with use cases that will resonate with our clients.  One outcome will be use cases that IBM can take back to SAP to bring in to the SCP Private offering.  Other outcomes - IBM point of view that will be presented at SAP Tech Ed in October 2018; IBM Redbook focused on SAP Cloud Platform (Private) in IBM Cloud for SAP and potentially create solution asset ideas which will help differentiate IBM from our competition, show IBM Cloud at an advantage, display IBM's thought leadership in this new and niche area. The other by-product of this initiative would be to increase involvement of technical leaders into Academy initiative, specially in North America & India.
finalOutcome: The outcome of this initiative results in a point of view and potentially a presentation at major conferences such as IBM Think, SAP SAPPHIRE and SAP TechEd.
closeValue: This study helps to create synergy between IBM Cloud offerings and our SAP expertise from GBS so that we can have an impactful SCP Private offering for our clients.
publicationDescription: SAP Cloud Platform Private (SCP Private) provides an opportunity for clients who need to adhere to more stringent rules of data privacy and regulatory compliance, to use this platform of innovation, with their own instance in an isolated infrastructure. So far, SAP has partnered with IBM as a trusted infrastructure provider in terms of delivery, provisioning and operations, to provide this service. This service opens a huge arena in terms of enabling these customers who have had no other options to build the use cases possible with the SAP Cloud Platform. This report provides details about state of readiness of the SCP Private for clients and also calls out the next steps to take for discussion with SAP so as to have a robust offering.

title: TLC-BR - TechDay Horto 2019
executiveChampionReason: Decio Miname is the CTO for LA, covering all IBM BUs and with an outstanding mindset to promote the One IBM approach. He supports the TLC-BR and wants to promove the integration and knowledge sharing among the Technical Community.
description: Day-long event for the professionals in Hortolândia site, bringing several subjects related to innovation, career and development, specially to the Technical Community at this site.
problemStatement:
As a result of a Design Thinking session done in 2018 with the technical community, it was identified an integration gap of the technical community in Hortolândia. 

Hortolândia technical team is mostly from Service Delivery Center, and usually, the team is so immersed in the daily issues that they don't find time to integrate with the broad technical community and learn new technology.

In November/2018, the TLC-BR run the first edition of TechDay Horto, which was greatly recognised as a good opportunity to address the concerns raised, and new edition of the Event with new themes and even recurring themes is needed, as a continuous way to address the integration gap for the Technical Community on this site.
outcome: The TLC-BR expects, with this new edition of TechDay Horto, to engage more professionals, and bring more opportunities to develop and know about IBM portfolio and innovation, at the same time that brings the professionals close to the TLC-BR and the opportunities generated by this team.
finalOutcome: This initiative brought to the IBM Hortolândia community, specially the technical teams (but not restricted to them) the opportunity to update their knowledge in valued themes, such as Career, ZOWE, Red Hat, Blockchain, DevOps, Security and AI, by presenting newest information and sessions on these areas. The initial purpose, which was successfully achieved, was to update the team's knowledge, while promoting the network among the participants from several areas and BUs, and continue leveraging the transformation journey and the changing mindset.. The event counted 600 individual subscriptions, in the 20 sessions, and 19 Speakers, and 85% of the participants who provided feedback returned good or very good. New themes of interest were mapped for next Editions of this initiative.
closeValue: Continuous development and sinergy, specially for the Technical Community at IBM Hortolândia site, with several BUs.
ratingComments: This was a milestone for the integration of the Brazil technical community.  This 2nd edition had approx. 6x the participation of the first one, with also great feedbacks and especially suggestions from the participants. That is key for the evolution of the initiative, as we learned from the feedbacks of the first to enhance this second one and so on. The engagement of the organization staff is a special highlight, for being a 100% voluntary effort counting on members from different areas and locations, including TLC members and non-members. There is much more we can do and this experience shows that we are on the right track.

problemStatement:

title: Multi-Level Security for Regulated Government Clouds
executiveChampionReason: Sreeram is the Global Managing Director for Public Sector Worldwide. He defines the strategy for the Industry within IBM and connects with all key markets, clients and accounts.
description: This AoT Initiative aims to formalize a Multi Level Security architecture for highly secure government cloud environments to meet regulatory requirements mandated by NATO MLS / other Cloud Acts
problemStatement: a. For mission critical applications, Governments are keento have on-premise private cloud, and will not go outside to public clouds. b. There is increasing uptake of IBM Cloud Private that addresses this need.  c. There are different operating models and some of them mandate additional security requirements to be complied with (such as NATO MLS) , if the cloud is being operated by multi agencies operations. d. The gap exists in defining an E2E Security Architecture in context of private cloud architecture, which spans , Infrastructure, Containerization Platform, In-memory security amongst others, particularly for highly secure and regulated Government Cloud.  e. We need to address this as part of all the ongoing and upcoming MoD deals in EU.
outcome: The outcome of this study will define a secure private cloud architecture and recommendation report for highly regulated government cloud using ICP.  In addition to the regulated government cloudds, this will also be usable across IBM with Multi Level Security requirements.
finalOutcome:
1. Our unique value proposition and capability across IBM and RedHat to address multi-level security (MLS) needs in highly regulated clouds is identified with specific solution capabilities . This will help us address the upcoming opportunities in this space in EU, and also qualify new opportunities in US Federal.
                                                                                2. We also identified few gaps (internal - within our portfolio) and external (in analyst reports) that need to be addressed. It will help us consolidate and strengthen our position in the market.
closeValue: It arms our technical sellers, partners and client teams, with specifics on how we can meet the MLS requirements in highly regulated clouds, and grow our market share in this space across industries.
publicationDescription:
Agencies like Defense,  Healthcare handling multi-level security (MLS) classified (e.g. Top Secret/Classified) information often have isolated physical IT resources. This study identifies a. the key requirements that an MLS system must cater to, while adopting cloud , b.specific IBM +RedHat capabilities that address the MLS needs and finally it also c. identifies gaps both internal and external , to be addressed.

ratingComments: The MLS Study and the associated value proposition is critical for many agencies within the Public Sector who have unique requirements from a Security perspective. Congratulations to Lavanya and Mark for a great study and for being proactive in identifying this need.

title: Cognitive computing for education and personal learning:
executiveChampionReason: x
description: Cognitive Education
problemStatement: The scope of this initiative is to leverage cognitive computing to help humans in education termed as cognitive teaching assistant (CTA). CTA is expected to disseminate information in multiple contexts via multiple channels depending upon the need termed as contexts. Few examples of contexts are detailed below:,•	Goal context i.e help the student towards preparing for exam ,•	Situational context: When the student is in urgent need or otherwise,•	Receptive maturity context: When the student possesses dummy, learning or matured in intelligence in the given subject area,•	Age context: When the student is a kid or adult,•	Miscellaneous context: When the student is requiring special needs for channel and context ,etc,In reality the need may be complex encompassing one or more contexts. CTA is required not only to curate and deliver content but align its behaviour closer to humans learning day by day.
outcome: This initiative by the Academy intends to define a cognitive framework , identify various gaps (process, competency, Governance, Tools)  and propose mechanisms to overcome the gaps,This will  boost up IBM's thought leadership in cognitive industry well ahead in the market by equipping in various facets.
finalOutcome:
the study makes two important contributions:
It consolidates findings from within and outside IBM on the necessity and application of cognitive computing in Education. The report can thus serve as a valuable reference for readers who wish to understand the transformation that the Education industry is going through, as well as technology thought leadership (especially from IBM) that can drive the transformation.
The study highlights skill development as an emerging area of key importance globally, explains the key areas of innovation required to address this at-scale, and how various companies, both start-ups and major IT vendors are positioning themselves to drive market value. The report reviews IBM’s efforts in this area and provides a series of actionable recommendations that can help IBM establish itself as a market leader.
closeValue: "The greatest impact realized by this initiative is to put the focus on the cognitive transformation of the Education and skill development industry, present an informed perspective on the key players and IBM's strategy and competitive differentiation, and provide actionable recommendations to help establish IBM as a market leader."
publicationDescription:
Cognitive education is one of the top ten themes chosen by the IBM Academy of Technology for year 2017-2018. A team of volunteers from different IBM business units formed a team to conduct a study on this theme, with the following objectives:
(i)	review the state of the Education industry to determine the drivers for the application. of cognitive technologies to Education and identify the key players in the market.
(ii)	understand IBM’s strategy in cognitive education and explain how the strategy is being executed.
(iii)	identify gaps in our strategy, or, emerging areas of importance to IBM.
(iv)	recommend actions to IBM management to address these emerging areas

title: Infusing Industry into the Smarter Technical Selling Academy (STSA) 2019
executiveChampionReason: Ongoing program owner, sponsor for 2019 event
description: Leverage industry experts to drive an industry focused approach and deliverables at the Smarter Technical Selling Academy 2019 Event. Identify key industry assets (microservices, data models, reference architectures, etc.) that can be leveraged to design and prototype breakthrough solutions to be used in the event of a natural disaster.   Examples: E&U:  A microservice that shows the location of downed power lines (that could be combined with traffic data to alert first responders) Distribution:  An API to identify inventory item availability in a given zip code (i.e., 40 generators available in Houston) Public: An IoT Sensor tracking service (when combined with building plans could identify where firemen are located in a burning building) Create a template for such assets that could be packaged into a catalogue that architects and developers can consult for usage and use case scenarios.  (~200 client-facing IBM architects attending a F2F enablement event in Houston, TX April 1-3,  2019)  	 ALT Sponsors:   Krishnan Ramachandran, Chandra Narayanaswami
problemStatement: Previous events have focused on building hands-on skills with our technology, leaving the attendee to "connect the dots" and adapt the solutions for their client's industry.  The agenda will include technology topics and hands-on activities with cloud, cognitive, IoT, weather & edge computing.   For the hackathon portion of the event, we'd like to provide attendees with industry "nuggets" (solutions or pieces of solutions) that could be composed with other micro-services to deliver industry solutions that could be used in the event of a natural disaster.
outcome:
Incorporate technology and industry expertise to drive breakthrough thinking of how IBM, our clients and industries can contribute solutions to make the world a better place.  The initial set of assets could be hardened and expand to become a catalogue of services available globally.
                                        https://w3-connections.ibm.com/wikis/home?lang=en-us#!/wiki/W0b61b6ee37eb_4a27_9476_8089cf05d776/page/Welcome%20to%20the%202019%20Smarter%20Technical%20Selling%20Academy
                                        https://academyweb-prod.w3ibm.mybluemix.net/initiatives/52d1eaa84eaf3f82398a77d05b1a2cc3
                                        https://w3-connections.ibm.com/wikis/home?lang=en-us#!/wiki/W0b61b6ee37eb_4a27_9476_8089cf05d776/page/Agenda
finalOutcome:
Summary: 1) Engage IBMers in architecting and designing actionable solutions across the spectrum of a disaster: Preplanning, Responding, Rebuilding. 2) Provide an opportunity to collaborate with peers while leveraging IBM tools and strategies in a collaborative hands-on environment to build a sense of community and personal network around a recognizable social issue.
Key Outcomes: 230 Attendees across 3 business groups and 5 countries - held in April in Houston. 28 Solutions developed  in 1.5 day hackathon and one named finalist for IBM Call for Code.  Interest by Office of Emergency Response in developing new offerings as SaaS for Emergency Response. Follow-on events included a derivative session at the ATEC Western Canadian POD meeting – 5 locations where the model was used to drive networking and engagement. 
Three categories of solutions created - Citizen Collaboration, Command and Control, Connecting People and Needs.
Derivative Project - 1) Crisis Bot (https://ibm.ent.box.com/file/480655587915?utm_source=trans&utm_medium=email&utm_campaign=collab%2Bauto%20accept%20use) Selected as Finalist in the IBM Call for Code. 2) Western Canadian POD meeting – Doug Kinnaird Coordinator - Simultaneous sessions in 5 Canadian Cities to replicate the working sessions from Houston.
closeValue: Selling Academies are no longer powerpoint events, but infused with industry expertise, live coding, hackathons, and prototypes, leading to derivative projects and AoT Initiatives.
ratingComments: Great job by the team.

title: PREVAIL 2019 - An #IBMAoT #WWPACoP Topical Conference addressing Performance, Availability and Security
executiveChampionReason: Leanne Varker is the executive champion of the worldwide community of practice for performance and availability and supports the topical conference
affiliateName: WW CoP for Performance and Capacity
description: The purpose of this initiative is to organise a topical conference on performance, availability and security in 2019/2020.  The conference will be open to technical professionals from IBM and from IBM's clients.  It will address topics such as Agile resilience, Embedding resilience into DEVOPS, Site Reliability Engineering for organisations that are NOT Google, Design patterns for performance and availability in Cloud and Hybrid etcetera.
problemStatement: During the AoT NFR Best Practices Exchange in the TJ Watson lab in Yorktown Heights from February 10 to 14, 2014 several panelists, speakers and members of the audience mentioned that whenever the Quality of Service related topics such as performance, availability and security comes up in conversations with our clients, the client’s CxO more often than not refers to companies such as Google, Amazon or eBAY. They want the user experience of their business services to be as "fast" and "always ON" as they perceive the services from these companies to be. And it does not help if we explain to the CxO in question that his applications are doing something completely different from what Google, Amazon or eBay do. The CxO does not want to be bothered with technical details! Her focus is on new functionality that will help drive the business and Non-Functional aspects are simply implied and expected to be excellent. In this conference we will address that challenge and provide technicql professionals with practical guidelines how to keep the non-functional aspects away from the CxO, using modern agile and DevOps compute paradigms and cloud-native technologies in combination with brownfield.
outcome:
The 2019 Prevail conference is an AoT non-functionals Topical Conference for both IBMers (early tenure as well as experienced) and for external Clients.
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                The conference will create new capability for innovation using technology. Attendees will learn about performance, availability, capacity and security, creating greater technical depth, but also gaining insights into cloud, DevOps and cognitive and their non-functional characteristics. The lectures will be recorded and published in the IBM Academy of Technology affliated Performance and Availability Community of Practice Education Series. 
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                The conference will also raise members internal and external eminence where they are able to present lectures in the sessions open to external clients and for all participants through participation in the unconference sessions. It is our objective to publish the content from the conference sessions either as a book, or Redbook to demonstrate IBM capability (and by extension the authors') to external business and technical leaders.
finalOutcome: The PREVAIL conference has provided many useful insights, best practices and guidelines how to deliver chapter 2 with resilience, performance and security in mind.
closeValue: Technical eminence, visibility of technical professionals, best practices to engineer modern IT solutions with resilience, performance and security in mind
publicationDescription: Conference proceedings will be published through Lighthouse / Box
ratingComments: I would like to thank you all for your dedication to the WWPACoP community and the leadership you provide.   It has been a year of transformation and your initiatives guided and supported the wider teams as they navigate our new more complex environment and technologies.   There were two outstanding initiatives in 2019 PREVAIL 2019 conference addressing performance, availability and security which was very well received Lecture series on Effective performance, availability and security in a DEVOPS environment Achievements:  PREVAIL conference  3 AoT showcases were delivered in advance of / as teasers for the PREVAIL conference A team of volunteers from the community with help from the Watson IoT center took responsibility for the organisation of the conference, including submission selection, invites, help with visa, recording 6 keynotes, 3 panels on 14 breakouts in the performance track, 14 breakouts in the availability track and 14 breakouts in the security track were delivered The Resilient DEVOPS community initiative was also integrated into the content Ran meetup (4 sessions) that was well attended by external technical professionals from the Munich region, sessions were recorded and have been globally shared  Chris Winter, retired IBM fellow shared his wealth of knowledge with the new generation of resilience engineers Simon Whelband, lead architect from AP Moeller Maersk, spoke about their journey to cloud and containers Another outstanding year, I thank you all.   Leanne

title: How to Write an Invention Disclosure of Project Management
executiveChampionReason: Koike-san is an executive sponsor of TEC-J, and he is also leading Technical Professions including project managers in IBM Japan.
description: Share knowledges how to write a project management relaed invention disclosure, and make a guide so that every project managaers can write an invention disclosure.
problemStatement: Project managers may prejudice that it is difficult to write a project management related invention disclosure. But we could breakthrough this prejudice. We could file two invention disclosures of project management until now, and one another invention disclosure is under search. We implemented cognitive technologies, Watson, into invented systems in all three invention disclosures. This project management patent is a quite new area, and nobody has knowledge about this.
outcome: We will share our experiments and knowledge about how to write an invention disclosure of project management. And we will develop a guide to write an invention disclosure of project manager as outcome. By referencing that guide, we expect every project managers can write an invention disclosure. We hope that we could be #1 position in this new area to differentiate project management expertise from competitors.
finalOutcome:
Project managers may be under the impression that their area is not good for patent activity. But we were able to overcome this erroneous assumption and have already filed Three invention disclosures for Project Management.
We have implemented AI and Watson based technologies for all three invention disclosures. Project management is a new area for patent activity, and very few people have the skills in this area. We believe IBM can write more invention disclosures to become the leaders in this new area and differentiate us from our competitors.
closeValue: Providing patent guidance for a specific job role - in this case project managers - should really help bring additional people to the world of invention.
publicationDescription:
With the infusion of AI into many of our daily activities and business processes, Project Managers have the opportunity to apply these technologies to address problems and develop improved processes in the Project Management domain. IBM has the opportunity to capture some of these solutions conceived and developed by project managers and their teams and turn them into Invention Disclosures as part of the Patent process.
Traditionally, project management activities are not candidates for patents. This is due to the project management domain typically develops processes to solve their problems.
Through a deliberate approach to engage project managers as they enable new capabilities using AI, the IBM Japan team was able to facilitate the idea generation through submission of invention disclosures. Using this method in one project alone, the team was able to facilitate the development and filing of Three Invention Disclosures.
This guide describes the lessons learned and techniques to allow project managers throughout IBM to write a project management patent.
ratingComments: To share this experiment and knowledge, the team developed the guide describes the lessons learned and techniques to allow project managers throughout IBM to write a project management patent.The IBM Japan team initiated and led this IBM academy initiative with support from world wide. Totally 152 members joined this initiative, 14 members from Japan and 138 members from world wide.

title: TEC-J Showcase #1
executiveChampionReason: Kuse-san is an executive sponsor of TEC-Japan
description: TEC-J Showcase is a new initiative inspired by AoT Showcase. TEC-J Showcase provides opportunities for TEC-J Working Groups to present their thoughts, best practices and innovative ideas that have been discussed in their study and researches with other TEC-J members in timely manner. It also enables TEC-J Working Groups to exchange ideas and receive various feedbacks from TEC-J members and SMEs in a broad context. In this very first TEC-J Showcase session, we discuss on secured information distribution method for iOS devices, which is initially designed for Japanese government project.
problemStatement:
Most of smartphones are purchased by individuals, mass-produced, and have been sold in various sales channels. When the service provider distributes the exclusive secret information for each user, the following 2 issues needs to be resolved: 
                                                                                                                                                                1. It is difficult to guarantee that secret information is indeed stored on the owner's smartphone.  User may store this secret information on other smartphones owned by others. In this case, there is a security problem that others can use the service on behalf of the real user, regardless of intention.
                                                                                                                                                                2. It is difficult to confirm the system requirements of smartphones where proprietary secrets are stored. User may store in a device with insufficient security functions that do not meet the system requirements. Also in this case, regardless of intention or not, there may be security problems such as information leak or spoofing by others.
                                                                                                                                                                There is a need for secured secret information distribution methods for smartphones, which can be used in secured business usecases.
outcome: Participants will be able to acquire the best-practices of secured information exchange method designed by GBS and reuse/deploy those knowledge to other mobile business projects in IBM Japan, in addition to be able to understand the basic of security topics such as key exchanges, encryption and iOS-unique restrictions/technical impediments. Mobile is one of the key business driver in Japan, so reference architecture and implementation must be required to be more competitive. By providing showcase series as a horizontal cross point of WG, it is expected that each working group is vitalized and becomes aware of the other activities to utilize their knowledge and experiences. Each WG leader can present the outcome at this showcase and publish it to AoT blog, and promote those studies to AoT initiatives that will involve much more SMEs in the world if necessary.
finalOutcome: Participants will be able to acquire the best-practices of secured information exchange method designed by GBS and reuse/deploy those knowledge to other mobile business projects in IBM Japan, in addition to be able to understand the basic of security topics such as key exchanges, encryption and iOS-unique restrictions/technical impediments. title: Predicting Recovery Time
executiveChampionReason: Works closely with team, expertise
description: Use analytics to create predictive recovery times for IBM storage clients. This is tied as a "sub-initiaitve" to the storage component of the AoT Systems Core Team initiaitive.
problemStatement: Clients today have wide variability in recovery times that is often unknown until the time recovery is needed. Customers have an assumed level of ‘comfort’ about how long a restore will take, but that is often based on incorrect assumptions of the underlying issues.  New complex issues face customers including ransomware attacks, and old complex issues include mass recovery efforts following disasters, or massive hardware failures due to power outages.
outcome: We will use analytics, gathered from e.g. our global data lake to help develop predictive backup and recovery times by Client based underlying data (e.g. large Database Files over the network take longer to restore than small text files) and weave this knowledge gained by IBM to provide the Client with predictive recovery times and data protection solutions that meets their requirements. We will also compare/contrast the underlying methods used by software vendors that affect how long recovery takes and the trade-off between speed of recovery and depth of protection. This will provide the Client with a cost/risk/reward investment strategy to leverage data/fact with risk of recovery to the business.
finalOutcome: This study provides visibility to the customer on the time required to perform a backup and restore of a select group of data and enable IBMers to consult with the customers on archiving or their recovery needs and consult regularly with IBM for updates.
closeValue: We IBM understand how we can predict recoverability to meet customers SLA and RTO requirements using analytics and machine learning methods.
publicationDescription: The purpose of this IBM Academy of Technology study is to give the IBM technical community and AoT guidance around data protection (backup and recovery) and educate our customers and ourselves, to obtain a more detailed understanding of our customer’s Service Level Agreement (SLA) and Recovery Time Objectives (RTO) requirements. This helps determine whether current predicted SLA and RTO meets customers business and contract requirements of their mission critical data and business applications. In many situations, projecting the predictive recoverability will enable IBMers to consult with the customers on archiving or their recovery needs. IBM succeeds when it supports these use cases.

title: How to win a cyber war
problemStatement: In November 2015 the British Government acknowledged the risks that cyber attack poses as part of the wider terrorism threat and stated that the UK will develop offensive cyber capability to strike back.  The nature of the threat is asymmetric and comes from individual hackers, criminal gangs and rogue states as well as jihadists.,Strong defensive capabilities are needed to counter the cyber threat, but he asserted that these are now insufficient: a capacity to attack is a form of defense.  Tackling the asymmetry between attack and defense requires deterrents to dissuade people from attacking the Governments and Critical National Infrastructure in the first place.  Deterrents will be underpinned by an ability to hit back at those who attack the nation states.  The UK (publicly) and other states (perhaps more privately) are investing in the tools and capabilities to respond in any way that they see fit to defend their nations.,Such risks are faced by many nations around the world.  IBM has a long track record on technology innovation in the field of security.  It has also established a security business unit that focuses on protecting organisations from the cyber threat.,However, we are seeing that the technologies that are being used to plan and execute serious crime, terrorism, cyber attack et al are changing.  This is placing greater demands for flexibility in how technology is employed by Governments to counter the threat.,IBM, and we believe the industry, lacks a point of view that shows that we understand the challenges that Government departments such and defense ministries now need to tackle.  We do not have an approach with tools, capabilities and practices which can be widely applied to establish and defend a safe national environment for Government, commerce and society.
outcome: This project will produce a point of view written for Government departments on handling the heightened cyber threat faced by individual nations.  It will describe how to approach dealing with the threat, how to control the threat, and how to win.  It will include a view of our capabilities underpinned by a reference architecture that can be employed by a nation’s Government departments to fight a cyber war.  A summary of the point of view will be published internally at end of 1Q and externally by end of 2Q.
legacyParticipantType: The initiative is open to those with expertise in one or more of the following areas to ensure a diverse team:n•	Security intelligencen•	Analytics on network and security data (eg netflow)n•	Analytics platforms (eg Spark, Streams, Hadoop)n•	Analysis and visualization of large data setsn•	Network analysis and graph technologiesn•	Ethical hackingn•	Security operationsn•	Smarter Cities and the Intelligence Operations Centre; command and controln•	DevOps, agile development, cloudn•	Reference architectures
legacyValue: This project will develop a point of view in a rapidly emerging area not currently being addressed.  It is an area which is an increasingly high priority for public investment because of the increasing level of threat.  This is expected to be the case for several years.,We shall harness our security and analytics pedigree to develop a point of view that will help establish IBM as a leader in this field.  It will offer thought leadership that can be used by sales teams to develop propositions for their clients and assets to aid solution design.  Solutions will make extensive use of IBM technology and services for delivery and operation.,By forming a single IBM view of how to tackle the cyber threat that nations face, IBM will be able to build intellectual capital and assets from early engagements that are reusable thereby aiding future sales, lowering delivery risk and increasing margin.

title: Framework of patterns for managing an hybrid multi-cloud estate for an enterprise
description: This initiative will define a structure or framwork of patterns that can be further elaborated for enterprise tooling that can manage defined types of applications in hybrid multi-cloud environments for an enterprise client and structure further detailed pattern alignment
problemStatement:
In the old world of traditional data centers things were easier to mange as they we generally tied to physical things in your very physical data center.
                                        Cloud has changed all that by removing visibility of the physical and enabling more dynamic deployment patterns and easier deployments in many different places.
                                        This flexibility has left many clients in an uncontrolled state where they don’t know what they have, what state it is in, or how much it is costing them. Not understanding these things can lead to operational issues, security breaches and spiraling costs.  For example, security teams don’t necessarily even know what boundaries they need to secure.
                                        The challenge they are now facing is how do they bring their hybrid multi-cloud enterprise back to the level of operations they had when it was simply in their own buildings, especially with added pressure to avoid vendor lock in.
                                        80% of applications have yet to move to cloud and even with the things that have gone to cloud already proving to be a challenge for enterprise management and this will only get harder as more and more complex applications move.
outcome:
A framework of patterns will be created for enterprise tooling interlinked for Hybrid Multi-cloud and enabling understanding what the whole enterprise is.  Hybrid multi-cloud deployment of applications require a multi tiered implementation of the tooling to support that.
                                         - Central tooling to provide enterprise view of Services to enable single dashboards for service management and Cognitive Enterprise integration
                                        - “Local” cloud or DC tooling to meet operational requirements to “onboard” each cloud to the enterprise.
                                        - Application centric tooling to manage/monitor/control different types of application (VM, Container, serverless etc) – i.e. The Route to Live
                                        Integrated offerings and physical deployment patterns should be developed to support this and standardise to optimise quality and cost of service
                                        This initial framework will enable the production of consitent consumable solution patterns and best practice that integrate to support enterprise operation.

title: Omics: The missing DNA of IBM Healthcare strategy?
executiveChampionReason: Bruce is a VP for Watson Health, Life Sciences
description: The scale of data and complexity of analytics associated with the study of the microbiome, antibiotic resistance, food safety and other areas is challenging and offers a unique potential for IBM to become a leader by applying  AI and ML techniques to large-scale omics data.
problemStatement: 'Omics' (genomics, proteomics, metagenomics) aims to understand and harness the function of biological molecules to influence health and function at the level of organisms. Recognized as the next frontier of discovery,  it has many applications in drug discovery, personalized medicine, gene editing, food safety, the microbiome and beyond, and we believe it the missing DNA of IBM's Healthcare strategy. For example, food safety and gene editing are expected to grow to  $18 billion and $6 billion industries, respectively,  by 2022, and microbiome-based patient diagnostics is expected to grow to a $900 million industry by 2025. The scale of data and complexity of omics data and analytics is challenging and offers a unique potential for IBM to become a leader by applying  AI and ML techniques to large-scale omics data. With this initiative, we expect to analyze the key areas where IBM has a unique advantage and suggest the most promising areas for investment.
outcome:
The outcome of this initiative will be to analyze the requirements, use cases and technology associated with the microbiome and make recommendations for strategic areas for IBM to invest, such as:
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                         
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                        1.    Microbiome 
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                        2.   Gene Editing
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                        3.    Drug Discovery
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                        4.    Patient Diagnostics
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                        5.    Food Safety
finalOutcome: We determined that a large market exists where IBM can strategically invest within the area of therapeutics, diagnostics, and nutraceuticals of the Microbiome. A CAGR of > 9.5% is expected through 2026 and an expected market size of $4.1B. Many startups and large companies are beginning to show interest in investing within the Microbiome with IBM's opportunity in the early stages of therapeutics and diagnostics by providing cloud services to accelerate these companies' R&D. IBM can leverage its existing portfolio of assets such as data management services, cloud, analytics, AI & ML and Research assets including OMXWare and PRROMenade to begin a transformation within the Microbiome arena. Based on this information, we have introduced different potential engagement models and summarized all findings and presented results as a set of informative slides to our Executive Champion.
closeValue: Microbiome is an emerging market and IBM should monitor this space closely and try to leverage existing assets to accelerate discovery by potential clients in order to increase their business value and time to market.
ratingComments: The team working on this was passionate about their initiative and that showed in the quality of the work they did and in the presentations and discussions.  The team was highly collaborative with me and they were very receptive to comments, suggestions and coaching especially around the business aspects of the initiative.  The team's work was well received in our review with the Watson Health executives (our VP of strategy, and my manager, the head of development for WH).  I'm looking forward to continuing to work with the team past the end of this activity.  Kudos to this team for a job well done.

title: disruptive-NEW AGE ARCHITECTURE (d-NAA)
executiveChampionReason: Srivats is the Exec Sponsor for this initiative. He has seen a strong need for such a initiative and plans to consume the output for different industries in relevant deals.
description: There is a gap between the many legacy Reference Architectures (Industry Ref Archs included) and how they should be positioned in todays Digital ecosystem. This initiative will address the need of a new Reference Architecture for the modern days of disruptive economy and eco-system which will leverage the power of emerging technologies of Cloud, Mobile, AI, Blockchain, IOT, Web, Digital, AR/VR, NoSQL DB etc.
problemStatement:
Most of the reference architecture and frameworks available today were developed at a time when above disruption intensity was not explosive. Hence legacy reference architecture and frameworks were focused on organizing the IT capabilities to help business scale. 
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                        But now, Ability to operate at hyper-scale is not enough. Ability to hyper-personalize and quickly adapt to changing market needs and respond to competitive threats is critical. Net-net, there is a huge focus on how to deal with disruptive eco-system. 
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                        Hence the need of a new Reference Architecture for this modern days of disruptive economy and eco-system.
outcome: Reference Architecture employing modern architecture patterns and technologies .
finalOutcome:
It is about how to craft an architecture which is disruptive- i.e., how it enables an enterprise to become disruptive rather than getting disrupted. It focusses on following three business concerns:
                                                                                                                        1.	Customer Experience. Usually, experience expectation bar is influenced by the likes of Facebook, Twitter, Google, Apple, Amazon. d-NAA suggests architectural patterns and relevant emerging technologies that help deliver ‘AMAZING’ experience to customers.
                                                                                                                        2.	Business Environment is disruptive. d-NAA suggests architectural patterns and technologies that help in dealing with the disruptive business environment.
                                                                                                                        3.	Technology Adoption @ exponential pace. d-NAA suggests architectural patterns that help the adoption of newer technologies.
closeValue: There are Architecture Patterns and technologies that can make an enterprise disruptive.
publicationDescription:
Most of the reference architecture and frameworks available today were developed at a time when above-mentioned disruption intensity was not explosive. Customers were not very demanding.   Hence legacy reference architecture and frameworks were focusing on organizing the IT capabilities to help the business scale.
                                                                                                                        However, now, the users are not just information consumers! They are generating the content themselves!!!  They are reviewing the product and rate the product with their remarks. They do chat and expect two-way participation in the process of sales & service. They are EXCHANGING VALUE which is far beyond mere INFORMATION EXCHANGE. 
                                                                                                                        Ability to operate at hyper-scale is not enough. Ability to hyper-personalized is the key. Ability to quickly adapt to changing market needs and respond to competitive threats is critical.  
                                                                                                                        Hence the need for a new Reference Architecture for this modern-day of disruptive economy and eco-system. 
                                                                                                                        
                                                                                                                        The proposed architecture document provides a maturity assessment framework so that the enterprise can assess their current state and then chart out the roadmap to become a Cloudified and Cognitive Enterprise. It suggests what architectural and technology shifts are going to be needed by the enterprise in its journey.

title: Making learning content into Learner Aware content using Cognitive Intelligence
executiveChampionReason: Gaurav is very enthusiasting and supportive leader, he played a pivotal role in building IBM Watson Education business in his earlier role. He is perfect executive champion for this idea.
description: The key objective is to make learning content into learner aware content using cognitive intelligence.
problemStatement:
“Students who do not get it the first time are not likely to get it the next several times you teach it the same way”
The future reality of education will be a more bite-sized and personalized experience and crafted from finest content suiting to each individual student. Most often students tend to drop out midway due to lack of interactivity with the learning content either it be a lecture video or text document. The key objective of this project is to enrich the content to be interactive, learning on a continual basis how students interact with that courseware and provide increasingly appropriate answers to students’ questions. Student can query Watson using natural language to ask questions. Based on the student’s responses, Watson can provide hints, feedback and explanations and ultimately work with the student at their pace to help them master the topic. But it will also give instructors real-time insights about how well students are navigating through their course materials. That in turn, should help instructors manage their entire courses more effectively and identify students more quickly who are struggling.
outcome: The key objective is to make the learning content intelligent by enriching the meta data of the learning content (videos, text etc), and make the content learner aware by bringing more personalised learning experience through cognitive interaction with learning content while the learner is viewing the content, the learner is guided through out by and also evaluated instantly, and will receive the feedback instantly ,Benefits and Impact:,Enrich and enhance the learning content through cognitive intelligence.,Students are engaged in more personalised way through cognitive interaction with the learning content itself.,Teachers can craft targeted learning experiences from the content with highest confidence.,Skills required:,Software Skill: No-SQL database, Web framework like Django/Flask, Python/Java, Cloud,Machine Learning Skill: Machine Learning Algorithms, NLP, Deep Learning,Optional / Preference Skill: Watson APIs (Speech to text, NLU, Watson Conversation).
finalOutcome: This project helped us to research and proto type a personalized, conversational system that is designed to improve a student's engagement with learning content. It makes the learning content into intelligent and learner aware content.
closeValue: The great team work IBM'ers can bring to the table when it matters.
ratingComments: The end user interaction with the system needs to be considered & completed.

title: Affiliate Challenge: Myth-busting series on what Watson is NOT
executiveChampionReason: advised by Susan Schreitmueller  as this is the affiliate challenge
description: Video series to bust some common misconceptions about Watson and AI
problemStatement: There are many common misconceptions among IBMers and clients about what Watson can actually do. Often people will refer to Watson as an omni-powerful black box, a magical component in a solution that will solve any problem. We propose a video series of 4-6 topics focusing on “What Watson is Not”.  We will ask senior technical leader like Rob High to launch the series based on his work in this area and with clients, followed by additional speakers.
outcome: Our affiliate will capture a list of the top myth topics,  leveraging  insights from the "on the spot" IBMer interviews (see https://aot.raleigh.ibm.com/aot/aotact.nsf/activitiesLUBM/Sus52581CB004AEFB4?open&id=52581CB00615880),We will find Cognitive/AI experts to work with, starting with Rob High and leveraging the AoT community to collect a good cross-section of experts across IBM.,We will then work with selected experts on those myths to capture short videos.  We will share both shorter more-consumable videos as well as a compilation video for each myth.,Other topics in the series may be: “How close are we to real AI”?, “What is data science really?”, “What is the difference between analytics and cognitive”.
finalOutcome:
While we did not generate the videos originally planned, however this did lead to a collection of the top 6 myths and increased awareness of the myths of Watson, and the presentation of three sessions. 
                                        
                                        
                                        e.g: 193 practitioners  joined live and others watched replay:
                                        In just 1 hour, we drove a: 
                                        56% increase in practitioners who agreed or strongly agreed that they understand the current capabilities of our Watson APIs, and
                                        49% increase in practitioners who are prepared to talk with our client about the importance of quality data when launching AI initiatives.  
                                        
                                        Top 6 Myths: 
                                        Watson is a single product that can Learn, Understand, Reason and Interact
                                        Watson contains general knowledge about every topic in the world and it can answer questions and understand situational context
                                        Watson is an AI entity, like in the movies.  It can creatively solve any problem if it is given enough data
                                        Watson can consume any data in any format and extract relevant information and insights without training.
                                        Watson is continually learning unsupervised and automatically gets better over time
                                        Watson out-of-the-box can read any set of digital data or documents and learn the information contained and then answer questions on that information
closeValue: Increased awareness of Watson Myths and increased education of the true capabilitities of our Watson products

description: Start using D3 Kanban as the new management system for project & certification badges in the Architect Profession in the Americas.
problemStatement: There are currently multiple issues and delays in the badge management and approval process. There is no overall-macro view for all badges being managed, nor metrics about how they are handled. The process does not allow for a dynamic reassignment under review. These elements lead to a significantly slow process that is causing a problem in the Architect Certification process as a whole. Candidates are having their badges wait up until 6 weeks until they are properly reviewed and the user experience is really poor. There are also multiple reviews that are failing due to language barriers and the current process does not allow for an easy identification of them
outcome: Enabling a collaboration platform in a single pane of glass will lead to reducing dramatically the turnaround time for Architect profession badges (project & certification). Profession Leaders will have an overall view of everything that's under review, how the SMEs are performing, have real time information about the end to end process to make decisions to ensure an even better turnaround time. It will also allow to highlight all badge reviews where a language barrier is limiting a fair judgement to be done. From a candidate perspective, having a lower turnaround time will lead to better user experience.
sponsorMessage: This does not sound like an Academy initiative more a piece of work already underway. Happy to discuss.

title: Supply Chain Ind4.0 Maturity Assessment
executiveChampionReason: New technology adoption (IoT, Blockchain, etc) into Supply Chain Engineering operation is one key elements in Supply Chain Engineering Strategy in 2018. Tory Johnson, as the VP of Supply Chain Engineering is selected as the outcome of this initiative has direct input and deliverables into his strategy.
description: An assessment of the current capability in Supply Chain w.r.t IoT and Industrial 4.0
problemStatement: While System Supply Chain is making good progress on skill acceleration and Cognitive VI roll-out in the iIoT space, there is much need to fully assess our maturity level in all aspects in iIoT ecosystem. The assessment adopts key concepts from “Industrie 4.0 Maturity Index” from Acatech (German Academy of Science and Engineering) and is modified into a tailored maturity index for the context of IBM System Supply Chain and the supplier base
outcome: There are a set of IoT related solutions being prototypes in Supply Chain as "grass-roots" effort. While we encourages such "grass-root" effort and nurture innovation under Supply Chain Engineering IoT council team, it is important for us to understand the current level of our maturity index in terms of IoT adoption, so that we will be able to steer the efforts to ensure they deliver maximum business value. The outcome of the initiative includes a holistic view of current IoT maturity in Supply Chain that identifies the gaps. TEC SSC will partner with Supply Chain Engineering IoT council team to execute this initiate. The outcome will be used to prioritize efforts and resources within supply chain to maximize business value delivered from all IoT solutions. In another words, the outcome of the assessment will serve as the cornerstone and “lighthouse” for IoT-centric solution development and deployment in 2019 and beyond.
finalOutcome:
Holistic view of current Ind4.0 maturity in Supply Chain Engineering through “Voice of Employees” 
-Validate our assumptions of general IT pain points and practices at working level
-Uncover any new insights into general IT pain points and practices at working level

Identify gaps in user experience, IT development practices, organizational collaboration and culture

Follow up deep dive in specific area if necessary

Prioritize action plans in collaboration with Quality Council and Blockchain Council
closeValue: a set of strategic recommendations to close gaps in i4.0 maturity in Supply Chain Engieering
ratingComments: Very comprehensive analysis of our i4.0 progress and gaps identified to increase focus on areas of improvement.

title: Machine Learning for IT Operational Analytics - Asset Creation
executiveChampionReason: Dirk is leading a global AI initiative that includes R&D, GBS and chosen client teams. The proposed AoT initiative is linked to Dirk's AI initiative, and will contribute and provide added value by delivering a concrete asset that can be leveraged by client facing teams to accelerate Machine Learning deployments related to IT Operational Analytics.
description: Objective is to creat a reusable asset from a number of client engagements worldwide on Machine Learning for z/OS for IT Operational Analytics. The asset should enable client facing teams to accelerate ML deployments.
problemStatement: Today's clients are faced with an ever increasing complexity in managing and predicting behavior and constraints of their IT operational environment. With ML for z/OS, IBM provides a tool that can augment operational analytics with sophisticated data exploration and prediction of key KPIs/measures, such as elapsed times and resource consumption. The objective of this initiative is to build an asset based on numerous client engagements and solution deployments that can accelerate ML deployments in the IT Operational Analytics domain.
outcome: The intent is to build an asset that is comprised of analytical models, a methodology, and workshop material that relate to a customized usage of the Machine Learning for z/OS tool for IT Operational Analytics. This will further accelerate ML deployments and helps client facing teams to sell a higher-level value proposition to their clients.
finalOutcome:
We have generalized 3 Jupyter notebooks with corresponding data csv files. This has been derived from client engagements using Watson ML for z/OS. 

The Jupyter notebooks are as follows:
a.	A1_BatchJob_Preprocessing_ITOA.ipynb (this Notebook doesn’t use any data; just used for preprocessing purposes)
b.	A2_BatchJob_DataExploration_ITOA.ipynb (runnable with local dataset) 
c.	A3_BatchJob_Prediction_ITOA.ipynb (runnable with local dataset)

The notebooks can be executed on the WML for z/OS system in the IBM Boeblingen R&D Lab, or on any other WML for z/OS system. This has been derived from various PoCs and pilot implementations. The ‘ipynb’ files and corresponding data csv files can be imported to another WML for z/OS system and executed on that platform. They can be used for demo purposes as part of the WML for z/OS discovery workshop. They may also be customized or used as accelerators in other PoC engagements. 

Local datasets:
a.	widetable_D_loan_ITOA.csv
b.	widetable_D_MIFID_ITOA.csv

The assets can be downloaded from the following IBM Connection Community site: https://w3-connections.ibm.com/communities/service/html/communityoverview?communityUuid=7ec38a97-c8be-4348-ae9d-8f3f7d772505
closeValue: Worldwide enablement of IBM client facing teams to discover and advance Watson ML for z/OS opportunities.
publicationDescription: We intend to publish a 1-page AoT TechNote to further describe and promote the deliverables of this AoT initiative. As the outcome of this initiative will enable client facing teams worldwide to discover and advance Watson Machine Learning for z/OS opportunities, we anticipate noticeable impact via an AoT TechNote. The TechNote will also be relevant for clients by increasing their awareness regarding a set of IT Operational Analytics use cases that can be implemented by using Watson ML for z/OS. Since a major part of the deliverables are a number of Jupyter Notebooks, the TechNote should include a description of usage and meaning of the deliverables.
ratingComments: Very business-relevant results. Great cooperation across business units.
