title: Solving the Plastic Problem in Packaging in Consumer Industry
executiveChampionReason: Cathy is leading as VP the CPG/Retail/Agri industry in Europe and hence is a perfect champion for this idea.
description: Helping the Consumer Industry to have access to a source of truth which provides the most environmentally friendly packaging and highlights the impact of it
problemStatement:
Would it not be great to live in a world without plastic pollution. Let's jointly tackle this problem!
                                        We have to change the way CPs & Retailer do packaging. Away from plastics to recyclable & re-usable material for packaging. This could help to change the world by reducing plastic pollution & ozone decline.
outcome:
We need to help CPs to analyze their packaging processes, packaging data, available / possible packaging material & characteristics, product requirements, ... come up with new ideas / suggestions on where to tackle what problems. If we can help clients to put the right focus where to start the plastics reduction in packaging, i.e. where the low hanging fruits would be, that would already be a very good starting point. This analysis could / should expand beyond and then also look into other ideas on how to make the supply chain / production process / ... more efficient to optimize the plastics & packaging problem.
                                        
                                        Current best idea:
                                        * build an engine which can give advice how to best package goods to reduce plastic pollution but guarantees the quality of the goods
                                        * maybe it needs molecule information and could leverage parts from Chef Watson
                                        * provide the costs / environmental impact of each variant (manufacturing, shipping, installing, usage, landfill)
                                        * Team around IBM’s VolCat might provide valuable insights (https://www.plasticstoday.com/recycling/ibm-s-volcat-process-uses-molecular-sorting-turn-mixed-waste-recyclate-virgin-grade-pet/78573423860251)
                                        * Potentially Nestle could be approach as a partner (Michi is on this account and they see it as a hot topic)

title: Machine Learning on DDP
description: A  Machine  Learning  Component  to  Classify  and  Retrieve  Spectrum  Scale  Configuration Profiles Based on Environment Characteristics.
problemStatement: For its optimal performance, the configuration of Spectrum Scale requiresto be tuned based  on  the  environment  characteristics  (HW,  SW  and  workload). Commonly,  this  work  is executed  by  highly-skilled  personnel  that  expand  their  experience  along  with  the  tuning  cases that  they  solve. Currently,  this  knowledge is  not  being  collected  and  classified  to  be  used  by others in cases with similar characteristics; producing experts work-overload, delays in customer service, and  knowledge-leakage.
outcome: The  objective  of  this  initiative is  to  design  and  develop  a software prototype to classify and retrieve the Spectrum Scale configuration profiles based on the  environment  characteristics.  Once  a  configuration  has  been  tested  and  validated  by  the expert, it can be stored and classified providing the characteristics of the overall environment. Then,  when  a  configuration  is  needed,  any  engineer  can  provide  the  description  of  the  new environment and the system will retrieve the most similar past cases previously stored. Having this, any engineer can rely on the aggregated experience from all the experts in a single place. Furthermore,  by  retrieving  the  most  similar  solutions  to  a  new case,  this  software  module will reduce the tuning times since engineers will not start from scratch.

title: Brainstorming session toolkits
executiveChampionReason: Bill is the GM for Intellectual Property for IBM and an advocate for the WW Women Inventors Community.
description: Create tookit for brainstorming sessions that provides best practice content, curated prior art, and questions to get a team focused on invention gaps for a particular technology or problem area
problemStatement:
Many inventors, both new and experienced, can run into idea blocks. When new to brainstorming, a group might not know where or how to begin. When experienced, a group might have run out of inspiration or new ideas.
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                Proposal: Create brainstorming kits, focused on a particular problem area or technology. These kits can include:
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                Best practices for holding a brainstorming session
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                A curated set of prior art, including some patents, patent applications, papers, articles, links to videos etc. to indicate the current boundaries, problem areas, and possible gaps for invention
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                A set of general questions to get the group talking and thinking about how to apply what they've learned from the prior art to current/future problems
outcome: Curated and vetted content that inspires, informs, and supports successful brainstorming sessions, where a group of folks that may or may not know each other initially can come together and successfully produce and articulate ideas, some of which can be integrated into the business and submitted through normal invention processes for review and potential patent application filing
finalOutcome: Set of 20 toolkits around portfolio invention areas, that folks can download and use in brainstorming sessions.
closeValue: Understanding that anyone can invent in any technology area with a little research and understanding of problem areas.
publicationDescription: Will be working with Communications to create standardized, AoT branded toolkits. A follow-on Initiative is being created before any publication will occur.
ratingComments: Exceeded my expectations. A model for future inventors to use which we definitely need as we add teams like RedHat to the IBM community

title: Opportunities for IoT, Machine Learning, and Cloud in the Beer Brewing Industry
problemStatement:
Brewing beer is a complex process involving mechanical engineering, thermal dynamics, biology, and chemistry. The process requires taking frequent measurements, adjusting parameters, and relying on experience to turn out a good product with low enough costs and waste to make a profit. Innovations in the IoT space, Machine Learning, and Cloud are opening new doors in many industries. The Brewing Industry should be no exception. Through interviews and diving deep into the brewing process from brewing to packaging and shipping, what opportunities exist to improve the quality of products and/or lower costs in the brewing industry? 

One such application has been published here: https://www.ibm.com/blogs/think/2019/04/ai-and-iot-help-perfect-the-brew-at-sugar-creek-brewing-company/

The above application is specific to packaging, but there are many other opportunities for this kind of work.
outcome: A paper that starts with an outline of the brewing business, processes, challenges, etc. The paper would then identify areas that could have synergies with IoT and Machine Learning technologies. The paper would conclude with some ideas on the application of these technologies, and how those applications would improve the brewing business or industry. The paper would be published and/or presented at a technology or brewing industry conference.
ideaMigrationComments: Sounds great - looking forward to seeing the progress on this....when will you issue a call for participation ?

title: Industry Academy Affiliate & AoT Traditional Affiliate Collaboration to leverage AoT Initiatives for Client Value

problemStatement: The relatively new Industry Academy Affiliates often find opportunities in AoT initiatives or other activities that could benefit their clients, but they often do not have members who can work on all of these. Conversely, traditional AoT Affiliate members could benefit from identifying AoT initiatives and other activities that might be well suited for them and could also benefit particular clients or industries that Industry Affiliates have knowledge about. Our Carolinas TEC Affiliate has a relatively large population of skilled and knowledgeable members willing to work on initiatives and other activities but might not be able to identify those that could best exploit their skills for positive impact. The Electronics Industry Affiliate identified some AoT initiatives that could benefit their clients and wanted to ensure that these initiatives are successful.
outcome: Pooling our resources will help match skilled, interested parties with activities of significant benefit to our clients, as determined by the Industry Academy Affiliates. In particular, we selected the "Reproducibility of Machine Learning Models" AoT Initiative (https://academyweb-prod.w3ibm.mybluemix.net/initiatives/479163d38f0ce219bc1456256ce5369a) for cross-Affiliate collaboration, as it is of interest to the Electronics Affiliate and is addressing an area in which the Carolinas TEC Affiliate has interest and resources.
finalOutcome:
This new form of collaboration between a "traditional" AoT Affiliate (Carolinas TEC) and an Industry Affiliate (Electronics Industry) helped to contribute to the success of another AoT Initiative that is important and valuable for clients in the electronics industry and beyond. We identified an initiative important to those clients and recruited talent in the Carolinas TEC Affiliate who could join with others to produce the AoT paper that is the outcome of the selected Initiative -- and we believe that this will be valuable to many clients in and beyond the electronics industry.

We also believe that other AoT Affiliates could use this collaboration model. It is low investment with substantial potential return, and it can produce "win-win-win" for all parties involved.

title: Build tight Istio integration with IBM Cloud
executiveChampionReason: Peter Wassel & Jason McGee are responsible to drive adoption of Project Istio in IBM Cloud.
description: Initiative to drive multiple innovations to build tight Istio integration with IBM Cloud, by seamlessly leveraging IBM Cloud existing capabilities.
problemStatement:
Istio, an open platform to connect, manage, monitor, and secure microservices, was launched on May 24, 2017 with a joint announcement by IBM, Google, and Lyft. As a founder of the project, IBM has been contributing heavily in Istio with ~8 full time contributors.  While Istio can run on IBM Cloud container service, it doesn't currently provide a fully integrated experience by leveraging the existing capabilities of our cloud such as IBM Cloud Log Analysis, IBM Cloud Monitoring, or VMs.  
                                        
                                        We are proposing innovations to enable IBM Cloud users to use/leverage Istio seamlessly & natively.  Specifically, this includes the following 2 big pain points:
                                        * Istio add-ons for IBM Cloud services: adapters for IBM Cloud Log Analysis and Monitoring. 
                                        * Istio mesh expansion for non-containerizable workloads on VMs: single service mesh management solutions for services  spanning IBM Cloud container service and VMs.
outcome:
The following outcome of this initiative, will augment the upcoming release of 'Istio on IBM Cloud' with materials for the developer community - to widely adopt the technology & solution:
                                        * Adapters to integrate with existing IBM Cloud Log Analysis and Monitoring service.  The adpaters will be installed and enabled by default for Istio running in IBM Cloud and provide advanced log and metrics visibility into user's microservices deployed in Istio.
                                        * Developer journey & related artifacts for service-mesh involving non-containerizable workloads on VM.  Users will be able to have microservices running on Kubernetes or VMs and have Istio manage the services on either Kubernetes or VMs as a single service mesh.
                                        
                                        Note:
                                        1. Many of these capability do not exists, and are critical for the client adoption in real-world production scenarios.
                                        2. These outcome will be delivered incrementally, by multiple squads, in parallel sprints.
finalOutcome:
Outcome:
                                        Resulted in TWO DeveloperWorks styled article (1) “Sending Istio metrics to IBM Cloud Monitoring service” & (2) “Sending Istio Logs to IBM Cloud Logging service”; and ONE proof-of-technology - “Mesh Expansion of K8s cluster on IBM Cloud, to non-containerizable services running on Softlayer VM”.
                                        
                                        Business impact: 
                                        Outcome of this effort is taken-up for immediate productizing the following, in this Y2018:
                                        * Istio integration with IBM Cloud Monitoring service
                                        * Istio integration with IBM Cloud Logging service
                                        * VM Expansion of Istio Service mesh to non-containerizable services running on Softlayer VM
closeValue: Learnt a new technology - Istio, validated the concept of integration with IBM Cloud, and ready to productize the results.
ratingComments: ISTIO is an emerging technology for Cloud Native Microservices-based workloads - it is great to see our technical leaders being motivated to make IBM relevant in this space.

title: IBM Point of View on Cyber Resilience for Enterprise Data
executiveChampionReason: There is a high degree of focus on this topic by our IBM Z clients and hence interest from the Offering Management team in understanding our capabilities and communicating this to the sales teams and clients. The results of this initiative would be a valuable asset in doing this. This is also a major area for the Resiliency Services organisation and so they have a similar interest in positioning their offerings as part of the overall IBM story
description: Many of IBMs largest clients are looking to protected themselves against logical corruption/destruction of data whether this is from malware, hacking or a priviliged insider. Responding to this requirement touches many parts of IBM including Systems (Storage, Z and Power), Security, Analytics etc and our customer facing professionals would like an IBM point of view covering all these aspects
problemStatement: Clients would like to see an overall IBM Point of View regarding our solutions to protect themselves from an attack against their enterprise data. This should cover specifics of capabilities for IBMs Systems infrastructure including Storage, Power and IBM Z, IBM middleware and IBM security capabilities. This material does not exist today which makes it very difficult for IBM client facing professionals to articulate the IBM value proposition.
outcome: The main focus of this initiative would be to create a paper and associated presentation providing an IBM Point of View on Cyber Resilience for Enterprise Data. This would be used with clients to enable them to understand IBM's capabilities and how they could apply them to their environment. It may be that it makes sense to produce platform specific materials especially for the Power and IBM Z platforms where IBM owns the majority of the stack as well as a more general version including Intel or Cloud platforms.
finalOutcome: Providing a cross IBM viewpoint on the Cyber Resilience topic
closeValue: Providing a cross IBM viewpoint on the Cyber Resilience topic

ratingComments: Very good job team!

title: Virtualize PEMMX and D4A education for performance and availability engineering and management

affiliateName: WW CoP for Performance and Capacity
description: This initiative spans a number of sprints and aims at creating a fully virtualised training for performance and availability engineers, testers and availabiluty and capacity managers to replace the 2-day classroom education
problemStatement: The Architecting for Performance and Design for Availability classes are not only outdated; we also have trouble scheduling these classes onsite due to travel restrictions. To make performance engineering and management (PEMMX) as well as availability engineering and management (D4A) education available for a large group of technical practitioners we have therefore started an initiative to update and virtualize the PEMMX and D4A education.
outcome: The expected outcome is 5 clusters of performance related education,A: Introduction,B: performance engineering,C: performance assessment and testing ,D: performance and capacity management,E: performance and CAMSS. This education will not only be available for IBM technical professionals; the education modules can also be offered to customers as a reusable asset. An example of this type of use is the education for technical professionals in the context of the Nationwide Building Society Operational Resilience programme. Also other customers have requested for education on the topics covered by virtual REMM.
finalOutcome: Several virtual education modules covering performance engineering and capacity management topics were delivered and can be taken by IBM technical professionals at their own ace could serve as the basis for billable education in customer situations (e.g. Nationwide Building Society in the UK)
closeValue: Increase of awareness and knowledge of performance engineering
legacyParticipantType: The education is meant for technical practitioners, who come across performance problems in their day-to-day jobs.nTo deliver the education we are also looking for people who have experience with virtual education platforms.
legacyValue: Whenever the topic of NFRs, Non-Functional Requirements such as performance, availability and security comes up in conversations with our clients, the client’s CxO more often than not refers to companies such as Google, Amazon or eBAY. They want the user experience of their business services to be as "fast" and "always ON" as they perceive the services from these companies to be. And it does not help if we explain to the CxO in question that his applications are doing something completely different from what Google, Amazon or eBay do. The CxO doesn not want to be bothered with technical details! Her focus is on new functionality that will help drive the business and Non-Functional aspects are simply implied and expected to be excellent. This education helps IBM practitioners to help our customers to achieve their SLO's for performance.
ratingComments: Always impressed with this team and the education they provide.  Thanks for the great work.

title: Reproducible, immutable, ephemeral and idempotent environments. Or how to do environment automation in the Cloud-native era.
description: This AoT study will study the approach of relying on declarative assets to automate the creation and management of Cloud-native environments. We discuss GitOps, Infrastructure as Code, Configuration Managers and CI/CD pipelines and some of the tools that help DevOps and SREs do their day to day work.
problemStatement: Cloud-native deployments are different from traditional application and environment provisioning.  We are looking to study and give guidance on how to provision and rebuild environments as part of a CI/CD pipeline and DevOps processes. This study aims to help Services organizations (GTS/GBS and Cloud CSMO) with patterns and practices with concepts like: Build to manage, GitOps, SRE, Rebuild instead of Fix and Always On.

title: Effective performance. availability and security engineering in a DEVOPS environment
executiveChampionReason: Leanne is the executive champion for the world-wide community of practice for performance and capacity
affiliateName: WW CoP for Performance and Capacity
description: This initiative will provide guidance how to effectively embed non-functional aspects in DEVOPS environments
problemStatement: DEVOPS is the new paradigm for IT solution development, test, run and maintain. DEVOPS is rooted in lean practices for manufacturing and builds upon Agile ways of working. Although the DEVOPS community acknowledges the importance of meeting the service level requirements for performance, availability and security, the DEVOPS community largely consists of partitioners with a development background who traditionally are focused on the functional rather than on the non-functional aspects of IT solution creation. executiveChampionReason: Kelly leads the worldwide IBM Z support teams which build and support high quality systems that allow our clients to transform the way they run their businesses. description: TechConnect is an annual event hosted by the Mid-Hudson Valley Technical Vitality Associate (MHV TVA). It is a competitve poster session that provides a forum for our IBM Colleagues to showcase their to with peers, technical leaders, and executives
problemStatement: The work in the Mid-Hudson Valley produces a wide range of hardware and software deliverables that have a major impact on IBM's success in the marketplace. We need a way to share the glorious variety of MHV work with the technical population in the area to spark the kind of creative thinking that only occurs through exposure to different ideas and approaches to problem solving. outcome:
TechConnect provided an opportunity for employees to present their work in a format (poster) that outlines their accomplishments in technical innovation/invention, process improvements, quality enhancements, and other strategic priorities. It was the most attended and participated TechConnect we had in our 12 year history of organizing this event. We had a record 50 posters, close to 100 authors/co-authors of those posters, 25 judges, 10+ volunteers, 265 People's Choice votes,  and 350+ attendees. The posters were well diversified, with 22 posters from Hardware/ISC and 28 posters from Software. Further, there were 20 posters in the Early-Tenure Category (those who have been in IBM for under 5 years) and 30 posters in the Open Category.

title: TCA - How to create my first project as Data Scientist
executiveChampionReason: Javier is Director of GTS Client Innovation Center Argentina and Leader of all CICs in Latin America. His organization includes the largest technical professionals population in the region (+3000 technical professionals). His sponsorship is critical to achieve more certified professionals.
description: Main Goal: increase the Knowledge of Data Science methodologies, products, tools and concept for future Data Scientist technicians.
problemStatement:
Data Scientist career and activities are quite a very young emerging skill, comparing it, with the IT Architect and IT Specialist traditional career with more that 10 years of history. So during 2018, the Data Science board built a new certification path: the Data Scientist certification that finally was available in January of 2019. Built in a similar way than his predecessors, the certification has 3 levels regarding the experience and complexity of the candidates and need to be supported and promoted world wide to get the first wave of certified professionals aiming to the challenges of the new technologies such as machine learning, artificial intelligence, more accurate predictions in real time, tons of information to be analyzed in minutes, millions of sensors taking and sending data to be processed, etc. These learning plans have been provided or curated from the business and service lines. 
                                                                                                                                                                                                        In the other hand,  specific industries in our country are interested in the used of data science products to extract information to create new business plans, specific customer strategies, etc. Local Argentine Banks and credit cards customers are the pioneers developing new products and solutions with the assistance of IBM Data Scientists.
outcome:
Expectations included 2 main goals:
                                                                                                                                                                                                        a.- Contribute with the World Wide Data Science board to create a primary knowledge network that can help to create educational material, courses, organize meetings, etc. to promote Data Scientist certification for IBMers.
                                                                                                                                                                                                        b.- Select specific Data Science courses and teach them into IBM Argentina to create the necessary professionals required by the customer with Data Science skills.
finalOutcome:
We got about 70 really interested candidates in Data Scientist certification roadmap from Argentina after performing many conferences, trainings, courses, mentoring hours, etc. Many of them belong to different areas such as GBS, GTS, other are technicians or the worked as administrative or as people manager roles today.
We created a local roadmap to prepare them for the first Data Scientist basic knowledge level. As second step, they will follow the official Data Scientist worldwide roadmap to complete all course and later they will start a local data scientist project in the 1Q 2020. Finally they will try to approve the Data Scientist certification during 2020. 
At the same time, we contributed to the Official worldwide Data Scientist  career with one course, designed, created and tested in our CIC Argentina, having very good results during the deployment of this methodology.
closeValue: We created a critical mass of 70 really interested candidates in Data Sciencetist certification roadmap from Argentina so they will try to approve the Data Scientist certification during 2020.
ratingComments: I hope we will have the 1st project in Q1 2020, and certifications during the year.

executiveChampionReason: Naeem is the CTO for SpaceTech at IBM and has an extensive background on IBM technologies applied to the aerospace landscape. His expertise is of high value for this initiative.
description: In cooperation with the school of engineering of the University of Conception, the event seeks to strengthen the development of ecosystems for entrepreneurship and technology-based innovation from the BioBio region to the world with a focus on the space industry. Hence, encouraging the foundations for the creation of the aerospace industry in the Science and Technology Park (PACyT) of the BioBio region.
problemStatement:
The initiative aims at positioning IBM as a main provider of Cloud technologies since the early stage of the SpaceTech landscape in Chile. William Carbone has led the NewSpace conference and series of workshops in Conception (Chile), the very first milestone of this Space opportunity in Chile, in order to promote the usage of IBM technologies applied to the Aerospace sector. Several key players of the Aerospace & Defense industry have been present, together with military high-raking officers, with the purpose of seeking investments into the A&D sector for Chile. 
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                The main purpose has been to play a key role in the formation of the Aerospace landscape in the country and to provide IBM technologies to the several players - ranging from local institutions to corporations.
outcome:
The event seeks to strengthen the development of ecosystems for entrepreneurship and technology-based innovation from the BioBio region to the world with a focus on the space industry. Hence, encouraging the foundations for the creation of the aerospace industry in the Science and Technology Park (PACyT) of the BioBio region by using the IBM technologies, dedicated to SpaceTech. 
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                The development of standards, changes in design philosophies and technological advances have broken down barriers and opened opportunities for non-traditional actors in the space market, valued at 360 billion dollars. Startups such as Planet Labs, Spire Global, Space-X, among others, have raised an investment of the order of 13 billion dollars, and are part of the so-called New Space, where the private sector plays a key role as an actor in development and exploitation of space.
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                The event brought together international experts with representatives from industry, academia and government, who participated together with attendees in dynamics and tech talks that allow each player to better understand this industry and navigate in search of opportunities.
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                This also developed within the framework of the 50th anniversary of the Apollo XI Moon landing, in which IBM played a key role.
finalOutcome: The initiative aimed at positioning IBM as a key provider of Cloud technologies since the early stage of the SpaceTech landscape in Chile. The intent of the AoT initiative was to set a milestone in the Spacetech arena in IBM and help conglomerate business opportunities, value generation and community engagement for space activities and technology. During the first week of October 19', the event brought together international experts with representatives from industry, academia and government, who participated together with attendees in dynamics and tech talks that allow each player to better understand this industry and navigate in search of opportunities.
closeValue: The initiative positioned IBM as a key provider of Cloud technologies during the dawn of SpaceTech.

description: Modern Information Architect Skills Set required to support new and emerging technologies and available resources for Re-skilling. problemStatement:
In this era of digital transformation, more and more projects are incorporating new and emerging technologies. The Information Architecture remains either an important and major component or even serves as a foundation of these new technologies. The focus of this initiative is the new and emerging technologies to identify critical Information Architecture skills required to support projects using these new and emerging technologies; and how Information Architects can retool and update their skills enabling them to support projects using following technologies:

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                ii.	Blockchain
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                iii.	Artificial Intelligence
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                iv.	Quantum Computing
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                v.	Data placement in Hybrid Cloud
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                Timeline:  Use March to prepare and register with AOT and broadcast a call for participation at the AOT site after registering.

Plan for 3 Sprints of 4 weeks each

Complete first sprint by collecting information and contributions from participants

title: Risk Based Testing Framework for Large Scale Cloud Migration program
problemStatement:
Cloud Adoption has been increasing rapidly. Organisations are modernizing IT through Cloud migrating their applications and database workload from the legacy state to the private and public cloud. 

Cloud Migration program faces a challenge to define a test startegy that is effective providing agility, currency and lower cost without compromising on test coverage and quality.
outcome:
A Risk-Based Testing (RBT) Framework designed for a large Cloud Application Migration Program. 


The business benefit of the Risk Based Testing framework will provide

1. Speed and Agility - in testing where only the right areas are tested with adequate test coverage

2. Currency - whereby the application runs on the latest generation of superfast technology meaning great performance

3. Lower cost - without compromising on test coverage and quality. A clear test requirement is provided by the Risk Based Testing framework for a test team limiting their scope and increasing quality by targeting the right test areas

4. Migration completed in time-boxed window
ideaMigrationComments: This has the elements of a good initiative and addresses an area strategic to IBM.

sponsorMessage:
Folks, just beware on creating initiatives that might sound self-serving (part of someone's day job).

Things can be a formal initiative if they are:
- Creating a new capability for innovation using technology (that capability could be tooling, education, courses, knowledge, a CoP, environment etc.)
- Creating new technological innovations (could be reports, knowledge, tools, patents around a theme etc.)
- Raising members external eminence

BUT the activities should not be part of, or necessary, for them to perform their day job.

Examples:
- Run hackathons using existing templates, [yes, if the intention is to create a new capability, or if external]
- Deliver university lectures using existing materials, [yes, eminence]
- Teach partners to use a tool using existing content [not sure, need a concrete example, isn't this someone's job?]
- Educate school children on robotics (or any topic) using public materials [yes - eminence]
- On-board IBMers to an open source project by using existing tutorials [yes, if the intention is for them to be active on it and it is not part of their day job]

title: Participate and support external Hudson Valley Technical Festival : Conference and Hackathon
executiveChampionReason: Larry advocates for the technical well being for IBMers in the region and sponsors the Manhattan Technical Vitality Community
description: A number of IBMers are engaged in supporting the Hudson Valley Techical Festival - Conference and Hackathon at SUNY Orange on 11-12 October 2019. The event is founded by local entrepreneur Yulia Ovchinnikova to drive innovation in the region
problemStatement: In New York & New Jersey, software & hardware developers  and engineers often prefer to work in Manhattan. However, IBM needs to hire many technologists in the Hudson Valley. Entrepreneur Yulia Ovchinnikova is working to build community & to drive innovation in the region.  This initiative is about identifying and motivating IBM volunteers to support Yulia's efforts in an effective way. The activity has also been advertized on the IBM volunteering portal https://ibm.yourcause.com/home#/newvolunteer/event/732770
outcome:
A more vibrant technical community in the Hudson Valley.
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                 Increased on-the-ground engagement with local universities and educational institutions
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  Increased awareness of IBM technology in the region
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                More avenues for hiring IBMers in the Hudson Valley
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                Increased appeal for technologists to work in the Hudson Valley
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                Coming together on philosophies around diversity, ethics, inclusion, teamwork, and team collaboration
finalOutcome:
One of the major challenges facing IBM, the technology industry, and the Hudson Valley is the ability to find high-caliber, sustainable, technical talent through the coming decades. By partnering more closely with local groups ((like Yulia Ovchinnikova and the Open-HUB project, producer of the event), we can more effectively reach larger audiences for collaboration and sources of experienced talent. We can also tap into educational institutions, local government, and high schools (like NFA P-TECH), in order to more proactively influence and grow the Hudson Valley into a respected leader in the development of a technology corridor, here in New York State.

Outcomes/Impact:
- Better awareness for IBMers to see what is being done around us
- Future networking and collaboration
- More avenues for IBMers to directly work with students
- Follow-up, external networking to help collaborate more around #IBMZ #IBMPOWER #CLOUD and other IBM platforms and services. Also, to help ensure we grow the talent we will need in the future.
- The conference categories aligned well with IBM: Career & Small Business Development, Civic Tech, Dev, Cloud & Security, Edu Tech, and Open Technologies
closeValue: This initivative and conference provided collaboration between IBM and local businesses, educational institutions, and government, to help strenghthen our brand while addressing future talent opportunities.
ratingComments: The Mid-Hudson Valley Technical Vitality Affiliate had another impactful year.  Thanks to the entire squad for making a difference!

title: Cluster API Integration with IBM Cloud
executiveChampionReason:
Ajay is the Distinguished Engineer for IBM Cloud, and he fully support we go with this solution to integrate IBM Cloud and Kubernetes to help customer create Multi Cloud or Hybrid Cloud. Besides, Ajay can also provide some technical support for us related with IBM Cloud.

description: Integrating Cluster API with IBM Cloud to provide Multi Cloud and Hybrid Cloud solutions.
problemStatement: The cluster-api is a new Kubernetes project which is designed to manage (create/delete cluster, add/remove node from cluster) Kubernetes clusters on different cloud providers, such as it can enable end user to manage Kubernetes clusters on different cloud providers, like aws, azure, openstack, vmware etc.   But for now, there is no cloud provider for IBM Cloud (https://github.com/kubernetes-sigs/cluster-api#provider-implementations), so I was planning to create a new cloud provider to integrate with IBM Cloud.    With this cloud provider, we will be able to enable end user can create a Hybrid Cloud or Multi Cloud based on IBM Cloud with ease.   This project is mainly integrate with IBM Softlayer.
outcome:
An open source project for cluster api provider like here https://github.com/kubernetes-sigs/cluster-api#provider-implementations , the project is now being incubated at https://github.com/gyliu513/cluster-api-provider-ibmcloud
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                        
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                        This can enlarge the eco-system for IBM Cloud as well, attract more customers to run Kubernetes Native Applications on IBM Cloud.
finalOutcome: Help to provide Kubernetes/OCP as a services on IBM Cloud.
closeValue: Enable end user create hybrid/multicloud with ease.
publicationDescription: cluster-api-provider-ibmcloud can enable end user manage native kubernetes clusters on IBM Cloud (Softlayer), including create, delete, scale, add/remove nodes etc. This can enable the end user create a hybrid cloud automatically with cluster-api-provider-ibmcloud and IBM Cloud Pak for MCM.

                                                                                                                                                                3.- An increased professional network between participants and instructors across the business units.

title: Blockchain & Security for IoT Hackathon with the Lucerne Graduate School of Applied Sciences (HSLU)
executiveChampionReason: Dr. Christian Keller is the Country Manager of IBM Switzerland. In the time of War of Talents, it is in the central interest of IBM Switzerland to bring students of the Lucerne University of Applied Sciences and Arts (HSLU) closer to Hyperledger Fabric in the form of a two-week hackathon. Even more so, this initiative is important since the HSLU is located in the Crypto Valley of Switzerland. In these two block weeks, IBMers from different Business Units (Global Services, Global Markets and Cloud) together with the company Legic (a dormakaba company) teach and coach the students from the development of Use Cases via the implementation with Hyperledger Fabric to the final pitch of the developed solution in front of a jury of experts.
description: 2 Block weeks for 13 students in the fields of Computer Science, Applied Computer Science, Industrial Engineer
problemStatement: During the block weeks, knowledge about blockchain and in particular IBM Blockchain Hyperledger Fabric and IoT is built up on the basis of a use case defined by the student teams. The interdisciplinary teams ensure different perspectives on the technologies and use cases. The block week is carried out together with IBM and Legic, who provide coaches.
outcome:
The Outcome will be:
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                Professional Competencies
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                F1: The students know the technical basics of Blockchain as well as the structure and function of Hyperledger Fabric.
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                F2: Students know the technical basics of secure wireless communication between IoT Devices and IBM Cloud Services.
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                F3: Students have been intensively involved with business ideas and business models in the combined subject areas F1 and F2. 
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                        
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                Method Competencies
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                M1: Students can derive business ideas from the technological principles.
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                M2: Students can apply selected innovation methods (e.g. Design Thinking). 
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                M3: Students can develop a prototype of an idea in a short time.
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                        
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                Social & Personal Competence
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                P1: Students can sell their own idea to a jury.
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                P2: The students worked intensively together in an interdisciplinary team and jointly developed a product idea.
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                Business Value:
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                V1: We will have the opportunity to identify new talents as potential new hires.
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                V2: We can teach the students as well as the professor the advantages of IBM Hyperledger Fabrics
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                V3: The Blockchain Hackathon is a 1st step towards using the IBM mainframe of the HSLU as a private cloud in 2020.
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                V4: The winning team can present their solution at the IBM THINK 2019 in Lucerne.
finalOutcome: The IT Department has so far mainly provided and used Etherieum for the students. Therefore it is immanently important that the degree of awareness and use of Hyperledger can be increased by such events. At this occasion we can discover young talents and motivate them to become enthusiastic about IBM's solutions and IBM as an employer. IBM clients have been donating their previous generation mainframes to the university since several years. The Blockchain Hackathon also serves as preparation for installing Hyperledger on System Z in the future. This will give us the opportunity to demonstrate the strengths of System Z as a transaction machine to students.
closeValue: To increase Hyperledger's visibility in the Swiss Crypto Valley and demonstrate IBM's expertise to the college, Legic and the participating students.
publicationDescription:
Together with the Lucerne University of Applied Sciences and Arts (HSLU) and the company Legic, we participated in an education module "Blockchain and Security for IoT" at the Innovation Park in Rotkreuz in the Swiss Crypto Valley.

Students of Computer Science, Business Informatics, Industrial Engineering, Electrical Engineering and Building Technology visited the module Blockchain and Security for IoT during the first two weeks of September. The module was supported by IBM and Legic.
Each of the four interdisciplinary teams had the task of developing a complete product from the idea to the prototype in two weeks. The focus was on "Smart City". In addition, the Blockchain technology and the functions of the Legic Crypto Chips, a specific hardware, should be used. This gave the students a deeper insight into Hyperledger Fabric and Legic's Crypto-IoT applications.
The 1st week was marked by expert inputs, hands-on exercises and ideation. For example, a design thinking workshop, coached by IBM, was held and the teams subsequently tested the developed ideas for their marketability through interviews with passers-by.
Week two was then all about implementation. During this phase, coaches from IBM and Legic were available to assist with the software and hardware components.
ratingComments: An initiative we absolutely need to keep and further expand!

title: 2019 European DevOps Architectural Decision Point development
executiveChampionReason: Rashik is the creator of the ADP initiative
description: ADP is a European initiative launched last year by Rashik Parmar with the aim of providing the sales and technical forces (with a particular focus on the global market) the tools to be effective in the face of clients when discussing some selected topics called Architectural Decision Point (DevOps, HybridCloud, Security, API, DPA, Data Insight). We are looking for volunteers with experience in DevOps for the development or sharing of assets that can be useful to other IBMers to develop a credible storytelling during a conversation with a client on DevOps.
problemStatement: DevOps not only a fundamental enabler for the digital transformation of companies but also a "glue" to drive IBM cross brand solutions like hybrid cloud, application modernization, cloud native development, data science, cognitive and security. Unfortunately, at present there is a certain gap between the potential opportunities for IBM linked to the DevOps world and those that we really manage to exploit due to a fragmentation of the individual offers by the various IBM divisions. The problem to solve is to help IBM sales forces (starting with the global market techSales) to acquire the right skills to articulate a credible and eminent “one IBM” storytelling to be able to engage the customer on DevOps issues.
outcome:
These are the three assets type we must be focused on that are in line with the ESP aspects of future.ready() initiative:
                                        1 - E= Eminence: PoV, target architecture, adoption road map, maturity model, etc
                                        2 - S= Show not tell: demo assets that will convince  the client that we have the technologies they needs.
                                        3 - P= Proof points: client or internal stories that prove we can deliver the outcomes our customers need.

title: Coercive Control Resistant Design
executiveChampionReason: This initiative was raised within the UKI TCG and Mark is a keen supporter of initiatives related to technology, diversity and bias being a Director in IBM Cloud and Cognitive software. The expected area for action would rest with the designers and developers of products and offerings that could be exploited to apply coercive control. He also has a wider network and influence within product development through Hursley with equivalent Lab organizations globally.
description: New technologies can bring immense benefits in a domestic situation, safeguarding us, easing our routines and enriching our experiences.  Unfortunately, they can also be exploited by abusers to control, monitor and torment their victims.  When used in this way, technology can make the victim feel the abuser is all-seeing, all-knowing and all-powerful.  In England and Wales, 6 in 100 adults experienced domestic abuse in the year ending March 2018 with an Australian survey finding an almost complete overlap between technology abuse and domestic abuse.
problemStatement:
New technologies can bring immense benefits in a domestic situation, safeguarding us, easing our routines and enriching our experiences.  Unfortunately, they can also be exploited by abusers to control, monitor and torment their victims.  When used in this way, technology can make the victim feel the abuser is all-seeing, all-knowing and all-powerful.
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                        
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                        In England and Wales, 6 in 100 adults experienced domestic abuse in the year ending March 2018 with an Australian survey finding an almost complete overlap between technology abuse and domestic abuse.  This is a worrying problem in society so a recent Technical Consultancy Group initiative has been looking at how we can make technology resistant to being used as a tactic of domestic abuse. 
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                        
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                        For this project the team chose to focus on coercive control, where patterns of coercive and controlling behaviour create such fear of another person that the victim will do anything the abuser requires.  This appears to be the area of domestic abuse that is most readily enabled by technology.
outcome: Guidelines for Product and Offerings Designers and Developers to mitigate the ability to exploit the technology for purposes of coercive control/ domestic abuse. Potentially to follow with external marketing and communication through other channels outside of IBM. IBM to be associated publicly as a thought leader with initiatives that promote "Tech for Good". The work done on the specific area of domestic abuse could have wider value in areas such as relationships with power imbalance.
finalOutcome: Created reusable asset of Guidelines for Coercive Control Resistant Design, Completed Academy Showcase and has triggered follow up activity in external communication.
closeValue: Changed how  designers and developers think about creating consumer technology to reduce opportunity for coercive  control.
publicationDescription: Created reusable asset of Guidelines for Coercive Control Resistant Design, Completed Academy Showcase and has triggered follow up activity in external communication.
ratingComments: The team have done a superb job in researching the issue and creating collateral which is very accessible. They have uncovered a very important topic and IBM has the opportunity to lead the way globally with raising the importance of designing and developing software and applications with a view to minimizing how it might be used for coercive control in the wrong hands. This initiative fits well with our "good tech" values and has the potential to be as influential as our work on ethical AI. The team are working hard at communicating the key messages both internally and externally and have, to date, presented to the British Computer Society, several university researchers, the IBM UKI Inclusion Board and a number of Connecting Women initiatives. I look forward to continuing to work with the team in 2020 to extend these communications further.

title: Developer engagement with federal and public sector integrators
executiveChampionReason: Dirk has a long history of direct involvement with developer engagement through his work with DeveloperWorks.
description: Identify technology, compliance, business practice, and cultural differences in engaging with developers for federal integrators, as distinct from developer engagement at cross-industry level.
problemStatement: The current IBM Code and Developer outreach models take a cross-industry approach to engaging with developers, by providing code patterns, sample code, assets, and other useful information. It has been observed by several technical leaders in federal and public sector that this approach likely needs to be adapted if it is to succeed for federal / public sector developers and integrators. Developers for integrators face a number of unique constraints such as strict RFP and compliance challenges that militate against a generic asset sharing approach. This thesis has support among Digital groups responsible for developer engagement as a means of getting developer, client, and industry mindshare. Since developers are a primary route to mindshare, try/buy, developer outcomes, and IBM business results, it makes sense to explore dimensions of developer engagement that may be different for federal or other public sector developers. This will help us to validate or revise a more general thesis that developer engagement should be industry specific in order to improve results.
outcome: This activity will bring together key technical and opinion leaders from the Digital and Washington TVC affiliates to explore the potential similarities and differences that would affect outcomes in developer engagement and uptake by federal integrators who represent the bulk of IBM's business revenue in that industry sector, itself a very large portion of IBM's overall business results. The leaders will explore and write a summary of key dimensions and ways of validating these, with an eye on technology and outreach recommendations for IBM's overall approach to developer engagement.  This may in turn change scope for several development projects and skunkworks efforts underway.
finalOutcome: We have created a high level overview of the Federal industry landscape developer experience. We have validated known challenges in the industry while discovery new nuances that will be critical to IBM success in the industry.
closeValue: This initiative will increase the effectiveness of developer advocacy and client engagement in the Federal Sector.
publicationDescription: This report documents an exploration into Federal industry developer experiences. We present various novel approaches for collecting and assessing these experiences from both IBM internal and non-IBM external sources.

title: Better Engaging the Developer Community
executiveChampionReason: x
description: Better engaging the developer community
problemStatement: In order to succeed in new markets such as Cloud & Cognitive Computing, we know that it's increasingly important to gain the visibility and respect of the developer community. Despite employing over 50,000 developers at IBM, achieving this position with the external developer community is not always easy. Developers often think differently than their colleagues on the business side and the psychology of a developer can be radically different from that of a marketer. Developers gather in their own tribes, especially online. This AoT initiative will focus on better defining why developer engagement is important to IBM, highlighting where we're succeeding today, identifying focus areas to be addressed and how we can better engage developers both inside and outside IBM to drive real business value.
outcome: This AoT initiative will deliver a set of best practices underpinned by a value proposition. Best practices will address focus areas for developer engagement i.e. technology, associated communities and key influencers. We’ll also produce guidelines and define channels for IBM developers to reach external communities e.g. meetups, tech conferences etc. ,We’ll build a worldwide community of practice with regional champions to tailor the message to local markets and drive local adoption.,A key outcome of this initiative is both the enablement and empowerment of the IBM developer community to engage externally thereby addressing the initial problem statement – growing visibility and respect of the developer community. Our initial sprint will focus on engagement with marketing & comms teams inside IBM already exploring aspects of this challenge.
finalOutcome:
Built a site on w3 dedicated to the output of this initiative: http://aot-engaging-devs.w3ibm.mybluemix.net/
                                        
                                        Surfaced quantitative insights into the IBM Developer Community's level of engagement with external developers. 
                                        
                                        Prepared a detailed analysis of developer engagement at IBM with associated recommendations to improve.
closeValue: <50 of IBM developers engage with external developer communities, while over 30% of IBM developers have said they'd like to - we have a huge untapped resource when it comes to external developer engagement & developer advocacy

title: Open Voice Challenge Pilot from Mozilla
executiveChampionReason: Rama Akkiraju (IBM Fellow) has a long involvement with voice data - the Mozilla Voice Challenge will help create an outstanding voice dataset
description: Mozilla Voice Challenge will populate the Mozilla Common Voice dataset via employees of corporations who will benefit from the dataset - This initiative supports the open voice challenge pilot
problemStatement:
Engaging employees in a prized competition ---- 
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                Because high quality datasets require thousands of hours of transcribed audio, representing a broad diversity of accents, ages, gender etc., the idea is that participating companies activate their most valuable resources – their employees. Through a cross-company campaign, Mozilla want to engage thousands of tech enthusiasts to gather an industry-leading set of relevant speech data, which can then be used by all participating companies and will be made open source and publicly available later. To increase the incentive for all employees, Mozilla will run the initiative as a prized competition – the team/corporation which contributes the most data will be able to donate to a good cause of their cho
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                With this initiative we will supply a list of up to 30 IBM volunteers to Mozilla - They will donate their voices and verify other voices - Each volunteer will devote one hour a week for three weeks in November - There will be "prizes"
outcome:
From the Open Voice Challenge Pilot (Nov 2019) - Mozilla will get feedback on their Open Voice Challenge tool
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                 From the Open Voice Challenge (2020) - Mozilla an its partners will be well on the way to creating the "Imagenet" for voice
finalOutcome:
IBM won weeks 1 and 2, Mozilla won week 3, IBM won the contest overall. 19 more recorded hours and 12 more validated hours of publicly available voice data.Together we also donated $5,400 to charity
                                              Through participation IBMers & their invitees gave $3400 to charity & recorded 9.9 hours & validated 7.8 hours of audio
closeValue: Helping to create the imagenet for voice:  IBMers & their invitees gave $3400 to charity & recorded 9.9 hours & validated 7.8 hours of audio
ratingComments: Great job, Susan! It's not easy to get people to volunteer time to collect data for training AI systems. 19 hours seems small but that's a lot of data in terms of human speech. Kudos to you in driving this with great enthusiasm!
