title: Digital Twin Reference Architecture
executiveChampionReason: Phil is the ISBD (industry solutions and business development) leader for UKI, so given the breadth of applicability of Digital Twins, but specifically for industrial applications, this is a very good fit. One of Phil's direct reports (James Mulliner) is a member of the study team, even though not a member of the TCG.
description: Define the scope of Digital Twins and develop a reference architecture and overlay of IBM products to map them to generic DT components
problemStatement:
The industry and many of our clients are starting to refer to Digital Twins and The National Infrastructure Commission (NIC) has launched a campaign for Brit-Twin, a national Digital Twin.
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                        This raises a number questions:
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                        * What exactly is a digital twin?
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                        * What is the business case for building one?
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                        * What value can IBM add, i.t.o. services and technology?
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                        * Do we have a PoV and a plan on how to engage on digital twins?
outcome:
This TCG Initiative will deliver the following:
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                        * Working definition for digital twin that applies across industries
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                        * High level reference architecture and IBM’s role in it
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                        * Two page(ish) PoV paper that explains why clients should engage with IBM on digital Twins
finalOutcome:
This study provides a reference architecture for the elements of a Digital Twin
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                Provides a well-argued case supporting the definition of a DT, a reference architecture and the solution components needed to build one.
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                This material is a door-opener to have a discussion with clients about DT without pushing specific technologies and shows IBM’s thought leadership in this area.
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                Mapping of our technology to the architecture provides signficiant opportunity for pull-through of technology sales and through defining DT as an SI project… provides significant services opportunities.
closeValue: This study provides a reference architecture for the elements of a Digital Twin
publicationDescription:

title: Create a semantic, context aware, teachable Common Knowledge repository with services to identify conflicts or ambiguities needing correction, and serving statistically most relevant knowledge given inconsistencies.

title: Creation of a professional basketball team simulator to identify team strengths and weaknesses and to predict future success
problemStatement: Three years ago a combined team from GBS Toronto and IBM Research in Yorktown created a system to help the Toronto Raptors with trades and draft picks (see https://www.vice.com/en_us/article/yp3bjw/toronto-raptors-nba-draft-day-ibm-watson and https://www-03.ibm.com/press/us/en/pressrelease/49011.wss). The system has been hugely successful. The Raptors steadily built a better and better team and this year became the world champions. However, the analytics that we used can be taken to the next level through the creation of a basketball team simulator. At the most basic level a user will create a team of players and the simulator will predict the season win/loss record of such a team. It will also try to identify what the strengths and weaknesses of such a team would be, and predict not just the season ahead, but seasons beyond that, considering many factors, and incorporating statistical feeds from the NBA and the SportVu service.
outcome: We would like to leverage our success with the Raptors and take the idea of building a winning team through the identification of individual and team strengths and weaknesses using machine learning to the next level, applying our ideas with greater power (i) in basketball, (ii) in other sports, and ultimately (iii) more generically to building teams across the IBM business and for our clients.

title: Smarter Infrastructure: Modeling the Optimal Placement of Logical Partitions on IBM Z
executiveChampionReason: Thomas owns IBM Z CEC firmware.  LPAR development falls within his realm of responsibility.
description: The purpose of this initiative is to build a mathematical model that will optimize the placement of the logical partitions/virtual machines on IBM Z.
problemStatement:
PR/SM is the hypervisor running on System z. PR/SM hosts logical partitions (LPAR) and each LPAR has its own OS. 
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                The placement of logical partitions on the CEC (Drawers/Nodes/Chips/Memory) by PR/SM is internally called the re-optimization process. Most logical partitions on System z use WEIGHTS to define their partition’s entitlement, exception being, partitions that use DEDICATED logical processors. The re-optimization process kicks in whenever there is an “entitlement” change. For e.g. an activation of an LPAR may take away some of the “entitlement”. Deactivation of a partition is another example. The re-optimization process needs to optimally re-arrange the partitions on the CEC for cache usage and performance of the guest.  
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                Two inputs goes into the placement process
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                1.) Physical Configuration  (CPs and Memory by node/chip)
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                2.) Logical Configuration (Logical CPs and Memory requirements by LPARs)
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                The current approach is a heuristic one where in we identify and place partitions one at time. We will investigate the existence of an optimization function for this NP-hard problem.
outcome: The deliverable will be a mathematical model of the placement process with multiple constraints and multiple objectives.  This should enhance LPAR performance and optimize cache usage for IBM mainframes to help improve the success of IBM Z in the marketplace.
finalOutcome: We developed a mathematical model that may be used to define the placement of partitions (LPARs) on IBM Z.  The model has been implemented using IBM CPLEX Optimizer and has been proven to successfully develop placement schemes that are equal to or better than those delivered by the currently implemented heuristic approach.  In addition, we believe use of this approach could significantly reduce the development time currently required to modify the code that implements the heuristic approach to placement, enabling rapid adjustment to changing requirements and more efficient use of the allotted development resource.  The one downside is the amount of time required by CPLEX to reach an optimal solution, which occasionally exceeds the allowable time frame for placement re-optimization.  Solution performance improvement is a work-in-progress.  In the meantime, this model based approach has been recommended for inclusion as a prototype in an internal "IBM ONLY USE " partition on the next generation IBM Z mainframe.
closeValue: We reduced complexity by converting an NP-hard problem into a 'tunable' mathematical model that could be solved by optimization software.
publicationDescription: This report describes the development of a mathematical model for optimal placement of partitions on IBM Z.
ratingComments: I rate both Anand and Robin very high. Both have done a deep technical analysis and came up with a mathematical model to improve placements over our current heuristic method. The results are outstanding and we can now go forward to use it in our system as next steps.

title: Test Automation Quotient & Maturity Baseline development across projects using the T-Square TAB approach and tool
executiveChampionReason:
Amitava Sharma is the Global Automation Program leader and Test Automation is a core tower. The Global Test Automation tower within the Global Automation Program drives an aggresive defensive automation agenda to increase the adoption of automation in testing so as to improve quality, speed and ROI. 

This initiative will enable defining the overall test automation maturity across GBS and will help in identifying opportunities for increased automation penetration. Account teams can build structured roadmaps with their clients based on the findings.  The T-Square Baseline appraoh and tool was developed with the executive sponsorship of Amitava Sharma and has already been used in 8 client engagements. It is being rapidly recognised as a easy to implement approach to drive base account growth.

By using the T-Square approach and using volutneers across the globe to conduct the baseline survey and perform assessments of the test automation maturity in accounts, we can rapidly build up a baseline of the organsaiton or clients test automation maturity, appetite and identify potential areas for increase automation. the exercise will logically enable development of a white-paper on the state of test automation.
description: Test Automation is becoming more curcial to quality engineering in the cloud world. As workloads shift to the cloud, automated testing across the lifecycle in an optimised manner will provide the necessary speed in quality. Even though test automation is not a new field, it is constnatly evolving. Today the focus is on reali-time ROI. Many clients are grappling with automation inlcusion for Cloud testing and in their Devops testing. To help clietn adopt the right test automation appraoch and tools, its first essential to understand thier currnet automation quotient and baseline thier test automation maturity. This initiavive aims to repidly establish the automation quotient and maturity baseline acorss client engangements. This will help GBS teams  understand the overall maturity of the test service provided and define a test transformation roadmap to help clients on their journey to cloud. The initiative will leverage the T-Square Test Automation Baseline approach and use the web based baseline tool to develop a standardized baseline across projects and client programs. Volunteers will be trained on the technique and guided to carry out the baelining exercise for the down-selected accounts/ projects. A consolidation of individual project scores will be used to establish an overall baseline across the industry domain and sector. Clients will be able to see how their test approach and automation quotient stands up against other IBM projects in their domain.
problemStatement: Most projects leverage test automation for regression or functional testing. Adoption of Cloud, Devops and Agile practices has increased the quantum of testing required to establish quality. This can be achieved only by adopting a strong START-LEFT Approachand driving transformation of testing with automation beyond regression and functional testing. There is a need for greater adoption of test automation across the lifecycle of activities - starting from requirements testing through to deployment into production.  To be able to drive innovative automation and test transformation, it is essential to first understand and baseline the test automation maturity of the client engangement. The T-Square TAB is a standardized solution and tool to establish and baseline the test automation quotient (maturity, penetration and adoption) across all activities in the dev-sec-ops lifecycle. The T-Square allows for rapidly aligning the test automation appraoch for the client with the IBM IGNITE (Test Automation) POV. It helps establish the tools and methods that are required for quality outcomes.  It will provide an objective assessment of the test automation maturity in the clients landsscape and across client projects.
outcome:
This initiativei will be a first of a kind in test automation and will help:
- create a baseline of the automation maturity across accounts in a standardized and objective manner
- identify opportunities to introduce new test automation solutions and the IGNITE QUALITY PLATFORM for defensive automation
- identify new areas for innovation in testing and automation
- identify new base account growth opportunites by identifying gaps in the automation approach 

The volunteers will be trained on conducting automation deep dives and will develop test automation solutioning and architecture capabilities and help in building the practice.

title: Indoor localization and motion analysis using Bluetooth Low Energy Beacon technology
executiveChampionReason: Bret is VP, Watson Internet of Things division. He and his team are very interested to leverage Beacon technology for activity tracking in commercial as well as consumer space.
description: Activity based tracking in dynamic environment leveraging Beacon technology.
problemStatement: Time and motion study is important to understand the optimal flow of goods and services in the workspaces ranging from warehouses, medical sites such as hospitals, clinics and skilled nursing facilities, to hotels, airports and many more. Often motion tracking involves humans performing different sets of tasks, or arriving at an optimal time to perform a given task. This tracking is time consuming and labor intensive, so it is not done frequently. On the other hand, the results are often used to set the operational standards for the given industry or individual businesses.  In situations where the nature of tasks changes often, these standards are often not useful, or find limited use in order to minimize the cost to serve.,The purpose of this initiative is to understand and recommend the use of Bluetooth Low Energy (BLE) beacons with the initial focus on hospitality and healthcare industries.
outcome: IoT is already bringing visible changes to businesses. The ecosystem of varied sensors with beacons can provide additional information from the human resource management, as well as facility operation points of view. It will enable strengthening the relationship between employees and the customers they serve, bring alive the indoor facility that has its own story to tell, and also drive employee engagement.,This study expects to generate the following outcomes,1)	Identify strengths and weaknesses of BLE beacon technology,2)	List use cases, and identify markets that IBM should target,3)	Develop recommendations for IBM executives.,4)	Design and Architecture for using the Beacon technology within the realm of IBM IoT framework. ,Business value: ,The expected market size for the indoor tracking and navigation technology is expected to grow from about $5B (2016) to about $23B (2021), at a Compound Annual Growth Rate (CAGR) in excess of 35%.,The study will highlight IBM’s potential to leverage this business opportunity to sell an appropriately customized IBM IoT stack, along with analytics to optimize the resource flow. Apart from optimizing flow, it can tap into the industrial market for the security and well being of the employees which in itself is a large opportunity.
finalOutcome:
The study opens the new avenue for IBM to leverage BLE technology and provide solutions that can have significant impact in optimizing resources, inventory controls, social and improve safety for our customers.
                                                                                                                                                                                                        The outcome of the study can be summarized by following sections in the report:
                                                                                                                                                                                                        1. Technologies and ways to perform indoor localization, with a focus on BLE.
                                                                                                                                                                                                        2. Market conditions and adoptions trends for BLE technology.
                                                                                                                                                                                                        3. Propose an architecture to deploy BLE solutions.
                                                                                                                                                                                                        4. Examination of use cases where BLE technology is being / has been used.
closeValue: The initiative provides proof points of BLE technology coming of age and how IBM can develop offerings to enable its customers to further optimize their operations and safety.
publicationDescription:
Indoor positioning systems have become widely available due to the increased number of sensory technologies and edge devices deployed in common places worldwide. Especially, BLE technology is at an inflexion point, moving from a lab or evaluation novelty to mainstream adoption. The proliferation of BLE enabled smart devices, and low power consumption, have made BLE an attractive technology for many applications, including indoor localization and tracking.
                                                                                                                                                                IBM should take advantage of the space and become key provider of services to its large customer base. This AoT report provides in-depth view of BLE Technology, deployment architecture, use cases and IBM portfolio that can the service provider.
ratingComments: This was an excellent piece of work you and your team provided on in-door localization. The report is excellent with helpful descriptions of technology, vendors, opportunities and gaps as well as case studies I rated it "Highly Satisfied". This technology will play a key role in "real-time system optimization" which is applicable to factories, buildings etc.

executiveChampionReason: Francesco is the VP of the Public Sector in Italy, where the major Clients, in different flavours, are starting the business transformation process through the Modernization of their applications
description: Modernize "on-premise" applications moving them in the Cloud using IBM Methodologies, IBM Tools, best practices and leveraging leading edge technologies
problemStatement:
IT organizations continue to spend 80% of their budget on simply maintaining their existing applications while only spending 20% on new innovation.
                                                                                                                                                                
                                                                                                                                                                The study will analyze and describe the best practices to migrate on-premise monolithic applications to the Cloud in order to:
                                                                                                                                                                
                                                                                                                                                                Accelerate digital transformation . App modernization is driven by the need to transform business to build new capabilities and deliver them quickly.
                                                                                                                                                                Improve developer productivity. Enabling self service for developers through adoption of cloud native and containerization.
                                                                                                                                                                Improve operational efficiency and standardization . DevOps enablement drives a culture of automation and transformation of operations
                                                                                                                                                                 
                                                                                                                                                                
                                                                                                                                                                Leading edge technologies like:
                                                                                                                                                                - Containers
                                                                                                                                                                - API Gateway
                                                                                                                                                                - Microservices
                                                                                                                                                                - Cloud Services
                                                                                                                                                                - Serverless
                                                                                                                                                                - DevOps

outcome: Presentation and Client case studies of migrating a customer-like on-premise app to the IBM Cloud

                                        - The importance of providing an effective transition strategy of «legacy» application to cloud

                                        - Real customer scenarios
                                        - Outcomes: strength and weaknesses, lessons learned in the application modernization roadmap

title: Better AI for Better Prosthetics
problemStatement:
Current Prosthetic devices solve movement by using movement controlled by other body parts.  For example: if someone has a limb difference where they are missing most of their forearm and hand on either arm they might be fitted with a prosthetic forearm+hand that is either: 1) controlled by their shoulders and arm position, which would allow them to grasp stuff or 2) controlled by buttons or other device implements which will allow the user to digitally control the prosthesis with the remaining hand.  

Both methods are serviceable, but using modern camera, sensor and touch feedback technology, it would be possible to provide enough data to an AI that it would be able to grant more human control over the prosthesis without any sophisticated interface to the brain or nervous system.
outcome: A workable prototype and/or workable design concept which can readily be implemented into a prototype.  Then shared with the limb difference and/or medical community.  This would drive use of and leverage Watson to make choices based on sensor input for the prosthesis without user input, fueling a whole new life experience for anyone suffering from limb differences and also open Watson to a whole new market of usage.

title: Future Skills Outlook
executiveChampionReason: Bill's primary goal for 2019 is "People". Identifying the future technical and soft skills we will need to delight our Clients in the next 5 years is perfectly aligned with this goal.
description: Initiative to look at the current and emerging (over next 3-5 years) landscape of technologies and soft skills, to inform a programme to make our technical and client-facing people future.ready()
problemStatement:
We have quite a good outlook on what the future technologies are likely to be, with the 5-in-5, extrapolation from where we are today, the Research Vision, etc, but what we don’t have a good handle on, is what our Future Skills Outlook is. This includes not only the technology areas we should be addressing, but also soft skills to enable us to survive and thrive in the future landscape.
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                        It is important that we look at the wider spectrum of technologies, and not only those being highlighted and championed by IBM Research (as in the 5-in-5).
outcome:
We will produce a report and presentation of the findings of an extensive literature survey of governmental and international bodies. This will be the first report of what will hopefully be an annually updated rolling 5 year outlook on the emerging skills landscape.
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                        The results will feed internal education programmes (such as the UK Digital Skills Academy), will drive a more cohesive technical community, will inform technology directions for the future DE pipeline, provide valuable input to University curricula through our involvement with Industry Advisory Boards, etc.
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                        It will also give us a valuable point-of-view on this very important subject.
finalOutcome: A valuable guide to the focus areas needed for us to be skilled-up to meet the needs of our clients in 5 years time. This should inform education programmes and provide guidance for career shaping.
closeValue: Highlights the technology skills and the "soft" skills we will need to meet the needs of our clients in 5 years' time.
publicationDescription: This report uses 3rd party published reports and data to assess the skills need for 5 years' time. These are technical skills, based on the emerging and sustaining technologies, and also for the "soft" skills needed to successfully navigate and thrive in the world we find ourselves in.

title: Reproducibility of Machine Learning models
executiveChampionReason: As the current Chief Scientist for IBM Research, Ruchir is well positioned to inform and act on insights and actions from this initiative. Ruchir is also making recommendations on scope to be addressed, additions to the team and overall client impact from this initiative. Ruchir has also guided previous initiative teams similar to this one for successful completion and uptake by IBM and its clients.
description: Reproducibility is a critical topic for adoption of AI technologies. It is imperative for IBM to understand the scope of reproducibility issues and deliver solutions for reproducibility for IBM & it clients. We will develop a PoV and short term deliverables for action by IBM
problemStatement: Adoption of Machine Learning models are becoming pervasive. ML models are increasingly used for analysis/projections in business applications, which are then relied on to make business decisions or  significantly influence business decisions.  Sensitivity to training conditions of ML models makes it difficult to establish reproducibility.  This is a business risk that must be addressed by organizations embracing ML for Analytics
outcome:
1. Whitepaper on Best practices / Point-of-view for verification of reproducibility of ML models
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                2. Study the industry state-of-art with respect to ML reproducibility, and determine how to tailor to platform/systems. 
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                3. Share the findings with practitioners directly affected by reproducibility issues so that they can act on it
finalOutcome:
Initiative established that reproducibility is a critical component of trusted AI and is a great influence for adoption across AI and Data Science.
                                                                                
                                                                                
                                                                                This realization and the importance of reproducibility will impact the way we continue to build our AI and Data Science portfolio. This becomes a differentiating business value across the platform. This awareness of reproducibility helps us in improving the trust of our clients in AI.
closeValue: Machine Learning Reproducibility is a must to AI and Data Science adoption, and should be achieved with contributing and influencing factors of ML development as described in the study.
publicationDescription: Adoption of Machine Learning (ML) models is becoming pervasive. ML models are increasingly used for analysis/projections in business applications, which are then relied on to make business decisions or significantly influence business decisions.  Sensitivity to training conditions of ML models makes it difficult to establish reproducibility.  This is a business risk that must be addressed by organizations embracing ML for Analytics.

title: Scaling Compliance in Digital Enterprises
executiveChampionReason: As BISO for Digital and in his responsibility for IBM web domains, Dirk has direct knowledge and connections to the challenges of managing compliance in complex portfolios for digital solutions.
description: Digital platforms require new ways to achieve and demonstrate compliance across enterprise boundaries. How will IBM solve this challenge for itself and clients?
problemStatement: The shift from enterprise cloud to multiple cloud providers is changing the nature of compliance. Digital platforms are now owned and operated by multiple organizations, where the technology underpinning digital offerings is often unfamiliar or even a black box to practitioners. This places responsibility for compliance activities in the hands of many organizations. This poses strong risks for enterprises that cannot effectively manage compliance activities across the digital landscape in which they participate. New modes of interacting around compliance  within and across organizations and teams. This Digital Affiliate will work with compliance stakeholders in DBG and other business units to gather information on industry trends for digital experiences, will explore and prototype new digital experiences with an initial with a focus on GDPR, but with an eye toward the larger set of compliance issues facing large enterprises.
outcome: The team will explore issues and  document real-world challenges, with an eye toward managing  current challenges in privacy, security, and other areas of compliance. We will also ensure evaluation of tools that might make viable products or offering enhancements through DE-level technical mentors, focused on public sector / US Federal and in alignment with CISO. Leveraging tooling and PoCs delivered for GDPR in 2018, we will develop connections to our target audience for these assets, client IT Architects and technical practitioners in the federal and public sectors, and produce descriptions and educational material on these assets, and make assets available through github, asset repositories, and IBM Code site if and where applicable.

title: Colorado PTECH
executiveChampionReason: Beth Rudden is a significant contributor to the IBM Boulder Community , continually working to develop and promote ways to ensure Colorado has a strong technical eminence.  Beth is also heavily involved in St. Vrain Valley School District, where IBM Boulder PTECH school is located. She is also a primary role model for girls/women interested in technical fields.
description: Interaction with PTECH students to promote careers in 2 areas systems and programming
problemStatement: There is a current shortage in the workforce of people with skills in programming and with system experience. IBMers have these skills, and many others, to share with our IBM Colorado P-TECH students. Promoting P-TECH to the IBM Colorado community is critical to ensure these students have outstanding mentor experiences, and to find optimum ways to engage these students within IBM before and after their internships. Many of the P-TECH students are first-generation college students, and their family backgrounds have not exposed them to many soft skills and other worldly aspects necessary to succeed.
outcome: Finding new ways for IBMers to engage these IBM Colorado P-TECH students to encourage them to pursue careers in Systems and Programming will help close the gap within the workforce. Mentoring these students not only helps them learn they are supported in their educational efforts, but also helps the IBM mentors think outside the box in sharing their expertise with the students. P-TECH mentoring provides opportunities for these students to develop soft skills (such as communication and presenting), which is equally as important as their formal technical skills education. These students will learn invaluable skills from IBMers that they can use throughout their lives, and for many of the students it will provide a sense of being supported and valuable. Many of these students don't have expertise in navigating the college education world and IBMers can also assist in this. The CTVC promotes IBM Colorado P-TECH involvement throughout the year, and highlights the positive outcomes, such as three P-TECH interns getting part-time jobs at the Boulder site once finished. We want to engage these students and educate IBMers on how they learn from us, but also how we learn from them.
finalOutcome:
It was determined there is a greater need to engage IBMers and P-TECH schools to design curriculum around these focus areas.
                                        It was also determined there is a need to work with local IBM technical leaders to determine where the greatest technical skills are most needed for IBM site employees to better engage the P-TECH students, creating a valuable and useful learning experience.
                                        The promotion of employee mentoring for P-TECH needs to continue, but focus should shift to how all IBMers can be mentors - not just the highly technical leaders on site.
closeValue: IBM sites need to work closely with P-TECH schools to better enable employee mentorship participation and achievement of the students' long-term goals.

title: TEC-J Showcase #3: PM as a Technical Profession WG
executiveChampionReason: Kuse-san is Executive sponsor of TEC-J.
description: TEC-J Showcase provides opportunities for TEC-J Working Groups to present their thoughts, best practices and innovative ideas that have been discussed in their study and researches with other TEC-J members in timely manner. It enables TEC-J Working Groups to exchange ideas and receive various feedbacks from TEC-J members and SMEs in a broad context. In this TEC-J Showcase session, the speaker presents "Challenge to IBM Academy Initiative - How to write an invention disclosure of project management"
problemStatement: Currently, project management role tends not to be considered as a technical profession therefore project managers are unable to become DE/Fellow. One of TEC-J Working Groups, "PM as a Technical Profession", is working to develop a technical career path for project managers becoming technical professionals, DE and IBM Fellow in the end. The working group is seeking for a way of developing a technical career path for project managers to become DE/Fellow and they considered applying for a patent could be one of ways to prove their technical capability.
outcome:
In this session, the activity of this working group is introduced giving the audience perspectives on how to become a technical profession (DE/Fellow) from a project management profession and showing a role model of it.  The members of the working group have been trying to write invention disclosures of project management for years, and could successfully file three invention disclosures so far. To share this knowledge in global, they started IBM Academy Initiative last year, and the outcome was published as Academy Report formally. The new patent portfolio was developed for IBM, too. The speaker will share his experience on Academy Initiative led by Japan team with 152 global members from 24 countries. 
                                                                                                                                                                Although project managers have been regarded as business management professionals rather than technical, the working group proved that they could also be technical professionals by filing three new patents in project management area. This must encourage people who have aspirations of being a technical profession from a project management role.
finalOutcome:
Katsuroh Hayashi, the leader of PM as a Technical Profession WG, presented their WG activities and shared his perspective on how to become a technical profession (DE/Fellow) from a project management profession. 
He explained that filing for patents in project management area is a good proof of being technical professionals and at a same time, IBM can show its presence through such an activity. He introduced three keys to write invention disclosure of project management and the audience could have clear understanding how to write invention disclosures to take a step forward in their technical career.
closeValue: The speaker introduced three keys to write invention disclosure of project management and the audience could have clear understanding how to write invention disclosures to take a step forward in their technical career.

title: IBM Community Health: Project Eliminate Hep C - Experience Dashboard
description: Develop Experience Dasboard component of the Louisiana Pilot to eliminate Hep C.
problemStatement: Hepatitis C is the deadliest infectious disease in the United States - yet it is curable. In 2017, Louisiana was only able to treat 400 of the estimated 70,000 patients who suffer from the condition. Hepatitis C care costs the State of Louisiana over $100 million per year. In 2019 LA made a major breakthrough in lowering the cost of the treatment enabling Medicaid to lift former treatment restrictions. Today, everyone can and should be cured. However, patients face numerous barriers to treatment including transport to appointments, stigma, historical treatment failure, lack of trusted support, social determinants of health, and more. Patients need a way to connect with trusted community health coaches who can reward them and guide them on their journey to cure.
outcome: IBM and LDH co-designed and started development of the IBM Community Health Platform to help patients connect with community health coaches who support them on their journey to cure. The solution is built natively on IBM Cloud, is moving to Red Hat Open Shift, and has been a ONE IBM project with GTS, CSR, GBS, Global Markets, IBM Research, Watson Health and now AoT. This initiative will support the development of one of the components of the solution. We believe this Open approach to solving a Social Impact Moonshot is what IBM is all about.

title: IBM Db2 pureScale using Docker
executiveChampionReason: Matt Huras, IBM Fellow is the chief architect of Db2 LUW
description: IBM Db2 pureScale using docker will help cloud deployment very easy
problemStatement: I have been working in Db2 pureScale from last 9 years and one of the biggest hurdle of Db2 pureScale adoption is the initial difficulty of pureScale instance creation. Creating a Db2 pureScale docker deployment using TCP/IP will alleviate the Db2 instance creation issue.
outcome: Design and code Docker deployment scripts using python to create Db2 pureScale instance for 'n' number of hosts given a topology and the instance is created without any user assistance,
finalOutcome: The business value will be in millions of dollars of additional revenue to IBM when productization is complete and solution is made available in cloud environment.
closeValue: To make Db2 pureScale cloud ready by containerization - this will make Db2 pureScale available in cloud platform
publicationDescription: We undertook a task that was thought to be very difficult to containerize Db2 pureScale which is a combination of three different technologies 1. Db2, 2. GPFS and 3. RSCT/TSA. The containerization was done by getting core changes done in the GPFS core engine by working with the GPFS team in China Development Lab. A successful prototype was done which was tested at Mayo Clinic and a joint presentation was done at Think 2019 conference. This study paves the way for productizing Db2 pureScale to come up as a true replica sets in a cloud native environment.

title: IBM Blockchain Bootcamp Mexico
executiveChampionReason: As Mexico CTO, he is responsible for the blockchain evangelization efforts and business related initiatives in the country.
description: Blockchain Academy (BAM) is the major blockchain community in Mexico City. They have trained more than 1,000 people in several technologies and topics related to blockchain such as smart contracts, Ethereum, RSK, blockchain for business, blockchain for lawyers. IBM Developer Ecosystem Mexico partnered with them to help them deliver a Hyperledger bootcamp. BAM delivers the hyperledger open source training, and we deliver the Blockchain on IBM Cloud training. Attendees receive an open badge upon finishing the bootcamp and passing an exam. https://bit.ly/blockcampbadge2
problemStatement: Blockchain is a new technology that's becoming popular because of it's promise to change the way companies interact with each other. Nevertheless, many people don't actually know how blockchain works and when they do, there is a lack of skilled talent that prevents companies from creating prototypes to finally deploy a successful project. This bootcamp aims to fulfill that skilled talent, trained on our technology either open source, or available through the Cloud.
outcome:
By the end of 2019, 100 people trained on hands-on skills of Hyperledger and IBM Blockchain (on IBM Cloud), including community developers, ISVs, MSPs and IBM customers.
                                                                                Opportunity Identification: the team is working with Baltazar Rodriguez, the responsible for Blockchain business development (part of Huibert Aalbers's team) to identify and follow-up identified opportunities.
finalOutcome:
The Blockchain Bootcamp Program created in a joint effort between the IBM Digital Business Group and Blockchain Academy Mexico (BAM), delivered Blockchain related content to 97 students during 2019. Those professionals participated in one or more of the two programs available (Intermediate Level Hyperledger and Hyperledger for Business), and approximately 25 IBM Blockchain Developer Bootcamp Badges were delivered for the alumni of the first course.
                                        The DBG team is following up with the graduates to identify potential business opportunities as well as preserve and strengthen this raising community. The Badge and the program is recently being redesigned in order to comply with new policies of the World Wide Team in charge of the IBM Badges.
closeValue: This initiative is allowing IBM to be positioned as one of the Blockchain on Cloud Provider among the developers and startups ecosystems in Mexico, increasing mindshare and having more technology experts on the field.

title: TLC-BR - Technical Agenda - TechDay Horto 2019 - 2nd Edition
executiveChampionReason: Decio Miname is the CTO for LA, covering all IBM BUs and with an outstanding mindset to promote the One IBM approach. He supports the TLC-BR and wants to promove the integration and knowledge sharing among the Technical Community.
description: Day-long event for the professionals in Hortolândia site, bringing several subjects related to innovation, career and development, specially to the Technical Community at this site.
problemStatement:
As a result of a Design Thinking session done in 2018 with the technical community, it was identified an integration gap of the technical community in Hortolândia. 
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                Hortolândia technical team is mostly from Service Delivery Center, and usually, the team is so immersed in the daily issues that they don't find time to integrate with the broad technical community and learn new technology.
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                This is the 3rd time running this event in Hortolândia (previous events were on November/2018 and April/2019), due to the great recognition from the professionals and leadership in Hortolândia. 
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                This Edition brings new themes, new speakers, innovation and challenges for the participants, speakers and staff.
outcome: The TLC-BR expects, with this new edition of TechDay Horto, to continue engaging more professionals, and to bring more opportunities to develop and know about IBM portfolio and innovation, at the same time that brings the professionals close to the TLC-BR and the opportunities generated by this team.
finalOutcome: This initiative provided a new opportunity to bring to IBM Community (not only Technical Professionals) valued themes, such as Security, Mainframe, 5G, LGPD, Microservices, Power, Docker, Red Hat, Career and others. In a single day, more than 20 hours of knowledge was shared - in 4 parallel tracks and 44 sessions, by 56 different speakers (29% Women & 71% Men). 235 IBMers from Hortolândia (and other sites) subscribed for the event, and the attendance was more than 375 professionals - 20% of these professionals not on Technical Career. The event was evaluated as good, very good or excelent by 83% of the participants. Besides the clear value (knowledge and networking) brought to the IBM Community at Hortolândia site, opportunities and information to support other initiatives and actions were mapped during this event and its results analysis.
participants: Fernando Augusto A de Oliveira Souza
Rogerio Cesar Barbosa Dos Santos Da Silva
closeValue: Continuous development and sinergy with the IBMers Hortolândia site, and new opportunities mapped for IBM Brasil (Managers/Executives and HR Brasil) and TLC-BR in 2020.
ratingComments: Congratulations on this 2nd edition of 2019 Tech Day Horto! This edition demonstrated clearly how the initiative evolved, resulting in a more robust planning and execution, as well as gathering information on both preparation and execution phases, that helps understand the population of our largest technical location in LA and fine tune the event at each edition. Such insights are valuable to discuss and define other initiatives as well.

title: Drive Visual/Acoustic Insights adoption in manufacturing industry
executiveChampionReason: solution sponsor in CDL
description: Visual/Acoustic Insights is a new solution in IOT for manufacturing portfolio. It provide the cognitive visual/acoustic analysis in the manufacturing quality inspection domain.  The solution got a lot of interest since released, we had conduct two rounds of WW enablement to the service and field team and build a strong customer pipeline. Moving forward, we need to build real reference cases for this solution and collect continuous feedback from customer to polish our solution and make it unique in the market.
problemStatement: The defect detecting process today in manufacturing is heavily reliant on manual inspection which had low efficiency and high cost. Growing demand on visual inspection automation for product quality to reduce labor cost and improve efficiency and increase analysis consistency in the manufacturing domain.
outcome: Drive Visual/Acoustic Insights landing and enhance product through engagement feedback to improve unique cognitive capability in IOT for Manufacturing portfolio.
finalOutcome: As a strong industrial AI solution in GCG, visual insights had built a lot of client reference cases and a strong pipeline in manufacturing with differentiating capabilities since 2017.This including the successful deal such as CSOT, YunNan BaiYao, Small Pot Tea, Shanghai TianMa, SAB, MaoTai, Unicom, Schaffler, Opton Optical, and contribute $12M+ revenue. It is the first SaaS offering landing on the Unicom cloud and was the key factor that drove the collaboration between Unicom and IBM. VI also got a bunch of WW successful deals around asset performance management including H3 Zoom who is using drone + Visual Insights to do building inspection. As well as Michelin, Toyota, ABB, Schuetz, Samarth Udyog.
closeValue: Visual Insights is an end to end solution combine AI technology with specific industry scenario that drive clear ROI for customer. It expand the strength of IBM in the enterprise solution domain and generate a great business impact.
ratingComments: Visual Insights is a great offering with good initial market success, but, the potential is much bigger and we have more work to do to capture much larger market leveraging offerings like VI.

title: IBM Digital - Nation Competition Egypt
executiveChampionReason: Wael Absoush, IBM Egypt General Manager is the executive sponsor of the IBM Digital - Nation Competition for Egypt.
description: The IBM Digital - Nation Competition for Egypt addresses environmental issues in Egypt such as air pollution, water pollution etc.  Youth are asked to leverage IBM online training platform Digital - Nation Africa to learn and build innovative solutions to tacke this problem.
problemStatement:
The problem of environmental pollution in Egypt is becoming alarming. There are several forms of pollution (air, water, noise, light, ...etc) that can cause massive fatal and chronic diseases like lung cancer, strokes, hearing loss, and hypertension.   
                                                                                                                        Natural disasters too can be tied to unnatural causes like pollution. Studies show that air pollution is linked to drought, flooding and even hurricanes. Human activity can, and already has, driven large-scale regional climate changes which in turn drive storms, floods, volcanoes, … etc.
                                                                                                                        Polluted air holds much higher concentrations of water-soluble particles, and, as such, clouds formed from the polluted air tend to have more, and smaller, droplets compared with "natural" clouds, according to the NASA Earth Observatory.
                                                                                                                        Looking from another angle, pollution can cause more damage on top on the effects of a natural disaster.   When a large river floods, many pollutants, such as farm waste, detergents, chemicals from processing plants, and fertilizers from crops, are swept downstream and deposited on land. These large deposits pollute drinking water and farmland. In addition, floodwaters deposit sediments, sand and moisture in homes and other buildings. This leads to mold production, and many forms of mold are hazardous to humans.
outcome:
IBM aims to reach out to thousands of young developers across Egypt to support them to compete in the Global IT job market, foster innovation, and promote economic growth in Egypt. 
                                                                                                                        The IBM Digital – Nation Africa Competition for Egypt is a nation-wide competition under the auspices of the Ministry of Communications and Information Technology and in partnership with prestigious entities like ITI, United Nations Development Program (UNDP), and the American Chamber of Commerce (AmCham).
                                                                                                                        Youth are challenged to innovate using the latest technologies like AI, Cloud, Blockchain, IoT, and Data Science using IBM’s latest online training platform IBM Digital – Nation Africa, to help reduce pollution in Egypt.
finalOutcome:
Promoted IBM Online training platform Digital - Nation Africa and IBM Cloud platform and services to to more than 7,500 young developers. 
                                                                                Availed IBM AI, Data Science, IoT, and Cloud tracks to the youth.
                                                                                Built a pool of potential IBM hires from talented young developers
closeValue: IBM Branding among the youth
adminComments: 12/12:  Closed as highly satisfied per Wael Aboush email.

title: IBM WMATVC and Red Hat Hands-On Cross Training Initiative
executiveChampionReason: Andras is a lead sponsor of the Washington Metropolitan Area Technical Vitality Council and serves as the IBM Federal Chief Technology Officer.
description: A joint initiative between the IBM WMATVC and Red Hat Partner Team providing Hands-On Training for both IBM and Red Hat Technicians in the WMA
problemStatement: IBM and Red Hat technicians on the Washington metropolitan area are looking at how they can learn more about each other's capabilities and offerings.   While there are web materials that are available, there is no substitute to actually seeing and touching the actual technology.   Currently, there is a lack of free hands-on and in-person technical training for this target audience and subject matter.  This problem can be addressed by reaching out to the Red Hat community to both receive hands-on education and to offer sessions to the Red Hat team as well.
outcome: The expected outcome is to enable both IBM and Red Hat technicians on our technology and provide them with real hands-on experience with that technology.  This will allow both teams to better understand each other's offerings when selling, architecting, building and operating those offerings and capabilities.
finalOutcome:
Our initial results from this initiative have been extremely successful. Two Red Hat OpenShift hands-on workshops have been hosted by the  Red Hat team in Tysons, VA, with another scheduled for January of 2020. There has been great demand for these workshops. The first workshop “sold out” in less than one hour. Approximately 85 students have received the initial training. Feedback from the first wave of students has been extremely positive. Here are some of the quotes that we have received:

“I find the hands on lab much more informative, more relevant to my work. It provided me an environment to find out how OCP worked”

“I liked that the presenters were knowledgeable, accurate, and helpful. I also liked that there were several people in the room to help!”
closeValue: The greatest impact of this initiative was providing real hands-on enablement to WMA-TVC technicians by Red Hat subject matter experts.
ratingComments: We see the WMA TVC as a primary channel for engagement. Not just an extra leadership opportunity. Leveraging the community facilitates participation and add credibility to our strategy for engagement and enablement. It's also got the Red Hat team excited to participate.

title: New Generation Audio Guides
executiveChampionReason: Francesco is the VP for health and public sector in Italy. The asset produced by this academy study could be used as show case in conversations with the Ministry of Cultural Heritage in Italy and several museums directors supporting existing contracts or opening the dorr to new opportunities
description: Enhance the multimedia support in museum leveraging artificial intelligence and IoT
problemStatement:
The current multimedia experience in museum is not flexible, not easy to update, not using standard devices, not scaling according to the number of attendees, needs continuous effort for language translation and supports only a small subset of languages, cannot easily be extended to new technologies, may come with hygienic concerns (i.e. multiple people sharing over time the same devices, they are typically not accessible to people with disabilities.
                                                                                                                        The tourist is often trapped into too crowded rooms. The possibility to identify alternate paths to visit the museum, coming back later on, will reduce the stress on the attendee and make the exhibition more enjoyable.
                                                                                                                        Having the possibility to make the multimedia support independent from the exhibition itself but hooked up to the masterpiece make the technology investment (i.e. buying the multimedia app) valid all over the world. The attendee can be able also be provided with the possibility to see multiple multimedia resources from all museums/events where the masterpieces has been hosted/is hosted.
                                                                                                                        On the exhibitor side, controlling the flow of attendees, providing for example discounts for low flow periods will improve the overall experience and help better manage the exhibition facilities.
outcome:
A presentation that describes the proposed solution prototyped and as-to-be in a production environment 
                                                                                                                        A working prototype that will show the basic scenarios: recognize a masterpiece, provide suggestions on similar masterpieces present in the museum ordered by usability of the exhibition location, audioguide service for the selected masterpiece, conversational interface to navigate the museum and its facilities, sample historical reports
finalOutcome:
We built a reusable asset that can be used for demos and proof of technologies to sow how to leverage Watson IoT, Watson Studio and Watson Visual Recognition to improve the museum visit.
                                        The mobile application we built takes into consideration diversity and inclusion providing the possibility to deliver the guide information via speech, text and in advanced or simplified flavor so to address accessibility and visitors'age concerns (e.g. a kid may find more enjoyable and understandable the simplified version, an art expert will go for the advanced one).  
                                        The code can be expanded also to support cross museums experiences.
                                        The set of skills gained in designing and building the prototype can be reused to scenarios not limited to the museums world.
                                        The proposed solution can run completely in IBM Cloud (as in the prototype case) or can have critical pieces running on premise to address special privacy and legal regulations.
closeValue: We built a reusable asset that shows how IoT and Visual Recignition technologies could modernize the museums world
ratingComments: very well thought solution to a real business problem

title: TEC-J Seminar: Understanding and Protecting Nazca Lines with IBM’s AI Technology
executiveChampionReason: Sonomi Ohkubo is Director of IBM Systems technical sales and Lab service of Japan and she has been managing Deep Learning Systems CoC who contributed to discovering new geoglyph in the Nazca Lines by utilizing IBM Systems products and technologies.
description: Special seminar to acquire the insights behind the joint research project with Yamagata University which tried to discover new geoglyph in the Nazca Lines by IBM's AI including remote sensing technology
problemStatement:
IBM helps discover new geoglyph in the Nazca Lines.  This news has been covered in many media outlets, but the coverage was limited and we did not know the whole part of this project including background, real objectives, techniques, insights from PoC and their future even though we are IBMers. Japanese clients in insurance and other industries are also starting to get interested recently, so that we need to understand this project correctly. 
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                        
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                        TEC-J will present special seminar to address this problem. TEC-Japan AoT Affiliate will invite 3 members from the joint research project - Akihisa Sakurai (DE, IBM Research), Masao Hayashi and Yiru Lai (both from Deep Learning Systems CoC)  and setup the seminar to allow IBM Japan employees to understand via direct-communication with them.
outcome: By  receiving the explanation directly from this project members, participants will be able to understand the objective, insights from PoC and its future plan correctly. In addition, participants will be able to acquire the knowledge of IBM PAIRS which Japanese clients in insurance and other industries are starting to get interested recently.  Participants will be excited about IBM’s technology contribution to this historic discovery, and will become to be interested in this technology and its application.
finalOutcome: This seminar was held on January 30 with enrollment by over 700 IBM Japan employees. According to the questionnaire comments after the event, many participants understood not only ‘biased’ presentations in various media but also the real world of this project, showed a strong interest in them, and also deeply understood AI PoC by Systems Business Unit and PAIRS by Research Division.  These two technologies are listed as IBM Japan’s focus this year, and more people's understanding will contribute significantly to our business expansion this year. The goal of this initiative has been successfully achieved with kindly support by executive champions. title: Practical Operational Modelling - Improving the approach
executiveChampionReason: Jenny Ang is closely supporting this initiative.  Gary is the VP which Jenny is reporting to.
description: Reviewing new modelling techniques and graphical representations for Operational Modelling
problemStatement:
Operational modelling is a powerful technique used to model IT systems.  It has been well established, and has excellent credentials, however there are some areas which should be re-assessed.  A team in the Netherlands has been doing just that (led by Merijn Weiss).  This study looks to review this work and establish whether this should be reflected back into standard Operational Modelling.  Two specific areas are a focus.
                                                                                Firstly, the graphical representation which is used is extremely basic - this is due to the graphical constraints which were available when the modelling language was first created many years ago.  This study aims to challenge this and look at the use of shape, color and icons to convey more information in less space.
                                                                                Secondly we will be reviewing the information which is represented to identify whether this can be optimised
outcome: To improve the Operational Modelling approach to make it more appropriate for modern usage
finalOutcome: The Study has identified multiple ways to improve the visualization notation used in Operational Modelling which will allow more information to be conveyed in a more appealing manner within a simpler diagram.  This is a great step forwards for Operational Modelling and will help to bring it into this century.  The approach is clear, but the notation needs to be agreed where possible across IBM as part of the implementation.  We can then incorporate the changes within Cognitive Architect.
closeValue: Bringing Operational Modelling visualization into this century

executiveChampionReason: Gustavo is the regional leader for Watson IoT solutions. He is the main sponsor for this initiative, as his main goal is to develop the business ecosystem around IoT solutions and expand the market share around IBM IoT Portfolio.
description: Collaborate with Watson IoT Business Unit to develop an ecosystem of business partners, startups and service providers by enabling them in our IoT portflolio.
problemStatement:
IBM Argentina is facing an emerging market eager to be part of the world’s business digital transformation and has become extremely informed and demanding, and willing to innovate. Many industries in our country (agriculture, chemical & petroleum, electronics, automotive, etc) fights thought the same constrain: customers know that technology is ready for their industries, however they don't know where to start and who can be their technology partner for that. 
                                                                                                                        
The problem is that this demanding market is not familiar with IBM's cognitive and IoT portfolio  and so being capable to tackle their needs. In addition to this, our business partners are very limited and not skilled about all our IoT solutions: Maximo and all the SaaS solutions sush as Worker Insights, Connected Vehicle Insights and more; or Tririga neither Watson IoT Platform in IBM Cloud. Many startups and entrepreneurs are emerging to be IoT solutions providers and they are not starting with IBM. We need to map the IBM Argentina's IoT ecosystem, enable them with our technology and transform them in the strategic partners that will be able to install, deploy, manage and deliver IoT solutions using IBM technology.
outcome:
Target new possible Business Partners and MSPs in Argentina that can be able to gain the skills and develop their offerings embedding IBM technology within the Watson IoT portfolio.
Enable and develop a committed relationship with this targeted ecosystem. 
Gain market share for the Watson IoT brand in Argentina.
Enable new business opportunities.
Onboard new MSPs and Business Partners to IBM.
finalOutcome:
From this initiative, we have developed a large ecosystem of MSPs, BPs and Startups, and generated a tremendous impact in the market with our products, an most important, we developed relationships of trust and commitment with them.
We participated of the IoT Networking Day, the most important IoT event in Argentina, with an audience from government and Oil&Gas industry leaders. IBM was the only Cloud company with presence in the event.
We have enabled 7 new MSPs for IBM who are consuming our products into their offerings: Smartminds; Fidumtec; SortBoks; UALI; Tuten; AESA. 
We also participated of the Drone Day organized by the Argentine Drone Chamber and discussed about uses cases from the combination of drones and AI.
We participated for the first time to the Think Argentina event with 3 stands related to IoT: Maximo, IoT Lab (growth initiative), and a MSP, UALI (drones using IBM technology).
We had for the first time a 3 day IoT + Maximo hands-on workshop with international teachers for our ecosystems including MSPs and Startups.
We develop a new strategic alliance with the Argentine Internet Chamber.
We develop an alliance with MCElectronics and we participated in their IoT event in 3 countries.
closeValue: We have made of IBM a trusted, valuable and commited partner to our ecosystem in IoT.

In-person, co-located collaboration is the most effect medium and is essential if we want to increase patent activity in the Southern California region.
                                        
                                        We expect to facilitate the creation of multiple, primarily co-located patent "squads" in Southern California offices. We hosted periodic guild-wide meetings to share knowledge about the process and provide support to the squads. In this way, more IBMers will become engaged in the process and do so more productively.
                                        Ultimately, this initiative will significantly increase the number of invention disclosures originating in the area lab. After one year we'll assess our success in terms of number of active squads, invention disclosures, and patent filings.
                                        
                                        2017 marked a significant reorganization of the initiative with Ned Bader and Patricia Gatewood leading the effort to move to a Smartify model. By moving to a Guild/WorkPod model, the team was able to retain the majority of experienced team members and recruit new members into the organization (5 additional teams members have been recruited this year) . There is quarterly meetings held of the entire guild,  providing training and leadership to all the guild members.
                                         Three pods or work teams are active.  These pods meet on their own schedule and work on patent applications that interest the specific squads.   One team's focus area is Big Data and Data analytics, another focuses on Case management functionality, while the third pod is focusing on general ECM activities.  
                                        
                                        Given the success of this initiative, we will relaunch this initiative in Jan 2018. Going forward, it is hoped to develop pods focusing on remote team members, and product focused teams for CE/PE.
