title: Best Bots for Business: Chatbots, Assistants and Agents
executiveChampionReason: Kendra will lead offering management and staffing up for the Watson Personal Agent offering coming from Watson IoT. But she is dependent upon runtimes, tools, methods and technologies from IBM Design, Watson & Cloud Platform, IBM Research, GBS.
description: Document Best Practices, Tools, Methods and Runtimes used across IBM to produce text-based chatbots and speech-based chatbots and Virtual Personal Agents. Identify gaps (if any) that will prevent IBM from being best in the industry at rapid, cost-effective production of maintainable, scalable and secure agents.
problemStatement:
By 4Q2018, IBM can using skills that exist in sufficient numbers in the IBM engineering population, and with a time-line measured in weeks (or even days), create a text-centric or audio-centric chatbot for itself (IBM) or for any client… which is:
                                        a)	Performant and scalable
                                        b)	Uses the information it emits (text or audio) in an appropriate way that provides maximum clarity and consumability by the intended user population
                                        c)	Maintainable – those user utterances which were not understood or which were misunderstood by the previous version of the agent are now understood properly after a simple update-training of the agent
                                        d)	Can work in any of the languages that the Watson stack supports (i.e. English, Spanish, French, Arabic, Japanese, Korean, Portuguese, German)
                                        e)	Deliverable directly (through Watson UX services) or via channels such as Facebook Messenger, Microsoft Cortana, Google Now, Amazon Alexa, Apple Siri, Oracle, SAP Leonardo and equivalent services from TENCENT, Baidu, Samsung.
outcome:
Overall Goal: By Mid-2018, IBM is developing the tools and documenting the process so that 4Q2018 IBM can at a reasonable price, using skills that exist in sufficient numbers in the IBM engineering population, and with a time-line measured in weeks (or even days), create a text-centric or audio-centric chatbot for itself (IBM) or for any client… which is:
                                        a)	Performant and scalable
                                        b)	Uses the information it emits (text or audio) in an appropriate way that provides maximum clarity and consumability by the intended user population
                                        c)	Maintainable – those user utterances which were not understood or which were misunderstood by the previous version of the agent are now understood properly after a simple update-training of the agent
                                        d)	Can work in any of the languages that the Watson stack supports (i.e. English, Spanish, French, Arabic, Japanese, Korean, Portuguese, German)
                                        e)	Deliverable directly (through Watson UX services) or via channels such as Facebook Messenger, Microsoft Cortana, Google Now, Amazon Alexa, Apple Siri, Oracle, SAP Leonardo and equivalent services from TENCENT, Baidu, Samsung.
finalOutcome: While Watson & Cloud Platform along with Watson IoT were focused on Inquiry chatbots for customer self-service, we identified numerous other kinds of conversational agents that were needed by our customers, and a set of methods and tools which are missing in order to do conversational agents with this richness in short-time and with high quality.  This information has been shared with Watson Assistant offering management and selected engineering leaders, including substantial information about the need to support conversational agents where English is not the only language used in the conversation.  We have proposed 7 actions that could enrich Watson Assistant's early 2019 offering.  We have also gotten many groups in IBM which were unaware of their own "private tooling" efforts in direct conversation with each other.
participants: HELOISA CAROLINE DE SOUZA PEREIRA CANDELLO
closeValue: Practices that we are now calling "BotOps" are documented  -- iterative improvement of conversational agents using analytics of user experiences and resulting user loyalty -- were recommended and we mapped numerous tools in use in GBS and IBM Research that are candidates for an Enterprise version of Watson Assistant Studio.
ratingComments: Thank you for the great insights!  We will be using them to shape the offering and determine next steps in our roadmap along with our customer feedback.  Very helpful to have uncovered so many initiatives across IBM we can leverage and tie into as well.

title: Promote patent in CDMX and MTY
Discontinuous Manufacturing Processes
executiveChampionReason: Luis Raul is the Storage & Appliances Eng Director who is sponsoring this project
description: Manufacturing Discontinuous processes
problemStatement: In the current Manufacturing test process for Power Systems, Storage and Appliances there is a lot of variability and uncertainty due to the high complexity of the configurations and the unpredictable behavior of the interruptions within the process. There are millions of records available that at this point are not analyzed, which represents a great opportunity to use cognitive and predictive tools.
outcome: Create a Analytic and Cognitive application that can understand, analyze, predict and learn from that complex environment in a simple manner, including the following concepts: Cycle times, Test cell occupancy, Variability, Efficiency, Failures and interruptions, Prediction Certainty, using bluemix services and Analytics tools.
finalOutcome:
The DMP provided three major functionalities
                                                                                1. Cognos analytics dashboards that provides real time information for test cell efficiency and usage.
                                                                                2. Test Cell Occupancy calculations and management through big data analysis and presented in a Cognos Analytics Dashboard. The information is presented by product family and model, in a weekly trends, by day or even by hour. The TCO provides test trends and breaks the test cycle into all the elements that adds time to the test cycle time, like attentions, debug and waiting time, among other factors, that allow the technical team and production team to have a better understanding of the test process.
                                                                                3. A predictive model base on TCO inputs and some other critical information gather from the MFS data bases. This predictive model show the trends for an specific family of products (Brazos as an example), machine type model and by specific configuration, with an accuracy of 80% using data science methodologies and big data management in a bluemix environmet, showing the result in a Cognos Analytics dashboards
participants: Oscar de la Torre del Rio
closeValue: Predictive tool for a very complex process.
publicationDescription: The Discontinuous Manufacturing Process or DMP is a tool designed to provide insight information about the Power Systems test process in Guadalajara, like test cells efficiency and usage, TCO or Test Cell Occupancy, and a predictive model based on data science methodologies.
ratingComments: This project " Discontinuous Manufacturing Process "  meet our expectations in two dimensions.   a) It was great based on the new set of technical skills that was generated  and b ) The POC was implemented for one Power server family , end  user saw the benefits of this predictive tool, but the effort to replicate or deploy it on the reminder power server families is huge and this put in question the affordability of this tool.     Great experience and great technical knowledge.

title: Towards an End-to-End ambient AI for Medical Intelligence
problemStatement: Today, the Healthcare ecosystem is at turning point: the system is under pressure because of an increasingly ageing society, new epidemic challenges and a growing gap in healthcare assistance between developed and developing societies. This growing pressure impacts fundamentally the quality of Healthcare service provided by clinicians who spend more time on administrative and clerical tasks than on the patients themselves. But Artificial Intelligence is posed to change this situation: the Next Generation Healthcare system empowered by virtual assistant, ambient voice to text transcription, images recognition for fast and accurate diagnostic and automatic healthcare path recommendation will bring back the medical staff to focus on their primary concern, which is the patients well being. Of course, there are still many technical challenges before getting to this ideal scenario, but the scientific community has already done major leaps in different disciplines in Machine Learning and Ambient AI. The task of this initiative will be to envision the Next Generation Healthcare system, identify the technical breakthroughs in AI that could be leveraged to this task and pinpoint the not-yet-addressed challenges while proposing potential solutions.
outcome:
Business Outcome: a roadmap that provides Healthcare organisations WW with a 360 degree view of the Next Generation Medical Ecosystem empowered by AI and new technologies and the major challenges to get there. 
Technical outcome: for each major step in the Healthcare pathway,  we propose a set of Machine Learning techniques that could be leveraged to address a particular pain point and optimise the quality of medical service. The technical  outcome should encompass a bibliography study of ongoing research, a description of candidate algorithms and the challenges to address for these algorithms to be deployed within the Healthcare system.

This study will produce a set of best practices to help practitioners directly affected by reproducibility issues:

title: Education series on the various Operating Systems that run on IBM Z Systems
executiveChampionReason: Barry oversees a large team in IBM Z Software. His team is often involved in making the right offering to the various IBM clients, especially when it comes to the issue of choosing the operating system that is the most suited for the client needs.
description: This initiative will host several education sessions on various operating systems that run on IBM Z systems. The goal of these sessions would be to help participants understand the different operating systems, especially as they pertain to running on Z machines. A further objective would be to allow the participants to gain insights in comparing and contrasting the strengths and characteristics of different operating system that run on Z.
problemStatement:
The IBM Z systems run on several different operating systems including z/OS, z/VM z/TPF, and z/Linux. Each operating system has its unique strengths and characteristics, and the IBM Offering Management teams work closely with our customers to choose the operating system(s) that are best suited for their needs.
                                                                                                                        
                                                                                                                        The purpose of this initiative is to help the Mid-Hudson Valley IBM community to
                                                                                                                        •	Learn about the various Operating Systems that run on IBM Z Series.
                                                                                                                        •	Understand the strengths of each operating system and gain better insights into choosing one versus another.
                                                                                                                        •	Foster a collaborative environment that allows the teams to share / leverage best practices from their peers and SMEs.
outcome:
This initiative will deliver a series of education sessions that provide the history, overview, core concepts, evolution, and strengths of various operating systems (z/OS, Z/VM, etc...) that run on Z systems. A set of subject matter experts (SMEs) will be providing these education sessions in a face to face setting in IBM Poughkeepsie. Speakers of these sessions will share insights on the reasons for choosing the different operating systems, and also share some of the client success stories.
                                                                                                                        
                                                                                                                        Several seminars will be organized between May and October 2019 as part of this initiative, and the event will be widely publicized to allow for wider participation. The sessions will be video recorded and made available to all IBMers, and a blog post will be written at the conclusion of this initiative.
finalOutcome:
As part of this initiave, a total of 3 education sessions were given. The first one was on z/OS Part 1. This event was presented by Luisa F Martinez and Ryan Rawlins, and was held on May 21, 2019. The second session in the series was z/OS Part 2, and it was presented by Andrew C Hicks & Edward B Pryor on Jul 25, 2019. The last session was on Virtualization. This talk was given by Robert R Rogers  on Oct 30, 2019. The sessions were held in the Building 705 Cafeteria in IBM Poughkeepsie, and were video recorded.  

All these sessions were well attended, and provided a good overview of the different Operating Systems on z systems.
closeValue: Quoting Nelso Mandela: "Education is the most powerful weapon which you can use to change the world." -- and this initiative followed that Mantra.
ratingComments: Good/important content, delivered/executed very well!

title: ** COVID-19 ** | Global broker for managing flow of PPEs from suppliers and excess capacity locations to COVID-19 hot spots across the globe.
executiveChampionReason: Auto Selected from Admin Page
description: This is an initiative for an intelligent global broker for managing and coordinating supply chain for essential medical supplies and resources just-in-time where these are needed.
problemStatement: COVID-19 and similar infectious disease pandemics spread with exponential speed with within a population and overwhelm the local healthcare systems very quickly. During the first wave, we witnessed a mad scramble for PPEs, respirators, test equipment and even for qualified healthcare workers. Some of this was driven by actual needs, some by anticipated worst case scenarios and by fear leading to hoarding. Large inefficiencies and supply imbalances were observed. But the spread of disease across the globe is not instantaneous. With intelligent tracking and modeling of the disease, it is possible to manage and direct the essential supplies and healthcare skills just-in-time where these are needed. This requires (1) tracking and modeling the spread of the disease across the globe, (2) global inventory of essential equipment, test and treatment capabilities, and human resources, and (3) global production capacity of key supplies.  IBM is uniquely positioned to develop and deploy such a global broker that can coordinate the effort across the global and help nations in controlling the spread of COVID-19 without overwhelming local healthcare systems. This initiative is to develop the architecture of such a global system and provide a deployment plan.

title: Providing best practices to families impacted by Autism
executiveChampionReason: John Kelly, SVP Cognitive Solutions and Research, is supporting this initiative at corporate level.
description: The key objective is to define how to provide best practices to families that have children/relatives diagnosed with Autism Spectrum Disorder.
problemStatement:
Autism Spectrum Disorder (ASD) is a long-term handicap that deeply affects families. It requires a constant and costly effort to help and integrate the autistic people in the society. As of today:
                                                                                                                        
                                                                                                                        1) causes of autism are not known,
                                                                                                                        2) there is no defined, assessed and validated approach on how to build a sustainable ecosystem and collaborative platform to address this problem. Most knowledge is empirical.
                                                                                                                        3) parents are often left alone on how to proceed with their child once they are diagnosed with ASD (what to do, how to behave, whom to consult, how to get advice and a clear roadmap of actions for the near, mid-term and long-term, what are the risk factors, etc.). In this initiative, we will focus on how to provide best practices for parents having a child or relative diagnosed with ASD.
outcome:
This study will:
                                                                                                                        1) deliver a POV on Autism at IBM corporate level by focusing at first on how to provide best practices to improve quality of family life,
                                                                                                                        2) define support material for directions to move forward on how IBM could get these ideas into Watson Health,
                                                                                                                        3) allow to better understand how it could be replicated to other mental health issues as Autism embeds a lot of cognitive challenges,
                                                                                                                        4) gather thought leadership on Autism.
finalOutcome: Autism is a major concern for the society and family representing a huge and expanding market. We defined and validated by parents a high-level description of a machine learning model that could deliver personalized program (and recommendations) to autistic person and people in charge or in contact with him/her. This approach puts the person's context such as his complex personality and his environment of life at the center throughout the lifetime including his abilities and challenges. This personalized approach and continuous learning are not restricted to autism and could be proposed to any chronic or non-chronic disease as well as other domains (education, employment, etc.). The market is large as it is covering many cognitive challenges and it could be the foundation to propose custom-tailored services. The study also discussed about building Collaborative Platform for data creation and data sharing between parents, autistic persons, experts, researchers and health professionals. Our next steps are mainly 1) to start a more in-depth data architecture study evaluating data sources, type, quality, security constraints, etc. to measure final model feasibility 2) to look how this approach could be integrated into the Watson Health cognitive services
closeValue: A Machine Learning Model determining autistic person’s uniqueness, strengths and weaknesses and delivering a continuous improvement to personalized support

title: How to unlock the power of customer's Supply Chain data with IBM Sterling Supply Chain Insights with Watson
executiveChampionReason: At the time we started the piece of work, Andrea Agnello was the Director of the Industry Solutions in Italy and he owns a strong experience in Supply Chain projects.
description: Short Description: An agile supply chain is key to an agile business. One of the greatest supply chain hurdles is a lack of transparency that makes it difficult to predict and proactive manage disruptions. The objective of this study is to explore the supply chain topic through of use cases, by identifying how IBM Sterling Supply Chain offerings can help driving the client's conversation. Every supply chain is unique, depending by customer industry, as well as inside the same customer environment can exists multiple supply chain types. If we think of the very actual topic like circular economy and green hype, the waste management companies will be pushed to increase efficiency in the recycling process. We analyzed this use case in the study and describe how Supply Chain Insights solution may help.
problemStatement: An agile supply chain is key to an agile business. This topic is key to open conversations with customers and we have a set of solutions that can be leveraged to help our customers to improve their business results. One of the greatest supply chain hurdles is a lack of transparency that makes it difficult to predict and proactive manage disruptions.
outcome: Provide a document and a demo giving an introduction of Supply Chain topic and may help to drive the conversation with clients. Starting from real customers' examples, the study doesn't claim to only be a technical description of the usage of Sterling Supply Chain Insights with Watson offering, but aims to be a cue for starting a customer conversation where Circular Economy is a business target, partially or completely. In particular,we believe that in a moment like now in which disruption is essential, anyone should make the effort to think outside the box, in order to apply current solutions and technologies also to a completely new scope and environment. Moreover, this piece of work demonstrates that IBM Cloud strategy owns all the elements to easily and efficiently modernize applications and infrastructures of clients, whatever industry they belong to.
finalOutcome: IBM specific solution for Integrated Waste Management and Circular Economy, fitting in IBM Journey to Cloud strategy.
closeValue: Initiative shows an innovative and disrupting usage of Supply Chain Insights solution with the aim to with the aim of attacking a new market sector and seizing new opportunities
ratingComments: Very interesting work with interesting implementation opportunities

title: MCMP Solutioning Guide 101
executiveChampionReason: Sean Brady is the VP of the IBM Cloud Solutioning Center - West and owns the solution design of several complex deals that build on MCMP. Archana Vemulapalli is the GM responsible for the Infrastructure Services Offering Strategy, Management and Development and owns with her team the solution guidance for MCMP.
description: Given the nature of the IBM Multi-Cloud Management Platform (MCMP) as a framework, the aim of this initiative is to develop a repeatable, consistent approach for designing and successfully delivering solutions involving MCMP in order to create an improved user experience for the Client, while lowering the cost of building those solutions.
problemStatement: MCMP is fairly new as an offering and its multi-component, multi-layered architecture comes with an inherent complexity that prevents a fast and easy adoption into solutions for Clients. There needs to be an easy to consume guidance for use by Cloud Solution Leaders and practitioners in the field how to design and deliver reliable and sustainable solutions using MCMP in a short term time frame.
outcome:
The initiative will deliver a comprehensive solution guide how to create design and deliver solutions involving MCMP. A MCMP solution template will be provided as a supplement to the MCMP solution guide. The MCMP solution template will be reviewed by the Cloud Solution Center and approved for use in the deal certification process by Cloud Solution Board.  The MCMP solution guide and template will be verified using selected reference engagements before their final release.
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                        
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                In detail, the MCMP solution guide will address the following solution aspects: (1) Value Proposition of MCMP, positioning in 14-in-4, (2) Identification of user roles of Client and the delivery organization(s), (3) Mapping use cases from Clients on MCMP capabilities, (4) Design of the solution architecture, identification of interfaces and component interactions, (5) Security and Compliance, (6) Solution sizing, (7) Delivery planning (RACI, project plan), (8) Costing.
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                        
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                The MCMP solution template is intended to document at a minimum: (1)  Use cases and capability of MCMP selected for the solution, (2)  Architecture decisions related to the use of the specific MCMP components, (3) Integration and Interfaces used in the solution, (4) Customizations to be applied for the solution, (5) Solution Sizing, (6) Deployment and Delivery Model.
finalOutcome: As a result of this AoT initiative, an easy-to-use solution design guide for MCMP has been published to Lighthouse under ibm.biz/mcmp101. The initiative involved multiple members of the global Cloud Solutioning Centers (CSC) and engaged them together with the broader MCMP team and with SMEs from other IBM organizations. The initiative gathered various materials about MCMP, broadened the knowledge about MCMP and created deeper awareness about MCMP across CSC, the GTS Service Integration Hub (SIH) and in context with Red Hat. With the solution design guide at hand, IT architects and Solution Leaders are now equipped to have a quick start with MCMP, understand the MCMP Solution Design Process and learn how to configure the MCMP solution for sizing and costing and which solution artifacts have to be created prior to solution certification.
closeValue: Created an easy-to-use guide to the solution design for MCMP and increased the knowledge about MCMP in the wider IBM community.
ratingComments: Also communicated outcome well  to the team

title: Top Trends in Artificial Intelligence & Machine Learning
executiveChampionReason: Martin Fleming is the original requester behind this initiative idea.  He sent an email to Bill Chamberlin on December 10, 2019 asking for the AoT's point of view around AI/ML/DL.
description: This goal of this initiative is to create and document AoT's point of view on the current and emerging trends in Artificial Intelligence and Machine Learning
problemStatement: In his role, Martin Fleming regularly is asked for a point of view on where AI/ML/DL is currently and where it is heading.   Before this initiative, the AoT did not have a point of view updated for January 2020, so the timing was perfect to create such a point of view.
outcome:
This short-term outcome will be a slide deck with a list of 10 trends in AI/ML.  The deck will be set up as initially as a one-on-one discussion document vs. a "one-on-many" client presentation deck.  The deck can then be used by IBMers and AoT Members to harvest ideas and content from the deck to be used in presentation decks they develop and customize for their use...  both internally and externally.    
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                        
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                        The overall outcome is to demonstrate value to others by having a thought leadership point of view on AI/ML... both current and future.
finalOutcome:
- Martin Fleming was able to leverage this research and PoV as input for his presentation at the Open Group Meeting in San Antonio at the end of January 2020.  Bill Chamberlin also spent time reviewing Martin's presentation and providing feedback prior to the Open Group Meeting. 
                                                                                - The deck has been published on Bluemine and as of February 13, 2020 it has been viewed 1,973 times.   
                                                                                - The deck provides a point of view from the AoT perspective on important trends in AI that should be addressed across IBM organizations, but most importantly by IBM Research Scientists and those across IBM in Technical roles related to AI and Data Science.  
                                                                                - The framework presented in the deck (Preparing, Advancing, Trusting, Scaling, Distributing) attempts to integrate both how IBM Research explains the work to be done around AI (Advancing, Trusting, Scaling) as well as how our marketing and sales teams go to market (e.g. the "AI Ladder")
                                                                                - Bill Chamberlin presented the deck on a recent Data Science Governance Board meeting https://w3.ibm.com/w3publisher/data-scientist-profession/governance-board
closeValue: The AoT now has a published point of view on the important technology trends and critical research that must be carried out in order to enable the successful adoption of Artificial Intelligence solutions that will benefit society.I
publicationDescription:
This deck was created as a result of an IBM Academy of Technology initiative to identify technology trends that will impact the future of Artificial Intelligence and Machine Learning.   The primary audience for this deck are those in technical, R&D and Offering Management roles. This deck discusses 10 important areas that will impact the successful adoption of Artificial Intelligence (AI) in the coming years.  The trends discussed highlight specific areas where tech improvements in AI technology will be required.  
                                                                                
                                                                                The framework presented in the deck (Preparing, Advancing, Trusting, Scaling, Distributing) attempts to integrate both how IBM Research explains the work to be done around AI (Advancing, Trusting, Scaling) as well as how our marketing and sales teams go to market (e.g. the "AI Ladder")

title: Nordic TEC - Data Platform
executiveChampionReason: Allan Coulter was selected as executive champion. This subject is in its nature both technical and business and very broad. It requires someone that can see the problem from many different perspectives as well as see the business value of data in many different perspectives both for our clients and for IBM.
description: The data transformation, going from Data warehouse to Modern Data Platform
problemStatement:
Today Data is the new Oil. It is the natural resource that is being used to drive both business optimisation and efficiency. To achieve this objective we however need to have the right Data Architecture in place.
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                        This Data Architecture is in itself driving a transformation from classic data warehousing approaches to a shift towards open-source data platforms that can consume data from proprietary and external sources. So most of our customers see an urgent need to modernize and transform their data and analytics landscape. They see the data layer as the foundation for analytics and AI, but also for automation and transformation of operational processes and are setting data high up on the agenda. We therefore as IBM need to define the right approach, to exploit this transformation.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                         
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                        There is a need for alignment on this subject across IBM LOB’s and across different aspects e.g. business transformation, cloud and infrastructure, software and applications, data and integration architecture, governance and ownership etc.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                         
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                        There is also a need to understand and to be able to compare different offers from our competitors/partners like Google, Amazon and Azure, as well as Accenture, EY etc.
outcome: This initiative aims to produce a cross IBM LOB description and point of view of the current situation of our customers, including typical and common questions and starting points relating to the data transformation. The initiative also aims to produce an overview and description of the different products, solutions and offers from different IBM LOB’s in the data area and how they relate to each other (if applicable). Finally, an overview of different significant IBM competitors and cloud providers and how their offers in the data space are positioned to our clients should be described (subject to limitation/prioritization).

outcome:

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                        * Real-time status and details of impacted components and recovery status on ongoing, on-hold and resolved issues with filters to see historical outage details.
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                        * Improved recovery time, timely communication and status reporting resulting in reduced MTTR and SLA penalties. 
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                        * Improved Client Experience and reflect positively on the Delivery NPS score.
finalOutcome:
Standardization: A common dashboard for internal (IBM) users to subscribe to preferences for receiving CritSit Notifications using multiple filters and selection criteria, which can be directly linked to user profile using w3 ID/credentials.
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                        Benefits: The subscription model for receiving CritSit notifications, helps with the following:
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                        a) More focussed notifications based on user preferences and removes both clutter and risk of missing out on critical updates
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                        b) Ability to receive notifications via different means i.e. email, Slack and mobile
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                        c) Enables for future for direct customer notifications
closeValue: Greatest Impact:  Personalized Notification and Dashboard view with integration with CritSitWiz for better and meaningful user experience based on user profile preference.

description: IBM Skills Academy training agreement with the Supreme Council of Egyptian Universities
problemStatement:
We have been delivering IBM Skills Academy in universities in Egypt for the past 5  years working with individual universities and focusing on students and fresh grads. 
In an effort to centralize efforts, and ensure the reach out is structured and disseminates to all regions in Egypt, the UR team in Egypt has reached out to the Supreme Council of Egyptian Universities to deliver the training to faculty staff in all governments universities (focusing on Faculties on Computer Systems and Information).
outcome:
In 1Q 2020, IBM Egypt University Relations trained and certified 300+ faculty staff members in 24+ universities across Egypt leveraging IBM MEA & Global University programs.

Each university was offered 4 IBM Skills Academy tracks of 160 training hours from emerging technologies (AI, Cloud, Big Data, Predictive Analytics, IoT, and Blockchain). The trained faculty staff can now enable thousands of university students across Egypt on our latest technologies.

We completed 20 training sessions in Cairo, Alexandria, Luxor, and Mansoura. It was an extraordinary experience to teach in various regions - meeting academics to exchange ideas on  bridging the gap between academic curricula and global IT job market need.

This milestone comes as a result of an MoU signed in 4Q 2019 with the Ministry of Higher Education for a strategic partnership  to train academia across Egyptian universities and enable them to embed technologies within their curricula.

This collaboration adds to our continuous promotion of IBM footprint in academia and in youth capacity building in Egypt; where we have trained more than 13,000 university students and 1500 faculty members in over 50 higher institutions. title: Measuring impact of OCR on word embedding models like word2vec or BERT
problemStatement: AI relies on a large pool of knowledge to pre-train its word embedding models.  We ingest million of documents to build these models.  Often times you can pre-train using wikipedia or domain specific like on-line medical encyclopedia.  However, sometimes you are limited to documents in picture PDF formats that requires OCR (Optical Character Reader) to convert to text that AI models can read.  OCR technology, like image recognition, is far from perfect generating misspelled text that can negatively influence the quality of AI model training.
outcome: We want to assess how OCR text output quality can impact the performance of word embedding models like word2vec or BERT.  For example, count the misspelled words or 'gibberish' per page that is used to pre-train the models then measure the performance using various metrics like precision and recall.

title: Engineering Week in IBM Romania
executiveChampionReason: Hary as leading Europe CICs, technical communities.
description: Schedule a series of tech talks delivered using Webex, one hour per day, during one week, with various tech presentations focused on real project architecture examples and the problems they solve. The goal of this initiative is to raise the knowledge of real architecture examples and their usage within the various projects, offer examples of dos and donts above the theoretical aspects, and discuss lessons learned and trends for the future. Each presentation will last 45 minutes, leaving 15 minutes for participants to interact. The presentations will be done by architects in the domains mentioned below, and will be focud on the problem that architecture is solving and the solutions considered. 1. eCommerce web application 2. Cognitive chatbots 3. Liberty mobile microservices architecture  4. Devops SRE 5. Enterprise application migration
problemStatement: Especially now in the new working from home reality the opportunity to interact with other projects and learn from their mistakes and success stories is very limited. outcome: Increase experience through real examples, stronger tech community.
finalOutcome:
During the course of one week, 25-29 May, one hour each day, we have scheduled a technical presentation of an architecture, with real examples of the problem it solves, and lessons learned from the implementation. 
Mon, 92 participants, we discussed about Cognitive Assistants and the implementation at Siemens  
Tue, 82 participants, we reviewed an eCommerce monolithic architecture and its path towards decoupling
Wed, 72 participants, site reliability engineering was presented
Thu, 91 participants, we discussed about application migration in an enterprise setting
Fri, 65 participants, Mobile Liberty Architecture and how it can be tailored was presented

ratingComments: Frankly, I did not expect such a large presence... congrats to the initiators and many thanks to the speakers!

title: Improving IBM's Technical Eminence in Japan Academia - Phase 2
executiveChampionReason: Dr. Kazushi Kuse is a CTO of IBM Japan and an AoT Sponsor Executive. He has strong relationship with Japan academia including key academic societies and universities. He used to lead Research and Development of IBM Japan (a.k.a. Tokyo Laboratory), so has strong influence to IBM researchers and engineers.
description: Continuing our previous effort to improve IBM's technical presence in Japan academia.
problemStatement: IBM needs to improve its presence in academia to get IBM recognized and to hire high quality talents.
outcome:
Increase IBM's technical eminence in Japan academic by (1) holding internal seminars to encourage IBM engineers and researchers to publish more papers, (2) making presentations and lectures in domestic conferences and Japanese universities, (3) contributing to conference committees and academic society boards, and (4) having academic society members recognized with an advanced membership grade (e.g. senior/distinguished members). 
                                                                                How to track the outcomes: (1) Speak at Lab-wide social gathering events and other occasions to promote external publications, and identify potential mentees who are interested in publishing papers and need help. (2) Identify important academic conferences and match-make with potential speakers from the mentees, and identify academic contribution opportunities through collaborative programs between IBM and Japanese universities and match-make with our resources. (3) Keep track of important positions (terms/vacancy for steering committee positions , etc) in strategic academic societies and match-make with potential resources. (4) Keep track of the membership duration of strategic academic societies for each mentee and other identified technical resources to encourage them to apply for an advanced grade when its conditions are met.
finalOutcome:
The members held internal seminars to encourage IBM engineers and researchers to publish more papers, using Lab-wide social gathering events and other occasions to promote external publications.
The members made presentations and lectures in domestic conferences and Japanese universities, and also started a collaborative programs between IBM and a Japanese university.
The members contributed to conference committees and academic society boards, like as board members and PC members, and also supported other IBM people doing similar contributions.
The members helped people to be recognized from external societies in Japan.  Especially, a member received the 1st IPSJ Research and Engineering Award, which is an evidence that IBM's Eminence was increasing in Japan Adacemia.
See a BoxNote https://ibm.ent.box.com/notes/601240650735 for more detailed outcomes.
closeValue: The members made several internal presentations to encourage IBM engineers to publish more external papers, made external presenations and lectures, served as committee members in important areas, all of which helped improving IBM's Technical Eminence in Japan Academia and resulted in a member receiving an award from an external society.

title: Develop skills in statistic and predictive models.
executiveChampionReason: Director of the program <Spectrum Scale> from where we are collecting the data to generate the Analytics models.
description: Mastering the statistics and predictive skills in technical people in the Data Scientist career path.
problemStatement:
Data science is one of the IBM hot skills. Several IBMers are willing to start the data science Path to fulfill IBM client needs but there is not enough projects with real data where these skills can be applied.
Performance  analysis  is  one  of  the  most  important  aspects during  the  testing processes of  any software-defined storage product and it does generate a lot of data that is normally misused. 
                                                                                
Providing   visual   insights   about   the   performance   results   is fundamental  for  the  decision-making process.  Showing historical or aggregated data through a series of graphics  could significantly enhance the performance evaluations.
outcome:
The objective of this initiative is to increase the skills of statistic and predictive models which are fundamentals to become a data scientist.   Through the creation of interactive dashboards that visually present data obtained from the performance evaluation of a software-defined storage product. The participants, who are volunteers from  mostly GDL site and belong to different BUs ( Finance & Operations, GBS, System Storage, System Technical Operations) will significantly increase their skills by implement analytics in real data and validate their models with feedback from people who generate and consume the data. 
                                                                                                                                                                                                         
As business value, this  will  help  to  improve  the  efficiency  of  the  overall performance  evaluation process and strength  the  decision-making based in the data displayed in dashboards, removing most of the manual steps. This will transform the current process for performance evaluation in the development process for Software-Defined Storage products like Spectrum Scale, and this could be extended to any other software running performance evaluation as part of their development process.
finalOutcome:
Streamline the process for generate a performance evaluation report. Reduced from 1 day to 5 minutes the time tooks to a performance analyst to process, format and publish the performance evaluation report..  This represent aprox 20% of 1 PY for a Performance Analyst. 
- Transformed the Performance Evaluation results into data simple and accessible, allowing querying to produce tailored views. 
- Enabled dashboards with graphics that provide visual aids to the performance analyst as support in the decision-making process. 
- Around 15 IBMers were able to apply and increase their BD&A skills focused in the analytic and visualization methods, as well increased their eminence by generate Intellectual Property:  
1 international publication ( In Spanish) in the Revista Ibérica de Sistemas y Tecnologías de Información: http://www.risti.xyz/issues/risti36.pdf Page 50.
1 disclosure submitted with the proposal of a methodology for store, classify and recover expert knowledge.
closeValue: Improve the efficiency of the Spectrum Scale core Performance Regression by adding dashboards with visualization of performance trends and insights through the implementation of statistics, predictive and descriptive models. Increase the technical eminence impacting around 15 IBMers that applied analytics methods and models.
ratingComments: Very pleased with this project and the value it brings to ESS.  This is a partcularly nice piece of work given that it has been done completely in the team's spare time as an extra assignment.  The team collaborated well and did valuable work for Spectrum Scale.

title: IoT and Security
executiveChampionReason:
Julian is the Leader of the BU Security in Europe and has an immense interest in supporting this initiative to create more business in this area.
                                                                                                                                                                                                        John Cohn is an IBM fellow and has been the previous technical leader of the Watson IoT HQ. With his acclaimed expertise and experience, he would be able to promote the topic further.
description: This initiative aims to create a security framework for IoT, OT and IIoT in which security architectures can be derived for different IoT, OT and IIoT use cases.  These architectures should merge IoT and IIoT solutions with IBM Security features and technologies.
problemStatement:
The IBM IoT and Security BU's have created Point of View documents in 2015/16 on IoT Security. Other initiatives have created reference architectures, e.g. IoT-A, or baseline security recommendations for critical infrastructures from ENISA. Since then, the IoT, OT and IIoT space had been dramatically developed and increased. IBM has gathered more and more experience in these areas, especially with the Watson IoT unit. 
                                                                                                                                                                                                        There is no security framework which can be used to create a security architecture for specific IoT use cases.
outcome:
This initiative will create IBM PoVs and intellectual property on IoT, OT and IIoT security to demonstrate IBM’s leadership in this area and to be efficiently and effectively used in IBM’s IoT use cases. 
                                                                                                                                                                                                        The study will be created through 3 sprints with 4-6 weeks each. The first sprint will create a taxonomy for IoT, OT and IIoT. The second sprint will take three different use cases (pilots) to derive security architectures for these pilots. We have chosen one use case each from the strategic topics in Watson IoT: robotics in environment (related to manufacturing), smart train (related to transportation) and building insights (related to facilities management). The third and final sprint will take the results from the previous sprints and create a security framework for security architectures for IoT, OT and IIoT with the regard to the taxonomy.
finalOutcome:
The AoT Study focused on the challenges faced by different areas in the IoT space, looking for similarities and differences, developing security architecture(s). Key areas addressed through the study includes: 
To create a security architecture for Smart Building Management Systems, actuators were added to the IBM TRIRIGA Building Insights system in the assessed scenarios for the completion of the security considerations. The results are for a generic Smart Building Management System but can be applied to the IBM TRIRIGA Building Insights system to create a specific security architecture.
Robotics have to be viewed from 2 different angles: makers’ and operators’ point of view. Security perspective of both views is different, same as threat consideration and risk perception. The makers are often seen as being a threat for operators, not really considering operators security needs. This leads in terms of security to even conflicting targets that need to be considered. 
The majority of automatic train control systems used worldwide are based on the European ATP/ERTMS (automatic train protection/European rail trafﬁc management system). Through the study the business risks around jamming incident affecting GPS data and monitoring has been reviewed thus deriving a security architecture that addresses the risks and threats.
closeValue: For all three areas, the study gave best in class technical insight, enabling IBM to share knowledge across. Consulting teams can faithfully argue based on findings in other areas, emphasize importance of dedicated security controls and comment on impact of future trends as well as enhance current offerings.

title: Next Generation Media Platform
executiveChampionReason: Mr. Ramieri leads a team of technical experts that deliver market-leading capabilities to clients in emerging technology: Software Defined Infrastructure, Hybrid Cloud, Big Data, Workload Management and Data Movement, Cognitive, Blockchain. industryName: Telecom Media and Entertainment Industry Affiliate
description: M&E Industry has been shifting to UHD video technology. This study will assess requirements and provide a point of view on how to solution for it.
problemStatement:
M&E industry is shifting to Ultra High Definition (UHD) video technology as 4K or 8K. Higher performant systems including higher speed networks are required. It leads the customers to hybrid cloud/multi-cloud services, and IBM is ideal cloud vendor to develop this offering.

3. Link technologies or products as an integrated business workflow

Development of a reference architecture will enable solution teams
finalOutcome:
The report describes how IBM helps the M&E customers run high cost performance businesses shifting to the Hybrid/Multi Cloud environment with the following IBM products or technologies:
•	IBM Spectrum Scale provides a single file namespace across many operations through a workflow optimizing storage cost. 
•	IBM Flash and Tape (FLAPE) Storage provides a long term and secured data archive. 
•	IBM Cloud Object Storage provides a scalable object storage suitable for unstructured data
•	Aspera provides high speed data transfer on both file transfer and streaming
•	IBM AI services with Deep Learning and Machine Learning technologies
•	IBM Edge Computing powered by 5G enables a quick and rich data transaction
•	AREMA orchestrates the above and provides a value-added services
The concept of Next Generation Media Platform gives the IBM colleagues who are working for IBM Media and Entertainment business how IBM’s strength is promoted in the same business view point as the customers, where IBM has a great advantage against competitors that IBM has wide variety technologies and products that covers end to end in the customers business flow. title: Payment FinTechs as the Canary in the Mine
executiveChampionReason: Chae An (Vice President, CTO, Financial Services Sector) and Laura Smith (Vice President Technical Sales, North America) lead teams of Subject Matter Experts responsible for bringing industry perspective and spotting emerging trends to position and promote IBM solutions and products with our clients.
description: The purpose of this initiative is to better understand how market disruptors such as FinTechs are impacting IBM's top financial services clients as well as what new markets are being created in the process.  Lessons learned can be used to shape IBM's offerings across various industries.
problemStatement: Many industries, including the Financial Services industry, are facing digital disruption today.  FinTechs currently focused on providing new global payment solutions and building new commerce ecosystems could provide an early indication of what digital disruption will do to other industries. This will allow IBM to identify  new market opportunities globally.
outcome:
This initiative will identify new opportunities for IBM to:
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                1. Co-create with traditional IBM Financial Services clients on cross-industry platforms in the cloud.
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                2. Provide value-add business and technology services to FinTech companies leveraging IBM Cognitive Cloud at higher margins.
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                3. Leapfrog the cognitive cloud competition (Microsoft, Amazon, Google) by providing new SaaS offerings targeting Financial Services companies.
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                4. Partner with VCs who drive technology choice decisions for the startups they fund.
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                5. Capitalize on similar disruptive market opportunities within other industries globally.
finalOutcome:
It is imperative that IBM and Red Hat address the FinTech segment immediately as competition from big digital platforms companies (Google, Amazon, Ant Financial, and Tencent) is currently leveraging business and technical expertise to disrupt and modernize the financial services industry. They have created new platforms grounded in expertise gained deploying Multi-Sided Platforms touching consumers and businesses at scale. They already have the trust of their users and partners, as well as implicit permission to expand their reach into financial services directly or by partnering with incumbent financial institutions. 
Moreover, they are expanding their reach into technology services by providing cloud-based services and innovative applications to the incumbent banks. Their strategy aims to circumvent the traditional enterprise services providers by playing a controlling role on the technology side of the platform. 
To respond to “always on, just in time, optimal cost” expectations, the new “hybrid” IBM platform needs to be designed on the following Cognitive principles: “sense and respond” to events beyond platform boundaries, “algorithm-driven” and less “human labor-intensive” through advanced automation. Moreover, it would be managed as a new “Cognitive Business” at IBM.
closeValue: Identify a new approach and offerings to attract and retain FinTechs to IBM on a new Cognitive Platform.
publicationDescription:
With the right resources, some FinTechs have the potential to leapfrog both Financial Services incumbents and their technology providers who are slow to catch up with the “always-on, just in time, optimal price” client expectations in our era. IBM/RedHat can use the new understanding of FinTechs’ behavior and the state of their influence in Financial services, to plan their participation (reseller, input supplier, multi-sided platform, or a hybrid) in new ecosystems. 
There is a significant risk that by the time FinTechs reach an accelerated growth stage, it will be too late to attract them away from the top cloud incumbents. IBM and Red Hat need to design a strategy and a platform to attract FinTechs at all life stages. Moreover, by working with FinTechs and Financial Institutions early in their cloud adoption journey, IBM and Red Hat could provide critical advice to avoid re-platforming and re-architecting their solutions to scale securely and cost-effectively. Moreover, IBM could provide critical AI capabilities in support of business decision making as well as automation to take the burden from FinTechs while dealing with monetizing new assets, controlling costs, managing risks, attracting talent, acquiring new technologies.

title: Vulnerability management in DevSecOps
executiveChampionReason: Chris is a CTO and DE in the cloud security division. He is interested in this initiative of improving the DevSecOps process. Chris has been interested in pursuing this for some time and expressed his interest in supporting this initiative.  His expertise and perspectives will be invaluable as well. His expertise is very much needed for the successful completion of this project.
description: Development teams are often asked to use several application scanning tools. All of which generates an “n” number of vulnerabilities and tasks for developers. There is no way to correlate the task of all tools into one tool and limit the number of duplicate tasks generated by various tools. Services like SAST-DAST-IAST-Pentest. As a user of all 4 services - he is not getting a consolidated view of what actually needs to be fixed.
problemStatement: Services like SAST-DAST-IAST-Pentest. As a user of all 4 services - he is not getting a consolidated view of what actually needs to be fixed. For example, while SAST tells you how many vulnerabilities there are in the source code, DAST can tell you how many vulnerabilities are actually exploitable.
outcome:
A mechanism for the dev team to correlate scans from these tools and come with a short and actionable list of task which should be addressed and not a list of 100 tasks from each tool. Also, come up with high priority tasks that are based on high pentest findings as externally reported vulnerabilities trump almost everything else because they’re practically demonstrated and pose a reputational risk.
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                         The end product would be a framework that bakes directly into DevOps process with CI/CD pipeline. The framework would “import scans in various formats from different sources”. It would run an analysis on the imported scan. Remove duplicate items and prioritize the task.
finalOutcome: We successfully demonstrated need of aggregation of vulnerability data for developers and teams to efficiently manage prioritized risk to their applications/servers etc. The MVP1 provides a link to github repo. Interested parties can fork the code and play with the tool.
closeValue: This would empower developers to prioritize relevant threats and focus on important vulnerability remediations
publicationDescription:
To build secure software, start with clearly defined mandatory coding design. We can realize secure software when we apply these requirements in design. Security in design drives security in coding, integration, in delivery, and in operations..

Developers and architects always use new tools and techniques to ensure that our production systems remain secure after they're deployed. But what about the management of scans ? This paper would focus on importance of Vulnerability management in DevSecOps environment

title: Discontinuous Manufacturing Processes
problemStatement:
A manufacturing process where you have operations in a sequence, repetitive, standard times, is called a manufacturing line, like a car assembly line. There are other production processes where there is no production line, is just a production or manufacturing floor, where each order is different based on customer orders specifics, that drives in different assembly processes, cycle times, test procedures including packaging, with all this variability it is very complex to estimate the capacity needed, equipment, work force, among other resources.
This type of environments may drive that companies invest in extra capacity, just in case is needed, additional work force, equipment, rework procedures as well product conversions.
This is very ineffective, inefficient and costly.
outcome:
As solution the proposal is to develop a analytic tool that provides the insight to understand the behavior of the process and the different products and configurations build in the current production environment. With this information as the base, develop a AI tool to predict how the process will be with the current variables, like customer order load (product and configurations) current assembly and test cycles for each product type and configuration. This tool should be capable to provide a recommendations on how to manage the process, what capacity is required, how to manage the orders to obtain maximum efficiency and output, reducing product reconversions or reworks. 
There are tools already developed to manage continuous flow processes that can provide this type of information, but for discontinuous manufacturing process there are very few methodologies and probably none based on AI.

title: Enhancing Airline Interactions Post COVID-19
executiveChampionReason: He came up with the idea.
description: A point of view on how airlines can limit physical interaction between airline employees and customers without diminishing the customer experience, using digital transformation of key touchpoints in the airport and during flight.
problemStatement: Airlines around the world are all working to be ready for when everyone is ready to fly again. As countries relax restrictions, people are eager to safely return to many things that they love, including travel. The airlines that will be most successful will be the ones that can re-think and enhance the customer journey, while adjusting to the new normal of physical distancing. Travel is an experience that traditionally brings people in close contact. There are key interactions in the airport and in the cabin that will need to be re-thought, and then delivered at scale to ensure customers can travel both domestically and internationally. This initiative will provide more details around key use cases and provide clarity around what the future will look like.
outcome: This initiative will provide a point of view deck on what an airline can do in the airport and in the cabin to provide an experience with reduced or no touch between airline employees and travelers. The PoV will provide perspective on high touch experiences in the airport (e.g. check-in, gate, lounge) and the challenges of being in the cabin, highlighting what the experience looks like today, and where behaviours need to change to ensure physical distance. The document will highlight where the airline has strong self-service or other technology in place already and where there are gaps. The purpose is to provide focus areas for the airline to use as a starting point to re-imaging an experience that is not diminished but rather enhanced!
finalOutcome: This PoV deck provided important perspective and discussion points for clients around touchless experience around the gate. It has also springboarded discussions in hospitality and airports as well.
closeValue: Generated discussions and opportunity leads with multiple airlines.
ratingComments: Great teamwork in building this out. Have had amazing take-up by our clients.

description: TEC-J Showcase provides opportunities for TEC-J Working Groups to present their thoughts, best practices and innovative ideas that have been discussed in their study and researches with other TEC-J members in timely manner. problemStatement: Token Economy is gaining wide attention in various industries with its potential to change or disrupt existing ecosystems and create new ones. finalOutcome:

In her talk, CBDC (Central Bank Digital Currency) was introduced as a concrete example of innovation around currency system. As there are on going attempts to manage assets such as securities or real estates as token, market size of blockchain could significantly grow. SMEs (Subject Matter Experts) are still working on solving issues of blockchain technology to apply to various use cases including data security. A blockchain demo application developed by Blockchain Working Group was also demonstrated. Replay is available.
closeValue: Token Economy was gaining wide attention in various industries with its potential to change or disrupt existing ecosystems and to created new ecosystems.
