title: IBM Developer JumpStart Program
executiveChampionReason: Primary Executive Sponsor for the IBM Developer JumpStart Program
description: Early Professional Developer Track
problemStatement: In 2017, IBM launched the Developer JumpStart for early professional developers who started in 2017. The program help new hires acclimate to IBM, build their network of peers & mentors, learn new technologies and best practices, sharpen their skills as they participate in the Tech Challenge. Through the Tech Challenge, developers will form small teams and work on real business problems, guided by mentors and design coaches. With support from our Research, Development and HR executives, the success of this program relies heavily upon engagement from our technical staff including DEs, STSMs, RSMs, technical mentors, agile and design coaches. We need the development community, in particular, our technical and design staff to support this initiative:,- Sponsoring challenges for the Tech Challenge, a six-month challenge where the new hires will form small teams and work on real business problems as a stretch assignment. ,- Delivering Keynote Addresses at the Developer Slam talking about Cognitive, IoT, Blockchain, Machine Learning,- Run hands-on workshops at the Developer Slam,- Be technical mentors to support the Tech Challenge,- Provide design coaching to the new hire teams,- Deliver hands-on Agile Practice exercises at the Slam,- Deliver hands-on Design Thinking exercises at the Slam
outcome: The IBM Developer JumpStart program seeks to expose our new hires to a network of peers and mentors, introduce them to IBM's latest technologies and practices, generate excitement across the IBM Development Community, form a One IBM culture and make IBM a great place work.
finalOutcome: The IBM Developer JumpStart program has developed the skills of our early professional developers providing them guidance on user-focused outcomes through IBM Design Thinking, IBM technologies and best practices and guidance on the IBM Patent process. The IBM Developer JumpStart program has engaged hundreds of IBMers across North America and through the AoT initiative has reached Europe and Asia driving engagement and excitement across the IBM Development, Research and Design communities.
mainCollaborationURL: Face to Face Engagement and Virtual Collaboration
closeValue: The IBM Developer JumpStart program has brought together hundreds of IBMers across IBM Development, Design and Research communities to build the skills of our early professional developers, to help them discover IBM technologies and best practices and to build a network of peers and mentors driving engagement and excitement across the labs.
publicationDescription:
Launched in Q2 2017, the IBM Developer JumpStart program started as an on-boarding program to help acclimate our early professional developers to IBM, introducing them to IBM technologies and processes and helping our developers grow their skills while building a network of peers and mentors. 
                                        
                                        Two years later we are discovering the impact of the IBM Developer JumpStart program to be much greater than intended. Over 1600 early professional developers have been enrolled in the JumpStart program. They have attended 45 Developer Day on-boarding classes, 55 all day Developer Slam events, launched 282 TechChallenge projects and attended 16 Patent Circle workshops earning the developers over 1500 digital badges and lending to the submission of more than 750 patents!
                                        
                                        Through the AoT Initiative program, we have been able to extend our reach beyond North America by connecting with mentors and coaches in Europe and Asia in addition to the U.S. and Canada. Through all day events, patent mentoring and coaching to deliver user-focused outcomes, the IBM Developer JumpStart program is growing the skills of our early professional developers while driving engagement and excitement across the IBM Development, Design and Research communities across North America and beyond.
ratingComments: Different teams from start to finish, but overall think the initiative has been very positive.

title: Brainstorming session toolkits, emerging tech
executiveChampionReason: Bill LaFontaine was the executive champion for the original Brainstorming Toolkit Initiative and approved this follow-on Initiative. He is also the GM for Intellectual Property and a huge supporter of the WW Women Inventors Community.
description: Follow on Initiative from Brainstorming session toolkits, to create curated set of information regarding specific technology area that folks can use to invent in that space.
problemStatement: Many inventors, both new and experienced, can run into idea blocks. When new to brainstorming, a group might not know where or how to begin. When experienced, a group might have run out of inspiration or new ideas.
outcome: Curated and vetted content that inspires, informs, and supports successful brainstorming sessions where a group of folks that may or may not know each other initially can come together and successfully produce and articulate ideas, some of which can be integrated into the business and submitted through normal invention processes for review and potential patent application filing.
finalOutcome: 20 toolkits created in emerging tech areas. Participants met new folks from across the company, learned about emerging tech areas, brainstormed ideas - 175 of which are currently being written for submission as disclosures.
closeValue: This model informs employees about important technology areas and helps them get out of their siloed constraints of thought and network.
ratingComments: Excellent piece of work. The goal now is to make it something that just happens organically by the technical teams.

title: Building the Tech Persona
executiveChampionReason: Vasantha Kumar and Eric Sall are the leaders in Marketing for India/SA. The need for showcasing the technical talent from the region came from Karan Bajwa (Regional Manager) for the country.  We will report the progress of these initiatives to Karan through Vasanth and Eric.
description: IBM has a strong tech image – IBMers aren’t seen to be so.   How can we use existing platforms like AoT and its members to build the tech persona and showcase IBM’s technical leadership externally.  This initiative shall be delivered Phase 1 – Pilot with the AoT members in Bangalore and drive Technical eminence in external platforms  Phase 2 - Extend it to other AoT chapters  Phase 3 – Allow the Black belts also into the program. The initiative shall provide consistent showcase of the technical talent across events and engagements for the region and  creating more IBM technical Influencers who will contribute to increase in SoV for IBM in social media platforms and communities.
problemStatement: IBM has a strong tech image – IBMers aren’t seen to be so.   How can we use existing platforms like AoT and its members to build the tech persona and showcase IBM’s technical leadership externally.
outcome:
- Consistent showcase of the technical talent across events and engagements 
                                        - Strong PoV vis a vis only representing the IBM PoV
                                        - Creating more IBM technical Influencers, creating a database of IBMers who will contribute to increase in SoV for IBM.
                                        - Promoting strong engagement on social media platforms and communities such as GitHub, Get Social Hub, StackOverflow etc.
finalOutcome:
The program was run in the agile model with three week sprints and a playback at the end of each sprint. Sprint 1, We did the enablement and got 33 AoT/TEC-I members to commence their social eminence journey. Sprint 2 and 3 were focused on content creation and reviews.  We got about 18 blogs published, more to be logged or not yet reported.
                                        
                                        The content covered topics on IBM Cloud (Docker, Containers, IBM Cloud Automation Manager, IBM Cloud Security Advisor),AI (Fuelling Automation with the Power of Cognitive!), Systems (ISDL Blogathon, Physical Design of On chip memories,HMC v9 Performance Improvements,IBM Spectrum Virtualize), GBS/SAP (SAP Digital Boardroom Implementation Checklist), Others (Diversity Event Kickoff, Women in Technology Event, Society of Women Engineers Event- SWE, Corporate Roundtable Discussion, TEC Hyderabad Quarterly connect)
                                        
                                        We would like to run the continuation of this initiative as Tech Persona 2.0. The second edition will focus on select members with an advanced agenda grouped by area of expertise to make bigger impacts.
closeValue: 33 A0T/TEC-I members enabled to commence their journey on social eminence

title: Build Proof of Concept to test whether Oniqua's inventory optimization capabilities can be used for Parts/ Products with "MRO-like" characteristics
outcome: The primary expected outcome is a determination whether Oniqua could be used to help manufacturers of large infrastructure-type products -- for instance, semiconductor manufacturing equipment, large servers/ routers, telecommunications base stations, etc. The manufacturers of these products do not generally have large MRO inventories, but they do have large inventories of parts and products with very infrequent, unpredictable demand. If the PoC is successful, or even if it points the way to some small improvements in the product that would make it useful for this purpose, it could open up new markets.

executiveChampionReason: Mark and Rhonda were both selected to represent different perspective.  Mark representing the CHQ Patent area and Rhonda representing the practitioner side.
description: The goal of this initiative it to produce an asset that can be used by anyone who is interested in leading an aspiring inventor initiative.  This as a service asset will contain instructions and material to lead and support successful aspiring inventor initiatives.
problemStatement: Aspiring inventors are confused about the inventing process in IBM.  There are many myths that need to be dispelled.  Some believe inventing is limited to a select group, you need to be very technical, have a working model and it requires a lot of time.  No organized program or solution exist to help address this problem at scale.
outcome: Produce a reusable asset (DIaaS) that can be use by anyone to lead successful aspiring inventor initiatives. The asset will include a program outline, curriculum, learning material, guide to organize and lead successful aspiring inventor initiatives.
finalOutcome: Globally available tool that provides educational and training material in a consistent format and flexible manner. With more inventors participating across the globe we expect to see a more diverse set of invention added to the portfolio.  We also expect to see the quality of inventions increasing and thus adding more value to the IP.
closeValue: Aspiring inventors have a single place to learn they too can be an inventor; dymistification of the invention process in IBM.
ratingComments: Garfield's enthusiasm, diligence and project management skills were excellent throughout this effort.   The final work product is very professional and IBM's inventor community should find it quite helpful.

title: Scaling the Go-To Market for Secure Data Serving with LinuxONE
executiveChampionReason: There is a high degree of focus on this topic by our New Client Acquisition team especially in communicating value proposition to the sales teams and clients. The result of this initiative would be a valuable asset in doing this, especially in identifying new channels and methodologies to scale our Go-To-market and reach.
description: The initiative aims to build out an innovative Go-To Market strategy able to drive, by leveraging IBM differentiators, significant penetration of LinuxONE-based OracleDB consolidation,  ideally resulting in the sale of hundreds of LinuxONE systems in the next years.
problemStatement:
LinuxONE delivers the agility, innovation and openness of the modern Linux ecosystem on top of hardware that has been engineered over the last 60 years to meet the needs of modern enterprises.  It is this heritage that has given this LinuxONE industry leading resilience, security, scalability and availability.  When combined with the modern linux-based cloud stack, LinuxONE simplifies IT so clients can focus on what really matters to them -- business outcomes, driving disruption and growth.
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                One key example of such simplification is Oracle database consolidation.   The scalability, resilience and security engineering of LinuxONE make it possible for clients to achieve quite dramatic consolidations of Oracle databases, thus reducing Oracle licensing costs and data-center footprint significantly.
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                This value proposition has however failed to scale to drive volume sales of LinuxONE in the market place as IBM channels and field teams have failed to capitalize on LinuxONE.
outcome: Build innovative Go to market approach leveraging "creative" thoughts about how to drive the broader IBM organization in reaching new sales channels and new clients.  Establish methodology how to characterize target clients quickly and at scale. Test the approach with some selected clients, as proof points of the assumptions made. Produce an Academy report to share internally as well as with clients, partners and the open source ecosystem. Business value will be in identifying clients (new, existing, SO, etc.) and opportunities at them to build an effective pipeline that might influence year-end business results
closeValue: Recommendations from the initative ideally will result in the sale of hundreds of LinuxONE systems in the next years.
publicationDescription: Issues, challenges and recommendations to scale worldwide IBM LinuxONE business.

title: Design Patterns for Blockchain based application development
executiveChampionReason: Ram is an IBM fellow and the CTO for Blockchain services. Ram will help evangelize the design patterns across IBM GBS. GBS is a good place for field adoption of these patterns directly into customer engagements
description: The purpose of this initiative is to document design patterns and development best practices when developing end to end applications using Blockchain. This initiative will look at live production applications such as TradeLens, Food safety etc along with regular client facing engagements as reference. Common problems will be identified and then appropriate solution patterns will be developed to solve those problems. These design patterns will then act as a reference for all enterprise grade Blockchain based application developement.
problemStatement:
Phase 1 of the design patterns initiative will tackle the following problems
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                        1. Building an interactive UI for complex Blockchain based applications
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                        2. Asynchronous API design for complex Blockchain based applications
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                        3. Securely sync Blockchain data on to an off chain cache for optimal search and analytics
outcome:
1. Design patterns for the problems mentioned that would include architecture, solution design and code samples where appropriate

title: Emergency Management Response - matching Suppliers to Consumers using AI
description: Using AI to provide the ability to rapidly ramp up emergement management supplies during a local/state/national emergency
problemStatement: During national emergencies (such as COVID-19 pandemic) there will always be a need to rapidly ramp up supplies in response to the emergency.  While the federal government could authorize the Defense Production Act (DPA) ideally normal market forces would be able to react and provide the supplies needed. In many cases this would require manufacturers, importers and assemblers to change their product (or process) in support of the supply chain needed to produce the needed supplies.  What is missing is the ability to quickly match the various types of manufacturers, parts or capabilities tuned to the specific need of providing the critical supplies.  In the COVID-19 example, the need for masks has led to a critical shortage and a somewhat inefficient ramp up of building masks since it has taken some time to match all the types of companies' capabilities/skills with the specific product needed.  I believe we could use an AI driven process that has access to all the small/large business capabilities in the U.S. (or any country) - capabilities being type of manufacturing process, type of skills, type of processes, geographic location, etc to quickly match them with the specs of a needed critical product.
outcome: Possible market opportunity for an AI driven emergency management product to make available to local, state and federal government entities (FEMA), hospitals, military and other organizations responding to emergencies.

title: Cognitive Patterns for VM based orchestration
executiveChampionReason: He is the Executive in charge of System Service Line
description: Patterns that can invoke cognitive functions, so that provisioned VMs are managed intelligently with reduced manual intervention
problemStatement: To create cognitive capabilities for solving commonly recurring problems for patterns based orchestrated VMs. This would be an important differentiated capability for our Systems Service Line. First and foremost orchestration is a $4.6b business (2016) growing to $12b by 2021. To make orchestration useful, patterns or blueprints are required to convert IaaS into a PaaS, and usable by the end-user/developer. But that is just the start. As application development evolves, requirements evolve and this requires the developer to fall back to traditional slow mode service management requests to solve his problems. Examples could be scaling of VMs for new performance needs, adding new volumes when disk space runs low, moving the workload to a machine with higher bandwidth, archiving and shutting down the VM when not required, etc. What we intend to do is identify key use cases and build patterns that enable these differentiated capabilities using our IBM Services Platform for Watson as the base platform.
outcome: 1. Identify cognitive use cases and capabilities that provide add value for Day 2 Operations,2. Identify SaaS capabilities inside and outside of IBM that provide Cognitive capabilities,3. Solution and integrate cognitive capabilities through patterns and orchestration,4. Implement demo case,5. Incorporate into Service Line roadmap and client proposals
finalOutcome:
This initiative has produced the following Core IP assets for security (for VMWare, AWS, IBM Cloud, Azure)
1) Host based protection services with Trend Micro 
2) Vulnerability Management with Qualys Cloud
3) Vulnerability scanner with Qualys virtual scanner 
4) Security monitoring with Qradar SIEM
5) Network security services with Fortigate, Palo Alto, Vyatta

These have been assimilated into IBM Multi cloud Deployment Services (MCDS) offering and IBM Managed Security Services (MSS) has used to further their use cases to clients.
The security patterns uses automation to apply security technology and apply policies to new cloud workloads at cloud speed. A wide range of security services are available in the form of security patterns ranging from host based protection services to vulnerability management, security monitoring and perimeter network security services requiring organizations to strive for embedding security features as part of cloud automation.
closeValue: Automation and integration of security services.

title: ** COVID-19 ** | Use of NPS survey and customer trust relationship to help businesses gain new customers
executiveChampionReason: Auto Selected from Admin Page
description: The system process enables businesses to enter to new client market, by combining the customers service experience and trust relationship with new potential customer based on cognitive analysis of NPS survey, market segmentation and customer's history records.
problemStatement: The Associated Press-NORC Center for Public Affairs Research "unveiled that 3 in 10 say Americans are not worried at all about the Coronavirus" (https://thehill.com/policy/healthcare/public-global-health/488427-americans-coronavirus-fears-spike-poll). This indicates that once businesses return to operations in post COVID-19 pandemic, they will struggle to gain 70% of customer's trust that they can provide their services without the threat of spreading the virus. Businesses will need to apply a process to reach new customers and gain their trusts on the mitigation procedures applied to avoid the risk of getting infected.
outcome:
The initiative will use the NPS survey results from a current customer when asking how likely will they recommend them to friends or family. If the NPS survey result between 8 and 10, the system process will trigger the customer's service history and market segmentation; it will request the customer's for referrals, base on social media friends. Once the customer accepts the communication, the system process will initiate a three way communication between the customer and the new potential client. The system process will share to the new potential client the service experience from current customer (including all measures to prevent COVID-19 infection). This will gain help business use the customer's trust relationship to gain new customers.

The IBM value:
1. High revenue opportunity. After COVID-19, business need to reinvent the way they do business through the adoption of cloud services. "While only about 37% of small and mid-sized businesses are using cloud-based apps this year, experts anticipate that number to reach 78% by 2020. title: Contract AI to Build & Test word2vec & BERT
executiveChampionReason: He owns this mission and requested help to accelerate completing it
description: Build a semantic similarity model for extracting & classifying contractual terms using word2vec and BERT
problemStatement: How valuable would it be to have access to the details in sales contracts at your fingertips, for instance, payment schedule, incentives you didn't know about, opportunity to up/cross-sell, or mitigate risks from non-standard language.   Current commonly used AI approaches for contracts like Watson NLC can be time consuming to build, requiring labeling and annotating efforts upfront.  We want the ability to build and test capability to extract and classify contractual terms quickly in the context of contractual language in English.
outcome:
OUTCOME:
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                > Enhancing the capability to search and extract contractual terms in English language using word2vec/BERT and large volume of contracts.  Save time & simplify efforts (fewer manual steps).
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                > Comparison and recommendation on implementing natural language models developed by the CAO ENAIBL team, i.e. semantic similarity model, entity resolution model                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                BENEFITS: 
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                > Enable shorter time to search and contract terms written in English compared to today’s cycle time
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                > Create capability to shorten cycle time of a typical contract POC (e.g. from 12 weeks to 8 weeks)
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                > Save time for building any NLC (natural language classification) model by eliminating manual labeling & annotation
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                > Increase accuracy of contract terms search or extraction
finalOutcome:
Accomplishments:
-  Developed a contextual modeling approach for extracting and classifying clauses from contract texts.
-  Experimented with the state-of-the-art word and sentence embedding models, such as Word2Vec, FastText, GloVe, and BERT.
-  Improved the accuracy of clause extraction from ~72% up to ~90% with all evaluated embedding models.
-  Determined that BERT model achieves the best overall results though with a caveat of critical dependency on GPU computing.
closeValue: A product team collected and leveraged knowledge from this initiative for 1 client pursuit (in progress) in Travel & Transportation industry..
publicationDescription:
Objective:
To develop and evaluate an optimal AI-based clause extraction & classification methodology for enterprise contract documents.

Accomplishments:
-  Developed a contextual modeling approach for extracting and classifying clauses from contract texts.
-  Experimented with the state-of-the-art word and sentence embedding models, such as Word2Vec, FastText, GloVe, and BERT.
-  Improved the accuracy of clause extraction from ~72% up to ~90% with all evaluated embedding models.
-  Determined that BERT model achieves the best overall results though with a caveat of critical dependency on GPU computing.
ratingComments: This team made a huge accomplishment in getting an impartial analysis and recommendation for the right approach for extracting clauses from contracts.  Thank you team!

title: ** COVID-19 ** | COVID@Home: an NHS app
executiveChampionReason: Richard is supportive of this initiative and will be the temporary executive champion until an appropriate executive stakeholder is assigned.
description: A mobile app with a calendar feature to allow users to track their symptoms and quarantine period over time. Provide NHS recommendations where possible, with the aim to relieve strain on A&E services.
problemStatement: The NHS and chemists across the UK are under a huge amount of strain with the current COVID-19 pandemic, so the motivation to reduce panic and unnecessary traffic to NHS services is high. Chemists and general practitioners are overwhelmed with the concerned public who are keen to seek advice regarding possible symptoms associated with COVID-19. We seek to find an alternative way to offer advice to the public, such as those affected by mild cases of coronavirus, those with unconfirmed cases or symptoms, and those at high-risk. We would like to empower the public to feel confident in managing their symptoms at home, by offering a single source of verified medical advice, as well as tools to record and monitor health, so that the number of people accessing emergency services is reduced.
outcome: The app would empower people to manage the virus at home, by tracking the progression of symptoms and therefore being able to advise on recommending longer periods of isolation or seeking more urgent medical treatment, for example. Data points such as temperature and other COVID-19 symptoms can be recorded in a calendar view. Partial pressure of blood oxygen levels is one such warning indicator of the coronavirus, which is suspected to be able to be measured using Apple watch technology, provided the software update be issued by Apple. The use of bio-sensing in this application would make the initiative medically more powerful.  If it is possible to collect the data centrally (with consideration given to GDPR) this would also provide the NHS with valuable information about the virus. The application could be a trusted source of truth for information about COVID-19 from a credible scientific community, reducing the panic that ensues from unverified medical information.
finalOutcome: This initiative went a rather different route than expected, and much of the effort originally aimed at this proposal was redirected to help with another urgent NHS request, known as the Nightingale project. Although not as planned, Project Nightingale was a huge success in its own right.
closeValue: The ability for IBMers to come together to make a difference to society when they are asked to.

title: IBM Services Mainframe Modernization Business Case
executiveChampionReason: Balakrishnan Sreenivasan is one of the IBM DEs responsible for the IBM Services Mainframe Modernization 2.0 initiative. He is also the executive championing the business case ROI tooling.
description: Mainframe Modernization represents a significant revenue opportunity for IBM Services.  Being able to quantify and demonstrate the potential TCO (Total Cost of Ownership) and ROI (Return on Investment) attributed to mainframe modernization is paramount if IBM is to win this business. This initiative will develop a Mainframe Modernization ROI Calculator to enable IBM Services to quickly demonstrate the tangible business value associated with each of the possible mainframe modernization plays.
problemStatement:
Many businesses and organizations are looking at modernizing their legacy mainframe applications. For many, transitioning to the cloud and modern contemporary technologies, such as containers and microservices, will help them achieve increased agility, flexibility, and scalability, with the objective of driving reduced time-to-market, lower costs, and ultimately business differentiation.
Mainframe Modernization represents a significant revenue opportunity for IBM Services.  Being able to quantify and demonstrate the potential TCO (Total Cost of Ownership) and ROI (Return on Investment) attributed to mainframe modernization is paramount if IBM is going to win this business.
The IBM Services Mainframe Modernization 2.0 initiative embraces Hybrid Modernization, In-place Modernization, and Mainframe for Cloud. Each of these scenarios is composed of a number of use cases that map to an individual transformation / modernization offerings. For example, the Hybrid Modernization scenario includes, and compares, transition to IBM zCloud, IBM CICS TX on Cloud, as well as more transformative options such as rewriting to containerized microservices.  
The intention of the Mainframe Modernization Business Case ROI Calculator is that it will allow IBM Services CAI/CAS Sellers and SMEs to quickly demonstrate the tangible business value associated with each of the possible mainframe modernization plays.
outcome: A Mainframe Modernization Business Case ROI Calculator to enable IBM Services CAI/CAS Sellers and SMEs to quickly demonstrate the tangible business value associated with each of the possible mainframe modernization plays.
finalOutcome:
Mainframe Modernization represents a significant revenue opportunity for IBM Services.  Being able to quantify and demonstrate the potential Total Cost of Ownership, Business Value, and Return on Investment attributed to mainframe modernization is paramount if IBM is to win this business. 

This AoT initiative delivered a Mainframe Modernization Business Case Calculator to enable IBM Services Sellers and SMEs to quickly demonstrate the tangible business value associated with each of the possible Hybrid Application Modernization patterns.
closeValue: Enables IBM Services to quickly demonstrate the tangible business value associated with mainframe modernization.

title: IBM Cloud Status Quo
executiveChampionReason: The Initiative scope has been discussed with Grady who is in favor of the idea, specifically, the intent to identify the issues today with IBM Cloud offerings, and means to address those issues
description: Analyze the status of IBM Cloud Offering, identify bottlenecks and recommend means to address those
problemStatement:
IBM is still in the run after our competition trying to determine the strategy to address various challenges we face in defining and delivering our cloud offerings to a wide variety of customers.   Even though various reports have been published that compare our cloud delivery capability to our competitors, IBM as an aspiring cloud services provider, don't appear to have a clear strategy on how to address various challenges we face in competing for the market share, which include marketing, architecting, designing, implementing and supporting cloud solutions for our customers. Some questions that are due answers include the following:
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                - Is the One IBM Cloud strategy effective, and are we executing it as expected?
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                - Are we considering all key factors in executing our cloud journey strategy in order to compete successfully for the market share?
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                - How IBM's cloud services capability compares to that of the other key cloud services providers? 
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                - What are major gaps and deficiencies in our cloud capability that need to be addresses?  
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                This Study will attempt to outline the most critical areas that we need to address as a cloud computing provider,  prioritize those ares, and recommend remedies, as appropriate.
outcome:
AoT Report produced jointly with IBM Value Institute and Market Development Organizations that will  include a  summary of key issues observed with IBM's cloud delivery capability, and  challenges we face as a cloud provider competing for the cloud market share.  
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                The Report will include to formulate Recommendation to the key problems identified, and share those with IBM Executive staff for further actions.
finalOutcome: The Study Report includes a significant intellectual capital that can be used for improving IBM Cloud Computing strategy.
closeValue: In depth anlysis of IBM Cloud computing capability today, and comprehensive recommendations for improvements that can be incorporated in IBM's cloud strategy to better compete for the market
publicationDescription:
Comprehensive Report assessing IBM Cloud Delivery capability, comparing IBM to other CSPs, and Recommending  improvements to operations as a Cloud Computing Provider.
                                                                                
                                                                                Please, request the access to the box where the Report has been posted.

title: Calling all Architects!  IBM Technology Roadmap Co-Creation Initiative.
executiveChampionReason: Ed Fung, GTS NA CTO was selected as the new Exec Champion in March 2019 because he is a passionate advocate for the use of  Technology Plans on Accounts to facilitate clear and succinct communications about digital transformation POV with client stakeholders and to work with them to create and maintain a technology roadmap for driving new value for their business.  His organization will potentially benefit more than others from the output and results of the technology roadmap going forward.
description: This initiative will be targeted at Architects working on customer accounts across IBM where a technology roadmap is quickly and accurately needed with innovative and quality content.
problemStatement:
Do you want to get more IBM content to be used by our customers? Want to improve our customers perception that we are innovative, creative, and thought leaders?  Want to get GTS to use more IBM products in their solutions?  
                                                                                                                                                                
                                                                                                                                                                Architects need a more efficient way to create technology roadmaps for clients.  Today, account architects create technology plans with significant customization.  Many different formats, databases and content sources exist sometimes for the same content.  The current way is very manual and time consuming for the architect in finding the right content across multiple databases and content repositories.
                                                                                                                                                                
                                                                                                                                                                There are many sources of information and many different formats.  This initiative will explore using new and innovative cognitive and automation technologies to search, access, and generate technical content for architects, technical leaders and clients.  Additionally, this initiative will allow you to ideate ways to continually improve and update the content in the technology roadmap over time and even contribute to the development and implementation of this new capability.  We will also differentiate what are real and deployed offerings and capabilities versus what are conceptual services and offerings.
outcome:
This initiative will address the pain point for architects in creating technology plans and forward-looking roadmaps by providing valuable content, reduced costs, and increase time to market using the latest technologies and services supported by IBM.
                                                                                                                                                                
                                                                                                                                                                This initiative will help architects be more efficient, all while giving them access to the latest technical content to add to their plans.  Our clients benefit by seeing our account architects helping drive proactive innovation and thought leadership.  A better technology roadmap for our clients will help give them access to the latest information while giving the architect back more time.  Ultimately our goal is to help our architects provide thought leadership and innovation and help them reduce time searching endlessly for technical content.
                                                                                                                                                                
                                                                                                                                                                Finally, those who aspire to become AoT members, Distinguished Engineers, STSM, or Certified IT Architects will get valuable giveback toward their career goals.  It is expected that you will have valuable ideas, technical skills, and content to contribute.  By contributing, you will also benefit from the generated output from this initiative.  For those that are already AoT Members or recognized technical leaders, your technical leadership and passion will be welcome to help contribute to the success of this project.
finalOutcome: The Tech plan coaching sprint has developed a new reusable asset for client architects to help guide them through the early stages of developing an annual technology plan for their clients.  This asset has been officially published in GTS Global Solution Architecture Repository (GSAR) under Global Delivery Architecture Plus (GDA+).  It as also been published in Lighthouse and can be used by any client technical architect who needs to infuse innovation and put a forward technology view to their client.
closeValue: This initiative has Increased productivity, reduced time, and increased quality of the annual technology plans created by lead architects on IBM strategic client accounts.
publicationDescription: As part of this initiative, we were able to ideate on a potential new collaboration crowdsourcing collaboration capability to continually improve the technoolgy roadmap for all of GTS.  In addition, we created a new published asset called Tech Plan Coaching Guide which helps chief architects on accounts create or update their annual technology plans in a much earlier way, helping show clients direct innovation and value with participation into the process and early validation of key projects before they get planned.

description: Update the deliverables from the AoT initiative (Red Hat OpenShift - Solution Design Guidance), make sure that the guides are effective, and publish suitable content of the guides externally including Architecture Center.
problemStatement:
Need published guidance on how to design optimal OpenShift and IBM Cloud Paks solutions for our clients, ensure architectural integrity, and proper delivery structure using the 14-in-4 offerings.

The first version of 5 (five) Solution Design Guidance for OpenShift were published as part of the AoT Initiative: Red Hat OpenShift - Solution Design Guidance: https://academyweb-prod.w3ibm.mybluemix.net/initiatives/a7f9863a166805f498ca962e06fe38ab

Since OpenShift and IBM Cloud Paks content are evolving rapidly, need to work on Red Hat OpenShift - Solution Design Guidance 2.0 to address the following:
1) Maintain the 5 guides 
2) Make sure that guides are effective and leveraged across brands to design optimal OpenShift and IBM Cloud Paks solutions
3) Publish suitable content of the guides externally on IBM Cloud Architecture Center.
4) Work with Red Hat to enhance the quality of the guides
outcome:
**Expected Outcome:**
1- Update the 5 guides produced as part of the earlier AoT initiative and publish on https://ibm.biz/openshift-solutioning
A) OpenShift Solutioning Guide 101
B) Cloud Paks Guidance
C) OpenShift Resilience Guidance
D) OpenShift Architecture Patterns
E) OpenShift Solution Clinic Report
2- Publish suitable content of the guides externally on IBM Cloud Architecture Center.

**Business Value**
A) Standardize and optimize OpenShift and IBM Cloud Paks solutions to our customers by having all the technical communities following the approach identified in the above five guides.
B) Validate the technical accuracy of the guides with broader technical experts cross business unit to assure we are delivering optimal OpenShift and IBM Cloud Paks solutions to our customers.
C) The guides will be leveraged across Cloud & Cognitive Software, GTS, and GBS as well as the wider IBM - to design optimal OpenShift solutions for our clients. This fulfills the need to ensure architectural integrity and proper delivery structure in our solutions which will result in better business outcomes for our clients and IBM.

title: Crisis and Recovery Management for Business Applications/Services - COVID-19
executiveChampionReason: Blaine is my mentor and can provide direction
description: Crisis and Recovery Management for Enterprises to act on Business Critical Applications during outbreaks like COVID-19
problemStatement: Crisis Management is the process in which an Organization deals with a disruptive and unexpected event like COVID-19 Outbreaks.
outcome:
Organizations would adopt a Crisis and Recovery Management Business Model to keep up the support of their business-critical services/applications.
Crisis and Recovery - From Reactive to Proactive
1. Identify Business critical application and services that need highest support during Crisis
2. Identify Employee/resources health status and availability – Plan for uncertainties
3. Create Crisis and KT teams to cross skill or train employees/resources 
4. Take Action ( Implement Changes ) on Business Critical Applications
5. Plan for the future demand post Crisis
6. Replicate and Manage across all businesses
sponsorMessage: As communicated in email:  When I asked about sending out a call for volunteers and also about the duration (the initiative start date is before the submission date), your response was "I am already in the process of development, am developing on ServiceNow SaaS platform so can launch it quick, I am happy to demo what I had done so far and take the feedback.".   This sounds like something you are working on as a part of your regular job, rather than an AoT initiative which requires cross business-unit and cross-geo participation.  The fact that you said "I" tells me that perhaps even if this is a team effort it is your immediate team.  This is what confuses me.  An AoT initiative focuses on a problem that reaches outside of any one team and requires collaboration from across the business.  Are you planning to do a call for volunteers to bring in more participants?  Or do you plan to launch this solution and make it available.  It sounds like something that could be valuable to IBM and our clients, it just doesn't sound like an AoT initiative.

title: We need a Virtual Agent to help us Pick which Virtual Agent solution to use
executiveChampionReason: We need to work with Susan on a x-LoB leader who will be impartial and supportive
description: Discoverying, Mapping, and Categorizing IBM's X-LoB + Competiive Virtual Agent Solutions
problemStatement: The challenge IBM currently has in Cognitive is much like we had with Cloud. Many parts of LoBs each building their own assets, developing their own go to market strategies and effectively competing with each other.  Historically, that confusing/duplication cause a critical delay in IBM's Cloud offerings getting to market.  There is a broad concern that this duplication in the Cognitive space may cause the same delays. ,This AoT initiative will gather, document and align an IBM-wide Dialogue/NLP/Cognitive enabled work flows/RPA approaches. title: ** COVID-19 ** | Virtual Fan Experience for Large Events
executiveChampionReason: Auto Selected from Admin Page
description: Our proposed idea will use video cameras, located in the different sections inside the stadium, as input. The user will use a VR platform as input to view the stadium field base  on the seat location the user selected. The user will have the option to connect with other users to interact on the game/show they are watching. The system and method will use AI techniques to pick older sounds of previous matches/shows to the current situation and capture as well sounds from the current match to feed it to the user's speakers. Speakers will also be located in the different sections inside the stadium to amplify the noises made by all the users connected in the system and method.
problemStatement:
The COVID-19 pandemic has affected the entertainment industry, cancelling live events, from live sports calendars games to live music shows. "Anything longer than a temporary shutdown would see the leagues unable to meet their commitments to broadcasters, limiting their ability to distribute income back to the clubs. The impact on the industry would be dramatic: no games mean no TV deals and no matchday income; no income means no clubs." ( https://www.weforum.org/agenda/2020/04/sports-covid19-coronavirus-excersise-specators-media-coverage/ ) When the National Basketball Association (NBA) in the United States suspended the season in March 2020, there were 259 games left in the regular season, making a estimated gate revenue loss between 350 to 450 million dollars. ( https://www.statista.com/statistics/1104004/coronavirus-revenue-loss-nba/ )
Current technologies and channels solutions are being use to engage fans, sports companies are looking to eSports or online simulated events to provide content to fans and musicians are going online and relying on streaming platforms. The problem is that the "fan experience" is lost as there are no fans in the stands. ( https://www2.deloitte.com/global/en/pages/about-deloitte/articles/covid-19/understanding-COVID-19-s-impact-on-the-sports-sector.html# ).
outcome:
Our proposed idea will enable the Entertainment Industry to provide "fan experience" to online platforms, by combining cameras, microphones and speakers inputs in stadiums with cloud base conferencing software platforms base on the seat locations in the stadiums.

The business value for IBM would be:
1. High revenue opportunity. "In 2018, the North American sports market had a value of about 71.06 billion U.S. dollars. This figure is expected to rise to 83.1 billion by 2023. The market is composed of the segments gate revenues, media rights, sponsorships and merchandising." (https://www.statista.com/statistics/214960/revenue-of-the-north-american-sports-market/)
2. High opportunity for IBM to promote different solutions through the platform.  
3. At IBM, we sponsor large events such as the Masters, ESPN Fantasy Football, US Open, Wimbledon and the Grammy Awards. Providing experiences such as this invention will create new revenue streams for and an increase of IBM brand in the $billions. Just a 5% increase in the valuation of IBM’s brand is worth $4.35B.

title: Security and Privacy Compliance Automation
executiveChampionReason: Bill Tworek is the Vice President of Product and Offering Security in the Enterprise and Technology Security organization. Industry and Regulatory Compliance for all IBM products, offerings, and services  fall into Bill's portfolio
description: This study will assess, identify, and determine new methods for driving automation and efficiency into the Security and Privacy Compliance Process at IBM
problemStatement: IBM has numerous processes, tools and resources working on compliance issues across the enterprise. This leads to the inability to identify clearly, across IBM, the risks in this area. This is also a largely manual effort that requires additional automation with new tooling.
outcome: We expect to identify the best in class processes and tools across IBM, develop consistency in process and tooling, and drive automation and new tooling for Security and Privacy Compliance.
finalOutcome:
There were 16 BU/functional squads identified for this study.  Seven groups provided information for the study.  Within the BUs there were over 500 unique compliance related tools inventoried.  There were over 100 duplication.  In some cases multiple deployments/instances of the same tool were noted.  
The tooling was broken down into 6 types supporting the compliance life cycle: Inventory, Applicability, Control Implementation, Control Validation/Measurement, Action/Improvement, Demonstrating Compliance.  The majority of tools, 46%, focus on control implementation.  Less than 10%, were identified as determining compliance applicability or demonstrating compliance.  The tools supporting applicability focused around privacy regulations.  There was little integration of tools at the BU or across BUs noted.  Most still utilize Box, Slack, and Excel for manual processes.  
In the control implementation space, the majority of the tools focused on Access Control and password management.  Secure development was the second area that much of the tooling supported, followed by configuration management. title: Equivalent Parts Finder / Cognitive Aid for Electronics Manufacturers
problemStatement:
Most parts used in electronic products are standard, meaning that they can be sourced from multiple companies. Examples include standard logic and analog ICs, diodes, transistors, capacitors and others. Additionally, for a number of reasons, most companies will find that they create multiple internal part numbers for either identical or very close equivalent parts. This is especially the case at Electronic Manufacturing Services (EMS) companies, but is also true at almost any medium-sized manufacturing facility or company. 
When there is a shortage or excess of one part, it is quite possible that an offsetting situation exists for an equivalent part elsewhere. Finding the equivalent part(s), and assessing which is the best potential match, is a difficult and time-consuming process -- but could be done very easily and quickly using cognitive computing. We envision using data from the company's Part Master (plus, potentially, PO records, the PLM system and other data sources) to identify possible matches; then using inventory and demand data from the ERP system to assess where a particular problem can best be met with offsetting inventory or demand elsewhere.
outcome: These situations can occur daily at some companies. Individual problems are not always "worth" a great deal (a reel of 5000 chip capacitors may only cost $40; a reel of 10,000 transistors may only be worth $800), but there is a very large amount of non-value-added labor associated with these problems. A significant reduction will reduce labor costs and improve performance at these companies. Also important: this is a widely recognized problem at hundreds of electronics firms. Being able to demonstrate a solution will open the door for cognitive computing at many new clients.

title: Business network design for supply-chain & insurance
executiveChampionReason: Anthony and Nitin are both Distinguished Engineers that have been focussing their attention on making blockchain work for the enterprise.  They are both keens on supporting this initiative.
description: For blockchain solution to "stick", they need to be representative of the business reality of its participants.  Hence, in designing blockchain solutions, one key activity is to get a proper understanding of the business network and the dynamic of the network. The approach proposed by this initiative is to focus on understanding market structures to see, for a subset of the business process, how the various participants and their relationships can be mapped to a blockchain network design.
problemStatement: The initial deployments of Hyperledger Fabric network took the approach where participants were either directly involved (ie were hosting a node) or indirectly participating (ie using the portal of one of the participants).  This approach typically yields a topology where bilateral channels were defined for every participant.  This has created exposure for IBM as competitors seed doubts about the scalability of the solution. In reality, while the solution can scale, this approach does introduce operational complexity.  Furthermore, in most cases, the reality is that participants only transact with a small subset of the network. To be successful with blockchain, we, as IBMers need to better understand the business aspect of networks.
outcome:
By understanding the market structure of a business network, we stand a better chance of defining a solution that meets the business reality.  The expected outcome of this initiative is two-fold:
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                        1. Demonstrate the value of understanding market structure by studying two main industry: Supply-Chain and Insurance
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                        2. Document a methodology for mapping a business network structure to a blockchain network, taking into account typical privacy and confidentiality requirements.
finalOutcome: The primary business impact that the initiative had is the improved synergy between the various IBM team working on blockchain.  The GBS organization is now looking at adopting the approach, and it was applied in projects like We.Trade, Proof of Trust and others. The general feedback received from practitioners is that customer appreciate the clarity the approach brings.
closeValue: It provides a methodology to improve the understanding of business networks, and offer a standard network role terminology that can practitioners define scalable blockchain network topologies.
ratingComments: This was a well conducted initiative. Both Annap and Luc have created a real solid reference guide for business network design that can be used by IBM clients and IBM teams (including GBS, Services and Garages) to develop best of breed blockchain networks.  A very nice piece of work indeed.

title: Using AI in Customer Support to translate human languages for customer communications
executiveChampionReason: Helena, as the Director of IBM Globalization, has made her career in human language translation, and understands the entire industry, from nuance to at-scale operations.
description: Develop methods for improving machine translation of texts in IT Support cases or Customer Service cases that are rich with technical jargon words.
problemStatement: IBM Support operates in all the countries of the world, and 20% of Support Cases are transacted in non-English languages.  As we are adding AI to parts of the Support process, natural language processing must happen in non-English as well as English.  We use Machine Translation (WLT) in many places for agents and in front of our AI.  However automatic language detection is still poor.  IBM Research has released a new, "trainable" language ID endpoint and we now must develop best practices for training this on technical texts that contain much industry jargon.
outcome:
There are two.  1) improved accuracy in IBM Support for Identify, unblocking millions dollars of business value for IBM.
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                        2) The ability to go to market with a trainable Identify function for Watson Language Translator, enabling the penetration of vertical markets that are dense with jargon.
finalOutcome:
1) the original business problem was solved another way.  We did solve it with preprocessing, not with training the WLT.identify() service to overstep jargon words as we originally intended.

Error analysis of the data discovered most (>80%) of errors were texts of single class. (Copy-Pasted machine-generated text, a.k.a. log and trace snippets) that were easy to identify and preprocess.
The trainable dark feature of WLT.identify() was engineered for a different purpose.  Our original intent was to make a "custom" model, where we could train WLT.identify() on counterfactual words.  
Example:  "ABEND" is not a word in any language.  Don't consider "ABEND" when deciding if the text is English or French.  The dark feature doesn't work the way described above.  The dark feature would have allowed me to create "Support-English" as a new language.  I could have trained WLT.identify() to recognize the difference between English and Support-English.  This would have been hard work, since we'd also need to create 13 other variations (Support-German, Support-Japanese ...)

3) the data we have gathered is not usable for the purpose we defined in the AOT project.  (We gathered counterfactural truth, not ground-truth.)
closeValue: We improved language detection via preprocessing by over 80% and didn't require a ML solution for this problem.
