title: An Open Data Marketplace for Data Transactions
executiveChampionReason: Dr. Inderpal Bhandari is the Global Chief Data Officer (GCDO) of IBM and responsible for all Data Science, Data Engineering, and Data Monetization operations and initiatives within IBM. Dr. Bhandari manages projects related to transformation of data into business value for IBM enterprise as well as for IBM clients. He is the Senior Executive leading the AI Acceleration projects with IBM clients.
description: An investigative study to explore the technical and business opportunities as well as challenges in establishing an open ecosystem for data exchanges. This initiative will publish a comprehensive report with a set of recommendations for actions.
problemStatement:
The advent of cloud computing and the explosive growth of data offer a new marketplace where anyone could catalog, store, advertise, sell/buy/lease data just like any other commodity. Of course, unlike other commodities, data has some sensitivities like authenticity, privacy, misuse, etc., which often warrant stricter governance and protection for all the transactions and storage. Estimation of the value for data or pricing is also complex. However, considering the ever-growing nature of data and the unique ways the data is consumed, analyzed, and re-generated, the business potential of establishing and managing such a Marketplace is an excellent business proposition. The vision of such a Data Marketplace may include
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                          -An ecosystem for storing (posting), advertising, maintaining, selling, buying, and leasing data in a secured fashion
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                          -A data store that may include IBM owned non-confidential data, public data curated by IBM & third parties, and third party owned data
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                          -A reliable and user-friendly infrastructure to support data storage and data movements
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                          -A robust governance scheme to authenticate data contents, sources, ownership, to set up secured transactions, conforming to regulations
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                        -A strategy for monetizing the ecosystem through the sale of data as well data services.
outcome:
The business value includes ability to manage a variety of data in dynamic environment where transactions can range from free public data to secured, confidential & private data sold/bought/leased for commercial and/or research purposes. Such a marketplace would provide valuable experience in building/maintaining massive data platforms, enabling large number of real-time transactions, and providing secured and reliable governance. Also, it would help experiment new ways of “packaging” and “transporting” data.  There are potential other opportunities for related data services like reporting, analytics, etc. 
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                        This initiative aims at finding answers to the questions such as
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                    What data areas IBM should focus and how to ensure authenticity of data sold/bought/leased/stored on the platforms?
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                    What should be the business models for sourcing trusted data?
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                    What are the data monetization business models to be adopted?
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                    What improvements to be made in platforms to support massive data exchanges?
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                    What global data regulations should be concerned with?
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                    What kind of other data analysis services should be considered?
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                    What kind of measurements, transactional logs should be gathered and maintained?                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                        
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                        Result of this deep investigation will be a comprehensive report along with recommendations for next steps which will be presented to the sponsoring executive.
finalOutcome:
Upon completion of the study, the team clearly identified a significant business opportunity for a Marketplace for Data and AI Models with a yearly revenue potential of about US $8 billion for IBM. The study report also outlined why this business opportunity is crucial to the future growth of the company based on IBM's technical and business strength, alignment with IBM’s current business, what IBM’s competitors are doing, and what the business analysts are proclaiming. A conservative estimate of “data and insights trading business” could be anywhere between $60 to $80 billion a year. In addition, the business opportunity and economic value of data – commercial, natural and governmental, as well as IoT generated data, will run into trillions of US dollars in the coming years as reported by Accenture.
The study resulted in identifying the technical functions needed with a gap analysis as well as the legal framework to be put in place. The study outlined high-level next steps for launching an open data marketplace as actionable recommendation. Based on the read out to multiple Executives, there is consistent strong positive reaction on the relevance, observations, and recommendations created by the study.
closeValue: The greatest impact realized by this initiative is an  well-defined proposal to invest adequate resources for establishing an Open Data Marketplace for IBM with an opportunity of generating new multi-billion dollar revenue through a multi-fold marketplace for data and data models and the positive reaction from many executives.
publicationDescription:
An investigative study to explore the technical and business opportunities for IBM as well as challenges in establishing an Open Marketplace for Data and Data Models.
The objective of this study to explore the use cases, understand and assess the market for a “Data Marketplace (DM) platform”, including existing players and IBM competitors, examine necessary  tools and functions,  technical and business prospects for an IBM Data Marketplace platform and  making specific recommendations on the feasibility of such a venture, with  short-term and long-term strategies, and the actions to be taken to execute them.
ratingComments: The AoT Initiative on "Open Data Marketplace" is very relevant to my organization, the Global Chief Data Office. We have developed the Cognitive Enterprise Data Platform (CEDP), which is the data and AI backbone for IBM, as well as the Internal 3rd Party Data Marketplace. I am glad that this study investigated the potential next stages of data monetization by evaluating the technical feasibility and market demands of open platforms for trading third party datasets and models. The observations and recommendations of this study provide valuable insights and we are actively considering opportunities to implement some of them and potentially advance the IBM business in the strategic Data and AI domain. I thank the Academy for facilitating this study.

title: Cloud Solutioning and Architecture Best Practices - Increasing the competitiveness of IBM cloud solutioning process
executiveChampionReason:
Grady Booch, IBM Fellow, Chief Scientist for Software Engineering, is both a great advisor and mentor who deeply understands the criticality of IBM's capability in cloud computing.  Grady Booch was an Executive Sponsor for the AoT Initiative on IBM Cloud Status Quo that was completed in 2Q2020. The key objecive for that Initiative was to perform an in depth analysis of IBM's capability as a Cloud Services Provider.  As an outcome from that Initiative, a Recommendation has been made to establish a focused Study that would analyze a broad range of factors that impact IBM capability to market, design, deploy and operate cloud solutions for customers.  

Ken McTique is the General Manager, IBM Services Hybrid Cloud Solutioning, and he leads the Cloud Solutioning Center, an Organization that is critical to generating IBM revenue in cloud computing.
description: Identify Recommendations in areas of cloud solutioning and architecture patterns to improve IBM's capability to market, design and deliver cloud computing solutions to customers.
problemStatement:
The design and delivery of cloud solutions for IBM customers is often a very complex process that involves multiple IBM internal organizations, as well as IBM Vendors who provide their technologies and services as part of IBM defined cloud solutions.
While IBM is aspiring to be the Leader in cloud computing, and there has been noticeable improvements in its cloud delivery capability in the last few years,  IBM still seems to be struggling to be able to produce competitive cloud solutions satisfying customers' requirements at a competitive price.
Cloud solutioning at IBM involves complex and often time-consuming architecture decision-making process, and it lacks a standardized  approach across various teams and organizations involved. That includes a consistent usage of tools and techniques, such as cloud environment sizing and solution pricing, as well as an effective reuse of architecture artifacts. 
Most of the custom solutions that IBM defines for the customers are built from scratch with a little or no reuse of the already existing references. In effect, often it takes a significant amount of time to come up with the best and most cost-efficient solution. 
There is also a need to reduce the perceived complexity of our offerings and approaches.
outcome: Executive Recommendations  to address deficiencies in areas of marketing, design, delivery, migration and architecture patterns. Recommendations for solutioning process improvements, and tooling in support of  cloud solutioning.

title: Knowledge Management Framework for IT Services in the Cognitive Era
executiveChampionReason: Charles Retired and my new VP is Richard Baird
description: This Initiate is focused at establishing a working framework for Knowledge Management in support of IT Services in the Cognitive Era
problemStatement: The lack of a well defined Knowledge Management Framework and related operating disciplines within IBM causes IT Service components to establish their own approach to manage the ”knowledge” they use. This situation is exacerbated in our Cognitive Era and can lead to islands of "insight" based on each IT Service component's point of view of the truth of the sources they are using which then can lead to disjointed and conflicting feedback to consumers.
outcome: This Initiative is focused at collaborating across IBM and selected Universities to establish a working framework for Knowledge Management in support of IT Services in the Cognitive Era.The expected outcome is a set of architecture materials that can be used to guide the design and implementation of IT Service disciplines supporting Cognitive transformation and delivery. The Business Value to IBM can include; reduction in duplication of knowledge management efforts across IBM, and increased quality of cognitive systems integration. The Business Value for Clients and industry can include the increased quality of cognitive insights across the IT Services enabling their business. The outcome is expected to materially benefit/positively impact IBM's Knowledge Management posture within IBM and within the IT Industry.
finalOutcome: Outcome: System Context and primary use cases created for a Knowledge Management System. Before his retirement, Charles requested additional use cases for the Engagement personas. This was done and work was then paused until a replacement executive was found so we could align next phases with their business needs/vision. We campaigned for many months across GTS in search of Executives that were aligned with and interested in sponsoring this Knowledge Management initiative. We are calling a close to the search following multiple attempts to get GTS leadership together to discuss KM ownership resulted in reschedule after reschedule which generally means the topic is of lowest priority. So, to avoid wasting any further time on this initiative, we are closing it. The net learning out of this initiative is that attempting to carry out what is essentially an architecture project as an AoT initiate with volunteers requires a super hot topic and broad based executive support for it to be successful.
closeValue: The impact of Knowledge Management System Context and use cases is yet to be quantified and is up to the reader to determine for them selves.

title: Consumer Industry Reference Architecture Modernization - Digital Operations (DO)
executiveChampionReason: Chris Wong is Vice President, Strategy, Offerings and Alliances, Global Consumer Industry and as such he leads the identification, building, go to market and life cycle management of Industry Solutions and Industry Platforms from our Industry Blueprint. This reference architecture, aligned with the DISCO framework (Digital Experience & Engagement – Intelligent Supply-Chain – Digital Enterprise Operations), will be the foundation, supported by the hybrid & multicloud strategy, for each of our blueprint assets and solutions. Marty Wolfe is VP, CTO Global Consumer Industry, and as such he owns the Industry reference architecture and leads the technical community that is continuously defining, updating and consuming those standard architecture artifacts.
description: The objective of this study is to deliver a modernized (Team Solution Design compliant) reference architecture for the key imperatives of our Consumer Industry Framework (DISCO) and selected use-cases
problemStatement:
This initiative is part of a group of 3 AoT initiatives and focus on the Digital Enterprise Operations imperative, and its associated framework domains : 
DO - Build/Manage nextGen Infrastructure & Applications
DO - Discover & Develop Next Gen Talent
DO - Smart Operational Insights
DO - Smart Buildings
For each of those domains, part of DEO imperative, we will create a specific initiative sprint and identify one market relevant use-case and modernize the associated Reference Architecture for the era of hybrid/multi-cloud and the Cognitive Enterprise. The Reference Architecture will be delivered through a set of fully vetted assets/artifacts:
1) In cognitive Architect:
- Overview 
- System Context
- Use Case
- IT System View (Agnostic)
- Usage Scenario
- IT System View (IBM capabilities mapped)
                                                                                
2) The usage scenario diagram will then be exported for public access in the IBM Architecture Center, after validation by the appropriate stakeholders.
3) The design of a containerized-based architecture (hybrid/multiCloud) leveraging IBM solution blueprint, supporting the proposed Reference Architecture for the selected use-case in each sprint. This design will include the high-level integration architecture, leveraging microservices and API based communication between components.
outcome: This Consumer Industry Reference Architecture set of artifacts supports the design, optimized for Cloud and AI, of a selected business scenario. These use cases selected represent a subset of the global Reference Architecture and focus on building blocks (functional) involved in the user-stories. It is built for maximum re-usability. It will drive our opportunities with clients forward and maintain and augment IBM’s thought leadership in the Consumer industry. Tap into the thought leadership from our client facing sellers and technical experts to drive the business. finalOutcome: The co-leaders and the volunteers actually delivered a tremendous set of outcomes, materialized by a Solution-Brief that is under publication on the IBM Architecture Center. Sophie Kuijt and Jaya B. Rao managed to lead a team of 11 volunteers, additionally to their daily job roles, with a effective leadership style and agile way of working. The Consumer global community will get great benefits while leveraging those "ready to use" solution briefs.
closeValue: This initiative delivered an industry-based (use-case) solution approach to facilitate and accelerate the engagements of our teams globally.

title: Multi-modal AI Assistants for Data Visualization, Analytics, and Decision-Making
problemStatement: IBM is making a serious investment in AI, but we are not paying nearly enough attention to how those AI capabilities should be consumed. In the consumer space, the rapid rise of voice-driven assistants such as Alexa, Google Home, and Siri -- now installed on a billion devices worldwide -- have demonstrated that humans find it compelling to interact with AI as a quasi-human via natural language. It seems obvious that business people would also prefer AI tools with which they can interact naturally -- but IBM has so far kept with the old paradigm of AI as a menu-and-mouse-based tool rather than AI as a collaborator. IBM needs to place a priority on developing multi-modal AI assistants that understand speech and non-verbal modes of communication that humans use with one another, such as pointing, head orientation, gesture, facial expressions, etc. New research and engineering challenges arise in this context, such as inferring human intent from multi-modal sensor data and context, and supporting extended conversational interaction with data, analytics, and decision-making tools. IBM risks its leadership in business-oriented AI if we do not make multi-modal AI assistants a research and strategic priority.
outcome: A successful AoT study of multi-modal AI assistants for data visualization, analytics and decision-making would establish a broad research agenda that cuts across most of the major areas of AI, and result in either a significant broadening of our current theme in human-AI interaction or an entirely new strategy area. It would expose gaps in our current research portfolio, and suggest how we might capitalize on existing skills and expertise to fill those gaps. To cite just one example among many, our current world-class work in computer vision might expand its purview to include more work on real-time recognition of human activity. Other research areas falling under this umbrella include speech, AI engineering (and the interplay between architecture and algorithms), and the potential use of neuro-symbolic AI to infer human intent from multi-modal signals on multiple time scales. On the business side, the study would seek to determine what are the most promising avenues for bringing such capabilities to market, for example via IBM Business Analytics or perhaps a more general framework that can be applied to a wider set of analytics and AI offerings. We would explore whether and how GBS could consume such capabilities, and make recommendations.

title: Develop Storage and Memory Predictions and Map Back to past Predictions
problemStatement: The computing industry, from cell phones, to desktops, to racks of servers, to edge compute solutions, all the way to cloud are constantly challenged by technology changes in the hardware they use. These all change at different rates and for different reasons. Poor prediction of these trends costs revenue and market competitiveness both for IBM and our clients. The problem we are trying to solve is to be able to predict short term and long term storage and memory trends in a way that better positions our products to be close to hardware and industry sweet spots. With memory many times being on the order of half of hardware costs, both small and big advantages impact the cost competitiveness of our servers. This also will mitigate issues with disappearing supply lines from technology going to end of life from our suppliers.
outcome: The expected technical outcome would be an analysis of past and future predictions and the development of best practices for developing plans for longer term system design and architecture as well as near term measurement of current behaviors and decisions. The expected business outcome would be to accurately predict current and future best practices to ensure maximum revenue and flexibility in offerings.

title: IBM Community Health: Louisiana Pilot - Project Eliminate Hep C
executiveChampionReason: Jim Batterton his the PEP Executive in Louisiana and is committed to help make LA Healthier, Safer, and Smarter. As the GM for Public Sector in GTS he is the perfect executive champion to usher us towards success.
description: The Louisiana Department of Health (LDH) and IBM have partnered to eliminate hepatitis C - the deadliest infectious disease in the United States. Our solution was designed to scale and support other health conditions including COVID-19. Together, LDH & IBM are working closely with patients, community health workers, NGOs, local clinics, and health care providers on a technology platform that will help cure all 50,000 HCV patients in Louisiana by 2024.
problemStatement: Hepatitis C is the deadliest infectious disease in the United States - yet it is curable. In 2017, Louisiana was only able to treat 400 of the estimated 70,000 patients who suffer from the condition. Hepatitis C care costs the State of Louisiana over $100 million per year. In 2019 LA made a major breakthrough in lowering the cost of the treatment enabling Medicaid to lift former treatment restrictions. Today, everyone can and should be cured. However, patients face numerous barriers to treatment including transport to appointments, stigma, historical treatment failure, lack of trusted support, social determinants of health, and more. Patients need a way to connect with trusted community health coaches who can reward them and guide them on their journey to cure. Our solution is currently being customized to support the COVID-19 outbreak in Louisiana.
outcome: IBM and LDH co-designed and started development of the IBM Community Health Platform to help patients connect with community health coaches who support them on their journey to cure. In April, IBM CSR will deploy 18 IBMers to Baton Rouge as a part of the IBM Service Corps program. Post pilot IBM will offer IBM Community Health to LA as a cloud SaaS offering via NASPO procurement model. This Platform is scalable to support conditions beyond hep C including substance use disorder, HIV, STDs, mental health, and more - including COVID-19. Additionally, it can be scaled across the U.S. and globally - IBM is already in conversations with PA around opioid addiction, and USAID for a global approach. The State of Louisiana has obtained a federal grant from CMS in support of this work and has contributed to marketing assets that will drive significant brand value. Our solution is build natively on IBM Cloud, is moving to Red Hat Open Shift, and has been a ONE IBM project with GTS, CSR, GBS, Global Markets, IBM Research, Watson Health and now AoT. We believe this Open approach to solving a Social Impact Moonshot is what IBM is all about.
finalOutcome: IBM Community Health was sold and delivered to Sonoma County, CA. Additionally, the platform is being pitched to dozens of clients including Cook County, Auburn University, TCU, San Diego, and more.
closeValue: This team was able to pivot a first of a kind asset to support the safe re-opening of Sonoma County, CA in the middle of a global pandemic.
publicationDescription: The IBM Community Health AoT Initiative helped Sonoma County, CA safely re-open during the COVID-19 pandemic. Our team has created a new IBM Asset that is opening doors with numerous clients.
ratingComments: Thanks to the team!

description: Blockchain Solutions Architecture Decisions - Update and Merging with Blockchain Solutions Architecture Reference
problemStatement: Currently, there are two distinct initiatives to drive blockchain reference architectures in IBM: IBM-wide Blockchain Architecture Board (BlockchainAB) and GBS-led Blockchain Solution Reference Architecture (BSRA). Although both have different objectives (BlockchainAB is solution-driven, BSRA is service-centric), there is a number of similarities in both form (markdown documentation based on github) and content (Hyperledger Fabric as a platform of choice). As a result, there is a risk of duplicating efforts affecting both contributors and reviewers, inconsistencies in architecture recommendations and content overlaps.
outcome: The objective of this initiative is to update and merge Blockchain Architecture Board Architecture Decisions with Blockchain Solutions Reference Architecture. The expected outcome will be a single source of information for architecture considerations and decisions encompassing both the platform and services. The business value arising from this initiative will be a unified Blockchain Reference Architecture for IBM with strong support from contributors and reviewers previously representing both initiatives.
finalOutcome: The initial scope was expanded to address a wider degree of requirements coming from both technical and enterprise architects, including industry-related factors, platform choice, operational aspects etc. This deliverables of this initiative will directly benefit all persons responsible for going through a full cycle of an architecture of a blockchain-based solution.
closeValue: End-to-end capability to perform a walkthrough (journey) with the Client to build a blockchain solution.
ratingComments: This was a true testament to pulling together the technical blockchain community across IBM and unifying artifacts to be used in Blockchain engagements into one central focal.   Great initiative and leadership!

executiveChampionReason:

description: Mobile app development is changing and as we can see part of this change is Swift UI and Combine. Two frameworks that will become more and more popular as this will be the basis of development on Apple platforms starting this fall.

title: ** COVID-19 ** | RT-PCR Test Pooling Simulator
executiveChampionReason: Auto Selected from Admin Page
description: RT-PCR test pooling simulator to allow scaling of COVID-19 testing capabilities without the need for more test kits
problemStatement:
There is increasing evidence that RT-PCR test pooling might be a viable alternative to rapidly increase COVID-19 test capabilities, as per articles such as https://www.technologyreview.com/2020/04/28/1000671/covid-tests-millions-per-day-crispr-biotechnology-advances/ and https://www.theguardian.com/commentisfree/2020/may/21/africa-coronavirus-successes-innovation-europe-us and https://www.timesofisrael.com/to-ease-global-virus-test-bottleneck-israeli-scientists-suggest-pooling-samples/.

Nevertheless, it is not obvious what is the threshold of average disease prevalence rate at which test pooling is not longer worthwhile or what is the optimal why to do a binary search within a batch that has one or more infected individuals.
outcome: A simple simulator, written in Python3, that, given a population size, prevalence rate, pool size and number of iterations, in a "Monte Carlo" fashions, makes multiple runs and informs the optimal (in terms of the smaller number of RT-PCR tests requires) divisor for the binary search within the batch, together w/ the total number of RT-PCR tests and swabs that will be spent.
finalOutcome: Create a pool testing simulator for COVID-19, do simulations for a renowned epidemiologist, publish the results and find the optimal divisor, when a batch has one or more infected individuals in it.
participants: Marcelo Lopes de Macedo Ferreira Cândido
closeValue: Contribute, indirectly, to scale COVID-19 testing.

title: Core Banking modernization - POV
executiveChampionReason: Bala is a recognized leader in cloud transformation and has been instrumental in building the move, build cloud offerings which includes modernization. He is also the current CTO for CAS (move, build). As this study is an extension to the generic modernization offering in CAS, his executive leadership would help to shape up the output of the study
description: Core banking system has always been the heart of banks, however on the flip side it does act as inhibitor to the bank in terms of digital transformation due to its monolith nature. This POV describes the nuances, methodology, progressive transformation approach very specific to Core banking considering the functional aspects as well
problemStatement:
Banks are finding stringent competion from fintechs who offer innovative digital products in record time. Traditional banks are not in a situation to speed up to fintech as the existing Core system being monolith and does not offer speeder time to market and innovative product set. Replacing the existing core system is next to impossible however there are ways in which banks can speed up to fintech through progressive modernization. This journey is not purely technology based however has to be looked from business value realization, non-disruptive transition through co-existence etc. 
                                        Also core banking systems do not operate in silos the integration points are significantly high which  impact the transformation and their disposition strategies also need to be taken into account. Plus the transformation must not dilute NPS, regulatory compliance and also must not call for massive change management which would impact the bank culturally.
outcome:
The study will generate POV both functional and technical aspect how the progressive transformation can be achieved. It will include assets such as BIAN based user journey approach, BIAN based API catalogue, functional sequencing. Transformation approach such as full transformation, Hallow out, Value realization framework, Partial replacement. The output will include multi-cloud based architecture to take care of aspects such as PCI-DSS, GDPR which Openshift as the foundational architecture.  
                                        Study also will include reference architecture for end state and co-existence period, estimation framework, squad model, Tooling strategy for discovery etc.
finalOutcome:
Any new bank modernization & transformation opportunity can leverage this POV to identify transformation variant from here.  Specific solution components from specific variation can be leveraged. 
This helps focusing on key characteristics of a variant, associated risks, mitigations & technical choices so that optimal solution can be narrowed down
closeValue: cookbook for core banking modernization
publicationDescription:
This AOT study brings in both the domain and technical aspects of core banking modernization. Though there are modernization offerings in CAS it does not cover the nuances in core banking.

For past two years there is significant pipeline in core banking modernization for agility, cost take out, flexibility, time to market etc.. This study would act as playbook for cloud and banking architects to identify the optimal modernization strategy, apply the approach, mitigate risks. 

In the current era there is a need for banks to operate in partnership with Fintechs and ecosystems partner which needs core banking transformation

title: Last Updated: 2020-01-08Contribute in GitHub:Open doc issue|Edit topic What is IBM Analytics Engine? IBM Analytics Engine provides a flexible framework to develop and deploy analytics applications on Hadoop and Spark. It allows you to spin up Hadoop and Spark clusters and manage them through their lifecycle. How is an IBM Analytics Engine cluster different from a regular Hadoop cluster? IBM Analytics Engine is based on an architecture which separates compute and storage. In a traditional Hadoop architecture, the cluster is used to both store data and perform application processing. In IBM Analytics Engine, storage and compute are separated. The cluster is used for running applications and IBM Cloud Object Storage for persisting the data. The benefits of such an architecture include flexibility, simplified operations, better reliability and cost effectiveness. Read this whitepaper to learn more. How do I get started with IBM Analytics Engine? IBM Analytics Engine is available on IBM Cloud. Follow this link to learn more about the service and to start using it. You will also find tutorials and code samples to get you off to a fast start. Which distribution is used in IBM Analytics Engine? IBM Analytics Engine is based on open source Hortonworks Data Platform (HDP). To find the currently supported version see the documentation. Which HDP components are supported in IBM Analytics Engine? To see the full list of supported components and versions, see the documentation. What node sizes are available in IBM Analytics Engine? To see the currently supported node sizes, see the documentation. Why is there so little HDFS space on the clusters? What if I want to run a cluster that has a lot of data to be processed at one time? The clusters in IBM Analytics Engine are intended to be used as a compute clusters and not as persistent storage for data. Data should be persisted in IBM Cloud Object Storage. This provides a more flexible, reliable, and cost effective way to build analytics applications. See this whitepaper to learn more about this topic. The Hadoop Distributed File System (HDFS) should be used at most only for intermediate storage during processing. All final data (or even intermediate data) should be written to IBM Cloud Object Storage before the cluster is deleted. If your intermediate storage requirements exceed the HDFS space available on a node, you can add more nodes to the cluster. How many IBM Analytics Engine clusters can I spin up? There is no limit to the number of clusters you can spin up. Is there a free usage tier to try IBM Analytics Engine? Yes, we provide the Lite plan which can be used free of charge. However, this plan is available only to institutions that have signed up with IBM to try out the Lite plan. See How does the Lite plan work? When you move to a paid plan, you are entitled to $200 in credit that can be used against IBM Analytics Engine or any service on IBM Cloud. This credit is only allocated once. How does the Lite plan work? The Lite plan provides 50 node-hours of free IBM Analytics Engine usage. One cluster can be provisioned every 30 days. After the 50 node-hours are exhausted, you can upgrade to a paid plan within 24 hours to continue using the same cluster. If you do not upgrade within 24 hours, the cluster will be deleted and you have to provision a new one after the 30 day limit has passed. A cluster created using a Lite plan has 1 master and 1 data node (2 nodes in total) and will run for 25 hours on the clock (50 hours/2 nodes). The node-hours cannot be paused, for example, you cannot use 10 node-hours, pause, and then come back and use the remaining 40 node-hours. What types of service maintenance exist in IBM Analytics Engine? Occasionally, we need to update the IBM Analytics Engine service. Most of these updates are non-disruptive and are performed when new features become available or when updates and fixes need to be applied. Most updates that are made to the system that handles service instance provisioning are non-disruptive. These updates include updates or enhancements to the service instance creation, deletion or management tools, updates or enhancements to the service management dashboard user interface, or updates to the service operation management tools. Updates to the provisioned IBM Analytics Engine clusters might include operating system patches and security patches for various components of the cluster. Again, many of these updates are non-disruptive. However, if there is an absolute need to perform a disruptive deployment, you will be notified well in advance via email communication and on the IBM Cloud status page. When a disruptive deployment is made to the system that handles the provisioning of a service instance, you will be unable to create, access, or delete an IBM Analytics Engine service instance from the IBM Cloud console or by using the service instance management REST APIs. When a disruptive deployment is made to a provisioned service instance, you will not be able to access the IBM Analytics Engine cluster or run jobs.
** COVID-19 ** | Safe To Touch
executiveChampionReason: Auto Selected from Admin Page
description: A cognitive technology based method and system which can tell the user whether a surface is safe to touch and also how to touch it without getting contaminated.
problemStatement:
To save people from getting contaminated by simply touching a surface  it is really critical to aware them with a prior intimation. Mobile devices like mobile phone, headphones, smart glasses, hatch-bolt, smart watch or any portable smart device being the all time with us can be easily leveraged to capture a image of the surface or object next to you and can get to know whether the surface can spread contamination or completely safe and how safely you can handle it and this way the person can be saved from being contaminated just by touching.

To further clarify we are referring to contamination by touching surfaces like door lock, door, window, lift button, handle, door bell, door handle, handrail, news paper, parcel, packet, box or any physical object which can possibly contain the virus and by using cognitive technology we can easily guide the person on how to safely touch a surface or refrain from touching it.
outcome:
The cognitive system and method works based on the following procedure where - 
1) Every time user approaches a surface user can take an image or the portable device can automatically capture the image of the surface.
2) Based on image the cognitive system and method immediately triggers an analysis of the image in the background and come up with the surface classification along with additional detail guidance.
3) Based on the guideline the cognitive system ask the user to confirm the decision on whether user actually touched the surface with safety measures.
4) In case if the surface can cause possible contamination the cognitive system and method registers the surface along with additional details like date, time, location.
5) In case of any future contamination of the user, doctors and users can refer to touch history and can probable identify the possible causes of contamination.
6) In case of high risk surface the cognitive system can even trigger communication to the maintenance department to take preventive measures and regularly disinfect the surface or object or to move it away.

description: Potential mentoring, education and interaction with local P-TECH students (Falcon Tech) during COVID-19
problemStatement: IBM Boulder is looking at how to regularly interact and maintain relationships with the local P-TECH School (Falcon Tech) students.  Since P-TECH  students and IBMers can't meet face-to-face for mentoring events that include education, we looked into ways to maintain that interaction and personalization in spite of this obstacle. This initiative will explore what Business Units can contribute to educating these students on technical topics. It will also determine how best to continue to mentor these students, now that all interactions must be virtual.
outcome: Hold multiple, virtual education sessions for local P-TECH students on various topics, including IT careers, Cloud Computing, Data Analytics and other relevant topics. Record all sessions for replay when convenient and for use in future semesters. After the virtual live sessions are held, host an online forum (platform TBD)  during which mentees can get feedback from local IBMers on what waslearned. Working in conjunction with the local community college, students can earn college credit if they do a report on the various topics and present their findings virtually to a group of IBMers for review.  IBMers will also recommend, mentor and review student projects.  IBMers in Boulder will document a best practice for virtual PTECH sessions that can be leveraged by other affiliates facing the same challenges.
finalOutcome: Over the summer IBM Boulder was able to hold multiple, virtual education sessions for the local P-TECH students (Falcon Tech) on cybersecurity. These sessions were recorded to be used for future semesters.  Groups of students researched specific cybersecurity topics (for college credit) and gave virtual presentations on these topics.  IBMers PTECH Mentors attended these virtual presentation and provided soft skills feedback to the students using an online google form created by the local community college.  This format allowed the local PTECH school, IBM Boulder and the local community college ways to continue to teaching the PTECH technical knowledge but also soft skills.  This initiative allowed us to see what can be done to continue the interaction with students virtually in the future.
closeValue: We can still make an impact in PTECH students lives even doing virtual sessions with them.

executiveChampionReason: Rory is the TME (Telco, Media and Entertainment) Industry Leader for the MEA IOT. He has a full coverage of TME Industry in the region. I believe that he can leverage the solution that we will try to develop. Also, he can provide us connections if we will need further support from the extended wider IBM teams.
industryName: Telecom Media and Entertainment Industry Affiliate
description: Leveraging Telco data to create new reveue strems for Telco clients by introducing a Digital Platform
problemStatement:
Telecom operators are not only providers of their own digital products and services but also enablers for other sectors, by providing the essential connectivity infrastructure for functioning and growing in the digital economy.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                        
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                        As the overall digital market grows, the door for new over-the-top (OTT) entrants is still open. Because, these digital natives are offering the same staple services of voice, messaging, and video calls that used to be the domain of traditional Telcos. In particular, OTT players such as Apple’s FaceTime, Google Hangouts, Skype, Tencent QQ or Tencent’s WeChat, and WhatsApp threaten to cannibalize these staple offerings with innovative, easy-to-use, and even more-attractive messaging and communication services.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                        
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                        At the same time, consumer behavior regarding traditional communication services is changing, and the total consumer spend on these services is expected to decline even while overall communications activity grows. Finally, as technological breakthroughs accelerate, more and more new digital natives are entering the core telco market with innovative business models and technologies, leaving many incumbents to wonder if they can keep up or if they will be displaced.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                        
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                        How Telco companies can create new revenue streams while utilizing their Telco data and how IBM can help?
outcome:
1-) Vision: We will define the scenarios for the future Telco Digital Platform Solutions
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                        2-) Research: We will explore the IBM Telco clients stories around the globe, dive into solutions behind these projects, assess the maturity and sustainability of solutions
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                        3-) PoV: We will aim to create a repeatable Industry Point of View which will be driven by IBM competitive advantage. We will select 2-3 clients to gain proper business context. Possible clients are Vodafone and Turk Telekom Group.
finalOutcome:
Sprint-1: Telecom operators will use data to increase customer satisfaction and improve product & service offering
Sprint-2: Telecom operators will create an ecosystem with the proposed model for data monetization
closeValue: Next Generation Telecom Digital Platform Reinvention
publicationDescription:
We did a study about how Telecom operators can utilize their data for the following items
1-) Increase customer satisfaction
2-) Generate new revenue streams 
3-) Develop ecosystem partnership with other organizations and industries

Overall, we analyzed the business problem, possible technologies and use cases, mapped them with IBM product and services, and recommended how to engage with IBM.

title: AI and Machine Learning Educational Roadmap
executiveChampionReason: Dario was the catalyst for this initiative. It was his and Susan’s call to action during our 2017 AoT Meeting in NY which inspired this initiative. We wholeheartedly agree with Dario’s view that all IBM employees should have a solid understanding of AI and Machine Learning.
description: During our AOT Regional Meeting in New York, VP of AI and IBMQ, Dario Gil, talked about what IBM is doing around Quantum Computing and AI, and presented a compelling argument why all IBMers must have a solid understanding of AI and Machine Learning. Inspired by his presentation and call to action, this initiative's goal is to create an AI and Machine Learning educational roadmap for all IBMers, from beginning and intermediate, to advanced learning.
problemStatement: Driven by the proliferation of data and advances in analytics and cognitive technologies, the global machine learning market is expected to grow to USD 8.81 Billion by 2022. This represents an enormous opportunity for IBM and its clients. However, many of our consultants lack the proper training in AI and Machine Learning, and so we often miss new business opportunities simply because our consultants are not equipped to talk to our clients about AI solutions and IBM’s offerings in this area.
outcome:
Our overall objective is to enable all IBMers, especially services consultants, to gain a solid understanding of AI and Machine Learning, by providing an educational roadmap that would enable them to propose and implement AI and Machine Learning solutions to our clients. We envision the following outcome for this initiative: 
                                        - Identification of a series of AI related courses through our Learning Journey, IBM Skills gateway, and IBM AI Academy. 
                                        We envision the following outcome for this initiative: 
                                        - Identification of a series of AI related courses through our Learning Journey and the IBM Skills gateway, classified into pre-requisites, essential learning, and advanced learning. These courses should provide a roadmap into AI knowledge and mastery for all IBMers.
                                        - The initiative deliverable will also explain why we’ve organized the courses in a specific order so that participants may better understand the bigger picture and which roadmap to pursue.
                                        - Where applicable, we will highlight the IBM Open Badges associated with different courses.
                                        - We will also recommend education on technologies from other market leaders, and cross-reference this information with our own catalog.
                                        - We will work with our Executive Champion, Dario Gil, to align our efforts with other initiatives.
finalOutcome: Mark Wegman, the team, and I accomplished what we set out to do with the aimlatibm@ibm initiative by proposing and introducing a new way of learning about AI and ML. We've presented the basis of our ideas to several folks and organizations within IBM through a demo website (aimlatibm.mybluemix.net). We will be creating a future initiative that expands on these ideas to create a hybrid learning platform, adaptable to other topics such as Red Hat OpenShift and Cloud.
closeValue: We've introduced a new, non-prescriptive, crowd-sourced way of learning about AI and ML within IBM.

title: Global Open Banking Landscape
executiveChampionReason: Chae An is the VP and CTO of IBM’s Global Financial Services Sector, and has worldwide responsibility for the technical strategy and architecture for business solutions for IBM's customers in financial services. Chae is providing architectural guidance and strategy on new technical innovations such as blockchain and digital transformation with APIs relevant for financial services clients.
description: Study the global open banking trends in major representative regions or countries worldwide
problemStatement: Open Banking has been gaining lots of tractions worldwide over the last few years, thanks to the PSD2 regulations in European Union. However, the level of adoptions of and approaches are very different among different regions or countries in the world. IBM clients are looking for understanding of key aspects of Open Banking approaches and level of adoptions to better define their business and technical strategy. IBM needs that market intelligence to better advise our clients and to define our own solutions strategy.
outcome: The main objective of this initiative is to study the Open Banking approaches and level of adoptions for each of the major regions / countries in the world, including Europe (UK, Germany, France), Asia (China, Japan), North America (USA, Canada), South America (Brazil, Peru), Middle East (UAE, Israel), Oceania (Australia), Africa. Key aspects of Open Banking approaches and level of adoptions will include main regulations / initiatives, technical standards from regulators or associations of banks, how the banks / fintechs / customers respond to that, and representative example applications in the marketplace. The results of the study, which will be delivered in a report, will enable IBM to define our solutions strategy to better serve our financial services clients.
finalOutcome: The initiative covers various aspects of open banking (regulatory / industry led activities, regulations and technical standards, use cases, and adoption levels by financial institutions and consumers) in 18 countries in 5 continents. The report also includes the consolidated view including executive summary, opportunities and prioritization matrix, use cases, technical reference architecture, and recommendations. The work is being used to support opportunities worldwide.
closeValue: This initiative covers open banking in 18 countries across the world with distilled insights that are valuable to clients in their journey to open banking.
publicationDescription: The report covers various aspects of open banking (regulatory / industry led activities, regulations and technical standards, use cases, and adoption levels by financial institutions and consumers) in 18 countries in 5 continents. The report also includes the consolidated view including executive summary, opportunities and prioritization matrix, use cases, technical reference architecture, and recommendations.

title: Rochester TVC Local High School AP Comp Science Tutoring for 2019-2020 School Year
executiveChampionReason: As the Senior MN Site Executive, Tory both has an interest in supporting outreach programs AND has a need to know what activities are occurring.  He's historically been very supportive of this program.
description: This initiative places IBMers in the 3 AP Computer Science classes, one per local public high school, on a weekly basis to tutor, provide insight on topics with which the teacher want more assistance, and to run a programming competition.
problemStatement: Local high school Advanced Placement Computer Science teachers reached out to IBM several years ago for tutors as a way to both assist with the day-to-day questions raised by young programming students, but also as an opportunity for the students to meet professionals in a field which they may want to work. outcome: IBM will place 1 tutor per week from October through January and then 2 per week from February through the end of school in June.  IBM will also develop and host a programming competition among the schools as the final project.  Finally, IBM will serve as SMEs for various topics as needed by the teachers.
finalOutcome: 19 IBM tutors provided over 70 hours of classroom tutoring in Java for the AP Computer Science curriculum for 64 students (50 male, 14 female) across three schools.  All involved -- tutors, teachers, and students -- found these interactions throughout the 2019-2020 school year to be highly rewarding. Unfortunately, the programming competition this year was cancelled due to COVID-19 school changes and after deliberation with the teachers. Additionally, this year tutors provided extra support for a long term substitute teacher providing nearly daily coverage for roughly two weeks.
closeValue: This initiative promotes IBM community giveback in the local AP Computer Science classes to mentor and inspire the next generation of programmers.

title: ARCHIVE Emb(race): Police and Judicial Reform and Accountability Call for Code Challenge
executiveChampionReason: Dale is the co-champion for the Emb(race) CFC Challenge.
description: Emb(race): Judicial reform. From traffic stops and arrests to sentencing and parole decisions, use technology to better analyze real-world data, provide insights and make recommendations that will drive racial equality and reform across criminal justice and public safety.
problemStatement:
This Call for Code Challenge will explore how we can use IBM technology to address 3 problem statements related to Police & Judicial reform.

Police interactions with members of the Black community disproportionately end in unnecessary and avoidable escalation.

The lack of transparent and accurate data available to assess police behavioural infractions means police reports can be falsified and contain other inaccuracies.

People in the Black Community are faced with harsher downstream effects (charged at higher rates, assigned more significant charges, convicted at higher rates, given longer sentences, and denied parole more often) than people of other races for similar offenses.

Full details including hills aligned to each problem statement can be found here: https://github.com/Call-for-Code/Embrace-Judicial-Reform
outcome: To create open source code which not only addresses the problem statements and hills specified in the Emb(race) CFC challenge, but can also be used by developers around the world in order to expand and amplify the solutions created by IBM & Redhat teams.

description: The Study is meant to get an understanding of industry trends in cloud computing, and strategies our competitors are following in defining their cloud offerings, as a response to the industry demands.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                   Technology
outcome:

publicationDescription:
The Objective of this Study was to understand the potential evolution of cloud computing in the next 3-5 years based on the tactical trends observed today, and in alignment with the strategies by major cloud services providers. Initially, as part of the study strategy, the plan was to establish a 15-20-year outlook for cloud computing. However, the team decided to address a shorter time frame due to the accelerated evolution of cloud computing technologies and underlying concepts, thus potentially increasing the accuracy of the prediction.

title: Blockchain-based 5G Infrastructure Management
industryName: Telecom Media and Entertainment Industry Affiliate
problemStatement:
Today, almost all telecom operators are focused on building their next generation 5G networks, which requires huge investments. In order to reduce and support those costs, a lot of those operators put in place some infrastructure sharing agreements, typically at a country level, and many times they also decide to spin-off the cell tower management in a separate company.

This allows to reduce cost by sharing some of them, but it also adds complexities in managing the business relationships between those entities and the rest of the ecosystem. Blockchain is a good technology to address some of those problems. 
In addition, creating a 5G cell tower has to be considered holistically, from finding potential investors, finding and managing the real estate location, building and managing the physical infrastructure, to deploying and managing the software part of the tower.
 
IBM, with RedHat, is very well placed to help operators in this approach, with at least 3 strong capabilities:
-	IBM Tririga Real Estate and Facility Management
-	IBM Blockchain Platform and Services
-	IBM Telecom Network Cloud Manager (TNCM) and RedHat to orchestrate the provisioning and operations of the Virtualized or Containerized Network Functions
outcome:
Outcome is expected at 2 levels:
1. Provide a Point of View on the combined IBM value proposition in this domain and provide suggestions and recommendations on future capabilities or pre-integration to build
2. At the technical level, provide a reference architecture for a blockchain-based 5G infrastructure sharing platform, integrated with Tririga. If time and resources permit, a PoC could be built.

description: The IBM Developer JumpStart program is a cross business unit two-year onboarding program for our early professional developers introducing them to IBM's best practices, emerging technology and building a community of top talent, a network of peers and mentors and generating excitement across design, development and research communities.
problemStatement:
Launched in Q2 2017, the IBM Developer JumpStart program started as an on-boarding program to help acclimate our early professional developers to IBM, introducing them to IBM technologies and processes and helping our developers grow their skills while building a network of peers and mentors.
                                                                                                                                                                                                        The IBM Developer JumpStart program is a premier onboarding experience for our early professional developers. The IBM Developer JumpStart program seeks to attract and retain our top talent in the industry to help drive innovation at IBM. The JumpStart program also attracts and engages top minds at IBM, Fellows, Distinguished Engineers, executive, design coaches, Master Inventors and technical mentors all brought together with the goals of building community, driving innovation and engaging our young talent. The JumpStart program seeks to break down the silos across the development, research and design communities and build a sense of excitement and energy across the IBM community.
outcome:
Since 2017,  over 1600 early professional developers have been enrolled in the JumpStart program. They have attended 45 Developer Day on-boarding classes, 55 all day Developer Slam events, launched 282 TechChallenge projects and attended 16 Patent Circle workshops earning the developers over 1500 digital badges and the submission of more than 750 patents!                                                                                                                                                                                                         
                                                                                                                                                                                                        The JumpStart program has engaged hundreds of volunteers as mentors, coaches, keynote speakers, facilitators and business sponsors including IBM Fellows, executives, Distinguished Engineers, STSMs, design coaches, master inventors, technical mentors, business sponsors and many more volunteers to help run the events and engage with our early professional developers.                                                                                                                                                                                                        
                                                                                                                                                                                                        Through the AoT Initiative program, we have been able to extend our reach beyond North America by connecting with mentors and coaches in Europe and Asia in addition to the U.S. and Canada. Through all day events, patent mentoring and coaching to deliver user-focused outcomes, the IBM Developer JumpStart program is growing the skills of our early professional developers while driving engagement and excitement across the IBM Development, Design and Research communities across North America and beyond.                                                                                                                                                                                                        
                                                                                                                                                                                                        Because of the success of JumpStart, we need a new initiative to record and maintain new volunteer support.
finalOutcome: From its inception in Q2 2017, the JumpStart program has enrolled over 2000 early professional developers and delivered 61 Developer Day on-boarding classes, 75 Developer Slams that launched 300 TechChallenge projects, offered 31 patent circles and issued over 1900 digital badges while bringing together thousands of volunteers including executives, DEs, fellows, STSMs, design coaches, master inventors, technical mentors and volunteers to drive engagement and excitement across our development, design and research communities.
