title: Cornell spring 2020 Project "Mainframe Quality Inspection with  IBM Visual Insights"
executiveChampionReason: Robert Edge Jr (Director, Worldwide Server and Solutions Fulfillment owns critical missions (quality, processing, testing, early manufacturing involvement with designs) in Mainframe and Power Manufacturing across multiple GEOs.
description: IBM collaborating with the Spring 2020 Cornell University students in the graduate class "Mgt of Technology" to researching the use of IBM visual insights & techniques to help automate the Mainframe quality inspection process by eliminating the human eye balling sensitivity which is error prone.
problemStatement:
The existing final quality inspection process is human controlled and uses a checklist criteria and iPads to document quality issues identified by the technician during the process. The technician’s comments and pictures are recorded/uploaded for future reference and investigation. This process is error prone due to human mistakes/negligence (i.e. visual misses, sloppy work, etc…) and there is no guarantee that the identified problem has been corrected, resulting in quality problems escaping to the field.

There is a need to develop an automated solution that will operate in real-time to address the quality issues escaping from the factory.
outcome:
The SCE executive sponsor, Robert Edge Jr (Director, Worldwide Server and Solutions Fulfillment owns critical missions (quality, processing, testing, early manufacturing involvement with designs) in Mainframe and Power Manufacturing across multiple GEOs.  This collaboration with the graduate students from Cornell is to focus on the research and design constraints around incorporating IBM visual insights (IVI) and other techniques into the Mainframe final quality inspection processes with goal of improving the error prone / laborious human based inspections currently in practice today.

Deliverables as an outcome: 
-	What is the optimal picture booth for performing this task ?   
-	What is the resulting cost analysis surrounding the setup use of the Gantry for the visual inspection?  
-	What are the models and expected results with the existing datasets ?
-	What is the framework for pre/post processing of IVI?
-	List of assumptions made throughout the analysis
-	Identification of risks and a mitigation plan for each risk
-	Final Report 
-	Cornell team to share a final presentation via WebEx or onsite to the IBM team
finalOutcome: The business value was based on utilizing technology to automate manual quality inspection processes in manufacturing for the main frame product in prep for customer readiness.  The manual inspection processes are tedious, boring, dependent on eye balling, can vary from person to person depending on skill/capability, hence leading to process inefficiencies and problems/defects escaping to the field.  These quality escapes to the field can lead to customer churn, loss in revenue for customer and IBM as well as additional service call that can be avoided.  The outcome of this initiative involved expanding our IOT team roster to include six additional team members from Cornell's MOT senior projects class.  This team performed research in the field of image recognition/defect detection and Gantry designs to support automation of manual quality inspections.  The Cornell students work utilized IBM visual insights to build and train models for detecting defects, several gantry prototypes, decision matrix of design attributes, pros and cons of the designs and cost analysis.  The impact realized from this initiative consisted of new ideas that our IBM team had not thought of or invested time investigating and concepts that we (IBM) can build on to improve our products overall quality.
closeValue: The opportunity  IBM's technology (i.e. in this case IBM visual Insights) enables for Students to innovate and solve industry problems

title: Work with 1-3 clients to build the business case for IoT/ AI-powered manufacturing.
problemStatement:
Many manufacturing companies already have some IoT devices in their operations (often embedded in existing equipment) but have not capitalized on the information that those devices could provide them -- and the analytics, using the data from those devices, that could provide them with business-critical alerts and performance information.

The proposal is to work with several manufacturing sites to (1) evaluate their current IoT capabilities (count no. of sensors/ machines with sensors, identify whether they are already 'connected', etc.); (2) understand why/ whether they have decided not to pursue IoT up to this point (or if they have simply ignored the idea); (3) obtain key performance & cost data for the site (OEE, rough operating cost, cost of downtime, capacity constraints, value of additional capacity, etc.); (4) put together a high-level cost estimate of the cost to install an IoT infrastructure and AI application; and (5) build a high-level business case for implementing an IoT infrastructure and enabling AI-powered manufacturing. 

We would most likely need to hide the actual identity of the facilities, but we would provide details of the business case to the facilities themselves.
outcome: This project would provide us with real life examples of client manufacturing sites and whether IoT and AI-power manufacturing would produce sufficient benefits, fast enough, to be a GREAT business case (low cost, high & fast benefits); a MODERATE business case (low to moderate cost, moderately high and 'steady' benefits); or a POOR business case (high costs, low and slow benefits).

title: AI Security - Benefit of AI in Security & Security of AI, complementing each other
problemStatement:
The main idea of this topic is to explore the security of AI, in terms of protecting the integrity and confidentiality of AI models and data, and thus preventing attackers from changing the inference results or stealing the data. This idea also highlight how the AI/ML mechanism will help most basic and important security aspects like RBAC, IAM, AUTH, ENCRYPTION, DATA @REST AND IN MOTION for business-critical solutions so that the solution can be prevented by the attackers after applying self-judgment and decision-making capabilities of AI/ML.
This idea will mitigate the common security challenges as mentioned below: 
-	The code, AI models, hosting platforms, and machine chips attacked by attackers
-	Infect malicious data in AI Model that destroys the data integrity. 
-	AI model cloning to effect on confidentiality
-	Impact on Data privacy
-	Unsmart and traditional security pattern (RBAC, IAM, AUTH, ENCRYPTION, DATA @REST AND IN MOTION)
-	Critical security attacks, threat and vulnerability.
outcome:
The goal of this idea is to provide a confident and secure the traditional application using AI/ML and secure the AI application environment by aiding AI enabled intelligent security world. In order to tackle the security challenges, this idea will provide a technical proposal and realization how to defence the traditional and AI application for being secured using AI/ML mechanism. The main approach will be:
-	Propose a reference architecture of intelligent defence mechanisms for known attacks on traditional and AI components. 
-	Design for AI model robustness.
-	Create a secure architecture with various security mechanisms to safeguard business security.
-	Step by step guidelines of the architecture/design by considering simple Use-case.

title: 2020 Texas JumpStart SLAM: Intentional Inclusion Tech Challenge
executiveChampionReason: Rhonda is the AoT Executive Sponsor for the Austin TVC.
description: The Tech Challenge project is the pinnacle of the IBM Developer JumpStart program. The IBM Developer JumpStart program provides professional development, networking, and skills enhancement opportunities for IBM entry-level software and hardware developers.  The 2020 Intentional Inclusion Technical Challenge for the Texas cohort will empower JumpStarters to expand their knowledge beyond their day job and use their skills to support IBM's commitment to  equity, inclusion, and diversity.   The JumpStarters will form a cross-unit team to develop an innovative and engaging before and after demo UI that will help developers and UX designers better understand the barriers people with disabilities face so that they can in turn build more inclusive accessible products or quickly fix accessibility issues.
problemStatement:
Accessibility continues to be an enormous challenge for all organizations. The typical struggles include limited budgets, shortage of accessibility skills and an overwhelming number of accessibility issues lurking in their business applications and services creating a business liability that results in bolting in accessibility rather than building it in. 

The IBM Developer JumpStart program is a key differentiator for IBM that helps with recruiting in a competitive marketplace and supports efforts to engage and retain top technical talent. The SLAM helps new hires get hands-on tutorials in strategic technologies, practice and develop collaboration skills, and apply Design Thinking methodology through the  "Tech Challenge".  

The Intentional Inclusion Tech Challenge will look at ways to provide a fun, interactive, real-time experience for UX/Content designers and developers to learn about the barriers people with disabilities face navigating/interacting with the web content and understand the accessibility requirements to build more inclusive accessible products or quickly fix issues with an innovative, engaging before and after demo UI.
outcome:
Participants will be aligned in teams to work on a self-directed "challenge", with guidance from SMEs and IBM Design Thinking coaches. They will present a working prototype for executives to review and select the "best" (effective solution, design, and impact) at the second SLAM event. 

The Intentional Inclusion Tech Challenge will empower JumpStarters to expand their knowledge beyond their day job and use their skills to support IBM's commitment to equity, inclusion, and diversity. 

A small cross-unit team will develop a before (with accessibility issues) and after (issues resolved) demo UI that demonstrates accessibility problems and how to address those.  

Building inclusive accessible products can become a key differential for IBM products in the market place and minimize business risk. The demo UI can be used to educate designers and developers in IBM product development teams and help maintain IBM’s leadership in equity, inclusion, and diversity.

15% of the population has a disability, and we have a moral obligation to be inclusive of this population in our designs. Also, designing to be inclusive of the 15% of people with a disability improves the experience for the 85% of people without a disability as well (overlap in best practices).

title: Technology Gaps in Contract Consolidation, Conversion and Cognition
executiveChampionReason: He owns this mission and requested help to accelerate completing it
description: The purpose of this initiative is to crowdsource info on IBM contract quality standards, pain points and existing technology that can be leveraged to address known issues for retrieving completed contracts using a consistent set of standard metadata and applying cognitive tools to gain rapidly gain insights to the contract content.
problemStatement:
Companies are seeking better, faster ways to analyze contracts to understand obligations and risks, and to close the deal faster during contracts negotiation. Revenue leakage due to risky language in contracts is identified as a major root cause. Often it is due to clients requiring special contract clauses that derivative from our standard sales contracts, like “bank guarantee”, or sending their own contracts template. This not only introduces risks but also requires tremendous amount of time in iterative contract legal reviews.
                                                                                Advanced analytics and cognitive/artificial intelligence technologies add value in pre- and post-contract signing. However, there are many gaps to be addressed throughout the technology pipeline. Starting from consolidating contracts from the fragmented repositories into one, to converting the picture ‘pdf’ contract into text for processing, to enhancing the metadata associated with each contract, to making it easily searchable by sellers are examples today’s challenges and pre-requisites before we can even run any text analytics. Furthermore, we need to address technologies to extract metadata, compare clauses for the various use cases from the legal, procurement, delivery, accounting perspectives in order to reduce risk exposure and speed up contract signing.
outcome:
White paper
                                                                                Technology assets
finalOutcome:
Overall:
                                        created awareness of contract AI within IBM via AoT Blog in Feb 2019 with 318 views and 13 likes
                                        shared state-of-the-art with Manish Goyal's GBS AI team in face to face meeting with Ulrike Zeilberger and subsequent meetings with team
                                        Educated AoT initiative volunteers on contract AI challengers & techniques
                                        
                                        Metadata (workstream 1) saves manual up front labeling of contract documents by introducing clustering technique.
                                        
                                        Table extraction (workstream 2) identified 2 table extraction tools. C&C and CCS that are viable alternatives for performing extraction of key contract data.
                                        
                                        Annotation of contractual terms (workstream 3) i) identified a tool called Watson Knowledge Studio to help SME lable contract terms with ease, ii)  WS3 introduced supervised & unsupervised techniques that can further save manual up front labeling of contract terms by attorneys or legal SME.
                                        
                                        Generated reusable asset about the existing technology capabilities in AI contract processing pipeline.
closeValue: Manish Goyal collected and leveraged knowledge from this initiative for 1 client engagement in the Financial Services Sector
publicationDescription: Report will contain summary of  information collected, tools assessment and selection results and path forward for the Contract AI initiative.
ratingComments: We've been leading the charge on gathering, storing, converting, and analyzing contracts for valuable insights across the enterprise for a few years now.  This AoT study has helped us overcome significant obstacles that we have found in our journey.  Thank you!

title: TEC-J Showcase #5: Deployment of P-TECH in Japan and Role of Engineer
executiveChampionReason: Kuse-san is an executive champion of TEC-J.
description: TEC-J Showcase provides opportunities for TEC-J Working Groups to present their thoughts, best practices and innovative ideas that have been discussed in their study and researches with other TEC-J members in timely manner. It enables TEC-J Working Groups to exchange ideas and receive various feedbacks from TEC-J members and SMEs in a broad context. In this TEC-J Showcase session, the speaker presents "Deployment of P-TECH in Japan and Role of Engineer ".
problemStatement: P-TECH is a program to develop IT engineers with high school and two-year advanced education, which IBM has started in US since 2011. Even though it is required to solve lack of IT engineers and improve working condition of high school graduates, there is few opportunities to consider how IT engineers in field  should be involved with education.
outcome: This talk will give an introduction of P-TECH and how to deploy it to Japanese educational institutions. A pilot project has been started at Tokyo Metro from last year towards formal open in 2022. TEC-J P-TECH working group has been established last year and has supported target schools for specialized subjects, mentoring, and carrier education with investigating what kind of people IT companies actually require. It will help the audience consider how engineers in field should be involved with education.
finalOutcome:
TEC-J Showcase #5 has just been held on May 25th, 2020 to share the TEC-J working group activity by Namba-san.
Firstly, she introduced global P-TECH, Pathways in Technology Early College High Schools, which IBM has started in US since 2011. Its main objectives are solving lack of IT engineers and improving working condition of high school graduates. In her talk, an activity of TEC-J P-TECH working group was introduced. It has been supporting target schools for specialized subjects, mentoring, and carrier education with investigating what kind of people IT companies actually require. Through her experiences of teaching actual classes of IT basics (hardware, software, network, programming language and career design) at school,  one of the most important things that IT engineers in field should tell them is "relevance", said Namba-san. Telling them relevance of how IT technology relates to their society motivates students to study it.
closeValue: P-TECH working group get a lot of attention and the audience realized how to be involved with education through TEC-J WG activity.

title: Explainability of Machine Learning models
executiveChampionReason: Beth is and has always been passionate about Data science. Being an expert in the field herself and a role model for data scientists across IBM, it would be an excellent opportunity to take a deeper dive for enhancing the understanding of aspiring software engineers to get more visibility into the modeling of different ML problems and inspire the DataScience community across the globe.
description: Aspiring Data Scientists need to be aware of which models to use and how to interpret the models based on dataset. Aim is to create a white paper on explainability of Machine Learning models.
problemStatement: Many people say machine learning models are "black boxes", in the sense that they can make good predictions but you can't understand the logic behind those predictions.When we deploy an expert system in a scientific domain, the users are more interested in how the system arrived at the output, then they are in the output itself.
outcome: A better understanding of Machine learning models is required to assist the Data Science community. The ability to explain the outcome of different machine learning models based on data inputs and gather insights for the clients would be highly beneficial for IBM. Output/outcome will be to generate a white paper out of the initiative and share insights with the Data Science community. This would help the IBM community to drive their results and insights with clients in a more transparent fashion.
finalOutcome: This establishes more visibility about IBM's unique position in the field of AI and current efforts being conducted AI explainability. In this paper, we outlined the business drivers for AI Explainability, clearly articulated the need for embedding AI Explainability during all stages of AI model development, deployment, and monitoring, and shared a summary of the latest Explainability techniques and algorithms.
closeValue: IBM's position in AI explainability and the ability to fortify its efforts in explaining AI to clients, thereby increasing our eminence, which inturn provides a need for the explanation to be provided in the context of the business use case to further promote trust and confidence in AI.
publicationDescription: This report concludes with the key point that providing an explanation in terms of feature values may not be sufficient for the business users to trust the AI decisions and hence, there is a need for the explanation to be provided in the context of the business use case to further promote trust and confidence in AI.
ratingComments: Excellent report and timely as I will be able to leverage this with our clients immediately as well as use this for ML@Scale and AI@Scale offering packages. Clearly written and well articulated. I am very pleased with this project.

title: Designing Container Solutions on IBM Z: Cloud Native Strategy and Technical Design Approach
executiveChampionReason:
After presenting a proposal to SVP Tom Rosamilia on the opportunities for integrating the Mainframe into the Cloud Native strategy by leveraging ICP as a worker node platform - Tom asked for a comeback after evaluating the technical feasability. 
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                Rohit badlaney leads the IBM Z as a Service development team and has a vested interest in expanding the capabilities of Z to include containerized workloads. 
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                Holger leads the Enterprise Platform competency in the IBM Cloud Solutioning centers Europe and is perfectly positioned to drive the adoption and get customer feedback for the proposal.
description: Prepare and deliver an technical solution enablement for leveraging IBM Z as a platform for running containerized workloads - analyze the integration and migration options available. Published at: https://w3-03.ibm.com/services/lighthouse/documents/137748
problemStatement:
IBM Z is a key platform for many of IBM's enterprise customers and hosts the majority of critical business data.
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                While the capability to deploy containerized workloads (ex: Docker/ICP workers on Linux on Z) exists, customer adoption has been slow - due to lack of integration and enablement for the seller, solutioning and architecture communities - especially when compared to the Intel platform.
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                The risk is that workloads that are hosted today on the IBM Mainframe may not grow, and could slowly get refactored to a Cloud Native architecture and / or move off the mainframe, potentially to our competitors.
outcome:
Define a series of Design-Thinking exercises, publications and solutions guidance to share the container strategy for Z into key IBM deals.
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                We will create a series of re-usable assets, including:
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                1) Elevator pitch, value proposition and common scenarios for a consistent container strategy on Z
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                2) Design principles, technical architecture
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                3) Solution artefacts to create a blueprint for a fast start when defining client _solutions_
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                The target audience is solutioning. The assets will shared on Lighthouse and a series of webinars will be delivered to the IBM Cloud solutioning community, to start enablement and gather initial feedback.
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                Business Value:
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                1) Leverage our incumbency to drive and modernize customer workloads and make Mainframe a key part of the Cloud Native strategy
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                2) Increase Z footprint for applications connected to a backend, and DevOps workloads
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                3) Provide mainframe customers with an agile development approach for Cloud Native applications
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                4) Offer a well-integrated solution to Mainframe customers that leverages IBM Cloud and prevent bleed to Azure/AWS
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                This is part of a series of initiatives, that will include solutioning guidance, architecture and deployment patterns, demo, etc. As potential clients for engagements are identified, the deal team is accompanied for probing our outcome.
finalOutcome:
Kick-off the solutioning and technical community to focus on Mainframe and Container workloads.
                                                                                                                                                                                                        
                                                                                                                                                                                                        Includes:
                                                                                                                                                                                                        - Entry Point for Discussion: Motivation – why do this on Z?
                                                                                                                                                                                                        - Application Modernization as a Trigger
                                                                                                                                                                                                        - A Word on ICP and OpenShift
                                                                                                                                                                                                        - Typical Architecture Diagrams
                                                                                                                                                                                                        - Typical Architectural Decisions and Implementation Considerations
                                                                                                                                                                                                        - Typical Solutioning Aspects
closeValue: Hands-on solutioning assets for containerised workloads on Z and kick-off of the technical community moving
publicationDescription: Container-based solutions on the mainframe require bringing together two different perspectives: how can Cloud Native thinking be implemented considering the capabilities and attributes of IBM Z. The Academy Study on Designing Container Solutions on IBM Z provides on overview of the relevant aspects and gives guidance in the solutioning process.
ratingComments: great work thx
adminComments: 1/2:  Changed status from Req for Pub to Req for Closure.  They published report thru lighthouse on their own.

title: IBM zEnterprise Data Compression (zEDC) - Exploitation Use cases
executiveChampionReason: Francesco is the Director and Global Service Area Leader for Mainframe Storage Services. As this initiative is related to Mainframe storage and systems domain, Francesco has provided his consent to be the executive champion for this initiative.
description: This initiative is focussed on IBM zEnterprise Data Compression (zEDC) implementation and exploitation. The outcome of the initiative will be a white paper/ webcast which will include use case and experience from client environment.
problemStatement: IBM zEnterprise Data Compression (zEDC) express feature is available as Peripheral Component Interconnect Express (PCIe) device in all the latest Mainframe servers and it provides hardware-based data compression and decompression capability. As IBM Z systems handle large volume of data, this data compression component could play a vital role in the enterprise and help clients process data efficiently. Given the importance of this component, we still see that there is less penetration in client environments and technical teams are finding it difficult to understand the real benefits and devise focussed/ phased way to exploit this component.
outcome:
Participants involved in this initiative would build exploitation uses cases (White paper/ Webcast) which will provide the following.
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                Initiative Outcome: 
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                - Provide a use case analysis model to determine the component value in the environment.
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                - Phased exploitation approach without business impact.
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                - Implementation reference and best practices.
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                Business value:
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                - Enable easy penetration of this component across environment.
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                - Provides handy reference to technical team to accelerate implementation and continued exploitation.
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                - Significantly savings to the client in different areas related to data management and improves system effectiveness.
finalOutcome:
Initiative Outcome:
                                                                                                                        • Provide a use case analysis model to determine zEDC value in the environment.
                                                                                                                        • Phased implementation approach without business impact.
                                                                                                                        • Implementation reference and best practices.
                                                                                                                        
                                                                                                                        Business value:
                                                                                                                        • Enable easy penetration of compression technology using zEDC across environment.
                                                                                                                        • Provides handy reference to technical team to accelerate implementation and continued exploitation.
closeValue: Whitepaper is now available in IBM Techdocs repository and it’s going to be a handy reference to technical team to accelerate zEDC implementation and continued exploitation
publicationDescription:
Mainframe Services team recently completed AoT initiative focused on zEnterprise Data Compression (zEDC) implementation and exploitation. This initiative is part of IBM Z global initiative called “Break The Cycle”. zEDC provides significant savings to the client in different areas related to data management and improves system effectiveness.
                                                                                                                        To reap it’s business value, team proposed an idea of creating a technical asset which will help teams implement and effectively
                                                                                                                        utilize zEDC in client environment. Core team for the initiative included technical experts from Mainframe platform & Storage
                                                                                                                        systems. Initiative project plan followed agile methodologies and team created various sprints with defined timeline to keep it on track. After brainstorming discussions, focus areas were derived from identified pain points and participants actively worked on the project deliverables. The outcome of the initiative was a technical whitepaper comprised of zEDC study, phased implementation approach, implementation reference, best practices and exploitation view points. Team also effectively utilized prior implementation experience, lessons learned and subject knowledge which made the final outcome more valuable. After multiple reviews, team condensed the whitepaper into just 20 pages with all required information. This will be a valuable asset to the technical team in their deployment efforts.
ratingComments: This AoT initiative developed a whitepaper extremely useful for Mainframe Services in the area of data compression. It was a great opportunity to prepare an asset to make easy to understand and implement this technology. Moreover the core team was selected across IBM business units and across the Globe with a great opportunity for technical networking. Thank you!

title: 2020 Texas JumpStart SLAM: Cybersecurity Tech Challenges
executiveChampionReason: Rhonda is the AoT Executive Sponsor for the Austin TVC
description: The Tech Challenge project is the pinnacle of the IBM Developer JumpStart program. This program provides professional development, networking, and skills enhancement opportunities for IBM entry-level software and hardware developers.  The 2020 Technical Challenges for the Texas cohort will empower JumpStarters to expand their knowledge beyond their day job and use their skills to support STEM learning across the world. The JumpStarters will form small cross-unit teams and develop activity kits targeted for STEM events and donate them back to ibm.org. These activity kits will help students learn about new technologies and their applications in a fun way. This initiative is for the Tech Challenges that will create Cybersecurity Activity Kits.
problemStatement:
The growth of jobs that require technical skills in areas such as artificial intelligence, security or data science presents an opportunity for young people, as well as a challenge to prepare them with a skill base built upon STEM fluency which is the key to innovation and the future. 

The IBM Developer JumpStart program is a key differentiator for IBM that helps with recruiting in a competitive marketplace and supports efforts to engage and retain top technical talent. The SLAM helps new hires get hands-on tutorials in strategic technologies, practice and develop collaboration skills, and apply Design Thinking methodology through the  "Tech Challenge".  

The 2020 Technical Challenges for the Texas cohort will support STEM learning by creating "Activity Kits" for Cybersecurity.  Activity Kits enable volunteers to leverage their specialized skills and talents to easily deliver engaging experiences to help STEM students learn about new technologies in a fun way.

Cybersecurity is an important technology with many business and consumer applications. The Cybersecurity Tech Challenges will help JumpStarters learn more about how this technology work and its different applications as they create Cybersecurity Activity kits for STEM students.
outcome:
Participants will be aligned in teams to work on a self-directed "challenge", with guidance from SMEs and IBM Design Thinking coaches. Between SLAMS they will work together to solve their technical challenge using new ideas and fresh viewpoints, share progress with their cohort and then present a working prototype for executives to review and select the "best" (effective solution, design, and impact) at the second SLAM event. 

The Tech Challenge will empower JumpStarters to expand their knowledge beyond their day job and use their skills to support STEM learning across the globe. 

The JumpStarters will form small cross-unit teams and develop Cybersecurity activity kits targeted for STEM events. These activity kits will be donated back to ibm.org and will be used to teach STEM students about the Cybersecurity technology and its applications.

title: Blockchain and Industry 4.0
executiveChampionReason: Christophe is the Director for the Electronics Industry with a significant focus on Industry 4.0 and Blockchain.
description: PoV article for IEEE Xplore -  The Internet of Things (IoT) will permit companies to leverage data from the network of machines and sensors in their workplaces, to achieve significant new benefits, lower costs and improve quality. However, because many industries have been ‘intermediated’ (where OEMs no longer do most of their own manufacturing), the benefits of Industrial IoT are hard to achieve in a quick and easy manner. The combination of Blockchain’s (secure, private) distributed ledger technology with IIoT data and cognitive analytics offers a compelling solution. To be effective, a solution will integrate multiple components, often with blockchain as the integration mechanism. The specific solution discussed in the article is a combination of IIoT data, cognitive visual analytics, and blockchain with an ERP system Specifically, the Quality module of SAP S/4HANA.
problemStatement:
OEM or product manufacturer subcontracts all or a large portion of their manufacturing to outside service providers -- but they are still responsible for the quality/ conformance/ performance of the product.

The problem for these companies is that even though using outside contractors helps them with working capital (it shifts a great deal of fixed cost to variable cost), and it can reduce costs in other areas, it also causes them to lose the ability to monitor, manage and control the manufacturing process itself. The OEM doesn't generally need to be able to monitor/manage/control every subcontractor or even every process at some subcontractors -- but there are certain areas that are critical to the quality and performance (or compliance) of their products that they often need to be more transparent.
outcome:
IoT technology and Industrie 4.0 offer a new way to make key subcontractor processes transparent to a customer, but there is often a complicating factor: the subcontractor and customer generally don't have a 1:1 relationship. The OEM customer may have more than one subcontractor that manufactures a product for them; and the subcontractor may use its manufacturing capacity to serve multiple customers. In both cases, those multiple relationships may well be with competitors, so privacy is critical. The subcontractor can't just open up all IoT data from "Production Line #1" to Customer A because that line also runs product for Customers B, C, and D. 

Blockchain provides an elegant and cost-effective solution. 
Three key focus areas:
1. How IoT/Industrie 4.0 can provide critical data from a subcontractor to an OEM customer, making the processes sufficiently transparent for the OEM to be confident that its products are being produced correctly, with high quality and the correct process parameters, in the right quantities at the right time
2. How Blockchain can enable IoT/Industrie 4.0 functionality to be shared privately, securely, and in a timely manner between parties
3. How the combination of IoT and Blockchain can be used effectively
finalOutcome: Industry 4.0, IIoT, blockchain and artificial intelligence provide an opportunity to derive intelligence for well-established institutions, and how the expanding body of knowledge of best practices can provide the vision, strategy and the industry on a global scale to drive a new revolution for manufacturers and their partners. Execution to build the body of knowledge and continuously improve is the fabric of manufacturing and Industry 4.0. The benefits outweigh the risk; manufacturers and other industries should evaluate how they can take advantage of these technologies in their own operations, with all due haste.
closeValue: Reduced cost and time associated with manual visual inspection, improved quality, increased consistency, ease to deployment.
publicationDescription: : The Internet of Things (IoT) will permit companies to leverage data from the network of machines and sensors in their workplaces, to achieve significant new benefits, lower costs and improve quality. However, because many industries have been ‘intermediated’ (where OEMs no longer do most of their own manufacturing), the benefits of Industrial IoT are hard to achieve in a quick and easy manner. The combination of Blockchain’s (secure, private) distributed ledger technology with IIoT data and cognitive analytics offers a compelling solution. To be effective, a solution will integrate multiple components, often with blockchain as the integration mechanism. The specific solution discussed in the article is a combination of IIoT data, cognitive visual analytics, and blockchain with an ERP system .

title: Cognitive Telescope Network
problemStatement: No network of interconnected telescopes exist at a world-wide scope for transient follow up of astronomical events. The lack of monitoring of events that are being published from varies Astronomical organizations including NASA, ESA, etc and not having a network that can be activated for aligning for various experiments and followups restricts our ability to take any action on these events unless done manually. Weather monitoring, location, time of day  and other factors play an essential part in the filtering of the telescopes. But without a network none of this is possible.
outcome:
IBM IoT Platform with provide the backbone for such a network across the world where each telescope becomes a IoT device and may be centrally controlled from the IBM Cloud. This will assist in followups that had not been possible so far and lead to new and exciting scientific discoveries. The network will also assist in creating a community of scientists and amateurs alike to communicate and work together for the enhancement of science. The network will communicate with the telescopes using the INDI protocol which has now become the de-facto standard that all observatories are adopting to.
Once the application is build the same capabilities may be applied for other centrally controlled optical devices. The application may also be made available with support for commercial use in the future.

title: A Cloud reference guide for the Telecomunications Industry in Argentina
executiveChampionReason: Fernando is the Industry Sales Manager for Telecom companies in Argentina and in charge of the Strategy and Offerings for the domestic TME industry, and expert in the Telecom network cloud transformation. Fabrizio is the IBM Cloud Country Executive for Argentina and has plenty of experience dealing with the local clients regulations and concerns. industryName: Telecom Media and Entertainment Industry Affiliate
description: Create a Point-of-View on the Telecom industry in Argentina, provide a global and local perspective for clients in Argentina who are interested about cloud, but reticent to adopt the technology and its best practices. Conversations with clients have confirmed that having a reference guide was needed for them to embrace the change that the new technologies bring, and feel accompanied by IBM as an strategic technology partner.
problemStatement:
Telecom operators in Argentina are working to prepare their infrastructures to support  the next generation of 5G networks, in the particular case of Argentina, given that there are no big local Cloud providers with an in-country datacenter, the telecom operators are, also, investing in creating their own datacenters, instead of leveraging Cloud infrastructure.

In some cases, they became MSPs, but still don't became users of the inherent Cloud technology, mostly because of misconceptions or lack of local examples they feel comfortable replicating. 

Currently, IBM is quite well established in the Telecom industry and has plenty of global and local use cases, as well as a great deal of documentation that can provide some guidance or blueprint for these clients to follow, however, those are not in Spanish, nor compiled in a single document we can share with our clients, or aligned with local intrinsicaties and regulations, which is something that our clients require to address and no other Cloud provider is taking the time to do. 

The current state of affairs place Telcom operators in a competitor position instead of strategic partners, the objective of this initiative is to help shift this position and create a new collaboration space.
outcome:
The objectives of this initiative are:
1. Establish a clear picture of the tower market, key players, sponsors and technology trends, local, regional and global.
2. Understand and address clients concerns to help them adopt Cloud services in Argentina.
3. Create new collaboration and co-creation spaces, shifting the competitor/client position to strategic partners and collaborators.
4. Identify business opportunities for IBM and our clients.
5. Create a comprehensive reference guide for clients and the local sales force that will include different approaches and recommendations for cloud adoption, specific for this industry and for Argentina, information regarding regulations and how IBM adheres to them, security certifications and architectural guidance to assist our clients embrace the digital transformation, with IBM as their strategic partner.

title: An analysis of diversity within IBM to close the gap between the experience and band levels
executiveChampionReason: Rashik is leading initiatives on diversity for tech talent in Europe, and we discussed this project with him in advance. He is also our sponsor for data access.
description: Analysis of diversity, salary, and band levels from IBM HR datasets to ensure more transparency on the pay structure.
problemStatement:
More and more companies are embracing data science to address pay gaps and comply with equal pay regulations. Analysis of diversity, salary, and band levels from IBM HR datasets allow more transparency on the pay structure and will help HR experts identify where the widest gaps occur and ensure compliance with the equal pay laws.
Our aim is to request HR datasets and apply data science methods to see if diversity, equal work, and equal pay align as it is important in IBM. We will identify roles and experience level metrics and measure if band levels are homogeneous across diverse groups of employees. In particular, we aim to address the following questions:
1. What is the status of diversity in technical positions across IBM?
2. Is there a gap between the level of experience and bands? If yes, which groups and skills are subject to the widest gaps?
3. If data is available, does comparable work of equal value correlate with comparable band levels?
Data will be requested from the following source: HR Reports: https://hranalytics.w3ibm.mybluemix.net/exploreReports
The users of our results are mainly managers in technical roles and HR experts who enforce the equal pay regulations.
outcome:
- Create more transparency on the pay structure within IBM
- Close the gap between the experience and band levels
- Help HR experts identify where the widest gaps occur and ensure compliance with the equal pay laws

title: Collaborative Workloads
executiveChampionReason: He is the leader of GTS Labs. He is leading IBM Services Platform with Watson. This platform will be the runtime for the service (a final outcome of this initiative)
description: Workloads running on cloud platforms tweet their experience and learn from the experience of other workloads to make critical workload management decisions
problemStatement: Usage of cloud by all types of enterprises has accelerated. However, making important workload lifecycle decisions (for e.g., where to host a new workload?, which cloud to failover to in the event of a disaster?, etc) are still dependent on performance and scalability reports coming from independent agencies that run benchmarks on different cloud platforms for evaluating different clouds on different metrics. We believe that such reports may not be accurate and potentially biased. We also believe that cloud and technologies like docker will considerably reduce the timescales at which such workload lifecycle decisions are taken. To take the decision of where to host an existing or a new workload next will require more recent data about the clouds than what is available today. The question this initiative will answer is exactly this: how to provide a platform for storing and analyzing data about the "experience" of workloads on clouds. The "experience" includes any data that a workload can access from the hosting environment such as the resource utilization, errors, etc. We propose to create a world-wide service that would be operated by IBM GTS such that it will enable workloads hosted on any cloud
outcome: - We believe that it is inevitable that such a service comes around and it would be beneficial that IBM takes the lead than any other company,- The proposed service will be a single stop shop for accessing the metrics and insights about workload "experience" on different clouds; IBM Broker can leverage the service to make more realtime and informed decisions,- Create new revenue stream through creation of tools and services that provide data center and workload operational insights ,- This service will operate at scale and will provide IBM to perfect its ISPW (IBM Service Platform with Watson) platform (that is expected to host this service) to operate at scale,- Business model, Operational Architecture, and a PoC (software) are expected outcomes
finalOutcome: The generated report and a PoC (outcomes) provides IBM GTS SO a strategy and an initial implementation to follow with regard to how to use blockchain for different usecases such as Collaborative Workloads, Hybrid Services Integration, and ITSM.
closeValue: Recommendation to GTS SO to create a Collaborative Workloads usecase as a GTS Offering
publicationDescription: A conclusion is made that a blockchain based approach to sharing data betwen workload owners and IT insights providers based on the trends
ratingComments: This was a systematic study in an emerging area with high potential value for IBM and GTS. The authors have brought forth the expanding role of collaborative workloads and the importance of Blockchain in this context.

finalOutcome: This AoT report captures IBM's PoV on AI Model Lifecycle Management and outlines a detailed methodology including tasks, roles, processes, and tools needed to increase throughput from data science activities. title: A Cloud reference guide for the B&F Industry in Argentina
executiveChampionReason:
Fabrizio is the IBM Cloud Country Executive for Argentina and has plenty of experience dealing with the local Banking Industry regulations. He's already well versed in the local matters and has assisted me to understand who I need to work with and how this change in the legislation presents a great opportunity for IBM to expand its reach in the industry.
Alejandro Pelloni is the Territory Executive for Banking and Financial Services Sector in Argentina, has a deep understanding of the industry, as well as the constraints for cloud adoption in the region, his sponsorship and support provide an excellent guide to keep the document content focused and aligned with IBM objectives and relevant to the clients needs
description: IBM Banking Clients in Argentina are very slow to adopt cloud services, an investigation confirmed that the main reason behind this problem, is that due to miscopceptions and lack of understansiding, the Banks fear local regulations or believe it is very complex to migrate. Conversations with the same clients confirmed that having a reference guide was needed for them to embrace the change and answer to the local regulators in case of audits.
problemStatement:
The traditional Banking Industry in Argentina hesitates when adopting cloud, which impacts directly in a reduction in their market share against booming fintech competitors that are cloud native and force their hand towards digitalization. However, there is a lot of confusion regarding the regulations for cloud services usage for the banking industry in the country, this creates a major constraint for the more traditional banks, leading to a negative loop that is very hard to break, even with Garage or Journey to Cloud programs.

From an IBM Argentina perspective, IBM Cloud falls behind the competitors, one of the main reasons, according to our clients, is because Microsoft or AWS, have created a document or webpage where they explain how their Cloud Services comply to the local regulation and provide some recommendations for the clients in the B&F sector and, particularly, in Argentina. IBM has a lot of information about this topic available, but nothing adapted to the local regulations from Argentina.
outcome:
After a deep dive in the industry and their constraints, it was determined that the best outcome would be to create a document and an adapted Journey to Cloud program that aims to became a guide for the local Banking and Finance clients. The document will include different approaches and recommendations for cloud adoption, information regarding regulations and how IBM adheres to them, security certifications and architectural guidance to assist our clients embrace the digital transformation, with IBM as their strategic partner.

It was stated by the local sales force that this document could became a powerful tool for them to improve IBM Cloud position against our competitors and provide security for our clients to consider Cloud not only for non critical workloads, but also as a solution for productive environments.
finalOutcome: This document will be reference guide for clients from the local banking industry and the local sales force that opens the conversation with our clients in what regards to a much difficult conversation in Argentina, the usage of public cloud for banking operations. This is an area where IBM was lagging against its competitors in the country and with this document IBM is no only providing a comprehensive guideline, but also , recommendations for cloud adoption, specific for this industry and for Argentina, information regarding local regulations and how IBM adheres to them, security certifications and architectural guidance to assist our clients embrace the digital transformation, with IBM as their strategic partner.
closeValue: Debunked several myths regarding local regulation and provide assurance to our clients that IBM is their strategic partner for Cloud adoption
ratingComments: The team put together a great document that will help us improve our position in the banking industry, and most important, the conversations we face when we encounter regulatory barriers. Awesome job!

title: Automated explainable AI for omics data
executiveChampionReason: IBM Fellow Laxmi Parida is an expert on the topic and will be able to advise on the scientific and technical aspects of the proposal, as well as connect the pipeline to potential client use cases and business impact.
description: Developing an explainable, scalable, automated AI pipeline for omics data to support the discovery of novel healthcare & life sciences insights
problemStatement: There have been many AI methods and applications developed for prediction tasks using biomedical omics data. However,  the utility and adoption of such approaches by domain experts depend firstly on the capability to explain the "black box" AI predictions, and secondly on the availability of scalable automated pipelines. Our goal is to combine accurate prediction with extracting and interpreting the important features from AI models, in an automated way, to efficiently produce actionable insights from omic data.
outcome: We will develop an AI pipeline for delivering accurate predictions coupled with actionable explanations, from omics data. Example applications include phenotype prediction from microbiome or gene expression data. We aim to support the discovery of novel healthcare & life sciences domain-specific insights by developing and applying interpretable and explainable AI methods at scale. We will do this by building on the team's existing assets and expertise in AI and omics.

title: 2020 Texas JumpStart SLAM: Data Analytics and AI Tech Challenges
executiveChampionReason: Rhonda is the AoT Executive Sponsor for the Austin TVC.
description: The Tech Challenge project is the pinnacle of the IBM Developer JumpStart program. This program provides professional development, networking, and skills enhancement opportunities for IBM entry-level software and hardware developers.  The 2020 Technical Challenges for the Texas cohort will empower JumpStarters to expand their knowledge beyond their day job and use their skills to support STEM learning across the world. The JumpStarters will form small cross-unit teams and develop activity kits targeted for STEM events and donate them back to ibm.org. These activity kits will help students learn about new technologies and their applications in a fun way. This initiative is for the Tech Challenges that will create Data Analytics and Artificial Intelligence Activity Kits.
problemStatement:
The growth of jobs that require technical skills in areas such as artificial intelligence, security or data science presents an opportunity for young people, as well as a challenge to prepare them with a skill base built upon STEM fluency which is the key to innovation and the future. 

The IBM Developer JumpStart program is a key differentiator for IBM that helps with recruiting in a competitive marketplace and supports efforts to engage and retain top technical talent. The SLAM helps new hires get hands-on tutorials in strategic technologies, practice and develop collaboration skills, and apply Design Thinking methodology through the  "Tech Challenge".  

The 2020 Technical Challenges for the Texas cohort will support STEM learning by creating "Activity Kits" for Data Analytics and Artificial Intelligence.  Activity Kits enable volunteers to leverage their specialized skills and talents to easily deliver engaging experiences to help STEM students learn about new technologies in a fun way.

Artificial Intelligence is an important technology with many business and consumer applications. The Data Analytics and Artificial Intelligence Tech Challenges will help JumpStarters learn more about how AI works and its different applications as they create Data Analytics and Artificial Intelligence Activity kits for STEM students.
outcome:
Participants will be aligned in teams to work on a self-directed "challenge", with guidance from SMEs and IBM Design Thinking coaches. Between SLAMS they will work together to solve their technical challenge using new ideas and fresh viewpoints, share progress with their cohort and then present a working prototype for executives to review and select the "best" (effective solution, design, and impact) at the second SLAM event. 

The Tech Challenge will empower JumpStarters to expand their knowledge beyond their day job and use their skills to support STEM learning across the globe. 

The JumpStarters will form small cross-unit teams and develop Data Analytics and Artificial Intelligence activity kits targeted for STEM events. These activity kits will be donated back to ibm.org and will be used to teach STEM students about the Artificial Intelligence technology and its applications.

We live in a data-driven world. One of the challenges of producing large volumes of data,  it is hard to make sense of the data without some form of visual summary. While it is relatively easy to generate a chart based on generated data, there are two key challenges. 


1) Is the correct chart being used to visualise the underlying data? 
2) Are the best data visualisation practices being used to enhance the visual story?


Furthermore, there may be pockets of data visualisation experts within IBM, but there is no way to leverage their experts into a single solution stream.
outcome:
Our outcomes will be achieved through the following:
1) The "Call for Charts" to solicit submissions from all IBMer's to provide a series of charts and graphs in their preferred chart framework and language, along with the data sets required. 
2) The creation of a team of developers to work on the library requirements.


Our main expected outcomes are:
1)  To develop a library that will analyse a prior data set that requires charting, then provide a series of best practice data visualisation techniques. Such techniques may includes Pre-attenitve attributes as well as the Gestalt Theory of information Visualisation. 
2) To make visible the community of subject matter experts in the area of data visualisation.


Other secondary outcomes may include:
1) The ability to use data visualisation library in our products and data science assets.
2) The ability for all internal IBMers to have access to high-value chart templates 
3) Use the initiative to expand our IP portfolio in the realm of Data Visualisation.

title: Client Inhibitors to AI Adoption
Quantum Computing: Building use cases for Cybersecurity
executiveChampionReason: Dr.Gopal Pingali is the Global Vice President of GTS Labs. He can provide his expert insights to make this initiative as beneficial for IBM as possible.
description: building the uses uses and Business opportunity of using Quantum computing in Cyber security
problemStatement:
Quantum computers will be able to solve problems that are far too complex for classical computers to figure out. This includes solving the algorithms behind encryption keys that protect our data and the Internet’s infrastructure. 

Much of today’s encryption is based on mathematical formulas that would take today’s computers an impractically long time to decode. To simplify this, think of two large numbers, for example, and multiply them together. It’s easy to come up with the product, but much harder to start with the large number and factor it into its two prime numbers. A quantum computer, however, can easily factor those numbers and break the code. Peter Shor developed a quantum algorithm (aptly named Shor’s algorithm) that easily factors large numbers far more quickly than a classical computer.
outcome: Building uses cases and business use case for QC in cyber security

title: What is the future role of E,E&U in the circular economy
executiveChampionReason: SME
description: Define in a PoV what our view is regarding the future role of Energy, Environment and Utilities in the circular economy.
problemStatement:
The world is changing. The energy system is undergoing a large transformation in itself across all their domains.  We also see transformation happen within society, eco-system plays and engagements and cross industry drivers and challenges.  With all our E,E&U clients committing to the UN Sustainability Development Goals. Electrification is one of the drivers for the industrial industry, for buildings, for heating, for mobility, for cities.

New circular economy directions, plans and ambitions are defined by organisations and public institutions and government. (example https://ec.europa.eu/environment/circular-economy/)
The circular economy refers to an approach to business and consumption that focuses on reusing, refurbishing and recycling all of what we have, as opposed to the current mainstream linear business models based on the principles of make, use and dispose. It means managing production efficiently and, crucially, seeing waste as a valuable resource for economic activity.

What is current role of E,E&U within the circular economy and what will be the future role in a changing energy system landscape?  This may be addressed from the full E,E&U perspective or from the different sub industries.  Decentralisation, Democratisation, Regional Energy Markets, Renewable Energy, all these domains have an impact on the circular economy for E,E&U.
outcome:
To define answers and with that also create an IBM PoV this initiative will work on a 3 step / sprint approach:
- Collect information and vision on current state of E,E&U in the circular economy
- Create a perspective of the future role of E,E&U in the circular economy and also what IBM can provide as value. Also understand how the role may change over time and how it positions to other industries circular economy point of view (like https://www.ibm.com/blogs/industries/circular_economy/).
- Write an industry PoV on the future role of E,E&U in the circular economy.

All sprints should at least share first results through an internal blog post.
The PoV should be also become the foundation for an external blog post.  An Infographic or a poster could also be good outcome.

Therefore the initiatives is not looking only for E,E&U SMEs across all areas - electricity, gas, water, waste to contribute but especially also interested in cross industry expertise and vision.  Also IBM iX and design ideas will greatly shaping a tangible and comprehensible result (especially if we think in terms of infographic)

title: Practical Operational Modelling - OM Revisions
executiveChampionReason: Kathy is looking after the future of global solution design (with Jenny Ang)
description: Practical Operational Modelling - OM Revisions
problemStatement: How is Operational Modelling performed effectively?  Even in the Cloud world, the need to model a system in order to ensure that the Non-Functional requirements will be met is still just as important as ever. However there is often a gap between what modelling is actually performed on projects, and what the method says should be done. Further, the premise is that Operational Modelling for cloud could be optimised.,The word 'Practical' in the title is deliberate.  This is not intended as a theoretical study, but is intended to look at the practicalities of working within a real project, with the pressures which come from delivery, time-scales and cost.,The study is split into three ‘streams’,1.	OM for Systems on Cloud – how to adapt Operational Modelling to better handle systems which are being built to be hosted in Cloud,2.	OM for Cloud Services – how to adapt Operational Modelling for the build of Cloud Services (IaaS/PaaS/SaaS),3.	OM Revisions – how should the techniques and notation be revised for the new world,This stream is OM Revisions
outcome: Operational Modelling needs to change to reflect the architectures and architectural frameworks which are in use today.  The study will work on the Theoretical Model of OM and how it should be refined, and with then update the documentation and education in line with these.  The study will also look at how adjacent techniques (Enterprise Architecture, Component Modelling, Performance Modelling) are affected.
