title: ** COVID-19 ** | Predict & Prevent Potential Hoarding of essential products
executiveChampionReason: Auto Selected from Admin Page
description: During any kind of outbreak some consumer products may become essential overnight to prevent or control the outbreak based on latest guideline or research work published by different health organizations worldwide and based on which supermarkets or different selling outlets need to act immediately to determine the selling strategy and prevent possible hoarding.
problemStatement: During pandemic, beside health related concerns, another key apprehension that worsen the situation is unavailability of essential consumer products due to lack of manufacturing and potential hoarding. Study shows that hoarding is one of the biggest reason behind the shortage which goes unnoticed by authorities until demand of products arise at the very last moment ultimately triggering un-necessary rush or panic buy among the buyers. In the recent global pandemic people around the globe faced numerous challenges due to lack of essential consumer products like sanitizer, toilet papers, mask, hand-wash, baby products etc. in different consumer outlets or supermarket and ended up fighting with each other due to the shortage. So it’s very much essential and key important for different consumer outlets or supermarkets to determine the right selling strategy for essential product well ahead to avoid panic buy or potential hoarding.
outcome:
The proposed AI driven cognitive method and a system can predict and categorize a certain product as essential one based on the analysis of several factors including – 
1. Whether the product can help to prevent from an active pandemic or outbreak based on published guideline
2. Social media data where people are talking about the certain product which can help to prevent pandemic
3. News media feed where product is getting mentioned as potential prevention from pandemic
4. Sales record of previous years
5. Customer feedback about the product
6. Govt published guideline/restrictions
7. Customer inquiries about the product
8. Demands or selling records of the product in other countries 

Based on all the above and several other factors the cognitive method and system can categorize a particular product as a essential product and help the seller to take proactive measures to prevent hoarding.

description: Create a working framework for the day 2 message of IBM Cognitive Enterprise, grouping key messages, methods, reference architectures, ways of working, etc
problemStatement:
The Cognitive Enterprise message has been widely discussed around IBM and it has been adopted by all brands as the best entry point for the IBM transformational approach. 
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                However, the “Day 2” of this Cognitive Enterprise is not that clear: how to start if you bring the Cognitive Enterprise message to a client  and they say "ok, please do it"?. What architectures should we use, what methods are available, how to link all the layers of a Cognitive Enterprise (processes, platforms, exponential technologies use, data, applications, cloud)?. How to govern such a project?.  Why should the client do this with IBM?. Are there Cognitive Enterprise industry flavors available?
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                A cross brand group has investigated the state of the art of the different Cognitive Enterprise pieces. We have concluded that it will be good for our technical and sales professionals if we provide content and guidelines for a cognitive enterprise proposal. 
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                The outcome of this study is targeted for consultants, sellers and technical sellers who are trying to propose a Cognitive Enterprise project. It will relate existing assets (methods, architecture frameworks...) to the Cognitive Enterprise, but we will not develop new methods or frameworks within this study.
outcome:
We will be organized in 6 working groups, each one representing one of the Cognitive Enterprise Layers,  to produce these outcomes (documentation):       
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                     Wg1: Architecting a cognitive enterprise transformation: Culture, skills, ways of working. With special focus on Agile Enterprise Architecture
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                 Wg2: industry and technology platforms
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                        Wg3: Data /AI

Wg4: Applications transformation to cloud

title: Dataset construction for Vulnerability Analysis
executiveChampionReason: He is a sponsor of this activity, and understands the need and value of building this dataset
description: We are buiding the first reliable software vulnerability dataset to help advance the application of AI to assist developers build more secure software.
problemStatement:
Identifying software vulnerabilities is an inevitable aspect of software development, it eliminates potential application crashes and security breaches. A recent tweet about an old story https://twitter.com/Rainmaker1973/status/1288059169422159872?s=20 reminded us how an integer overflow brought down a rocket.  Tedious expert effort has been spent to build static analyzers; yet insecure patterns are barely fully enumerated and often create a large number of False Positives that developers tend to dismiss. This presents an opportunity for Machine Learning (ML) to help classify vulnerabilities and give better signals to developers. However, at the core of ML is the need for good quality data, and despite some datasets being available their labeling techniques are questionable or the data is of poor quality. 
At IBM Research we are pursuing the creation of a reliable dataset, using semi-automated techniques, and manually validating a large number of samples to improve its quality. We are leveraging large open source projects, some used in our cloud platform and by our clients, in C language first, and are looking to leverage the IBM technical community at large to join forces to help us in the manual verification process and ultimate goal of a high quality dataset.
outcome: Large number of vulnerability candidates manually inspected by C-language experts  (other languages may follow) to ultimately help create the first high quality dataset of software vulnerabilities for the industry to foster AI/ML research for the community at large.

title: How enhance the Cyber Security and Resilience in the Italian Financial Sector
executiveChampionReason: Because he is the Italy Security Leader and he is very interesting to develop this document with these topics
description: This document describes IBM point of view about managing IT Risk in the Italian financial institutions according to latest threat evolutions and regulatory position papers.  It is undeniable, Cyber threats to the financial sector are continuously evolving and becoming ever more sophisticated. The attackers – whether they be 16-year old script kiddies, hacktivist groups or even nation states – are dynamic and agile. They have different reasons for targeting the financial sector, but they have the potential to cause disruption. Besides stealing money and data, they can undermine confidence in the entire financial system.
problemStatement:
Several trends in the italian financial sector related to cyber risk have been observed in the latest years.
First, the close interconnection and complexity of the financial systems creates vulnerabilities which can be exploited by cyber attackers.
Second, attackers seem to be gaining an ever deeper understanding of how the financial system operates and this is enabling them to swiftly detect and exploit weaknesses more efficiently and should be a concern for us all.
Third, both banks and Financial Market Infrastructures (FMIs) are struggling to find staff with the skills and experience needed to fend off cyber-attacks. Indeed, the skills gap extends well beyond the financial sector.
For these reasons, all relevant stakeholders need to urgently work on strategies to make sure that our workforce has the right skills for our future economies, and that our society is able to reap the benefits of innovation.
outcome:
The outcome of this initiative is a White paper describing the IBM Italy Point of View when managing IT risk in the Financial Sector operating under Italian law and Regulation.
In particular, considering the landscape scenario evolution, ten domains of interest will be identified.
For each of them a brief description will be provided together with a strategy proposal comprised of IBM Capabilities and solutions. 
The ten domains considered are:
1.	IT Governance
2.	IT Organization and outsourcing
3.	IT Risk management
4.	IT Security Management
5.	IT Operations
6.	Software acquisition, software development and project management
7.	Data quality management
8.	IT Continuity Management
9.	IT reporting
10.	IT audit
They will be addressed in the rest of the paper providing an overview and a set of applied best practices.

executiveChampionReason: As a Global CTO of CAS, Shawn is leading the OpenShift Everywhere Programme and lot of the POCs that we are developing and the subsequent business opportunities will benefit from this initiative.
description: In the journey to cloud offerings, lot of our clients are looking forward to modernizing their applications to containers. Containerization is one of the favorite path that clients are choosing as their first step. Thought it looks trivial, containerization has lot of challenges. This initiative will bring the details on the approach of containerization.
problemStatement:
Containerizing applications poses lot of challenges if we do not know the applications well enough before venturing into containerization. Even after choosing the application for containerization, challenges that are faced during the containerization poses risk to the entire program. 
With this initiative, we are going to build a prescriptive approach for identify applications, identify the remediation required for application to work on containers, choosing the right strategy to containerize, effort required, deployment and testing strategies to consider and finally the operations of the applications.
outcome:
Outcome of this initiative will help the solutioning teams, architects and developers to have a right view on the challenges that needs to be considered in containerizing the applications. It will help reduce the failure of containerization and provide detailed step by step guidance on choosing the containerization strategy and also low level guidance on how to handle the changes.
This initiative will produce the following:
1. Containerization Assessment Questionnaire
2. Identifying the strategy for containerization
3. Step by Step guide to containerize the applications: High level assessment, code level assessment, identifying integration complexities, choosing the right container image, instructions to remediate the code, creating and customizing docker files, build and deployment steps.

title: Service Management in a Cloud and Cognitive World
executiveChampionReason:
I anticipate that this initiative and the resulting PoV will have cross-brand applicability, both to GTS, GBS and to Cloud.  
                                        
I have started with GTS because I believe it will highlight changes that need to be made in the way we deliver management services in order to remain relevant in a cloud native world.  However I expect it will also highlight management disciplines that remain vitally important to enterprise clients in this new world and we need to be better able to articulate the value that IBM brings.  
                                        
Additionally, this will be of direct interest to the the Cloud Architecture and Solution Engineering (CASE) team within Hybrid Cloud.  They are leading the work on Cloud Service Management and Operations, Site Reliability Engineering (SRE) and have published the initial reference architectures and patterns in this space.
description: Develop an externally oriented point of view paper on the evolution of service management in a cloud (native) and cognitive world
problemStatement:
In a cloud environment which values speed and agility above all else, there is a growing sentiment that established service management practices such as the IT Infrastructure Library (ITIL) are no longer relevant  in a cloud world.  ITIL and the disciplines it espouses are increasingly seen as outdated, too slow, too cumbersome and too expensive for a rapidly changing cloud environment. 
                                        
ITIL and its enterprise management approaches are the foundation for IBM managed services delivery - especially from GTS.  So doubts about the relevance of ITIL also cast doubt on whether our  managed services model remains relevant, whether we need to change and how.   
                                        
So the core question we will explore is .. "Is ITIL still relevant in a cloud and cognitive computing world?" and, if so  ... 
                                        
- What's different?
- Why? 
- What aspects remain valuable?
- What aspects need to change?
- How do enterprises make the transition?  
                                        
The proposed Point of View would explore these questions for the most common / important ITIL processes.  For each, it would examine the implications of new cloud technologies that change the types of environments and services we have to manage, and new tools and techniques available for managing them.
outcome:
The primary output from this initiative will be a external, client facing point of view paper that explores the evolution of service management in a cloud environment and takes a position on whether or how aspects of traditional ITIL-based service management remain valuable.
                                        
Externally, the PoV paper will assist in establishing the continuing relevance of the management services and practices we employ for many of our existing enterprise clients, while also demonstrating that we are proactively exploring and evolving those practices in response to change demands.  It will assist in maintaining our position as a thought leader in service management and in the adoption and management of hybrid clouds.   
                                        
Internally, the PoV will provide a vehicle to help sensitize existing teams to the changes that are occurring in service management and highlight how we need to adapt to meet those changed requirements.

title: Space Tech: Understanding of the Space Orbits & Habitats in LEO, MEO & GEO (Space Junk/Space Debris/Man Made Objects)
executiveChampionReason: Mac is my sponsor for Space Tech Initiatives
description: We are collaborating with UT Austin on Orbital Determination, Space Debris Collision Prediction. This is a major challenge as the Space Tech industry is growing and more and more space crafts are being planned to be launched.
problemStatement:
Space junk has the daily potential to alter satellites' operations and movement. This translates into real-world costs, as satellite operators field alerts about potential collisions. Satellites in low Earth orbit, such as those used for imaging and weather data collection, are especially vulnerable. "That could mean our climate models are less accurate, or we don't have a good way to track emitters. That could have negative impacts down the road," Weeden says. Space junk is also problematic for astronauts. The International Space Station is equipped with a tracker to monitor for collision risk. In the past, crews have performed avoidance maneuvers and hid in the Soyuz capsules when the risk for collision was too great. (source: https://www.npr.org/2020/01/10/795246131/space-junk-how-cluttered-is-the-final-frontier)
Build AI models for collision avoidance, determining various clusters in the orbital habitat etc.)
outcome: Build AI Models, publish research papers, blogs and patents

description: Create an IBM Point of View on Responsible Impact
problemStatement: The rise of the internet, mobile technologies and cheap sensors with disruptive technologies such as AI, IoT, 3D Printing, Quantum Computing, 5G and Blockchain has driven a proliferation into and have a pervasive impact upon almost every aspect of human life. It is starting to become at the forefront of initiatives that address social, economic and environmental challenges, from helping to save lives (SMS for Life), creating ‘new collar’ jobs, developing new skills, driving economic development and accelerating responses to disasters and emergencies (such as COVID-19). But these same technological advances could have unintended consequences, accelerating risks to the planet and society, if they’re not applied in a smart and sustainable way. We need a framework for the responsible use of technologies to enable positive impact – which technologies fit which scenarios, what governance is required, how should the outcomes be monitored and how do you measure the impact?
outcome: Prime objective and planned outcome is an IBM PoV and a framework for assessing and governing Responsible Impact.  With alignment to regional initiatives and coalitions with consideration given to regulation and industry standards. What does it mean to take a “tech for good” approach? What are good examples? What are bad examples? What are the key enablers? What are the inhibitors? How do you decide when to use technology? How do you govern? How do measure? What scenarios are there?

title: Building Offering Portfolio For IBM GBS Sales Team In Sustainability Domain
executiveChampionReason: Sonia is currently Global Director of Royal Dutch Shell Account and an expert of Sustainability issues of CP & IP issues. Anup is an IBM Distinguished Engineer and having experience in Technology solutions in Sustainability space.
description: Building Offering Portfolio For IBM GBS Sales Team In Sustainability Domain
problemStatement: Sustainability globally had become an important issue for companies across the globe especially post COVID 19. However, unlike Marketing or Finance, most companies do not consider sustainability / risk management as a regular business function and do not have one buyer like Chief Sustainability officer. Buyer for sustainability solutions and services vary a lot across organizations both in terms of role and seniority – starting from safety officer at factory to CSR Head in company board. IBM over the years had built many point solutions in this space mostly against customer request. This AOT study wants to enable GBS sales team with a list of potential offerings that can be positioned based on (a) client persona to whom in the client organization they are selling (b) type of opportunity for example sustainability package solution implementation or meeting carbon footprint objective – two may need very different solution portfolio (c) opportunity of creating new business by educating client on sustainability topics relevant for his industry, emerging compliance standards for his industry or capabilities available in Enterprise solutions that he had implemented / planning to implement.
outcome:
This AOT study will provide a detailed approach covering the following
(a)	A sustainability assessment framework that will help GBS sellers to assess the sustainability need of the client based on his industry, process scope, current application architecture and client specific sustainability objectives.
(b)	A methodology / approach that will help seller to recommend a portfolio of solutions / offerings based on the sustainability need identified in earlier step. The framework will also help seller to prioritize the solution / offerings based on client priorities as identified earlier. This will help seller to create a sustainability roadmap for the client.
(c)	Sustainability component business model for selected industries. This will help seller to create a quick sustainability heatmap for the client from selected industry.
(d)	Developing a set of simple excel based tools that help seller to compare company’s performance against few key sustainability benchmarks (Assumption: Benchmark data will come from IBM Benchmarking Wizard) from IBM Benchmarking wizard) to identify high level improvement opportunities in sustainability performance for particular client (Client data need for this will be listed in this study).

executiveChampionReason: Rhonda is the AoT Executive Sponsor for the Austin TVC.
description: The Tech Challenge project is the pinnacle of the IBM Developer JumpStart program. This program provides professional development, networking, and skills enhancement opportunities for IBM entry-level software and hardware developers.  The 2020 Technical Challenges for the Texas cohort will empower JumpStarters to expand their knowledge beyond their day job and use their skills to support STEM learning across the world. The JumpStarters will form small cross-unit teams and develop "Activity Kits" targeted for STEM events and donate them back to ibm.org. These activity kits will help students learn about new technologies and their applications in a fun way. This initiative is for the Tech Challenges to create Blockchain Activity Kits.
problemStatement:
The growth of jobs that require technical skills in areas such as artificial intelligence, security or data science presents an opportunity for young people, as well as a challenge to prepare them with a skill base built upon STEM fluency which is the key to innovation and the future. 

The IBM Developer JumpStart program is a key differentiator for IBM that helps with recruiting in a competitive marketplace and supports efforts to engage and retain top technical talent. The SLAM helps new hires get hands-on tutorials in strategic technologies, practice and develop collaboration skills, and apply Design Thinking methodology through the  "Tech Challenge".  

The 2020 Technical Challenges for the Texas cohort will support STEM learning by creating "Activity Kits" for Blockchain.  Activity Kits enable volunteers to leverage their specialized skills and talents to easily deliver engaging experiences to help STEM students learn about new technologies in a fun way.

Blockchain is an important technology with many business and consumer applications. The Blockchain Tech Challenges will help JumpStarters learn more about how this technology work and its different applications as they create Blockchain Activity kits for STEM students.
outcome:
Participants will be aligned in teams to work on a self-directed "challenge", with guidance from SMEs and IBM Design Thinking coaches. Between SLAMS they will work together to solve their technical challenge using new ideas and fresh viewpoints, share progress with their cohort and then present a working prototype for executives to review and select the "best" (effective solution, design, and impact) at the second SLAM event. 

The Tech Challenge will empower JumpStarters to expand their knowledge beyond their day job and use their skills to support STEM learning across the globe. 

The JumpStarters will form small cross-unit teams and develop Blockchain activity kits targeted for STEM events. These activity kits will be donated back to ibm.org and will be used to teach STEM students about the Blockchain technology and its applications.

title: [TLC-BR] Technical Agenda – TechDay Brasil Live  2020 – 1st Edition
executiveChampionReason: Decio Miname is the CTO for LA, covering all IBM Bus and with an outstanding mindset to promote the One IBM approach. He supports the TLC-BR and wants to promote the integration and knowledge sharing among the Technical Community.
description: Online event in 2 days, inspired on the TechDay Horto 2019, to bring several subjects related to innovation, career and development, specially to the Technical Community on IBM Brasil..
problemStatement: As a result of a Design Thinking session done in 2018 with the technical community, it was identified an integration gap of the technical community in Hortolândia. After TechDay Horto 2019 edition, it was the leadership's desire to expand the program to other locations: São Paulo city and Rio de Janeiro. Add to it, in 2020, given the world health crises by COVID-19, another challenge is presented: keep the event, but guarantee the Social Distancing.
outcome: Engage more technical professionals, by challenging them to develop (new skills and opportunities), explore (IBM and the Technical Communities), and promote (themselves, the Technical Community - TLC-BR and AoT, and IBM).
finalOutcome:
The TechDay event has been a successful event since its first edition in 2018. While all the previous editions happened onsite, in Hortolândia, due to the COVID-19 crisis, the TLC-BR decided to accept the challenge and move this event to the online format. This brought a new set of values and great outcomes:
- Participation of IBMers from other sites (48% Hortolândia, 32% São Paulo, 14% Rio de Janeiro, and colleagues from other regions in Brasil: South, North/Northeast, Center, and even some IBMers from other countries: US and Portugal.
- Increase of women participation as both: speaker and participants. While the last edition (TechDay Horto 2019) had about 28-29% women participation, this edition, this number increased to 37-38%.
Besides these numbers, there were some non-measurable outcomes for this event: accessible (Libras - Brazilian Sign Language) translation in some sessions, use of Events & Classes to register presence and collect NPS for each session, and the playback (video and presentation) available for each session for those IBMers who could not participate on the day.
All things considered, this was the most successful TechDay realized, impacting more than 700 IBMers with themes in Cloud, Innovation, Career, AI, Security and DevOps.
participants: Jorge Damiao D Barbosa Das Chagas
Ludmila Canuto de Melo Ferreira Salimena
closeValue: The ability to change and to adapt is ingrained in the TLC-BR volunteers, so that in 3 months, it was possible to move to an online format an event that impacted more than 700 IBMers (in Brasil and other countries) with technical knowledge and new perspectives.
publicationDescription: This TechNote's purpose was to share with other IBMers how TLC-BR team worked to move a face-to-face event (realized for the technical community in a single site) to online format, expanding the participation to all IBMers in Brasil (and other countries, considering Portuguese language). How the use of Collaboration tools and team work made it possible to concilate daily job activities, to the preparation of an online event from scratch, which resulted in more than 1500 participations in several sessions, and an average NPS +81.

executiveChampionReason: Varun runs IBM Cloud Advisory services globally Practitioneers in this practice typically face C-level executives at the clients on the topic of multicloud lock-in and portability. description: Many Enterprises have a multi-cloud provider strategy to power applications and data for digital services. With this model, they become less dependent on one cloud provider for all needs and can pick a best-of-breed service and can reduce vendor dependency and lock-in. Portable application architectures and operation tools on the cloud are essential to avoid lock-in, be able to negotiate the best price and have the flexibility to move between private and public clouds when required. This PoV will address the portability from different layers of the architecture and list the key use-cases.
problemStatement:
Many Enterprises have a multi-cloud provider strategy to power applications and data for digital services. With this model, they become less dependent on one cloud provider for all needs and can pick a best-of-breed service and can reduce vendor dependency and lock-in.
                                        
                                        Simply using multiple cloud providers does not immediately give benefits. Portable application architectures and operation tools on the cloud are essential to avoid lock-in, be able to negotiate the best price and have the flexibility to move between private and public clouds when required. Examples of questions the PoV should address:
                                        
                                        - what cloud data services should I use to make data portable
                                        - what PaaS services give portability, and which ones does not
                                        - how should I provision environments across multiple providers in a cloud-agnostic way
                                        - what DevOps tools are cloud-agnostic and portable, what should be considered
                                        - are containers in itself enough to make my application portable
outcome: The proposed PoV will arm our technical leaders and sellers with a constructive and objective perspective on what it takes to avoid lock-in and what to consider in the design, run, and operation of application and services on multiple clouds. title: Architecture and Design: Integrating for synergy and value
executiveChampionReason: We selected Charlie Hill because he is the IBM Fellow with leadership responsibility for IBM Design.  In this role, he is most likely to be able to effect changes within Design.  We invited Ray Harishankar as the Secondary Executive Sponsor because of his leadership in architectural thinking and methods.  We also have Jenny Ang as a participant and she has direct impact over Team Solution Design and Cognitive Architect.  We will also be consulting with Shankar Kalyana in his leadership role for Mosaic.
associatedBusinessUnitOther: reaches across all business units with designers and architects
description: Define the integration points between architecture and design, are there common assets that can become bridges?
problemStatement:
A successful project is driven by individuals who apply complementary skills and approaches to complex human and technical problems. Designers bring an empathic approach to framing problems through the lens of human outcomes. Architects bring an analytical approach to the technical design and integration of components. Agile adds a further dimension through emphasis on continuous iteration and learning. How might we define hills in a greenfield environment , architect the integration of new hills into existing complex brownfield engagements, and improve solution development?  
                                                                                                                                                                
 Proposed Sprints
1.	Define the current state with respect to the philosophy/approach to each and perceived challenges.
2.	Define the desired target integrated state and a proposed path to close the gap based upon Sprint 1.
3.	Align the Design techniques and artifacts with the Architecture Work Products as defined by the architecture method, creating an initial mapping by which design and architecture may inform one another in a closed loop approach.  Incorporate Mosaic, agile, enterprise architecture.
4.	Recommend modifications to both the Design framework and Architecture method to drive intentional synergy into all projects.
5.	Recommend education for designers and architects so that we can drive successful adoption of these new techniques.
outcome:
The alignment of philosophy and approach between design and architecture will provide value both inside IBM and will our clients.   For external clients, the alignment of design techniques and artifacts to architecture work products will enhance the clarity of vision we provide clients in large implementations through the demonstration of how design informs architecture, and architecture provides technical constraints within which design must flourish.  We expect to be able to take recommendations for our external client population and use them to inform our internal design and architecture.  This will allow our product and services designers and architects to better define the scope and approach of proposed offering enhancements to permit scalability of agile delivery. 
                                                                                                                                                                
Through this alignment and synergy we expect to drive increased effectiveness in win rates for proposals as well as greater efficiency in delivery:
 •	Increased ability to solve clients’ business problems, resulting in improved client business outcomes and user satisfaction and loyalty
 •	Improved execution / reduced risk / reduced waste for clients and IBM
 •	Increased follow on business

Standardized coexistence solution offering to our customers.

title: Client Inhibitors to AI Adoption
executiveChampionReason: Rashik is the leader of IBM’s European technical community and an IBM Fellow and previously President of the AOT. description: A study on the inhibitors to adopting AI for clients in the UK
problemStatement: Recent studies on the application of AI from well respected institutions show there is a great opportunity for a wide range of sectors but to realise the benefits there are barriers to AI adoption that need to be understood. We can infer from this that existing and potential IBM clients will experience some or all of these issues and possibly have other issues that have not been identified.
outcome: A short study producing a report (e.g. 6 months) bringing together existing external information with any internal information to deliver a list of inhibitors that prevent our clients from adopting AI solutions. Potential for further work in an extension to this initiative or a follow-on to make recommendations to the business that address the inhibitors.

title: Improving IBM's Technical Eminence in Japan Academia - Phase 4
executiveChampionReason: Norishige Morimoto is CTO and VP, IBM Research & Development of IBM Japan. He has a strong relationship with Japan academic societies, universities, and industries. He also has a lot of influence to IBM researchers and engineers.
description: Continuing our previous effort to improve IBM's technical presence in Japan academia.
problemStatement: IBM needs to improve its presence in academia to get IBM recognized and to hire high quality talents in IBM strategic area such as AI, Hybrid Cloud, Quantum, and so on.
outcome:
Increase IBM's technical eminence in Japan academic by 
(1) holding internal seminars to encourage IBM engineers and researchers to publish more papers,
(2) making presentations and lectures in domestic conferences and Japanese universities, 
(3) contributing to conference committees and academic society boards, and 
(4) having academic society members recognized with an advanced membership grade (e.g. senior/distinguished members).


How to track the outcomes:
(1) Speak at Lab-wide social gathering events and other occasions to promote external publications, and identify potential mentees who are interested in publishing papers and need help. 
(2) Identify important academic conferences and match-make with potential speakers from the mentees, and identify academic contribution opportunities through collaborative programs between IBM and Japanese universities and match-make with our resources. 
(3) Keep track of important positions (terms/vacancy for steering committee positions, etc) in strategic academic societies and match-make with potential resources.
(4) Keep track of the membership duration of strategic academic societies for each mentee and other identified technical resources to encourage them to apply for an advanced grade when it conditions are met.

title: Industry 4.0 Maturity Assessment Framework
executiveChampionReason: Andrea is the leader for IBM Watson IoT Center Munich. IoT plays a central role in i4.0 strategy and transformation.
description: An AoT Study and Recommendation of Industry 4.0 Maturity Assessment Framework
problemStatement: Industry 4.0 is in the Core of digitization strategy of business leaders in our clients. A reliable and repeatable Industry 4.0 maturity assessment is essential for any organization to evaluate their current state of preparedness in I4.0 transformation, as well as to measure the progress along the journey. There have been assessment or surveys that were based on various frameworks and performed either in internal manufacturing or external clients. However, there is lack of a systemic approach on a unified Industry 4.0 Maturity Assessment Framework for clients across different industries.
outcome: AoT is the perfect platform to assemble experts in different BUs, as well as from Industry Academy, to launch an effort to generate a reliable and repeatable Industry 4.0 maturity assessment for IBM teams to support i4.0 engagement with clients across different industries. The key goal is to establish one IBM approach based on a prominent framework and socialize it for use within IBM. Such approach can help IBM and their clients to better understand where they want to be on I4.0 journey.  This helps in two ways: 1) It set expectations on both sides based on ambitions, culture and their business areas.  2) It enable IBM to propose realistic solutions, thus maximizing the business outcome and increasing client satisfaction in their engagement with IBM. A unified approach will also help IBM team to have better benchmarking insights into the I4.0 status across different industries

title: Advancing Methods to Detect and Predict the Propagation of Wildfires
executiveChampionReason: Since there is significant economic and societal impact of wildfires, much of the financial risk is borne by insurance companies, banks, etc.  Opportunities for new capabilities related to wildfires would be strongest in the industries with which Ed and his team works.
description: Assess the state-of-the-art in wildfire detection and prediction, determine the challenges associated with gaps in these capabilities, identify what can IBM contribute, and provide recommendations for further research and development as well as customer applications.
problemStatement: Not a day goes by in recent summers where we don't see stories in the media about the homes and business destroyed by wildfires, their effect on people's lives and the brave men and women that fight them.  There is evidence that the problem is getting worse in many places due to a changing climate.  Since there is two-way interaction between fire propagation and weather, the ability to observe and predict wildfires is very complex.  Hence, there are significant gaps in assessing the effects of past events, monitoring and tracking of on-going events, prediction of events, and determining risk for future events.  Despite the significant amount of R&D on these problems for a long time, large gaps remain in the fidelity of information available to the government, businesses and the public to mitigate the impact of such events.  IBM Research has only dabbled in this area ranging from fire fighter scheduling to estimating risk to modelling smoke propagation.  However, wildfire monitoring and prediction fits within the new, broader environmental science strategy.  From a weather perspective, our commercial data services related to temperature, humidity and winds are relevant to determine the conditions for fire starting and propagation, but are insufficient.
outcome: This initiative will assess the state-of-the-art in wildfire detection and prediction to determine the challenges associated with gaps in these capabilities.  From there, there will be an identification of what can IBM contribute to addressing these gaps.  This identification will include a determination of needs from key IBM customer sets, including insurance, finance, government and other industries.  From there the initiative will provide specific recommendations for work in Research connected to the broader environmental science strategy, and development efforts within The Weather Company group.  Potential collaborations with clients that could leverage new assets from the recommended R&D will also be identified.

title: Cognitive Anomaly Detection of power subsystem for next generation System z servers
executiveChampionReason: Jason is the director of the hardware organization that is responsible for the z processor and system chip set. He is also responsible to provide leadership and technical teams to engage in future system z testfloor (lab) bring-up of new machines(z servers).  These teams drive all the required testing in terms of function, ship frequency, yield tuning, power consumption and margins; to ensure a successful GA at expected time with the highest quality.
description: Cognitive solutions will be investigated and developed for detecting anomalies within the power subsystems of the next generation System z servers.  Such solutions would increase the quality, shorten the time to market all at the same time, and can proactively look for situations that may cause outages in the field.
problemStatement: IBM System z will be targeting to ship newly designed power thermal subsystems for our next generation mainframe. Cognitive solutions will be investigated and developed for detecting anomalies within the power subsystems of these next generation System z servers.  Such solutions would increase the quality, shorten the time to market all at the same time, and can proactively look for situations that may cause outages in the field. However, implementing these solutions requires education and resources that not every department has, so crowd sourcing is key to helping to take the vision forward. The principle idea of this initiative is to approach every next generation prototype z machine as an IoT sensor. We want to record every power event, voltage, current, power, fan speeds and thermal data to look for anomalies.
outcome:
A cognitive solution that will monitor the power/thermal aspect of a z system to detect anomalies during lab bring-up and then can be applied to the field, such that anomalies can be detected ahead of any potential failure in customer's installations.  This is very important for the next generation z systems as new power subsystems are being incorporated. 
                                                                                                                         This monitoring system will collect all data associated with a “fail” or “anomaly” and then write a problem ticket to be analyzed by an engineer. The sensor data will be analyzed by using algorithms, such as nearest neighbor algorithms, to find components that could be performing at, near, or outside of specification limits and thus would need further investigation. To start, we will need to define all the “sensors” that will contribute to this “data lake”.  Then, use STELA* to collect this data at regular intervals. Once enough data is collected, we will apply data analytics (for example, by using the nearest neighbor technique) on the data to identify outliers and submit problem tickets containing all pertinent information. After we learn the patterns of component behavior, we can feedback our learning to our development and field support to monitor customer machines.

title: Chaos-Defined Reliability. How Chaos Engineering help run reliable and available mission-critical workloads.
executiveChampionReason: Bala is the CTO for IBM Cloud / RedHat and steers the company to become more cloud-oriented. Bala considers Chaos Engineering an important topic and bringing in to DevOps automation will be critical.
description: This Academy of Technology study will focus on the value of Chaos Engineering as a method, principle and a collection of tools to reveal application and platform weaknesses, architectural flaws and deployment gaps when deploying workloads on IBM Cloud (IKS, Cloud Paks, ROKS, OCP, VMware@IBM, CF etc…)
problemStatement:
Chaos Engineering is an evolution to business continuity and service resiliency planning. It is the discipline of experimenting on a service to build confidence in its ability to withstand failure in production. Chaos Engineering aims to introduce failures within a system to identify and fix failures proactively before they impact business operations. 

By adopting Chaos Engineering, we aim to evolve current resiliency and reliability practices from service recovery and service restoration such as DR failovers to transparently bypassing failures altogether. We call this disaster transparency. It is a crucial value needed for running reliable mission critical workloads while adopting Cloud-native architectures and SRE operational practices.

While IBM has defined the 4 dimensions of J2C, there are gaps to ensure a smooth transition across these 4 stages. Chaos Engineering as a method and collection of principles could help validating the reliability of a solution, and in turn provide feedback for improvement in pursuit of service reliability and resiliency. We aim to build a structure, framework and guidance around adopting and practicing Chaos Engineering during a mission-critical workload transformation and modernization on IBM Cloud Platform and IBM Cloud Paks on OpenShift.
outcome:
Chaos Engineering is built on many modern architectures, principles and methods such as Cloud-native architectures, Event-driven architectures, Site Reliability Engineering, DevOps and Always On architectures. 

The methodology and collateral will help IBM adopt broader Cloud-native principles and further strengthen services running on the IBM Cloud Platform and reliably deploy and run IBM Cloud Paks on OpenShift. We aim to create structured guidance materials to help IBM Sellers (Solutioners, architects, tech-sellers, consultants and specialists on the field) and IBM Product Engineering (Developers and SREs responsible for cloud.ibm.com and other IBM SaaS) to think differently about business continuity and have comprehensive guidance on adopting Chaos Engineering during client engagements and when maintaining IBM online services.

title: Self-Aware Systems: Towards Resilient and Ethical AI
executiveChampionReason: Jeff Burns is the Research Director in charge of next generation AI hardware. His team is linked to the new AI Center (Albany). He has been a strong supporter of our prior initiative on Adaptive Swarm Intelligence and associated (new) DARPA project. His current team is pursuing the development of the Sentient (AI accelerator) processor, and being in Research, that team is constantly looking at leading edge AI: from algorithms down to actual hardware support for new generation AI. We hope that with Jeff's help, as well as support from Jim Sexton (IBM Fellow and Director of Data Centric Systems) this initiative will produce a summary report that will formulate the long-term aspects of building "super-AI" systems of the future.
description: In the recent past, we have completed an Academy Initiative on Adaptive Swarm Intelligence (ASI). Building upon that study (which is now an established research project, with funding from DARPA), we have started up concept-level formalization of next-generation "self-aware" systems. These are envisioned to be AI systems in which individual compute nodes (within a distributed, mobile swarm IoT architecture) have built-in features of simulated consciousness. The specific attributes of relevance at the node level are: (a) the mobile agent's awareness of its position (spatial coordinates); (b) self-monitoring and self-healing capabilities; (c) awareness of other agents within a consciousness range; (d) ability to form and evolve hypotheses about friendly and unfriendly agents within a swarm team; (e) defensive and altruistic behavioral actions inspired by animal (and in particular, human) swarms.
problemStatement: Current generation AI algorithms and software, supported by appropriate system hardware architectures have been able to advance the state of the art in amazing leaps during the past several years. Nonetheless, fundamental deficiencies exist and present themselves as significant obstacles to widespread deployment of AI systems in the field serving as reliable human assistants. In hazardous operating environments where human resource deployment is unethical or overly stressful and error-prone, autonomous AI systems (e.g. robots, including self-driven vehicles) are preferable. However, without a built-in sense of self-awareness, such AI systems cannot always be trusted as unsupervised agents without human oversight and supervision. Current AI systems are (generally speaking) not aware of changes in the input data pattern, and are therefore unable to prevent catastrophic loss in edge inferential accuracy - neither are they aware of any need to self-correct. Similarly, malicious attempts in input data poisoning are not easy to detect and defend against. An individual compute node within a connected "swarm" computing model is also unaware of (or unconcerned with) "needs" of neighboring nodes. Hence altruistic behavior (common in animal - and especially human - swarm models) is not evident in modern compute clusters.
outcome: The IBM company has been interested in the notion of autonomic computing and self-healing systems well before the onset of the modern era of artificial intelligence. Now that AI is well established as key strategic initiative in our product planning, it would be good to start up Academy-led advanced thinking on next generation AI systems that are robust and continuously learning in the field. Self-aware systems, as conceived, will pave the path forward for next generation AI systems that are capable of protecting themselves against malicious attacks, while also caring about the resource needs of cooperating agents within its swarm (i.e. "teaming") circle.  This initiative will enable a set of skilled and interested IBM personnel to get together (across Research and product teams) and brainstorming the solution strategy against the backdrop of the "Problem Statement" given above. This will lead to a formal research project in this area, and will also help identify internal/external funding strategies to help grow the investment in next generation AI solutions.

title: A Novel, Unified & Simplified Architectural Framework Integrated with IBM's IoT,  Big Data Analytics, Cloud, AI/Cognitive, & Cybersecurity Capabilities for Federal Government Accounts
executiveChampionReason: As our primary executive champion,Nicholas Flood is the director for Australian Federal Government accounts who have accountability for client success, full visibility to the client concerns, value propositions, and IBM capability for the scope of this study. Secondary sponsoring champion, Eric Schnatterly, has served as the Vice President for IBM Cloud, Cognitive Software, and Security Services for Australia & New Zealand who also covered the Federal Government accounts until end of 2019. Eric, as our secondary champion will be consulted on requirements and strategy of our study based on his extensive experience in his prior role in Australian Federal Government initiatives.
description: The purpose of this study is to develop an innovative architectural framework integrated with the IoT,  Big Data, leveraging IBM's Cloud Paks (for Data, Security, and Integration & others as apply), Watson AI/Cognitive capabilities, and Cybersecurity principles. The industry focus is on Federal Government accounts initially piloting the Australian Government landscape and potentially can be customised and scaled up to other government accounts across the globe.
problemStatement: Big Data practice, Analytics, IoT, Cognitive, Cybersecurity, and Cloud are IBM's strategic technology focus and major business capability domains. However, our Federal Government accounts depict tremendous pain points related to these growing technology domains and not taking the full advantage of the capabilities to address the pain points. For example, in the latest Home Affairs industry summit, it was pointed out that the Australian Government don’t have effective predictive analytics capabilities despite the departments and agencies create a tremendous amount of data across the country. Due to the lack of this capability, critical cybersecurity services are not as proactive and effective as required to improve national security.  Our preliminary findings show that there are no single, reliable, and integrated architectural and capability framework that can use these empowering technology domains and business capabilities for effective digital transformation and service excellence across the country. Federal Government organisations in Australia require a unified architectural view and business capability to effectively transition and transform by leveraging unified technology and architectural capabilities for creating service excellence of country critical demands and enabling strategic business outcomes with agility. The pain points are evident as frequently reflected and repeated in the national press and media.
outcome: This study aims to create an innovative and simplified architectural approach proposing to integrate the key technology domains and capabilities to address fundamental client pain points by providing a coherent and simple architectural framework. The establishment of such a successful framework is expected to increase client confidence for quick decision making and IBM’s service excellence credibility in the Government industry. The study is designed to provide three major outputs: an informative executive report for IBM senior leadership, a unified and simplified architectural framework to inform the client executives, and  key architectural work products such as requirements matrix, use cases, viability assessment, system context, and high-level architectural construct with relevant descriptions for IBM internal use by architects, specialists, and the sales leads. This study is initially planned for the Australian Federal Government use cases as a pilot, then can be further customised and scaled up for other government organisations across the globe. This study is expected to provide useful and pragmatic insights to our senior executive teams and empower their communications with the key client stakeholders who are responsible for organisational technology adoption, purchase approvals, and transformational decision making.

title: Strategic Patenting
executiveChampionReason: The executive champions lead business units that can contribute to and especially benefit from this initiative's workstream.
description: We intend to study ways in which IBM can ensure that we are getting the right inventions at the right time from all inventors, and how IBM should select inventions for patent protection to best align IBM's patent investment with its technical and business strategy.
problemStatement:
IBM's approach to patenting is largely "bottom up" -- that is, we rely on innovators to disclose their inventions, often encouraged by their team leads, management, and master inventors.  This approach serves us well: IBM has long been the leader in US patents issued, demonstrating the depth of IBM's innovation.  

We also know that IBM’s patent investment is not necessarily aligned with IBM's technical and business strategy.  Such an alignment is needed to maximize the value of IBM's intellectual property.
outcome:
We intend to study ways to augment IBM's current bottom-up patenting approach with more targeted, innovation-focused approaches.  Aspirationally, we intend to make recommendations regarding:
- Ensure that all key innovations are protected, and investment reflects IBM's technical and business strategy.
- Ensure that all key innovators in identified innovation areas are encouraged to participate in the patent process
- Ensure that we have patent coverage in geographies that matter over relevant time frames
- Develop metrics that measure progress and results

We believe that these steps will help IBM optimize its patent investment and ensure diversity in the inventor population.

(Note that these suggestions are intended to augment IBM's current approach to invention generation, not to replace it.)

title: Revisiting our Technical Design principles: ensuring we are #InclusivebyDesign #EthicalbyDesign
description: We have been looking hard at AI, ensuring fairness and reducing bias, but are there other areas of our design principles where we need to do better, be better, in terms of ensuring fairness and inclusivity?
problemStatement:
Current events unfolding in the US led many IBMers to re-pledge under the #BeEqual initiative.

We, as a technology company, have power to affect real change. Our employment practices are part of that. However, from a Technology perspective, how we design our systems, and encourage our clients to design systems, can have a profound impact on the lives of different groups in society.

IBM is a leader in this space with approaches to Ethical AI, Trust and Transpareny - but, today, many IBMers ask themselves: What more can we do?

Our sphere of influence is Technology, our reach is far, our behavior has impact, our standards and practices influence technology across the globe.

I propose we explore further, looking to our core design principles to understand what a framework for EthicalByDesign and InclusiveByDesign might look like.

Three questions would frame the study:
- Are there aspects of Technical solutions, beyond AI, that can lead to negative outcomes for specific groups in society?
- Can we characterize elements that negatively (or overly positively) affect Technology outcomes associated with different groups in society?
- Can we shape design principles that reduce the risk of negative/skewed outcomes affecting different groups in society?
outcome:
IBMers are people who want to act to solve problems and improve situations, we always want to act where we can, this is one of our great strengths, and this situation is no different - however it is harder for us to understand how we can help and effect change. 

This initiative would allow us to explore themes, and build towards a framework that supports technical IBMers in their design decisions, actions and advise, in line with our shared beliefs, towards our clients and society.

IBM is already on a path as a world leader in Ethical AI, this would be the next step in that journey allowing us to be leaders in Ethical Technology, and Ethical Technical Leadership.

Building Brand awareness, but more importantly deserved Brand loyalty, by actively demonstrating that we continuously strive to improve, to act ethically, and to produce ethical technical solutions, in line with the global zeitgeist where many of our competitors are publicly failing to step up to the mark.
ideaMigrationComments: Thanks Vicky for proposing this. As we have discussed, this is a worthy initiative to take forward. We're moving this from the Idea Board into an initiative.

title: Telecom Tower Monetization
executiveChampionReason: Marisa is the VP in charge of the Strategy and Offerings for the global TME industry, and expert in the Telecom network cloud transformation
industryName: Telecom Media and Entertainment Industry Affiliate
description: Create a Point-of-View on the Telecom Tower market, and the IBM value proposition
problemStatement:
Today, almost all telecom operators are focused on building their next generation 5G networks, which requires huge investments. In order to reduce and support those costs, a lot of those operators put in place some infrastructure sharing agreements, typically at a country level, and many times they also decide to spin-off the tower management in a separate company.

Those tower companies currently manage mainly the passive part of a tower, but could also provide additional services in the future, in order to find new sources of revenue. They also need to find ways to reduce costs. 

Currently, IBM is quite well established in the Telecom industry, selling to Communications Services Providers (CSPs). But what about those Tower Companies? There have been some key references, mainly through the Real Estate and Facility management angle with our lead product Tririga. However, opportunities for tower companies have to be considered holistically, potentially including the active radio (software) part of the tower as well.
IBM, with RedHat, is very well placed to help tower companies and operators in this approach.
outcome:
The objective of this initiative is:
1. To draw a clear picture of the tower market, the main players, the value chain, recent trends
2. To analyze what services are provided by a tower company, now and what they could be in the future
3. To identify the business opportunities for IBM: what solutions, what capabilities? Draw recommendations for IBM to address this market. If time and resources permit, a PoC could be built, leveraging existing assets in the area (e.g. with Tririga, TNC-O, Blockchain, etc…)

title: Data placement for cloud applications
executiveChampionReason: Julie is a key advocate for SDS and Operational Modelling
description: Advice and techniques on data placement when architecting an IT system in a hybrid cloud.
problemStatement:
Delivering successful applications is dependent on good placement decisions – advice on this is currently lacking in Garage Method.  Making wrong decisions can and will cost our clients, and results in failing projects.

In many cases we underestimate the complexity of data interactions, leading to increased cost and danger of data accuracy issues. This gets even worse when regulatory compliance, such as GDPR, is required.  When building a new application in the cloud, the decision of whether to move the associated data to cloud (which could have security and compliance issues) or to leave it on-premise (adding complexity to data access) is complex.

This study will address this, by enhancing Garage Method to consider shareability, compliance (internal and external), security, auditability, data gravity, replication, latency, batch processing, systems management, recovery, and cost when doing placement. 

We will cover why proper placement is important and what needs to be looked at. We will also deliver technique papers to ensure that solutions are enterprise ready, robust and scalable. These papers will enhance our architectural methods and the Garage Method, so we can create enterprise applications that can be delivered safely and efficiently in the new hybrid multi-cloud world.
outcome:
Currently when IT systems are designed it is likely that cloud technology accelerators are used, but that other factors are not considered.  In consequence our clients encounter unexpected costs, elongated projects, complex regulatory processes and propensity for data inconsistency.

Designing systems for our clients that uses appropriate placement considerations will help us to select the correct hybrid cloud architecture and technologies.  It will also help us ensure that this aligns with the client’s business initiatives, and supports their mission critical systems. 

Avoiding unnecessary data replication will greatly improve the time to market for projects and drive down cost. All of that without impacting data accuracy and improving compliance to regulatory standards.

title: Experience Layer Evaluation for Commerce Platforms
executiveChampionReason: N/A
description: As headless / API commerce platforms become the norm, we are seeing a surge in discussions / debates / architecture evaluation efforts with our clients to help them with a recommendation and choose the right frontend to drive the experience of customer (commerce) platforms.
problemStatement:
As API-first a.k.a. headless commerce platforms become the norm, there is a surge in discussions with clients, globally, to help them with the frontend architecture and evaluation process to choose the right head / experience layer for the digital commerce platforms.Most standard commerce platforms come with “head” (reference storefront / accelerator) for a headless commerce implementation. While it may be natural choice to use the OOTB storefront if the commerce platform is expected to support close to 100% of the functionality. But if the customer engagement platform includes more than just commerce to serves as the frontend for additional backends such as CRM, CMS, Data Platforms etc. the decision to choose the experience layer (head) is not so straightforward anymore. 
This evaluation tool and POV is expected to provide an organized way to guide the recommendation.
outcome:
Objectives of this initiative:

Define the criteria that is used to determine frontend architecture and experience platform
Build the scoring model for each of the frontend choices for major iX Strategic commerce platforms:
SAP Commerce Cloud (Hybris)
Salesforce Commerce Cloud – B2C & B2B
Adobe Commerce Cloud (Magento)
HCL Commerce
Score the following frontend options for each commerce platform
OOTB Reference Storefront / Accelerator
AEM
Custom Frontend (React / Angular / Vue)
iXLiberty
Develop a POV on the frontend architecture / experience platform based on our experience and Lessons Learnt

title: AI-based team assignment and scheduling app
executiveChampionReason: Armand leads the Data Science and AI Elite team, which is the first test bed for this innovation.
description: Managers of teams who engage on mid-term client-facing assignments (e.g. 2-12 week assignments), face frustration and difficulty when trying to construct the best team squads matched to client needs. They need to consider not only the client needs, but the client's timing, the team member's skills and work dynamic between each other and with the client, the client project skill requirements, client and team member availability, and other other factors such as legal prerequisites and technical prerequisites that that lead to uncertainty in project start dates. Today, managers make these assignments using paper or Excel - the process is time consuming, and any change means a lengthy reconsideration of the assignment scenario. This tool will replace this frustrating process with a 1-click solution.

title: Foldable Mobile Devices Application Responsiveness and Test Strategies
executiveChampionReason:
Richard Hopkins is an IBM DE, an Executive IT Architect, Q Ambassador and a Fellow of the Institution of Engineering and Technology. Richard first reviewed this AoT Initiative proposal and realized the benefits of this AoT Initiative’s outcome and involved Scott Rushton, Matt Ganis from IBM Digital and iX Design groups to take forward this initiative. Richard can influence implementation of this AoT Initiative across business units in IBM. 

Srinivasan is a Partner & Leader for IBM North America Quality & Testing Services (NAQTS) group in GBS and has direct stake in one of the expected outcomes of this AoT Initiative,  i.e. Test Strategies for Foldable Device Applications Responsiveness.

Antje Kruse-Schomaker is an IBM Design Principal and Practice Leader Customer Engagement & Design. Antje is one of the stake holder of Design principles and best practices outcome of this AoT Initiative.
description: An IBM AoT Initiative to research and analyze Foldable Mobile devices application responsiveness and recommend design patterns, best practices, development approaches, testing and automation strategy.
problemStatement: As more and more Foldable mobile devices are expected to proliferate Mobile market, it presents new challenges for applications responsiveness design scalability, development, testing and test automation. What are the applications scalability challenges for both foldable/un-foldable layouts? Will there be any impact on application responsiveness based on different device hardware types involved? What application responsiveness and usability design considerations (including Touch and other gestures) are required to maximize user experience for foldable devices?  Can IBM’s existing iX design accelerators be used for foldable device applications and any updates required in same? What object locator strategies (for both foldable/un-foldable modes) should be adopted for automation of foldable device applications? How to host/launch mobile devices in foldable and un-foldable modes in mobile device clouds for testing?   The proposed AoT study helps to analyze these problems and recommend design patterns, development approaches, test strategies and automation approaches for IBM Digital/iX and Mobile QA community.
outcome: IBM Foldable Mobile device applications responsiveness design patterns, best practices, development approaches, recommended test strategies and test automation tools. Outcome of this AoT Initiative helps to analyze these problems and recommend design patterns, new design accelerators, development approaches, test strategies and automation approaches for IBM Digital/iX and GBS Mobile QA community.

title: SAP HANA Reference Architecture for Multi-Cloud
executiveChampionReason: Being IBM GBS Distinguished Engineer for SAP Michael is key stakeholder for SAP Multi-Cloud Architecture.
description: Goal of this effort is to define one community driven (open source) Reference Architecture that would be perceived and generally accepted as Industry Standard for deploying SAP HANA by all major IaaS vendors (IBM Cloud, AWS, Azure, GCP).
problemStatement:
SAP is supporting many different architectures how to deploy SAP HANA. On top of this each major IaaS vendor is presenting their own "Reference Architecture" - these are quite often very generic and not aligned to each other.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                        
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                        As result of this there is no "industry standard" how to deploy SAP HANA and each player in the ecosystem is pushing his own point of view. This is confusing customers and it is complicating migrations from on-premise to cloud as customers are insisting that cloud must support same architecture which they run on-premise.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                        
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                        It is also quite common that SAP is releasing features that are having architectural limitations (for example feature not supported for certain High Availability option). As result of this Managed Services teams are able to support only those features which are compatible with their architecture.
outcome:
One Reference Architecture accepted by whole ecosystem (including all major IaaS vendors) would help customers to understand what is the one architecture to use.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                        
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                        It would help all IaaS vendors to plan their development to be aligned with this One Reference Architecture. I would simplify all on-premise to cloud migrations and remove all the confusion about right or wrong decisions.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                        
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                        One Reference Architecture would also help SAP to plan their development so that they can ensure that all new features will be supported across all platforms.

title: Reversible binary neural networks
executiveChampionReason: VP of my Lab
description: Investigation of use of reversible binary neural networks for image processing
problemStatement: Designing the architecture of conventional neural networks is a black art and training them relies on heuristics and suffers from problems such as overfitting.  Training deep neural networks with back propagation also takes a lot of data and a lot of time.  Histon says:  "My view is throw it all away and start again." (from: https://www.axios.com/ai-pioneer-advocates-starting-over-2485537027.html).  This initiative is to investigate the use of reversible binary neural networks as an alternative to conventional neural networks; the first step being to see if they can be made to work at all.
outcome: We are going to try to solve MNIST digit recognition problem using the reversible binary neural network concept.  This will result in a new neural network architecture and a new training algorithm of some kind (backpropagation won't work).  If the new architecture eventually turns out to be better than conventional deep neural networks then there would be considerable business value.  This is possible but unlikely so the main business value is likely to be developing AI technical skills.  Use of TensorFlow library etc.

title: Event based Transactional Semantics in Microservices
executiveChampionReason: Ian is current CTO for App Dev Platform and is one of the potential catcher of the findings of this study.
description: In our first academy study (Transactional Semantics in Microservices) we looked at approaches to achieve eventual consistency in microservices. We now embark into using events and asynchronous mechanisms to achieve scale  while maintaining same transactional guarantees.
problemStatement: Event based programming for cloud native applications is a common pattern as it increases decoupling of microservices and offers the potential to scale applications. In our first study (https://academyweb-prod.w3ibm.mybluemix.net/initiatives/e8e00afd221dea3f035c0ed7e65580b9) we reviewed the space of transactional semantics in cloud native applications, studied existing solutions, and developed a protocol using synchronous mechanism. We now extend that study to use event based mechanisms and understand the differences and alternatives to achieve a high performance protocol that delivers the same guarantees
outcome: We expect to add asynchronous capabilities to the TXMS (https://github.ibm.com/tx-ms/poc)  protocol and enhance our website (https://pages.github.ibm.com/tx-ms/tx-ms)
