title: Edge Video Processing Platform
executiveChampionReason: Mr. Lartigue is a prominent leader in the Telecommunications, Media and Entertainment Industry. He is currently pioneering strategies and architectures about the cloudification journey at enterprises which will influence Telco networks. The Edge Video Processing Platform study being proposed aligns to Mr. Lartigue's vision of 5G and Edge Computing as it applies these notions to Video processing and consumption use cases.
industryName: Telecom Media and Entertainment Industry Affiliate
description: Asses requirements of video edge processing on order to position IBM technologies and services in that space
problemStatement: Video continues to be the main traffic on fixed and mobile network and will increase with 5G. One could argue that the internet is morphing from a data network into a video distribution network. Therefore, the industry explores technologies to reduce cost of transporting video traffic while improving user experience for video consumption in domains like perceived video quality and delay to experience content. Additionally, 5G IoT Use Cases in domains like video surveillance, monitoring of content supply chain, drones, AR/VR and live video broadcasting, all rely on efficient processing of video. The common denominator between those consumer and enterprise Use Cases is the need to process video at the edge of the telecom network. Processing downstream video to improve distribution on the last mile of a Telco network is different than applying AI to an upstream video surveillance feed. From an architecture perspective, the workload for both processes need to be deployed at the edge and tightly integrated with data and control plane, more and more implemented as Virtual Network Function (VNF) of the operator network. Edge Video processing is definitely a core enablers of many 5G consumer and IoT edge computing Use Cases.
outcome: The objective of the proposed initiative is to better asses the specific requirements of video edge processing to better position IBM technologies and services in that space (ICP, MCM, GBS Cloud network services, ALM, ASM). To achieve this, we will review the different video edge processing workloads (QoE optimization, visual analytics, AR/VR) requirements, look for lessons learned from existing IBM PoC including video edge processing (e.g. Vodafone 5G City Of Milan trial, SK Telecom and Sinclair for live broadcasting, etc.), identify key vendors and their strategy/roadmap for containerizing video workloads, define the options for effective integration of containerized video workload with existing Telco Virtual Central Office initiatives (like CORD and OPNFV VCO), validate the technical analysis by creating a prototype that integrates selected video workload deployed on ICP with virtualized network function both orchestrated by a Telecom network orchestrator like IBM Agile Lifecycle Manager.

title: The Interoperability Fabric as a H&HS Modernization Backplane
executiveChampionReason: Myles Lynch is selected as Executive Champion in his capacity as VP for GBS State/Local in the US. Included in this business portfolio are the US-based Health & Human Services (HHS) agencies that are in the planning stages of transforming and modernizing their enterprises.
description: The initiative will describe how the IBM HHS Interoperability Fabric can be used to modernize IT portfolios with Health and Human Services organizations, and establish an industry platform that embraces the opportunities and challenges of today’s H&HS ecosystems
problemStatement:
HHS is a key growth market in public sector, in US SLED and globally. Clients in this market vary widely in size and motivation – from a small County like Sonoma in California that is seeking to establish a Care Coordination platform, to a huge State like New York seeking to modernize its Medicaid portfolio. A common theme is the interoperability fabric, which connects various systems and modules such that the whole is greater than the sum of its parts. IBM HHS Connect360 answers this common theme, in spirit; its success in California and New Zealand underscores its potential. But how do we harvest this potential systemically and predictably? The key questions that must be answered - 

-	How do we penetrate the broader market with the interoperability fabric?
-	How does the interoperability fabric enable the strategy patterns for modernization?
-	How does the interoperability fabric play with hybrid/multi-cloud, OpenShift and Cloud Paks? 
-	How does the interoperability fabric converge with Red Hat synergy initiatives? 
-	How do we build a framework for reuse and innovation at scale, such that the interoperability fabric grows organically stays ahead of competition?
outcome:
The expected outcome is to enable a comprehensive Go-to-Market approach for the interoperability fabric. 

-	Deconstruct the market into client tiers and types, and define tailored base solutions for each tier/type. Consider funding sources, procurement methods and PtW to define a clear path towards signings and client value. 
-	Describe demonstration and PoC capabilities available to support GTM efforts. Outline a repeatable process that includes demonstration of the base solution, Design Thinking workshops to identify further tailoring, and PoCs for specific needs.
-	Describe how the interoperability fabric can be offered as a component, and an underpinning, of larger IT portfolio modernization engagement. Outline how the interoperability fabric enables the strategy, architecture, DevOps and deployment patterns for modernization. (Relate to earlier AoT paper.)
-	Describe the symbiotic relationships between the interoperability fabric and Red Hat synergy initiatives. Outline a Run Anywhere approach that helps the interoperability fabric fit into the broader hybrid, multi-cloud strategy.
-	Prepare a high level roadmap, based on asset harvesting at scale. Outline a path for organic growth, and systematic insertions of emergent technologies, such that the solution stays ahead of competitors in the longer term.

title: Standardisation of visual modelling notation
executiveChampionReason: Grady has experience of creating a modelling standard which was then adopted across the industry, which we are hoping to replicate in this study.
description: Color, Icons, Visual style – standardising the meaning across the Industry
problemStatement:
When modelling, pictures carry great value and meaning - but only when the person viewing the model has the same understanding of the visual notation as the creator.  Unfortunately that is unlikely right now - different parts of IBM and the wider industry have independently evolved their notation.  This particularly applies to visual aspects such as Colour, Icon and Style.  
                                        
In most modelling languages (SDS, TOGAF, UML) colour, style and icons are not included in the description, so usage is at the modeller’s discretion.  Other parts of the industry have been independently developing their usage of these aspects.  The net result is that models can be difficult to understand, with a particular colour or style potentially meaning different things to different modellers.
outcome:
This study looks to address that – first within IBM, but aspirationally to provide a standard for the wider industry too.  We intend to bring together the experience from Design Thinking, the Cloud Architecture Center, Cognitive Architect, and many other teams from within IBM to rationalise the meaning attached to Colour, Icon and Style and to look to align them into an industry-wide standard. 
                                        
We look to publish a set of standards which can then be used consistently across IBM - so for example a particular shade of green will have a known meaning, and a common set of Icons is available to all.  Achieving this will give a common visual frame of reference for all modellers. We will look to influence the different parts of IBM to adopt these standards within their standard notation and tooling. This can then be used as a route to influence the wider industry.

title: Define and build a framework for large scale Multi-Cloud Migration
executiveChampionReason: N/A
description: Define and build a framework consisting of process, method and tools for rapid migration and continuous modernisation on multi-cloud.
problemStatement:
To kick start large scale cloud migration/modernization, a robust cloud platform design is required. We need a predefined framework for identifying migration patterns and arriving at the most optimal migration path. This includes reference implementation architecture for target platform foundation and landing zones. A well defined acceleration framework for executing the migrations rapidly and subsequently managing with continous modernisation is need of the hour. 
At this moment, a framework is needed for building multi-cloud landing zones(that can support various workloads - SAP, Red Hat Openshift, Microsoft .Net, JEE, databases, datawarehouses and COTs products), leveraging the right security, network and shared services baseline templates. Additionally, to accelerate massive scale migrations, lack of pre-built migration patterns(with Infrastructure as code) and their unavailability via a ServiceCatalog approach makes IBM's go to market posture of enabling seamless, fast track migration/modernisation programs weaker.
outcome:
We expect to deliver the following:
1. Fit gap of current IBM capabilities and solution recommendations for accelerated migrations.
2. Landing zone framework point of view and design - this can be onboarded as an asset to any client's Cloud center of excellence.
3. Multi-cloud landing zone Infrastructure as code framework - this will help to establish Day 0/minimal viable landing zones.
4. Pattern catalog for multi-cloud migration supported by code assets.
5. A bottoms-up business case framework for massive scale cloud migration.

All of this will help IBM to:
1. Establish IBM as thought leader in massive scale migration in a multi-cloud scenario.
2. Accelerate multi-cloud migrations including migration to IBM cloud.
3. Accelerate adoption of Red Hat Openshift for migration + modernisation.
4. Increase IBM Cloud, Red Hat revenue and IBM services revenue related to cloud migration & modernisation.

description: This briefing will provide a technical introduction to peer-to-peer communications for mobile apps. It will touch on the following topics:  1. Overview and definitions  2. Description of the types of applications for which peer-to-peer communication can be appropriate.  3. Peer to peer technology  4. Technical challenges that typically need to be addressed  5. App integration and UX impacts
problemStatement: There are a number of use-cases which lend themselves to the use of peer to peer communication. For example, this technology can enable mobile teams to collaborate by direct exchange of information in environments that don’t have internet access. P2P connectivity can also provide a means to provide distributed functionality without the need for a central set of services to manage the whole process. This approach, however, comes with with a number of technical challenges.  Users may, at various times, be disconnected from their peers, which implies that data inconsistencies between peers will often arise.  Varying network conditions may also constrain the amount of data that can be exchanged for extended periods of time. Finally, shifting network topologies create their own set of challenges that need to be addressed. This has a direct impact on the type of applications for which this technology is appropriate and impacts how the user experience is designed.
outcome:
A technical briefing will be produced that will cover the topics specified above. It will describe the technical challenges associated with this technology and describe some of the ways in which these can be addressed.  Some of the key technical topics to be discussed include: 
Routing of data between peers
Identification and removal of redundant messages
Management of data inconsistencies, eventual state. 
User experience impacts

The discussion will draw from experiences made with a number of real-world applications that have been developed for public safety and aviation.  Current challenges along with future advances will be discussed. Some of the use-cases that may be highlighted include:

Public Health: Sharing weather alerts
Public Health: Covid-19 contract tracing support
Public Health: Emergency Response 
Aviation: On board seat changes
Aviation: Inflight Service Management 
Aviation: In Cabin Collaboration

The paper will provide technical analysts with an understanding of what peer-to-peer is and how it can be used to produce successful mobile apps.  Examples from United Airlines, The Weather Company and others will demonstrate show how the technology can be put to effective use. This should help to showcase IBM expertise in this field and may help to initiate conversations with partners or customers.

title: The Challenges in Data Storage in Autonomous Cars
executiveChampionReason: Works closely with team, expertise in subject matter
description: Study of the problems associated with a robust, scalable data storage solution for autonomous automobiles.  This is tied as a "sub-initiaitve" to the storage component of the AoT Systems Cote Team initiaitive.
problemStatement: Autonomous test vehicles are generating tremendous amount of data. A single test vehicle can produce about 30TB per day, which is 3,000 times the scope of Twitter's daily data. A robust and scalable data storage solution is one of the most important infrastructures for autonomous vehicle companies. Some of the key problems include (1) how to choose among on-premise, cloud, and hybrid model for efficient and cost effective data storage; (2) how to store high volume video streaming on the vehicle; (3) how the storage is used in different phases of the life cycle: data collection, machine learning model training, and inference. (4) how the data stored on different test vehicles can be shared and exchanged for better model training. (5) the backup and resilience plan. These problems have not been extensively studied.
outcome: We will provide insights and directions for potential technical breakthroughs with storage and autonomous cars in this white paper.

title: Legacy Modernization in the Cloud era: 2018 update and IBM Point of View
executiveChampionReason: Hayden has decades of experience in this area and leads the IBM DevOps portfolio development used by many customers to maintain and modernize their legacy workloads.
description: Refresh the IBM Point of View on the Legacy Modernization topic and opportunity in the light of latest offerings and new trends.
problemStatement: Most of the enterprise IT critical workloads, in every industry, still rely on techniques and technologies from a few decades ago. Legacy modernization is the opportunity to bring such application code to the latest development platforms (tools, languages) and techniques (devOps) in order to ease maintenance and change. Given its current and past leadership in IT over the past 5 decades, and its leading mainframe platform, IBM is uniquely positioned to offer a migration path to organizations facing the challenges associated to such modernization initiatives. Yet, given the breadth of the domains, it is hard for our prospects and sellers to navigate the many options and software or services offerings which IBM makes available. The objective of this study is to identify existing and relevant IBM resources and consolidate our Point of View into a single white paper.
outcome:
Objectives:
- (Re)formalizing what the topic means for IBM and its markets in 2018 (scope, definitions, segmentation, competition, opportunities);
- (Re)cataloging the IBM capability in this area (product offerings, service offerings, people), and publish/maintain it through an internal web presence;
- Publishing a PoV consolidating IBM's positioning and capabilities on this topic.
                                                                                
Business value:
Impact - Given IBM's  involvement in IT over decades, and billions of lines of legacy code still running critical applications around the world, this is a very strategic topic for IBM which requires an update to include recent IBM offerings
Effort - The tricky part, to keep the scope both manageable in a volunteer-based effort and content breadth.
Inclusive - We will reach out to SMEs across GBS, Research and the Cloud groups.
Consumed - Applying Design Thinking techniques, we'll identify the targeted personas involved in legacy migration initiatives to ensure we create content relevant to them, both internally and externally (AoT PoV).
Unique - The topic is certainly not new, but (1) there doesn't seem to be a central consensus on it and (2) we need an update actualized with recent capability wrt new plays from competitors and new trends (e.g. cloud, cognitive).
adminComments: 7/25: Per Jean Pommier - we lost our Executive Sponsor in June (Hayden Lindsey, who moved to the the competition at CA), and, earlier in March, our AoT Coordinator/Assistant (Monica Claeson, who also left IBM), that certainly did hurt. Yet, given the flurry of external messages in this area from all over IBM, building a single and consolidated PoV on Legacy Modernization has never been more important IMO. That being said, this isn't the #1 business priority for my boss, at least the one I had a month ago. I hope to make a stronger case with my new boss (just changed), so updated the target date to the end of the year. My co-sponsor is also willing for the study to continue and complete.With that, I will look for a new executive sponsor.  TC UPDATED EXPECTED END DATE TO 12/31/2018. TC

title: Adaptive Temperature Manager using Data Science Methods
executiveChampionReason:
Philipp Spaeti is the CTO of IBM Switzerland. In the time of War of Talents, it is in the central interest of IBM Switzerland to bring students of the University of St. Gallen (HSG) closer to data science and the cognitive and cloud applications IBM has to offer. Philipp Spaeti is involved in the development and execution of blockchain & security hackathons as well as the development of programs e.g. in the field of digital engineering at various technical colleges and universities. Philipp is therefore the ideal Executive Champion for this initiative. 

Furthermore, this initiative is vigorously supported by Dr. Martin Maehler in his role as IBM University Relation Manager in DACH.

The members of the Data Science & Technology Club (DSTC) of the University of St. Gallen, who accept this challenge together with the IBM team, have been up to 100 students in previous years. In several teams, they spend more than one semester dealing with the task and searching for valuable solutions.
description: Design of a Minimum Delightful Experience (MDM) of an Adaptive Temperature Manager using Data Science Methods
problemStatement: Appliances are  installed in data centers in racks. These racks are divided into standardized units. A lot of energy is used for cooling to ensure the perfect operation of appliances under all possible load conditions. Thereby the individual appliances and its position within the rack are not considered. A crucial solution piece is a mesh-like sensor array that can detect the incoming cooling air temperature more precisely at different heights in one or more racks. This permits precise determination of the actual cooling requirement of the entire area as well as of the installed appliances. The dense sensor mesh makes it possible to identify potential failure sources that would not be possible with a conventional room temperature measurement on the one hand and a purely isolated, appliance-based measurement on the other. The fine-meshed sensor grid not only allows statements to be made about the surroundings at different heights, but also an assessment as to whether there are deviations at the same height, on all sides or in the middle of the measuring surface. This can be used to proactively report and initiate repair or air duct adjustment before the affected unit is damaged or malfunctions due to inadequate cooling.
outcome:
We expect DSTC to develop one or more dashboards with the assistance of the IBM team, which among other things visualize:
1. Where and when anomalies occur and under what circumstances.
2. Which equipment is operating optimally.
3. Which devices are in danger of violating the maximum value or the minimum value specified by the manufacturer.
4. System recommendations on how to optimize the rack design
5. System recommendations on how much the room temperature can be raised or the air supply can be changed to achieve an optimal ratio between equipment performance and total energy consumption.

The students work with structured data (e.g. sensor data), but also unstructured data taken from the manufacturers' specification documents.

Like professional Data Scientists, the students should present their approach, findings and recommendations for the next steps in the form of a story.

As TSS, we want to offer our clients novel services in both logo and non-logo environments that optimize the operation of appliances in the DC in terms of availability, performance and energy consumption.

IBM TSS has filed two patents for this purpose.

title: How to create a fabric of semantic knowledge  across an enterprise
executiveChampionReason: Marcio has deep knowledge and experience in the areas of semantic layers, data fabrics and business consumption and can advise us on the best way to start and proceed and to provide the best possible product internally for our practitioners and, most importantly, for our clients.
description: Create a semantic fabric across the enterprise that will facilitate the integration of data and business knowledge that currently exists in different applications and data stores across the different LOBs and data silos.
problemStatement:
Most large scale organizations today employ a range of different applications or technological components from different vendors where the level of integration is often limited to the necessary technological connections. However what is often missing is any integration of the business knowledge that exists in these different applications across the different LOBs.

So what is required to enable the persistent and coherent sharing of knowledge across the organisation. How can a Data Scientist or Business User in a System of Insight know what are the business applications or business processes in the System of Record or  System of Engagement that would be relevant to the specific  business issue that they are trying to address. Or how does an Analyst trying to define the creation or a new Front end application or set of services know what are the relevant data assets needed to feed that application.  Currently in all such cases, that level of interconnect business knowledge is only gathered manually on a piecemeal basis and in a manner that is not of any reuse to the organization in the future. 

How can we persist, grow and curate such knowledge to the ongoing benefit of the enterprise.
outcome:
To the business - the ability to quickly find what is the full network of knowledge across the enterprise for a particular application, business process, service or data asset, means that the organization is better able to plan any necessary growth or change in their ecosystem and is also able to adapt much more rapidly to any changes in their business or competitive ecosystem. 

To the technical executives (CIO/CTO/CDO) - they are able to more efficiently define how the various different IT systems are being used to underpin/support different business challenges , and where to determine areas of future investment to best align with the organizations overall business goals. 

The semantic fabric differs from Industry-specific data models like TMF's Shared Information Data Model and IBM 's IFW model in that we would use those models as the baseline data foundation but would integrate disparate legacy and non-standardized data using these models as the baseline model allowing the business user to see the result as a single, common business taxonomy. This would allow the business user to focus on business outcomes and value rather than mapping disparate technical terms and data to a common taxonomy.

title: Form an Academy - Inspired "Problem Solving Academy" to focus on cultivating and developing leading-edge post-incident learning methods across IBM to directly benefit our clients.
executiveChampionReason: Ingo has a great deal of experience with operations and IBM Garage methods. He recognizes the need to enhance the historic view of ITIL based methods, which fall short. Ingo is a luminary in the field of SRE and understands how to manage and run blameless post-mortems, and how to get clients to reduce their technical debt and complexity. Ingo senses that the initiative has a very holistic component and would get not only client, but industry and university attention.
description: Our core team has significant experience with multiple disciplines including Root-Cause Analysis, Site Reliability Engineering, Resiliency. This initiative was on the original piloted "Ideas Board" back in late 2018 and for several months it was the top-trending idea. We plan to maximize learning from incidents.
problemStatement: Structured problem solving skills (RCA, FMEA, Fishbone, etc) and processes are very deficient across the IBM and client business units - on average, an estimated "level 3" on a scale of 10. Teams largely focus on fixing while spending very little time learning. Teams struggle along a variety of fronts, including differentiation of incident versus problem management; the inability to select the right tool / method for an incident; lack of critical thinking skills; lack of understanding and implementation of basic SRE principles; the propensity to play the "blame game" and / or to come into a situation with a pre-determined notion of the cause(s) of an issue. How do we and our clients maximize learning from high-impact incidents?  Do we learn when we go in with a preconceived notion, e.g. "someone screwed up and should get fired."  Do we learn when we go in with a preconceived idea as to the investigation technique that should be used (5-whys, FMEA, High Availability, Tree Diagrams, etc.). Do we learn when we say, even before the first meeting "we have seen this before. The recap should be short."
outcome: The expected outcome from this 3-month sprint would be that the team would create a set of world-class materials on the subject of post incident learning that would be used with IBM clients and IBM teams - a compendium of the common pitfalls / pain points in various business units along with solutions and best practices. There is a strong, untapped market for skills, product, and tooling in this arena. In the three defined sprints we will scope out and deliver materials (instructional and case studies) that can be used by any IBMer or client that revolutionizes their way of thinking regarding incidents, and provokes them to "think differently." Do they avoid the blame game? Can they distinguish between fire-fighting and post-incident analysis? Can they choose a good technique? Can they call out counter-productive behavior and encourage better behavior? Can they be torch-bearers for model behavior? Can they "teach others" how to become better problem solvers? Do they use critical thinking skills and rely on data and analysis and facts? Can they point to vetted materials to help "bring this subject to life" (e.g. David's blog, Alan's LinkedIn article, Ingo's YouTube video) dot dot dot...

problemStatement: Many IBM clients have built with IBM's help a Covid-19 Watson Assistant to answer citizens', clients' or employees' questions. Clients look to IBM to advise them how to monitor and maintain their chatbots. One aspect of chatbot maintenance is anticipating what new questions end users will begin to ask in a particular phase of the epidemic in a country. As restrictions and recommendations evolve, so will the questions end users ask. How can IBM support companies to proactively begin planning the intent training of emerging topics rather than reacting to new questions from users that the chatbot does not yet know how to answer?
outcome:
IBM is in a unique position to have a broad view across a range of Watson Assistant Covid-19 implementations. This initiative proposes a process and tooling by which IBM delivery teams can share internally the key trained intents and top intents asked by end users in the different use cases and industries. IBM delivery teams benefit by having a forward-looking view: they can view what new intents have been introduced in a particular use case, industry and country and advise clients on intents they may consider to start training. Clients will benefit from IBM's expertise by being able to better plan for subsequent improvement cycles of their Watson Assistant chatbot. 
Emphasis is on sharing of knowledge among IBM practitioners of how customer support requirements in Covid-19 use cases evolve, akin to the Watson Assistant Catalogue pre-trained intents today. In this initiative a client's intent local language training examples or responses are not shared as they are owned by each client, only the high-level "canonical" intents in English are created and stored in one centralized location allowing IBM practitioners' to build their industry and use case expertise.

title: Cognitive Telescope Network
executiveChampionReason: Naeem is the IBM CTO for Space Tech
description: Telescopic follow-up of transient astronomical events is one of the most desirable and scientifically useful activities in modern observational astronomy. From a scientific perspective, pinpointing a transient event can be essential for discovering more about the source, either by directing more powerful telescopes to observe, or to maintain a near continuous record of observations as the transient evolves. Very often transients are poorly localized on the sky and telescopes have a limited field of view thus pin-pointing the transient source is often a daunting task. Perhaps most importantly, the number of large telescopes on the planet is small, and they cannot be commandeered to randomly search for every transient of interest.    Modern sub-meter class telescopes, of the sort often owned by universities and increasingly by amateurs, if properly directed, could play an important role in enabling transient follow-up. Modern technology gives them the ability to be automated and controlled remotely and to make useful imaging observations that will enable follow-up work by other, larger telescopes. The Cognitive Telescope Network (CTN) will be a framework that takes notifications of transient events and intelligently instructs a network of sub-meter telescopes mapped into a grid and observe a large region of the sky that likely contains the transient event, based on the geolocation, weather and properties of the individual telescopes. The goal of CTN is to collect the data from this network of small telescopes, evaluate and classify that data to identify the most likely candidates for the transient being hunted and deliver the results to the astronomer community for further analysis by larger telescopes for directed and focused observations.
problemStatement: No network of interconnected telescopes exist at a world-wide scope for transient follow up of astronomical events. The lack of monitoring of events that are being published from varies Astronomical organizations including NASA, ESA, etc and not having a network that can be activated for aligning for various experiments and followups restricts our ability to take any action on these events unless done manually. Weather monitoring, location, time of day  and other factors play an essential part in the filtering of the telescopes. But without a network none of this is possible.
outcome:
IBM IoT Platform with provide the backbone for such a network across the world where each telescope becomes a IoT device and may be centrally controlled from the IBM Cloud. This will assist in followups that had not been possible so far and lead to new and exciting scientific discoveries. The network will also assist in creating a community of scientists and amateurs alike to communicate and work together for the enhancement of science. The network will communicate with the telescopes using the INDI protocol which has now become the de-facto standard that all observatories are adopting to.
Once the application is build the same capabilities may be applied for other centrally controlled optical devices. The application may also be made available with support for commercial use in the future.

title: AI-ops: realizing the full potential of AI in IT operations
executiveChampionReason: As Chief Scientist for Watson and AI, Ruchir is uniquely positioned to support this effort and ensure the broadest visibility in IBM business units.
description: A comprehensive study for infusing AI in IT-ops, emerging AI-ops use cases and growth opportunities
problemStatement: IT operations is central to IBM's business and the infusion of AI capabilities has the potential to take automation and insights to a new level. The industry has coined the term AI-ops to refer to that combination. Even though we have quickly embraced the new term, in certain cases more eager to exploit the hype than the essence, there remains ample opportunity to develop a deeper understanding of the techniques underlying AI, such as Machine learning, Deep learning, and Natural language processing and spread this knowledge farther in IBM. At the same time, a number of early successes applying AI in IT operations such as in problem determination, incident avoidance, conversational assistants (chatbots) and others can be used as examples to train our practitioners in solving a wide range of problems.
outcome: This study aims to develop a deeper understanding among our practitioners of the most common AI methods that can be used to solve IT problems. It targets technical leaders and practitioners in all IBM business units seeking to learn more about AI and its applications in IT operations. It begins with the proper foundation: Establish an accurate definition of the term "AI-ops", review present and past initiatives, introduce key AI concepts such as machine learning and natural language processing, study the most impactful use cases, and discuss opportunities for growth. While we saw some successes with early use cases, we are only beginning to realize the full potential of these techniques, and we hope that this study can serve as a guide towards realizing this opportunity.

title: Applying Visual Insights to Warehouse Operations
executiveChampionReason: Global Managing Director, Electronics Industry
description: We will evaluate the use of Visual Insights in a warehouse or stockroom, to determine if VI can recognize certain conditions. By comparing high-confidence VI conclusions to the perpetual inventory record, we can either (1) confirm that the perpetual inventory record is correct, (2) determine that the perpetual inventory record is incorrect, or (3) determine that a manual inspection is appropriate.
problemStatement: Whether large or small, warehouse managers have to balance the need for quick, efficient performance (picking and delivering parts to manufacturing, or to shipping, within hours or minutes of request) against the need for extremely high accuracy and fidelity of information (ensuring that the perpetual inventory records in their ERP system or WMS exactly correspond to what is physically in each location). Cycle counting is one way to ensure high accuracy, BUT it can be very time consuming and there is no guarantee that the cycle count team will encounter (and correct) the locations that have problems in them.
outcome:
We believe that the combination of Visual Insights to detect conditions in each location, with a comparison to the perpetual inventory record (and possibly reading the bar codes on each box or container) can help identify both those locations that ARE accurate in the system (and can count as perfect cycle counts), and those locations that may need attention. This should allow the warehouse team to move closer to 100% accuracy with no extra investment of time & resources. 
Beyond the value to the warehouse manager, there will be value to IBM: We would be able to sell a cognitive application to companies that wanted to enhance their warehouse performance, either in partnership with the handheld terminal OEM or independently. If successful, we could partner with Zebra, Honeywell, and other companies to sell this functionality.

title: IBM Methods/UMF and SDS – Consolidation and Ownership
executiveChampionReason: Richard is an advocate for SDS
description: IBM Methods/UMF and SDS – Consolidation and Ownership
problemStatement:
UMF is used within IBM to robustly deal with complex solution development and deployment projects.  SDS provides the metamodel which is used to describe systems and is the ‘standard’ which underpins IBM’s delivery projects.  It forms the basis for many IBM techniques, tools and methods, such as UMF, TeamSD, Garage, Mosaic, Cognitive Architect, etc.

They are currently in danger of being lost – we propose to address this by the following;
•	Connect together the various people and parts of IBM with an interest in UMF, SDS and related (Garage, TeamSD,…) 
•	Identify the location of and collect existing UMF and SDS Material and ensure it is held in an appropriate central repository
•	Work with the Garage team to ensure that appropriate parts of UMF and SDS are embedded
•	Determine longer term ownership for SDS as a foundation for IBM Methods and Techniques
•	Establish a structural AoT oversight
•	Move SDS to Open Source
outcome:
Whilst UMF, and its metamodel SDS, are vital to IBM’s ability to deliver complex solutions, often their value is overlooked. They are key building blocks upon which IBM depends - even the Garage framework is being built based on the content of UMF and SDS. 

However - because UMF-Methodweb and Connections are being retired by IBM by the end of 2020, the content of UMF, TeamSD and SDS which describes the basis and thinking behind them are in danger of being lost.

This initiative will collect and log the material, and put in place an ownership and governance mechanism.  The intention is to make SDS ‘Open Source’ as a route to ensuring ongoing success.

title: <client> Cloud Reference Architecture Playbook
executiveChampionReason: The asset is created to support both pre sales and post sales of Cloud Paks from an architectural perspective. MEA C&C VP would benefit from it based on the potential positive impact of the asset on the sales and success of Cloud Paks in MEA. MEA CTO VP also support the impact made by MEA technical community on IBM business in MEA.
description: To create an architectural asset that captures best practices around how the clients of our clients can use the Cloud Management Platform in a multicloud architecture in a standard, streamlined, and controlled way based on OCP and CP4MCM. It is intended to be reused by architects in presales and delivery to create a tailored version for a given OCP/CP client based on their priorities, needs, and level of adoption maturity in order to shorten sales and delivery cycle by providing a library of best practices for popular and common cloud consumer use cases.
problemStatement: Cloud adoption is a multi-dimensional transformational initiative that should be tuned for the goals and capabilities of each organization that plans to embark on a journey to cloud. Since each organization is different, it is important to tune how cloud is consumed by different parties in order to standardize the way cloud is used and align that use with the original goals of the organization of cloud adoption. With the wide range of technical capabilities brought by Red Hat OCP and IBM CP4MCM, the need for representing how architecture can realize an organization's goals through the application of such technical capabilities becomes evident. The mapping should be easily described to both business sponsors and technical practitioners. It also needs to be modular in a way that encourages building block reuse and ease of maintenance to reflect changes to technology and business needs.
outcome: A library of common cloud consumer use cases in the form of a playbook similar to sports playbooks where a "Game Plan" represents a collection of reusable "Plays" to achieve a certain outcome on the cloud that supports one or more of cloud adoption goals of an organization. Upon its completion, the playbook is intended to be customized by IBM architects to address the needs and priorities of a given client. The asset does not describe how a Cloud Reference Architecture looks like. It rather practically and strategically describes how one should be used to address certain goals. The outcome of such customization would be delivered to a client as the <client name> Cloud Reference Architecture Playbook.
finalOutcome: The asset is expected to help both tech sellers and delivery architects to show IBM though leadership in cloud adoption by providing guidance on how a client's cloud should be used and managed in the context of that client. It is a starting point that will be extended in separate AoT initiatives in two dimensions: 1- Further Cloud Pak focussed Game Plans to show IBM differentiation (such as in Data and AI), 2- Integration with other IBM content (such as Cognitive Architect and Cloud Architecture Center).
closeValue: Provides a framework of valuable content that can be extended and customized to meet client needs in support of both pre-sales and delivery activities.
publicationDescription: The deliverable is published in the form of a git repo representing the Playbook with supporting Game Plans, Plays, and Roles. The structure resembles a sports playbook. The playbook provides guidance on how a client's cloud should be used and managed. Each Game Plan represent a realization of a client cloud use case that achieves a certain outcome related to one or more of client's cloud adoption goals. The assets is intended to be used by tech sellers and delivery architects to be delivered to clients after being customized to the specifics of each client.
ratingComments: Very practical approach to guide clients and IBMers through their first steps of managing their cloud environment. We discussed to run an additional initiative to expand this to Cloud Paks as well

It is vital that we understand the existing uses of Connections and ensure there are adequate transition plans to other tools, like w3 Publisher, Box, Slack, MURAL, Trello, Git, etc. How will we make sure people can still work as efficiently as they did before the transition? What are the best practices we need to add/keep?

For example, how will the new system handle:
- Security and Export Control (cross-country sensitive data permission)?
- Social Connections (like Comments, Announcements, Networking, and Thanks)?
- Collaboration?
- Maintaining critical confidential data (like workbooks, design specs, reviews, etc.)?
- Folder/File Storage and organization
- Easy to compile wikis, web pages, graphs, tables, lists, etc.
- Ability to quickly document new, creative ideas
- Interactive collaboration (multiple, simultaneous users)
- Search consistency/capability
etc...

How can we help existing connection users be trained and prepared for the transition? What will happen to the critical legacy documentation?
outcome:
This initiative will provide information, support (e.g. tools), guidance, and training to help IBMers to continue their critical work while they transition to new tools. Each organization that is involved in this initiative will be able to assess their exposures, identify their needs, and be able to put together a plan that will work with their schedule and time frame.

The CIOs office will also gain insight into the current uses of connections to make sure IBM, as a whole, is ready for this next major transformation.

This work needs to be completed by the Sunset of Connections by 12/31/2020.

executiveChampionReason: Faisal is heading the GBS DS&AI people in MEA and is focus on building Data Science skills. He is the perfect champion to bring this forward and to help us roll it out in MEA.
description: Connecting all people in IBM MEA to support them on their path to Data Science, from building a network, training, projects, to certification
problemStatement:
Lack of sufficient number of skilled Data Scientists in MEA region for quick turnaround on RFPs / High Quality data solution build.
Absence of Data science related knowledge sharing forum local to MEA region to measure and plan for competency growth. Data Science knowledge still very scattered in disconnected pockets around MEA. Many people don't know where to go to get more information on projects, training or about the certification.
outcome:
Build a technical community of passionate Data Scientists, to keep up with technology, share knowledge and project insights across countries and practices in order to leverage their skills and increase IBM’s eminence in the field of Data Science. 
Bringing together all of MEA to exchange knowledge and enable growth and better Data Science.
Make MEA the leading Data Science region.
Increase the number of certified Data Scientists in MEA.

title: iDOR – Cognitively Context-Aware Intelligent Proximity Persona based Platform for in-Patient Touch Points - Augmenting Execution of Life Saving Actions in Smart Hospitals
description: iDOR – An IBM Service that can make more Precious Hours made available for Smarter Hospitals to save Human Life. Name derived from – “IBM Doctor On Rounds - iDOR ”
problemStatement: In every Hospital, daily Specialist Assessment Review is conducted by Specialist Doctors going on Rounds visiting for physical assessment of all in-Patients. Hitherto, this Phase is the most overlooked phase, not having been considered for Cognitive Optimization and Intelligent Cycle Time Reduction and elimination of Human infused errors. Critical hospital time (Man Hours) is lost in unproductive activities during this Phase. In an average 500 Bed hospital the loss could be as high as 38 to 75 man hours daily. The number gets much higher in larger hospitals or if there are more number of Specialist-On- review Rounds. Twice a day Specialist Round is very relevant as not all specialists come together, so eventually it breaks into 3 or more rounds with activities repeated. Prior deals with automating the delivery aspects of the therapeutic requirements. However, the sustainability of patient recovery is highly dependent on the actual daily Assessment reviews conducted by the concerned Specialist doctors-on-rounds and the corrective advises made based on patient condition and Lab results. Unfortunately much of the Precious care giving time is lost in unproductive activities which remains neglected so far.
outcome: iDOR – An IBM Service that can make more Precious Hours made available for Smarter Hospitals to save Human Life. Name derived from – “IBM Doctor On Rounds - iDOR ” HOSPITAL GAME CHANGER – Revolutionize In-patient Review cycle. The Proposed solution is a New type of Service called " iDOR " deployed as an Universal Intelligent Cloud App that Augments the Doc-Patient daily Assessment Review Touch-Points by inventing Cognitively Context-Aware and Proximity Persona based platform and also actively ensures end to end Advise Fulfillment. It drastically reduces Specialist Assessment Review & Actioning Cycle Time in a synchronized way for In patients. iDOR invention augments all Doctor and in-Patient touch point encounters at a Phase earlier than care giving / medication delivery and virtually Eliminates all manual forced time fillers in the process. Eliminates Doctor-Patient Engagement Intermediary steps Synchronous Multi Specialist Review, Re-Assess Re-Prescribe anytime, from anywhere, action-ed instantly. Augments Doc-Patient daily Assessment by Novel Engagement, Eliminates Post Assessment Time Fillers. Business value is delivered by iDOR service Bundling as an Advanced FaaS within IBM Cloud Pak for Global Deployment Availability. Practically any and all Hospitals around the world are potential customers.

title: Sustainable Management and Resilience Tool (SMART)
executiveChampionReason: I have been working closely with Allan and see him as a strategic thinker in the Business Process Innovation area. He also brings the architectural thinking that would be required to land this idea.
description: AI and blockchain based tool to capture and track external events that may offer opportunities or impose risks to sustainable business
problemStatement:
The success of business strategy is governed by external events, regulatory obligations and macro-economic factors. 
Most CXOs, busy with day-to-day operations, are unable to keep track of events which may offer opportunities to accelerate their business OR pose risk to sustenance of business.  
There is a need for monitoring external events by tapping into public & licensed information sources and assessing the impact on business strategy.
outcome: This would provide a crystal ball for businesses, allowing them to tweak their strategy and align their business objectives.

title: IBM Talent Week
executiveChampionReason: The Talent Week is the biggest event for Talent in Latin America and Deirdre, as Americas Talent Acquisition Director is the best focal for the promotion of the event and for replicating it in other regions.
description: A week of webinars, workshops and interviews for both technical and administrative external audience. Based on the hottest technologies of the market, our job demand of the year and trending frameworks, we designed an agenda con 27 different topics and 2 interview sessions for both Early Professional and professional audience.
problemStatement:
In Latin America, Early Professionals usually don't think about IBM as a leader in innovation and technology and put it behind other companies as they select their future employers. We needed a way to promote IBM's main technologies, frameworks and position it as the best employer brand, but also facing the issue that we have a very diverse audience, not only tech people but administrative, consultants, designers and analysts among others. 
During this pandemic, there is a need to reinvent our strategies of attracting talent and adapting to a virtual scenario.
outcome:
Our objective is to position IBM as an innovative and leader company in the IT ecosystem while we attract talent and promote IBM as an employer brand. We expect to generate more than 1500 leads from the event that could eventually become the next IBMers, and we are looking to have a big number of technical women to increase our diversity numbers in STEM positions. 
We're having 24 webinars and workshops about Cloud, Blockchain, Quantum, Security, AI, FrontEnd, SAP, Java and other technologies, as well as Design Thinking, SCRUM and career topics. Additional to that, we have 3 Ask Me Anything sessions with leaders were we are going to discuss about top technologies, the IBM student Program and what is IBM doing in Latin America. By the end of the week, we have 2 different interview sessions with the top talent that registered for the event, to cover our hot positions of the moment.
